I was sent out with a truck full of logs to a distant location. I barely got out of the parking lot without destroying multiple pedestrian vechiles before I was told to drive on the wrong side of the road.  I missed my first exit so I pulled an illegal u-turn with a giant semi truck hauling tons of cargo. It suddenly started getting darker and a rainstorm forced me to figure out how ot turn on the windshield wipers and the headlights. Soothed by the sounds of Russian Dance music I'm finally adjusted to the call of the highway. The moon is illuminating the darkness and in the distance I can make out the city that I'm headed towards but only slightly. It's all so calm and theraputic. Then I'm slapped with a speeding ticket because I don't understand European road signs very well. I finally make my way into the station and auto-park because after 10 minutes of trying to figure out how to make a giant truck move in reverse I failed. I was handed a few thousand dollars of a currency that I further do not understand. I'm given a shack that looks like the set of an indie horror movie and supposedly it's a "garage". I'm told that eventually I can start my own buisness, buy a fleet of trucks, possibly paint them all pink and put mech suit graphics on the side of them and make bank from this industry of freight trucks. I AM EXCITE!!
For a game that was less than 5 bucks on sale that I bought on whim, it managed to do what flashy next-gen graphics, "deep leveling up RPG systems", and the general overhyping of games haven't been able to do in a while... .It gave me a fresh experience and something that didn't feel scripted or a torn out page from "how to make games that sell good 101" handbook. I love driving games anyway so slowing it down a bit and giving it a goal in a realistic urban setting was surprisingly fun.
I've since only played a few hours, but I could stop right now and feel like the little bit of money I spent was worth it for that introduction alone. I won't though. I'm going to forge this trucking empire and dominate half of Europe. I'm going to wait for the new DLC maps that are coming up. I'm going to mod the game to death and back with all of this free content and I'm going to wait for American Truck Simulator with eager anticipation.
Until then.... Catch you on the highway with Outrun music blaring...

First things first, I am a HUGE Mad Max fan.  I grew up watching the original films and the newest addition, "Mad Max: Fury Road" is modern masterpiece.  If you haven't watched it yet, DO IT.
Now, the game.  The port is fantastic.  I have a quite outdated gaming laptop yet I can still run it at 720p 60FPS.  I hope to upgrade soon to MAX it out (pun intended).  I like this game and I will give it a thumbs up, however it must be said that the actual mechanics of the game can get quite dull.  The story is interesting enough and keeps me playing, but the combat is REALLY monotonous.  There are no special moves you can pull and it is very simple.  This I believe can be overlooked however because vehicular combat is ENTHRALLING.  There are tons of upgrades you can get for your car cleverly named "Magnum Opus".  It isn't the greatest open world game ever, in fact it is very similar to alot of other 3rd person games.  Yet, even with these similarities there are enough unique details that distinguish it.  The atmosphere of the films is recreated PERFECTLY.  There are random dust storms that spring up and you have to take cover, one time a storm came up during a car chase and I was trying to see as dust swirled around my screen, it was a scene straight out of "Fury Road" in a good way.  Another cool detail scouting is scouting for missions.  You use binoculars which are strikingly similar to scenes in the original trilogy.  This is the best Mad Max game that I think ever could be.  I am honestly surprised that this game is as good as it is.  The "Mad Max" films have always been about simplicity in story by using visual storytelling instead of narrative.  Because of this, I myself would have a hard time making a true to the franchise video game.  Props to Avalanche for making it happen!
If you are a fan of the franchise and looking for some Australian insanity I suggest picking it up :)
EDIT:  This game is definitely growing on me.  As I stated before it is really repetitive.  Normally I would say that is a bad thing.  Contrary to what I said prior however there are a few moves Max can learn.  They are simple but believable as he is just a dude who is stuck in the apocalypse not a super hero.  When you unlock the "fury combo chain" your fists just crack skulls, and boy is it satisfying.  By FAR my favorite thing to do in this game combat wise is sprint at people time a heavy punch about a second before I make contact so that way my fist just SLAMS 'em right in the dome.  As I stated before, this IS the best Mad Max game that possibly could be, well the only thing they could have added was motorbikes.  Besides that this game is just a really "fun" time.  Some reviewers don't like to use that word.  But that is exactly what "Mad Max" is.

The Mad Max game is a sandbox driving and brawling game that authentically recreates the look and feel of the films. Max has lost his signature V8 Pursuit Special to thieving Warboys led by the unfortunately named Scabrous Scrotus, and teams up with a crippled but gifted mechanic named Chumbucket, who has a vision from on high to create the perfect car: the Magnum Opus. Journey with the pair across the dried shores of a forgotten land, doing a handful of story missions and a whole heaping load of optional content. The driving physics are excellent. Those complaining about stubborn handling don't realize that the cars in Mad Max handle like actual cars- they have weight, friction, impact. You can customize the Magnum Opus to your liking, unlocking new internals and offensive attachments as you gather scrap, the game's currency, and reduce the threat level of the Warboys in each of the four major regions by destroying convoys, scarecrow markers, sniper nests and war camps. Where the Opus doesn't fit, Max can lay into his enemies with brutal hand-to-hand maneuvers, in a system not unlike the Batman: Arkham games but far less in-depth. While simply mashing attack will get you through the early fights, good use of blocks, counters and dodges will be needed later. I found the game oddly similar to Star Trek Online in this regard: while you spend much more time driving, the on foot segments will quickly make you wish you were back in the Opus. On the road, your combat options are far more powerful, and diverse: in addition to ramming enemies, with the option of using boost to enhance damage, you have a side-slam move identical to that seen in Sleeping Dogs, though it is far less effective here when compared to your other options: side flamethrowers, a harpoon that can rip wheels off cars or drivers out of the cars completely, explosive-tipped harpoons that annihilate cars outright, and of course, Max's trusty shotgun- capable of blowing a wheel off a car just as easily as it will one-shot any normal enemy while on foot. The sound quality is incredible. The shotgun makes just about the loudest bang I've ever heard in a game and when you FINALLY get your hands on the coveted "Big Chief" V8 engine near the endgame, you will hear its sublime roar and feel blessed. Dotted throughout the game are callbacks to the films, including the much-beloved Thunderdome. I cruised around the wastes for hours, only wishing the game had some better music. Mad Max succeeds where it needed to the most: Putting you in the driver's seat of the most deadly, awe-inspiring metal machine left on earth. Where it falls short is in a similar area to other "open-world" games- It is, in fact, TOO big a game. I clocked in over 60 hours and, if i were to be generous, perhaps 5 hours of that are actual story missions. Most of the game, as with Avalanche's flagship series Just Cause, is made up of optional content and there are only so many types of these activities, though the Death Run race events stand out. I found myself tuning out during long stretches of collectible farming, eventually resorting to binge-watching tv shows on netflix with the game volume turned down while I knocked activity icons off my map one by one. However, whenever I got back in the Opus, heard that engine, hit the boost, watched that blinding blue flame issue from my chrome pipes and slammed right into some unsuspecting warboy's pathetic scrapheap of a car, I remembered what I was playing and why. Mad Max is not a boring game by any stretch of the imagination, but it's a loooong one, and it has some slow stretches. Regardless, I enjoyed the better part of it- and the better part of it made me feel like I was in a world gone Mad.

Undertale is a blatant EarthBound ripoff that is significantlu better than EarthBound. The gameplay is alright, the music is awesome, and the artwork is acceptable, although bad. Many aspects of the dialogue are taken *directly* from the Mother trilogy, even certain character's personalities. Considering this is a plot based game, I don't really find this excusable. Otherwise, characters are well designed and have depth. Humor is crappy- early on, the game did make me laugh... but it quickly turned away from character oriented humor, and throws loads of cameos and more random humor.
Gameplay is very good. Most of it revolves around combat, which, unlike the games it takes ""inspiration"" from, is very different, using a bullet hell system that makes it possible for enemies to miss. Due to this, players don't need to grind; and it allows them to play the game the way they want. There are several kinds of endings based on what characters you (don't) kill, but beyond the extremities of what you kill, and all other endings are meaningless. None of your interactions with characters doesn't influence the game at all.
The game is really hard to replay though. Only certain endings allow you to restart your save file, otherwise characters remember past interactions. It's a nice touch, but not being able to reset a save file is irritating- especially if you plan on showing the game to a friend.
Overall, the game is pretty good, and I would reccomend playing it. It has several flaws, but those are more than made up for.

Kinda like a Castlevania/Ghosts'n'Goblins game mixed with a roguelike and a unique system of traits/inheritance. Gain gold in castle, die, pass your winnings on to your progeny, select an heir to enter the castle, buy equipment/upgrades, then enter the castle again. Repeat. The castle adjusts its difficulty to your level, causing more difficult enemies and layouts to randomly appear as you buy better upgrades/equipment.
Overall, it's pretty great! Worth 15 bucks, I'd say, though I got away with paying 10 in a pre-order.

Rust is probably one of the best early access survival games out on the market. So much has changed since the release of this game but the majority of the change was good. So far the the devs have gone from blue print system for crafting items, to a XP system, to a component system, and now a mix between the component system and blueprints.
The blueprint system was ok but there was way too much rng involved. It required the finding of items and or their blueprints, or using some blueprint fragments for the chance of getting the recipe. You only needed to find the recipes for higher tier tools and weapons. After that you would have the recipe until the server wiped the recipes.
Then there was the XP system which had a rather messy start with people abusing bugs but it was later fixed up. The XP system wasn't terrible but it was way too grindy. With this you needed to unlock most items in the game starting out with practically nothing. You also had to farm a lot to level up and get XP points to unlock the items you want.
Afterwards came the component system which is a lot better than the XP system. Everything is craftable but you must find the components for it. Only the mid to high tier items require components. Guns need springs, pipes, etc. Higher tier clothing needs sewing kits. It bring back a use for the radtowns which were somewhat useless during the XP system. It also adds more possibility for trade compared to the XP and BP system because you couldn't trade XP and after you had all the recipes most people didn't try to get extra recipes because it was unneeded.
Now its a mix of blueprints and components. Thankfully it has improved on a lot of the bad parts from the BP system such as the RNG when researching items and lowering the amount of scrap needed to research the item. This system is still in the works and its better than the component system because there is actually some progression

First things first, I am a HUGE Mad Max fan.  I grew up watching the original films and the newest addition, "Mad Max: Fury Road" is modern masterpiece.  If you haven't watched it yet, DO IT.
Now, the game.  The port is fantastic.  I have a quite outdated gaming laptop yet I can still run it at 720p 60FPS.  I hope to upgrade soon to MAX it out (pun intended).  I like this game and I will give it a thumbs up, however it must be said that the actual mechanics of the game can get quite dull.  The story is interesting enough and keeps me playing, but the combat is REALLY monotonous.  There are no special moves you can pull and it is very simple.  This I believe can be overlooked however because vehicular combat is ENTHRALLING.  There are tons of upgrades you can get for your car cleverly named "Magnum Opus".  It isn't the greatest open world game ever, in fact it is very similar to alot of other 3rd person games.  Yet, even with these similarities there are enough unique details that distinguish it.  The atmosphere of the films is recreated PERFECTLY.  There are random dust storms that spring up and you have to take cover, one time a storm came up during a car chase and I was trying to see as dust swirled around my screen, it was a scene straight out of "Fury Road" in a good way.  Another cool detail scouting is scouting for missions.  You use binoculars which are strikingly similar to scenes in the original trilogy.  This is the best Mad Max game that I think ever could be.  I am honestly surprised that this game is as good as it is.  The "Mad Max" films have always been about simplicity in story by using visual storytelling instead of narrative.  Because of this, I myself would have a hard time making a true to the franchise video game.  Props to Avalanche for making it happen!
If you are a fan of the franchise and looking for some Australian insanity I suggest picking it up :)
EDIT:  This game is definitely growing on me.  As I stated before it is really repetitive.  Normally I would say that is a bad thing.  Contrary to what I said prior however there are a few moves Max can learn.  They are simple but believable as he is just a dude who is stuck in the apocalypse not a super hero.  When you unlock the "fury combo chain" your fists just crack skulls, and boy is it satisfying.  By FAR my favorite thing to do in this game combat wise is sprint at people time a heavy punch about a second before I make contact so that way my fist just SLAMS 'em right in the dome.  As I stated before, this IS the best Mad Max game that possibly could be, well the only thing they could have added was motorbikes.  Besides that this game is just a really "fun" time.  Some reviewers don't like to use that word.  But that is exactly what "Mad Max" is.

The Mad Max game is a sandbox driving and brawling game that authentically recreates the look and feel of the films. Max has lost his signature V8 Pursuit Special to thieving Warboys led by the unfortunately named Scabrous Scrotus, and teams up with a crippled but gifted mechanic named Chumbucket, who has a vision from on high to create the perfect car: the Magnum Opus. Journey with the pair across the dried shores of a forgotten land, doing a handful of story missions and a whole heaping load of optional content. The driving physics are excellent. Those complaining about stubborn handling don't realize that the cars in Mad Max handle like actual cars- they have weight, friction, impact. You can customize the Magnum Opus to your liking, unlocking new internals and offensive attachments as you gather scrap, the game's currency, and reduce the threat level of the Warboys in each of the four major regions by destroying convoys, scarecrow markers, sniper nests and war camps. Where the Opus doesn't fit, Max can lay into his enemies with brutal hand-to-hand maneuvers, in a system not unlike the Batman: Arkham games but far less in-depth. While simply mashing attack will get you through the early fights, good use of blocks, counters and dodges will be needed later. I found the game oddly similar to Star Trek Online in this regard: while you spend much more time driving, the on foot segments will quickly make you wish you were back in the Opus. On the road, your combat options are far more powerful, and diverse: in addition to ramming enemies, with the option of using boost to enhance damage, you have a side-slam move identical to that seen in Sleeping Dogs, though it is far less effective here when compared to your other options: side flamethrowers, a harpoon that can rip wheels off cars or drivers out of the cars completely, explosive-tipped harpoons that annihilate cars outright, and of course, Max's trusty shotgun- capable of blowing a wheel off a car just as easily as it will one-shot any normal enemy while on foot. The sound quality is incredible. The shotgun makes just about the loudest bang I've ever heard in a game and when you FINALLY get your hands on the coveted "Big Chief" V8 engine near the endgame, you will hear its sublime roar and feel blessed. Dotted throughout the game are callbacks to the films, including the much-beloved Thunderdome. I cruised around the wastes for hours, only wishing the game had some better music. Mad Max succeeds where it needed to the most: Putting you in the driver's seat of the most deadly, awe-inspiring metal machine left on earth. Where it falls short is in a similar area to other "open-world" games- It is, in fact, TOO big a game. I clocked in over 60 hours and, if i were to be generous, perhaps 5 hours of that are actual story missions. Most of the game, as with Avalanche's flagship series Just Cause, is made up of optional content and there are only so many types of these activities, though the Death Run race events stand out. I found myself tuning out during long stretches of collectible farming, eventually resorting to binge-watching tv shows on netflix with the game volume turned down while I knocked activity icons off my map one by one. However, whenever I got back in the Opus, heard that engine, hit the boost, watched that blinding blue flame issue from my chrome pipes and slammed right into some unsuspecting warboy's pathetic scrapheap of a car, I remembered what I was playing and why. Mad Max is not a boring game by any stretch of the imagination, but it's a loooong one, and it has some slow stretches. Regardless, I enjoyed the better part of it- and the better part of it made me feel like I was in a world gone Mad.

In all seriousness, this game is an excellent story-centric RPG. It does a lot to make the story, world and machanics weave together more than the average turn-based RPG. During your turn, you pick what you want to do, pretty standard. But during the opponent's turn, you'll be dropped into a bullet hell box where you must dodge incoming attacks to avoid taking damage. In addition to that, you get through the entire game by talking your way out of fights insetad of kiling them. In this world, I suppose the pen really is mightier than the sword. Sure, you do get EXP for killing monsters, but not killing anyone seems like the right thing to do. An organic moral choice that is truly yours to make - not something you see to much in games. The level of strategy is almost non-existed, with most battles being part puzzle (what do I say to get this monster not to attack me?) and part bullet hell. That being said, the battles get EXTREMELY hard towards the end. You've been warned.
Despite how interesting the battle machanics are and how challenging the fights are end-game, this game truly shines through in its story, world and characters. The writing is fantastic. The writing (which includes what characters say, what yu say to monsters in combat, and all the descriptions of items you inspect) is clever and funny, but the story gets intensly deep at point as well. This game was once something I could get behind. A good soundtrack though rather reminiscent of certain other RPG games, decent sprite work, and a story with moderate good flow and characters. But this game in my opinion does not really live up to the hype or deserve it overwhelming praise.
Let's look at all the pros of this game:
- good paced music
- good for at least 2 play throughs with genocide and pacifist
- characters though overpraised are still likeable
These points combined with the fact that Toby Fox is an indie developer is impressive.
But there is a problem, this game is hardly the concoction of one person's imagination. Between the many obvious inspirations drawn from other similar games Toby modded before, to soundtrack a little too similar to those of games over a decade old is uncanny. I am not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the developer get, game development is hard and cudos to Fox for making something this big.
But my biggest problem is at the core of the popularity of Undertale vs other indie games and the community itself. The fact that Toby was not a one man army is often ignored by people, a common excuse given by people blindly defending the game is that he worked alone.
Tony had help, from the actual user Temie (yes Temie is the title of a artist who helped Toby), as well as the plentiful people providing additional ideas and character concepts.
People ignore this fact and worship a false image of a one man game making machine, the sad part is projects better than this game has solo creators and received none of the attention.
If people would like to stick to RPG themed projects then one must turn no farther then Bethesda fans. The mods for another acclaimed RPG Skyrim give up years of their life to make brand new worlds, mods so massive and packed with delicious content that it would take 1000 Undertales to hold a candle to them. Falskar, Enderal, the forgotten city which has literally won a writing award. All these amazing projects and the authors never received a penny or wanted any. They create for the enjoyment of others even better...and yet we are swooning over ludicrous spaghetti memes?
This brings me to the main problem I have with this community is the cash in fandoms. Things like Undertale have so many Alternative universe's that are exactly the same it makes me ill. Most are pure cringe or pure drivel and keep people from actually enjoying the game normally.
I have gotten off track and shall end here, between overpraise and cringe community I am done with this game.

Tem/10 buy this game.
In all seriousness, this game is an excellent story-centric RPG. It does a lot to make the story, world and machanics weave together more than the average turn-based RPG. During your turn, you pick what you want to do, pretty standard. But during the opponent's turn, you'll be dropped into a bullet hell box where you must dodge incoming attacks to avoid taking damage. In addition to that, you get through the entire game by talking your way out of fights insetad of kiling them. In this world, I suppose the pen really is mightier than the sword. Sure, you do get EXP for killing monsters, but not killing anyone seems like the right thing to do. An organic moral choice that is truly yours to make - not something you see to much in games. The level of strategy is almost non-existed, with most battles being part puzzle (what do I say to get this monster not to attack me?) and part bullet hell. That being said, the battles get EXTREMELY hard towards the end. You've been warned.
Despite how interesting the battle machanics are and how challenging the fights are end-game, this game truly shines through in its story, world and characters. The writing is fantastic. The writing (which includes what characters say, what yu say to monsters in combat, and all the descriptions of items you inspect) is clever and funny, but the story gets intensly deep at point as well. Don't get fooled by the childishness of some of the characters and art - this game can get very emotional, and even pretty dark at times. It also gets kinda meta at parts, but I won't say anymore about that. In fact, the less you know about the story going in, the better.
I highly recomend this to anyone who wants to experience one of the best stories told through a game. Play this as blind as you can. The story is worth it.

For anyone who loves a huge open world to explore with lots of collectibles, this will either be your wet dream or your biggest nightmare. Right off the bat there is so much to do in the world that it can quickly become overwhelming.
The game has the well-worn Batman Arkham style combat, but sadly it's not as fluid as those games are. If you don't press the counter button at the precise right time, Max will take a hit and this can take some getting used to, especially when you're used to being Batman and blocking no matter where you are in your combat animation. Max also carries a sawed off shotgun as you would expect but ammo is scarce and you're going to be spending far more time in melee combat than shooting people.
The driving feels tight and responsive, plus there are literally dozens of upgrades/tweaks you can make to Max's Magnum Opus, right down to the body style at the beginning of the game. I found the car mechanics to be similar to id's RAGE, but on a much grander and frankly far more interesting scale.
If you like exploration and open world, this game is a must own.

Short Review: The game is a lot of fun, if you like sand box games, like Shadow of Mordor, Batman and Farcry, this game is for you. It copies all the good parts of those games and make them work within the Mad Max world.
Good: -Combat is nice and becomes increasily difficult, so you always have a challenge (although I only have 8 hours into the game).
- As in the Mad Max's lore, the main focus is in the vehicles, upgrading your car is your main focus, similar to Black Flag.
- The graphics are beautiful, very well optimized, and very few glitches.
- Video Settings are abundant, you want to play in 4k 60fps? done; you want 1440p and 144fps? done; you want 1080p and 60fps? done and be also prepared for solid fps.
- WAY WAY too many things to do, this is good if you look for a lenghty game, bad if you are a completionist.
- The map and the "dungeons" are very-well designed, you can feel the effort in the design and that almost everything was hand-picked to be there.
Bad: - The main story is there, but don't expect to be blown away, I'm hoping it will improve towars the end. To be fair, for me gameplay and graphics are more important than the story. Also the lore within the game is abundant.
- I was not impressed by the sound, after watching the movie I had high expectations, maybe that was my problem...
- You can easily see that after 50 hours of driving and looting settlements, it can become repetitive. But the same is also true for the Witcher, Skyrim or Fallout.
BUY THE GAME, IT'S WORTH IT, for me it's a must-have game for 2015.

So, I think I've put in enough time to say that this is a great game. It captures the Mad Max vibe beautifully. It looks great. Its fun.
In many ways, this is the game that I hoped Rage would be. I enjoyed Rage, but it was really just a cartoony looking shooter set in a post apocalypse world. It was altogether linear and lacked any RPG elements. Mad Max fixes all of this. Roam the wasteland doing whatever you like. Build your car anyway you like. Deck Max out any way you like. Fight the way you want. Loot. Scavenge. Explore.
The fighting has been mentioned many times. It is what it is, but honestly, I think its great fun. Its smooth, the moves are impressive. I like getting out of the Magnum Opus and just kicking peoples' a**es. The shotgun and sniper rifle are nice, but there is little ammo. The shivs are handy, and melee weapons are great. Honestly, fighting in this game is simple and fun, which is what I want.
The wasteland is impressive. The music is good but not overpowering. The voice acting is superb.
Maybe my only complaint at this point is that my computer is finally getting on in years and this game is taxing it a bit where games like Alien: Isolation and Skyrim played fine. Its playable, its just a bit slow and occasionally choppy. 12 hours in, I don't think it will be a problem though. Even the road battles have been fine.
So, yeah, I don't usually review games before I finish them, but I love Mad Max, and this game is great. Play it!

ยอมรับเลยว่าผมติดเกมนี้มาก พอหลังจากเล่นเป็นผมก็เล่นไม่หยุด เล่นตั้งแต่สี่โมงถึงตีห้า คือต้องบอกก่อนผมชอบเกม open world มากยิ่งเป็นพวกเกม openworld ที่มีอะไรให้เราทำเยอะๆยิ่งชอบ ตัวเกมผลิตโดยค่าย WB ก็แน่นอนว่าตัวเกมนี้มีโครงสร้างแบบเดียวกับเกม batman แต่สิ่งหนึ่งไม่เหมือนคือตัวเกมไม่ได้ติดอยู่ในกรอบของ batman แต่มันอยู่ในโลกของ madmax

1+ hours in and I can say the following based on progression through zone 1 - that's the disclaimer for peeps who want to know what $60 will buy at release.
*Watch the cinematics; they're decently rendered and entertaining, at least the first time through.  Unless you're a twitch-monkey who just wants targets, you also may be interested in the plotline, and (so far) explain the point of each phase of the missions you perform.
**The E key is your primary form of interaction; controls are not difficult, and can be remapped easily.
1.) Linear progression as opposed to open world/WoW, where you can literally go anywhere you want, if you can live/get there.  This is in regard to advancing the plot.
2.) You can explore the zone you're in to your heart's content, provided you have the fuel or want to run (and run and run...)
3.) Combat is formulaic, rather than spontaneous, and at early stages you get key-hints to tell you "block" or use other skills.  Blocking nub enemies is only practice; you can just beat the snot out of them without defending.
4.) Weapon use is not yet part of the game, despite possession of a shiv and a shotgun, except for shooting nub vehicles to 1-shot blow them up.  This is on the quest to get your new car.
I'm having fun so far, but tbh, not $60 worth of fun.  I considered refunding the game on the basis of cost alone, but after 4-5 hours of download time, and the realization that I will want to play the game more, I'm gonna stick it out.
At this very early view of the game, I give a 7/10 review, and expect that evaluation to go UP as I play more.  Review will be updated later on.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
21 hours in; I've owned this game for ~4 days.
Madness.  Great game so far.  So good, in fact, that I've temporarily abandoned the storyline because mugging convoys for scrap is more fun than driving past them (i.e., letting them get away).  There's so many locations in the world, they seem almost endless in this stage of the game, and all of them are either NPC strongholds, lootables, destroyables, or some combination of the three.
The game remains linear in terms of plotline, but in order to advance it (and enter new terrirtory) you'll want to have some side missions done/locations explored.  Scrap is how you buy up your gear, both personal and vehicular - thus, you need to loot, and kill stuff to loot.
This brings me to the single down point I find in the game so far, unless I'm just not yet to the point where it changes: you can collect cars you defeat (unless they are destroyed) and bring them back to a stronghold for later use... but if you want to salvage parts from them, you have to destroy them on the road.  Funny how a whole car isn't worth much but the collector value, and a destroyed car is worth ~1/10 (if that) of the value of buying an improvement to your own car.
The obvioius up side to this hitch is that you have ("GET") to destroy more stuff on the road.
One thing that stopped me up at first was the enemy insignia in the camps; you destroy the Scabrous Scrotus insignia at these locations to 100% clear them.  Some are hard to find, and of those, some are too high to reach.  Thus, you need a shotgun shell (rare items, at first) or some other tool to destroy them when they're out of reach.  Have a shell on-hand unless you want to come back, but always look for the alternative - a thrown gas can, or an exploding spear, conveniently placed at various places throughout the enemy camps.
Current evaluation of the game is now 8.5/10.  Good ambiance, great cutscenes (except the one for putting a gas can into your car... that one is getting annoying), good character actors and rederning, easy controls, well planned plot progression, and fun combat and adventuring, both on foot and in vehicle.

Performance:
Runs silky smooth at 60fps on an i2500k / nvidia 670 on the 'very high' preset.
If it's a PC port - I can't tell. PC support is great, a lot of graphics options, including being able to change audio output device ingame (from speaker to headphones, for example). Haven't seen that in a game in a long time.
Controls:
Seamless transition from controller to keyboard/mouse - if you want to use your 360 controller for driving and kb/m for shooting (of honestly, there is little of), you can.
Almost all combat is either car or melee arkham-style punchin'. The very few times where aim is required, there are 'quickshots' available, so playing this all on a controller is perfectly doable.
Keyboard/mouse controls work fine. They're not bad by default, they're all remappable, and the melee combat controls are almost all centered on LMB/RMB. Remapping basic functions to a thumb or extra mouse button works, and the ingame prompts updated as expected.
Game:
Atmosphere is very much in line with Mad Max and/or Fury Road, melee combat is similar to the Arkham games. Car combat is (so far) fairly simple, but really fun.
There are upgrades. A LOT of upgrades. There's over a dozen categories of car upgrades - each with varying levels, at least a dozen 'passive' upgrads (fuel use, water consumption, scrap collection, ....) and then a bunch more Max-only upgrades for melee combat or cosmetics.
It being an openworld game, there is going to be some busywork to unlock them - but so far it doesn't feel like it because most of the encounters will have scrap, water, or fuel as a bonus - all of which you need.
Closest comparison with regard to the openworld game? Just Cause 2 and Far Cry 4 - Open world with unlockables, upgrades based on exploration, and camps to be liberated.
If you like the Mad Max setting, or want an openworld game similar to the Arkham series while also driving a spiky, flamethrowing, harpoon-shooting car across the desert wasteland; this is for you.
Minor beef: Playing on an AZERTY board, the controls (ingame and when remapping) will say, for example, 'W' for forward as per qwerty, but when remapping it will show no change. However it functions fine on azerty. It just makes some of the tutorials/ingame tips weird when starting out if you play on azerty.
Everything considered, Mad Max is a blast to play, with huge explosions, brutal combat, and a massive open world to explore to your heart's content. You will love it. 10/10. <3

So far I am only about 10 hours into the game so I will update this as time goes on.
I must first say: This is NOT a console port! (the PC version was made in house by Avalanche alongside the other versions)... AND... This is NOT a movie game! The game was being made before Fury Road was even in pre-production some 4+ years ago, with rumors of it being made going as far back as 2008. This is a "Mad Max" game, meant to be its own thing in the "Mad Max" universe.
This is how you do new game I.P.
A mix of "Burnout" racing and "Twisted Metal" meets "Carmageddon", with "Batman Arkham" fighting, "Shadows of Mordor" multiple approaches, and "Just Cause" series open world fun, all in a post apocalyptic setting.
This is an ACTUAL open world game! Not like GTA V was where you had the "illusion" of an open world until you did a mission and they only allowed you to do a mission in a certain way and you would fail if you did it any other way than how it told you to. Nope, in this game you get an objective and can accomplish that objective in any way you want (within the limitations of the terrain of course). You want to sneak into an enemy camp the back way and take them off guard? Go ahead... You want to snipe the camp from a mile away? Go ahead... You want to crash your car through the front gate and blow up everything in sight? Go ahead.
Oh yeah, this is the first game in a long time that doesn't have "regenerating health" so you actually have to watch your health and start to worry when you have run out of ways to replenish it... Now it can be annoying at times, but it adds certain urgency to fights and exploration much like older games did back in the old "med kit" days, and it really fits with the Mad Max setting.
I love the upgrade and customization system. Pretty much everything can be upgraded or customized, character armor, character stats/perks, main car "Magnum Opus", weapons, and allied bases/forts.
I have to mention the car upgrades! I absolutely love the way Avalanche did this! Instead of just having incremental upgrades where the best car is always the end game fully upgraded car, all vehicle upgrades have benefits and drawbacks, so if you want a light and fast car you have to go with less armor, or if you want a tank of a car you will have a slower car. You can build the main car "Magnum Opus" any way you like to fit your play style.
You don't even have to be a fan of the Mad Max movies to get into this game since this is NOT actually a "Movie Game" but more a game somewhat based on a Movie franchise, considering this game was in devlopment long before "Fury Road" was made, and George Miller actually helped with the initial outline of the game.
And the writing is spot on! It actually creates characters I can care about, gives them their own personalities instead of the usual "un-interesting NPC #20". Lot of little bits and stories out in the wasteland to add a much needed depth to the game world, and I can't help feeling this is like a post apocalyptic "Red Dead Redemption" at times, and that is a good thing for me!.
Speaking of the game world... All I can really justify is "WOAH! Holy crap!" If you like exploring, or taking screen shots, or games that are so amazingly detailed that you actually stop to admire the scenery, then Avalanche studios has done it again! They even included a photo mode... My screenshot folder is quickly filling up.
I have been having so much fun just driving around and exploring that I have not used the fast travel feature at all.
As for technical issues... This is one of the most bug-free, completely optimized, good looking, smooth running, Max settings running above 60fps stable releases, I have seen for the PC in a LOOOOOONG time!
*****EDIT*****
FInally beat the main story and side quests at about 30 hours. (there is still tons to do and explore even after finishing the main and side stuff) I wish it was longer because, well, I was really into this game and didn't want it to end (seriously Avalance, give us more areas and cars and upgrades! Add the Citidel and Bulletfarm and Bartertown please!). I'm already going to do another playthrough.
And the ending!

This is a game that I've greatly enjoyed, but I'll say that it's a MAYBE recommendation. To understand how much I've enjoyed this game: I've bought it twice, once on Xbox and once on PC, and bought all the DLC (minus cosutumes).
So what's so great about this game? It's a well written story brought to life by amazing characters. It's animation style is uncommon in gaming (yes, cel shading has appeared in other games but it's not a fequent occurence). The gameplay is a mash up of First Person Shooter and Role Playing Game. And there is so much unique loot! So many guns with so many variables to disposed of your enemies in so many different ways! The number of playable characters and their diverse skills makes sure that you will find at least one character that fits your play style. And this ties in to some awesome multiplayer experiences.
Shoo-on for Game of the Year, right? Yeap.
But this is why it's a MAYBE recommendation: if you're not a fan of shooters in the least bit, the gunlust won't drive you. Even the RPG side of the game gets a little annoying, as I spent so much time in my inventory going, "Hmm... now which one..." And evey weapon I came across, the same thing happened. I'm not compelled to run to town every single time my pack is full and filtering inventory winds up breaks the atmosphere.
And I'll call out Gearbox on this; milking the DLC. At points I feel like I'm doing microtransactions for DLC. Things like Headhunter maps and skins and characters and level boosts. Did I buy them? Yeap, all but the skins. But it still feels like it's being milked.
Oh, and really, really try not to play this solo as much as possbile. Once you hear the story for the 10th time and none of your friends are making commentary along the way, it gets old really quick.

Rust is probably one of the best early access survival games out on the market. So much has changed since the release of this game but the majority of the change was good. So far the the devs have gone from blue print system for crafting items, to a XP system, to a component system, and now a mix between the component system and blueprints.
The blueprint system was ok but there was way too much rng involved. It required the finding of items and or their blueprints, or using some blueprint fragments for the chance of getting the recipe. You only needed to find the recipes for higher tier tools and weapons. After that you would have the recipe until the server wiped the recipes.
Then there was the XP system which had a rather messy start with people abusing bugs but it was later fixed up. The XP system wasn't terrible but it was way too grindy. With this you needed to unlock most items in the game starting out with practically nothing. You also had to farm a lot to level up and get XP points to unlock the items you want.
Afterwards came the component system which is a lot better than the XP system. Everything is craftable but you must find the components for it. Only the mid to high tier items require components. Guns need springs, pipes, etc. Higher tier clothing needs sewing kits. It bring back a use for the radtowns which were somewhat useless during the XP system. It also adds more possibility for trade compared to the XP and BP system because you couldn't trade XP and after you had all the recipes most people didn't try to get extra recipes because it was unneeded.
Now its a mix of blueprints and components. Thankfully it has improved on a lot of the bad parts from the BP system such as the RNG when researching items and lowering the amount of scrap needed to research the item. This system is still in the works and its better than the component system because there is actually some progression
Finally the pros and cons.
Pros:
Graphics
Gameplay
Regular updates
Down to earth devs
Gunplay
Cons:
Anticheat isn't great
Performance can be iffy for computers of all specs

Performance:
Runs silky smooth at 60fps on an i2500k / nvidia 670 on the 'very high' preset.
If it's a PC port - I can't tell. PC support is great, a lot of graphics options, including being able to change audio output device ingame (from speaker to headphones, for example). Haven't seen that in a game in a long time.
Controls:
Seamless transition from controller to keyboard/mouse - if you want to use your 360 controller for driving and kb/m for shooting (of honestly, there is little of), you can.
Almost all combat is either car or melee arkham-style punchin'. The very few times where aim is required, there are 'quickshots' available, so playing this all on a controller is perfectly doable.
Keyboard/mouse controls work fine. They're not bad by default, they're all remappable, and the melee combat controls are almost all centered on LMB/RMB. Remapping basic functions to a thumb or extra mouse button works, and the ingame prompts updated as expected.
Game:
Atmosphere is very much in line with Mad Max and/or Fury Road, melee combat is similar to the Arkham games. Car combat is (so far) fairly simple, but really fun.
There are upgrades. A LOT of upgrades. There's over a dozen categories of car upgrades - each with varying levels, at least a dozen 'passive' upgrads (fuel use, water consumption, scrap collection, ....) and then a bunch more Max-only upgrades for melee combat or cosmetics.
It being an openworld game, there is going to be some busywork to unlock them - but so far it doesn't feel like it because most of the encounters will have scrap, water, or fuel as a bonus - all of which you need.
Closest comparison with regard to the openworld game? Just Cause 2 and Far Cry 4 - Open world with unlockables, upgrades based on exploration, and camps to be liberated.
If you like the Mad Max setting, or want an openworld game similar to the Arkham series while also driving a spiky, flamethrowing, harpoon-shooting car across the desert wasteland; this is for you.
Minor beef: Playing on an AZERTY board, the controls (ingame and when remapping) will say, for example, 'W' for forward as per qwerty, but when remapping it will show no change. However it functions fine on azerty. It just makes some of the tutorials/ingame tips weird when starting out if you play on azerty.
Everything considered, Mad Max is a blast to play, with huge explosions, brutal combat, and a massive open world to explore to your heart's content. You will love it. 10/10. <3

So far I am only about 10 hours into the game so I will update this as time goes on.
I must first say: This is NOT a console port! (the PC version was made in house by Avalanche alongside the other versions)... AND... This is NOT a movie game! The game was being made before Fury Road was even in pre-production some 4+ years ago, with rumors of it being made going as far back as 2008. This is a "Mad Max" game, meant to be its own thing in the "Mad Max" universe.
This is how you do new game I.P.
A mix of "Burnout" racing and "Twisted Metal" meets "Carmageddon", with "Batman Arkham" fighting, "Shadows of Mordor" multiple approaches, and "Just Cause" series open world fun, all in a post apocalyptic setting.
This is an ACTUAL open world game! Not like GTA V was where you had the "illusion" of an open world until you did a mission and they only allowed you to do a mission in a certain way and you would fail if you did it any other way than how it told you to. Nope, in this game you get an objective and can accomplish that objective in any way you want (within the limitations of the terrain of course). You want to sneak into an enemy camp the back way and take them off guard? Go ahead... You want to snipe the camp from a mile away? Go ahead... You want to crash your car through the front gate and blow up everything in sight? Go ahead.
Oh yeah, this is the first game in a long time that doesn't have "regenerating health" so you actually have to watch your health and start to worry when you have run out of ways to replenish it... Now it can be annoying at times, but it adds certain urgency to fights and exploration much like older games did back in the old "med kit" days, and it really fits with the Mad Max setting.
I love the upgrade and customization system. Pretty much everything can be upgraded or customized, character armor, character stats/perks, main car "Magnum Opus", weapons, and allied bases/forts.
I have to mention the car upgrades! I absolutely love the way Avalanche did this! Instead of just having incremental upgrades where the best car is always the end game fully upgraded car, all vehicle upgrades have benefits and drawbacks, so if you want a light and fast car you have to go with less armor, or if you want a tank of a car you will have a slower car. You can build the main car "Magnum Opus" any way you like to fit your play style.
You don't even have to be a fan of the Mad Max movies to get into this game since this is NOT actually a "Movie Game" but more a game somewhat based on a Movie franchise, considering this game was in devlopment long before "Fury Road" was made, and George Miller actually helped with the initial outline of the game.
And the writing is spot on! It actually creates characters I can care about, gives them their own personalities instead of the usual "un-interesting NPC #20". Lot of little bits and stories out in the wasteland to add a much needed depth to the game world, and I can't help feeling this is like a post apocalyptic "Red Dead Redemption" at times, and that is a good thing for me!.
Speaking of the game world... All I can really justify is "WOAH! Holy crap!" If you like exploring, or taking screen shots, or games that are so amazingly detailed that you actually stop to admire the scenery, then Avalanche studios has done it again! They even included a photo mode... My screenshot folder is quickly filling up.
I have been having so much fun just driving around and exploring that I have not used the fast travel feature at all.
As for technical issues... This is one of the most bug-free, completely optimized, good looking, smooth running, Max settings running above 60fps stable releases, I have seen for the PC in a LOOOOOONG time!
*****EDIT*****
FInally beat the main story and side quests at about 30 hours. (there is still tons to do and explore even after finishing the main and side stuff) I wish it was longer because, well, I was really into this game and didn't want it to end (seriously Avalance, give us more areas and cars and upgrades! Add the Citidel and Bulletfarm and Bartertown please!). I'm already going to do another playthrough.
And the ending!

Euro Truck Simulator2 is good because what it does it does REALLY well!  it lets you drive a truck around Europe!  Its that simple.  But not just one truck A LOT of trucks all the major manufacturers are included,  some not by name but you can recognise them.  It lets you, if you so desire own your own trucking company.  You can own your own truck, but you don't have to.  you can just be a driver for hire, which is what you start out doing.  you can then "test drive" all the truck types and pick your favorite.  By that time you might be in place to purchase said dream truck and away you go.
The routes are all faithfully reproduced and thankfully the map is cleaverly reduced.   You visit all the major cities of most of the European countries.  driving and delivering goods making money exploring the sights and finding agencies to hire drivers and dealers to buy trucks if thats your fancy.
The gameplay is relaxing,  you drive.  and that is what makes it so good.  There is no fastest lap, not pole position, just drive from point A to point B trying not to have an accident (not as easy as it sounds) or get fines for light jumping or speeding.
But probabely the best aspect of this games is the community that produce free mods.  And the developers freely allow this.  there are maps, trucks, sounds modifiers, you can add buses and cars and its all FREE! and any developer made mods are really very resonabley priced, unlike some other simulator game. (I'm point at you Dovetail)
this game is really worth getting, even if you don't like it at first you will be playing it eventually and then you won't stop.
Fun to drive around Europe, if that is your ambition.

Tight Metroidvania platforming meets roguelike randomness and difficulty in a tasty mix. Give this one a shot if these genres are in your wheelhouse.
In true roguelike fashion, death is a learning experience.You will die many, many times, but on good runs where you manage to accumulate some cash, you can buy permanent upgrades and unlocks, which makes this a little different from your average roguelike which gives you a clean slate every time. The random trait system is interesting: some are universally good, some are universally bad, and some are situational. You'll get a feel pretty quickly for which of your three random character options for a given run is the best, and each of the classes plays a little differently due to their abilities.

Brutal Rogue-like with old-school action/platforming in randomly-generated dungeons. You WILL die within the first 30 seconds, but when you start over you can buy upgrades to stats and gear that help you do a little better each time, and eventually you will win (hopefully). It's awesome.

Great fun! Not quite what I wanted, but still a good game.
Edit: After playing for a while longer, I don't really have too many complaints about the game. Yes, the melee combat is a bit on the simple, button mashing side, but it works in this case. (At least for me) Some of the open world "missions" (scavenging, taking out camps, ect.) can seem like you're just doing thge same thing over and over, but no more than any other open world game. To me this feels like a great mix of elements from Just Cause 2, Rage, and Fallout. The complaints about it not truly being an open world game are coming from those people who never got out of the intro / tutorial area. Once you get through that you can see that the world opens up and you can pretty much do what you want. There are also complaints about the "weak" story, NEWS FLASH, Mad Max was never that strong of a story. Watch the movies and you'll see that for yourself. Yes, they are good movies, but the story is a typical action movie story. I personally think that the story suits the game just fine, I didn't want some grand, sweeping narrative about Max, I just wanted to get in his car and blow stuff up. Could this game have been better? Absolutely, there is always room for improvement, but it's still a fun game. I'd give it an 8.5/10
TL/DR - It's a good game that does have weak ponts, but most people will probably find it to be a good time. If you like the Just Cause series or similar games, (Red Faction: Guerilla, ect.), you will probably like it.

A roguelike "lite". You play as a hero with the task to rid a castle of its monstrous inhabitants. The castle is procedurally generated, meaning it is going to be different every time you enter it. During your trip you defeat monsters, earn gold and (if you are lucky) you find blueprints for new equipment, or runes to enhance your gear.
When the time for your inevitable death comes not all is lost, because your heir will take over. When your character dies you get to pick a new one (they all come with different, funny abilities). All the precious money your previous character looted gets transfered to their heir and you can use that money to upgrade your own little manor. You can buy new services (a blacksmith, for example) or use it to unlock new character types, or to increase various abilities and stats (there is a ton of stuff to upgrade!). So even if you die (and you will die A LOT) you still progress in the game. Rogue Legacy has about all you could want from a side-scrolling action game - boss fights, secret rooms, challenge rooms as well as New Game+. The game has full controller as well as "Big Picture" support.

Alright, DayZ.
Despite all the bugs and all the crashes, i still enjoy this game; Even though it might just be a deathmatch game and not a survival game I still have lots of fun interacting with the many types of players in it and even though most will just KoS(Kill-on-sight) you there are some people that are actually fun to play with. I don't know why i enjoy it, i just do. What you will read below is my guide for the people who haven't bought the game yet.
The zombies in this game are more of a nuisance then a threat, they are way too annoying. Players are the ones you need to be scared of.
There is a crafting system in this game which is useful if you haven't found any good equipment just yet; An improvised backpack would help you carry items, or a bow and arrow if you haven't found any weapons.
Now, on to the bugs.
-Falling down only a few meters will break your legs and ruin your gear in your pants.
-Items can sometimes disappear randomly, this is quite annoying if you are in the end-game stages.
-Game sometimes crashes, very annoying when in a gunfight.
-Zombies can frequently attack through the walls of a building
There are a ton of bugs so i'm obviously not going to list them all, if you want to see them all just google. But remember this if you decide to buy this game.
More cons.
The game performance has improved after the 0.60 patch, but still alot of work needs to be done to fully polish the game experience.
Like previously mentioned, alot of the bugs are very annoying to deal with and need to be fixed.
The community in this game can be very toxic at times, and i have experienced this. Unfortunately we have deal with it i guess.
You do run a lot, and i mean
; This is why many people get bored with this game, because of this reason. So expect to do that alot of the time and even though this isn't really a con for me it is for a lot of people. You can also get cars in this game.
Don't get attached to your gear, i have spent many hours on looting and then coming to a PvP area and dying instantly. This can get very frustrating and this also puts off alot of people.
This is a huge map, and the maximum player density is 60, which means that players can be
; I have sometimes ran for long periods of time just to see if i could find anyone but i couldn't. Another reason why people find this game boring.
And so on, and so on and so on.
Now time for my final verdict.
If you are looking for a proper survival game, please don't buy this; This will only just waste your money and you will be frustrated and regret your decision. And if you are looking for a deathmatchy style game where some survival aspects are needed, then go ahead. Try it.

A lot of people have been asking me how this game is, so I guess I'll write a review for it.
This game is extremely addicting.  I picked it up last night, and between yesterday and today, I've clocked in almost 10 hours of gameplay, and it's probably going to be more when I go back to playing it later tonight.
I am not good at action platformers like Castlevania or Metroid, so I die a lot in this game.  I'm sure if you're somewhat decent at platformers, you'll probably have beaten the game by now if you were in my place!  The game feels very long, but that's because it always feels like there's something new to explore.  The rooms aren't exactly randomly generated, as you'll eventually start to recognize certain rooms and their layouts, but all of the rooms get shuffled around, so the castle layout actually does get randomly generated each time you start a new character.
This game is described as being a 'rogue-lite' metroidvania game, which I think is a pretty accurate description.  The first several hours I was playing this game felt like I was straight-up grinding for upgrades, and I was, but it was still very enjoyable to play each run, so it didn't feel like a grind since I was platforming the entire time.  If you don't know what a rogue game is, it's usually a very difficult game, where the game hates you and wants you to die.  In addition to that, in most rogue-like games, it's generally permadeath, which is sort of what this game is, which is why it's considering itself as a 'rogue-lite' game.  Each time you die, you pass on your level, statistics, equipment, spells, and upgrades.  You have to give up all of your gold as soon as you re-enter the castle each time though (although upgrades can reduce this cost if you feel like it).  Every time you die, you're given a selection of 3 heirs to choose from, each with random traits and spells and classes (that you unlock through upgrading).  The traits can either make the game easier or a lot harder, but its all in good fun.
The game feels like a retro platformer, and it is very pleasing in gameplay.  I have some complaints in some random bugs I've encountered, but it's not enough to detract from how fun the game is.  An example of the bugs is I saw an enemy spawn ONCE inside of the ground or attacking a shielding enemy can make the jumping physics get a bit whacky.  A complaint I have about actually gameplay itself is that after you kill a boss, they seem to remain dead and as far as I can tell in my current progress, you can't ever go back to try to kill them again.  Maybe they'll reunlock once I finally beat the game, but I think it's pretty lame that you can't fight the bosses again, even if for reduced rewards or something.
In conclusion, I think this game is definitely worth $15 if you are into action platforming games like Castlevania or Metroid.  You will also probably like this game if you enjoy the Binding of Isaac, as the level generation is very similar to that, but in a 2D platformer frame.  Either way, I recommend everyone to at least try this at some point, whether they got it on sale or paid full price.  I'd also recommend a controller, although keyboard controls seem to work fine as well~

Rust is probably one of the best early access survival games out on the market. So much has changed since the release of this game but the majority of the change was good. So far the the devs have gone from blue print system for crafting items, to a XP system, to a component system, and now a mix between the component system and blueprints.
The blueprint system was ok but there was way too much rng involved. It required the finding of items and or their blueprints, or using some blueprint fragments for the chance of getting the recipe. You only needed to find the recipes for higher tier tools and weapons. After that you would have the recipe until the server wiped the recipes.
Then there was the XP system which had a rather messy start with people abusing bugs but it was later fixed up. The XP system wasn't terrible but it was way too grindy. With this you needed to unlock most items in the game starting out with practically nothing. You also had to farm a lot to level up and get XP points to unlock the items you want.
Afterwards came the component system which is a lot better than the XP system. Everything is craftable but you must find the components for it. Only the mid to high tier items require components. Guns need springs, pipes, etc. Higher tier clothing needs sewing kits. It bring back a use for the radtowns which were somewhat useless during the XP system. It also adds more possibility for trade compared to the XP and BP system because you couldn't trade XP and after you had all the recipes most people didn't try to get extra recipes because it was unneeded.
Now its a mix of blueprints and components. Thankfully it has improved on a lot of the bad parts from the BP system such as the RNG when researching items and lowering the amount of scrap needed to research the item. This system is still in the works and its better than the component system because there is actually some progression
Finally the pros and cons.

Graphics
Gameplay
Regular updates
Down to earth devs
Gunplay
Cons:
Anticheat isn't great
Performance can be iffy for computers of all specs

Borderlands 2 is a very entertaining open-world fps-rpg game capable of making people have many fun hours playing. Best part of the game is in my opinion is its DLCs. There are so many DLCs that it is nearly impossible to completely finish the game, just when you finish the game Gearbox releases a new DLC and boom. More work to do.
-Graphics and gameplay
Game's graphics are kind of cartoonish, but it doesn't really harm the ambient, even makes it stronger. Even if it has a cartoonish style of artwork, textures are still pretty realistic. If you don't like the game's "original" graphics, you can turn off the cartoon effect from settings.
Gameplay is even funnier than I expected. The game mostly has a sarcastic and humorous atmosphere, thus making the game even more enjoyable. There are thousands of guns in the game, and each gun has a speciality of its own. If we need to make a summary of the gameplay, it's about shooting people and gathering loot. Looks boring right? Don't worry, it will prove much more entertaining than you expect, which will make the game even more interesting.
-Ambience and Story
As I mentioned above, the ambient has an atmosphere of its own, which makes the game original and even more fun to play. The story isn't as deep as ordinary RPG games, but since you'll be looking for loot all the time, you'll even forget there was a story at all. Still, the story is sufficent, even too good for a game of its genre.
-Co-op mode
The game has a cooperative mode which lets you play with your friends or random people around the globe. The co-op mode supports 4 players maximum. For every player added, NPC quantity increases in a ratio. For example, if you're playing with a single friend, the NPC quantity doubles, if there are 3 of you, there are three times more NPCs etc.
-Overall
The game has replayability, also promises a lot of fun hours for the players. Especially if you're looking for a game to play with your friends, I suggest you to buy this game.

I also very much like how the "counter attack" has been replaced with a "parry". For example, in Arkham/SoM you hit "y" to counter and you parry and automatically attack after. In this, hitting "Y" just parries the attack, and you have to hit "X" to initiate the counter attack.
You can also unlock being able to disarm enemies after a counter by hitting a different button, and it rewards you for doing a "perfect parry", you can do bone breaking counters that stun enemies or disarm enemies with weapons (although late game you can upgrade the disarm ability to be done after any parry, not just a perfect one)
The story is cool and interesting, although a bit short. I've barely put 20 hours into this game and I'm already done with the main story, and I did a fair amount of side missions as well. The different cheifs/warlords you can help (or ignore) are all unique with their own backstory/reason to lead.
Overall it's a cool game, even if you've never seen any of the Mad Max movies (i haven't). If you like the Mad Max movies I would imagine you will love this game.

Despite all the bugs and all the crashes, i still enjoy this game; Even though it might just be a deathmatch game and not a survival game I still have lots of fun interacting with the many types of players in it and even though most will just KoS(Kill-on-sight) you there are some people that are actually fun to play with. The zombies in this game are more of a nuisance then a threat, they are way too annoying. Players are the ones you need to be scared of.
There is a crafting system in this game which is useful if you haven't found any good equipment just yet; An improvised backpack would help you carry items, or a bow and arrow if you haven't found any weapons.
Now, on to the bugs.
-Falling down only a few meters will break your legs and ruin your gear in your pants.
-Items can sometimes disappear randomly, this is quite annoying if you are in the end-game stages.
-Game sometimes crashes, very annoying when in a gunfight.

There are a ton of bugs so i'm obviously not going to list them all, if you want to see them all just google. But remember this if you decide to buy this game.
More cons.
The game performance has improved after the 0.60 patch, but still alot of work needs to be done to fully polish the game experience.
Like previously mentioned, alot of the bugs are very annoying to deal with and need to be fixed.
The community in this game can be very toxic at times, and i have experienced this. Unfortunately we have deal with it i guess.
You do run a lot, and i mean
; This is why many people get bored with this game, because of this reason. So expect to do that alot of the time and even though this isn't really a con for me it is for a lot of people. You can also get cars in this game.
Don't get attached to your gear, i have spent many hours on looting and then coming to a PvP area and dying instantly. This can get very frustrating and this also puts off alot of people.
This is a huge map, and the maximum player density is 60, which means that players can be
; I have sometimes ran for long periods of time just to see if i could find anyone but i couldn't. Another reason why people find this game boring.
And so on, and so on and so on.
Now time for my final verdict.
If you are looking for a proper survival game, please don't buy this; This will only just waste your money and you will be frustrated and regret your decision. And if you are looking for a deathmatchy style game where some survival aspects are needed, then go ahead. Try it.

(As of writing this review, I have completed the neutral and true pacifist routes for Undertale).
In short, I do recommend this game, but this won't be as glowing a recommendation as most other user reviews on steam. Toby Fox himself said "It’s about an 8/10, niche RPG game." when reflecting on Undertale and its popularity and I would be inclined to agree. Undertale is a unique experience that carries a sense of style that many indie games try to capture, but few actually achieve, however the experience is diminished somewhat by a bland early-game, easy/patronising game design and a lack of cohesion at certain points.
The game starts off fairly slow, introducing you to a world where humans have banished a separate race of (not-at-all-monstrous) monsters underground, and the circumstances of the player character, who is a human that has been cast underground. This is known as the "ruins" section of the game and it is the portion of the game that is playable in the free demo. In all honesty this section is by far the weakest in the game, since your time in the ruins is mostly spent walking down repetitive purple corridors, being literally handholded through extremely basic puzzles and fighting (or sparing) weak, generic fantasy creatures. Apart from a few humourous moments and the climax of this segment, the ruins do not give a good first impression to the game. The design overall feels amateurish, and only serves to introduce the player to the core game loop.
Fortunately when the player has settled into the game and made some decent progress, Undertale starts to show its strengths and a lot of actual fun can be had. Being a game that is heavily inspired by Nintendo's Earthbound, Undertale is a top-down role playing game that focuses more on bizarre and creative smaller scenarios as opposed to a large narrative of epic proportions. This is even reflected in the combat, where sparing enemies is not just done by mashing a single option most of the time, but by interacting with them in different ways, which brings a basic but intuitive puzzle element to the combat. For example, there is a deer enemy in a early section of the game that you can either fight to the death, or take off all of the items attached to its head, making it want to stop fighting. These interactions later culminate into entire mini character arcs taking place in combat should you not kill the enemy. This sort of pacifist playstyle is a good way at encouraging players to take a risk and forego level ups to see interesting side content that they would not be able to see otherwise. It also creates an interesting dynamic where the player has to fight most of the major characters in the game at some point, which makes the characters feel more fleshed out in their own way.
Another key aspect that is influenced heavily by Earthbound is the focus on quirky humour. All of the characters in the game have pretty exaggerated personalities, such as Papyrus being a dumb goof and Undyne finding passion in just about everything. As you could imagine there are plenty of puns and jokes abound. In my opinion there are only around 3 parts in the whole game that are laugh-out-loud funny but the constant humour does give Undertale a sense of charm, which helps distract the player away from the otherwise bland environments. This focus on humour has resulted in an aspect of the fanbase which focuses entirely on the hit-and-miss humour, which has led to some annoying memes and such being associated with the game. Although this is obnoxious it is understandable to a degree and can be ignored when playing through the game. The humour is strong throughout, but it is sometimes used as a design crutch, such as the intentionally simplistic and bad puzzles in the snowy area, that can be a chore to do in repeat playthroughs since they are the same every time.
Undertale is quite a short game, and quite a small one too. There are only 4 major locations and 7 major characters, but the game makes good use out of this limited amount of content. There are multiple encounters with each of the characters, some of them being quite detailed, adding new rooms and songs that you won't have experienced before, and there are lots of other small details that you likely won't notice on your first playthrough, such as the solution to the waterfall's piano puzzle, dialogue that changes over time in locales such as Grillby's bar in the early-game, and phone calls that vary based on where you call the character.
What I also like about Undertale is the way in which the different playthroughs flow well together into a single narrative. In particular, being as vague as possible, the pacifist run does a good job at building-up narrative elements foreshadowed in the first playthrough into a feel-good hypetrain, which will make you glad that you played through the game again. The game entertains the idea that the characters in the game are real people that you, the player have control over, and despite the fact that of course these characters are just coloured pixels and lines of code, the game entertains this idea well enough to deliever a message that you can appreciate games without having to subject yourself to literally everything those games have to offer, which is quite commendable considering this game's narrative was written by a single guy.
Finally, the soundtrack for this game is pretty rad. I liked the Undertale OST even back when I was completely averse to the idea of trying this game out, and for good reason. Toby Fox really outdid himself when composing the soundtrack for this game, and it's a fairly sizeable soundtrack too considering the game is pretty short. The songs take inspiration from other soundtracks across the whole spectrum of videogames, from 8/16-bit platformers, role-playing games and even obscure doujin shoot em ups like the Touhou series. Each track also compliments the tone of the surrounding area or sequence of events very well, with a mix of vibrant upbeat songs, intense battle themes, and slower more emotional pieces.Needless to say I still consider the soundtrack to be the best aspect of Undertale, and for some people the game may be worth buying for the soundtrack alone.
While experiencing these fun and unique aspects of the game you may notice various flaws too. For me, the main aspect that limited the amount of fun I had with the game was the general lack of difficulty. The game hands out healing items like candy, none of the puzzles will be liable to hold you back for longer than 3 minutes on your first playthrough, and the combat mostly consists of avoiding simplistic shoot em up patterns. Most of these patterns should only be a challenge if you have literally never played a shoot em up before in your life. Although many people refer to Undertale as a "bullet hell" game, it is nothing of the sort. The only unique aspect to the shoot em up-style enemy attacks are the coloured projectiles - standing still will allow you to phase through blue projectiles, and moving through orange projectiles will allow you to phase through them. The problem with this is that the game rarely even utilises this mechanic save for a few scripted sequences towards the end of the game.
This lack of difficulty feels patronising at times, because characters constantly offer to help you even if that goes against their interests at the time, and the overly forgiving nature conflicts with the fact that this is supposed to be a world that is hostile to humans. It undermines the game's theme of "determination". It is hard to have determination when there isn't much to be determined about.
I hope that this review has cast light on some of the good and bad aspects of this game without spoiling major plot points, as I feel as though most fans are too vague when describing Undertale to newcomers, which can lead to hype-induced aversion.

Me, being skeptical over an 8-bit game thought to myself, "Why the heck is everyone so hyped about this?". Finally, at the end of 2016; I decided one day that to end off the year of fabulous games I had discovered, I would try this game and paid for it when it was on sale.
After I first incountered a character by the name of Flowey the Flower, I knew this was going to be a great game. Meeting all of these characters made me grow to love them instantly. The story was amazing and the gameplay was so different, but in a good way. I loved how meta the game was also.
Long story short, when I got to the end of the game, I was so moved and even shed a tear or two. I now understand why the hype was so huge for this game. There are 3 endings. I just completed the pacifist run. I hope to do the other endings some day. But for now, I will appreciate the hard work I put into it and move on to other games.
In my opinion, I feel that any gamer of any kind of level or dedication, should play this game. Like I said, one of the greatest games I have ever played.

Many big budget games nowadays focus on impressive and flashy graphics, which (more often than not) sacrifices excellent storytelling and touching a player's emotions. Undertale does the opposite; it provides some of the best story-telling and heartstring tugs with SNES-like graphics which, to be fair, do add charm to the overall expereince. You''ll laugh, cry, and smile the entire time you play this fantastic game, and the emotions will be enhanced by Toby Fox's incredible music throughout it. This game is highly praised by its countless fans, and rightfully so. I was both entertained and surprised by it the entire time, and its no wonder that others felt the same way.
This also one of the games that (SPOILER!) I will NEVER go through the evil route for. This is because I enjoyed the charaters and setting a bit too much; they felt real to me, and the thought of turning them to ashes was cruel by even my standards. Keep in mind that I'm usually the guy that usually goes full-blown evil in Fable, KOTOR, Mass Effect, and even BioShock. Undertale, however, will never receive a Potayto Apocalypse because I prefer MERCY over Genocide.
Oh, and get the Soundtrack Bundle if you plan on getting the game; it's one of the best game soundtracks I've heard in years.
