Rogue Legacy is very effective at blending a platformer with roguelike elements.
The lineage system and procedurally generated levels keep each playthrough fresh, and the upgrade system compels one to play "just one more game".
The difficulty curve of the original release had some troublespots if you upgraded certain things and ignored others, but that has been rebalanced somewhat in a recent patch. The addition of multiple save slots also makes it easier to show the game to friends who haven't played it yet.
One frustration is that there are certain achievement-granting special rooms that show up very, very infrequently. Some with challenges that you only get one shot at.
I've gotten an incredible amount of playtime out of this game and still haven't quite upgraded everything yet. If there's ever DLC for a second castle of levels released, I'll buy it in a heartbeat.

After I played this game for good amount of time, It’s time to write a review! I am going to write mostly pros and cons. Let’s begin! Under the pros and cons I’ll write my opinion and what’s game about.
pros:
- Really fun
- Rewarding
- Building system is awesome
- Graphics are stunning
- Crafting system is logical
- Updates every week
- One of the best developers
- Has plenty of weapons and items
- There are different building materials
- There is farming in the game, you can farm metal ore, high quality metal (you get really small amount in metal ore), stone that’s used for upgrading your base and sulfur ore that you can melt down using furnace ( same as HQM and Metal Ore ) to get sulfur.
- Has huge list of servers, some are hosted by facepunch, other are hosted by people
- It’s easy to host a server
- Shooting with weapons is pretty fun
- Weapons have logical recoil
- Weapons are easy to craft
- You can raid someone’s base using explosives (C4 or Satchel Charge) all tho they are hard to craft.
I’ll say that’s pretty much it for pros, there is a little bit more but I think this is enough haha! Now cons!
cons:
- The game is not great optimized for low end pc’s (It improves over the time)
- It’s hard to get started on official servers
- Some modded servers are laggy
- The community in game is 50-50, meaning half of players are not friendly and will kill you, half are friendly and will help you or just be nice in general
- It takes a good amount of time to get a base since there are a lot of players that will kill you ( although it depends on server itself, if there are more then 125+ active players It’s pretty hard to get a base )
- On most servers if you play solo you either gonna get killed by a clan or by a duo or trio
- Building mechanics are changing a lot which pisses off a lot of players
- You always have a risk of being raided by a clan and losing all the loot
That’s it for cons now let’s start write a little bit about the game itself!
Rust is survival, open world, fps and crafting game. You spawn on an island having just a rock and torch. Your goal is to start hitting a tree with a rock and stone too! You always carry risk of being killed by players with guns so keep that in mind! There are a lot of dangerous animals, but I recommend that you try to kill at least an pig. There are a lot of places where there is radiation so if you have no clothes do not go there! Your main goal is to get a base by farming tree and stone, of course you need at least a bow to defend yourself from animals and other players. After you farmed and killed couple of animals use your map by holding G to find a place to build a base somewhere! Do not trust anyone in this game, JUST DON’T! After you built your first base go to like gas station or supermarket to get some components since you need them for crafting stuff! Rust will give you different and fun experience from other games, you either gonna end up raided by a clan or raid with a clan O.o ! As they say raid or be raided, haha 😂! Thanks for reading this review guys I wrote about the most important aspect of the game and some tips haha 😂! Leave a like and GOOD LUCK IN THE RUST WOLRD!
Final rating; 9/10

DayZ...DayZ... well what can I say. Its been in early access for about 2.. wait no 3 years now. Progress in this game is very very slow, but it is there. The game is much more enjoyable than it was when I started playing it. Persitance and camp building is finally at a point where you can use it without worrying about the server wiping everything. This game was one factor which I have yet to see replicated in any other game, which is the adrenaline rush you get when you see another player. Almost 200 hours in this game and my hear still pumps when I see another player. I am hoping that the progress of the game is starting to speed up, but we will see. At least the weekly dev updates make it seem like it is.  One of the things I love about this game is the fact that zombies are not what this game is centered around. Think of it more like an apocalyptic survival game with zombies in it. Yes you do have to watch out for zombies, as well as other people, wolves (which rome and hunt in packs), bears, disease, and did I say other people? Overall if you enjoy an more realistic shooter like Arma (which is what this game is based from) with open world concept, then you'll enjoy this game. If you want a polished zombie game there are others out there that you'll enjoy. This game is not your traditional zombie game.

Rust is a multiplayer sandbox survival game with endless possibilities. On your first day of joining a new world you have a rock and a torch, with this rock you can now start collecting resources and build a base. Once you have your little one by one with a key lock and wooden door, you now must go hunting with the spear you have crafted with rusts crafting system. After you find an animal and you have at least 2 spears, you can now throw one at the deer,horse, or boar that you have found. After the animal you have found starts running, chase it until it runs into a rock or runs out of breath. If the animal you have found runs into a rock dont bother finding it, it most likely is far gone by now. Now that you have killed your first animal you now must craft some lowgrade so you can make a furnace. Once you have a small 1x2 with a furnace and some small boxes, you now have to find some metal to turn your vulnerable wooden doors to less vulnerable metal doors. On your way to get a node you encounter a player, no two players. You now have to choose, make friends, run, or kill. If you decide to kill, then you will most likely get rekt by the geared players on the hill behind you. If you decide to talk then the two players are most likely going to pull out their fully loaded P2s and murder you in the face. But if you run you have a 75/25% chance or getting killed by either players you run into, the players your running from, or some geared player hiding in the bush beside you. If you do get back to your base then you most likely got killed as you opened the door because some naked with a pipe shotgun is camping your front door. Now you have let the geared player which has killed the pipe shotgun holding naked and the 2 p2 holding players that you were running from, now you must spawn in the bed you placed. Your now stuck with a geared player on the other side of your wooden door. You try to wait him out. After about 5 minutes you start to hear millions of foot prints and voices outside your house yelling, "Burn it down","FLAME THAT NEWB", and "RIP your base". Second later you hear and see flames turning your door into char coals as you sit traped in the one by one you started with. After the door brakes you and the geared players look into eachothers eyes, and the geared player you let in your airlock says in a werid voice,"Say hello to my little friend"....PEW PEW PEW, now your dead and the geared players name is shown on your screen, "Killed by NOOBKILLER24". Now you respawn, join a clan, get guns, you get armor, and most importantly you get REVENGE. After getting ready you and the clan you joined look for a base to raid. You find a base surounded in high external stone walls all around with many many layers. You say to yourself, This is the one. *Queue Intence Music* Your clan pulls out their Rocket Launchers and 50 rockets each and blow through the first layer of walls in seconds then the second and third and forth. Now your at their front door, them trying their hardest to hit at least one shot, they fail you get to their loot room and destroy most of their base. You and your clan start looting the dead bodys scattered along the floor then you find him...a dead body with the name tag...,"NOOBKILLER24". You got your revenge and you go home. And thats rust a game with many many possibilities and endless hours of fun.

Are you put off by the graphics? Skeptical when people tell you its about the characters or that the story and characters make up for it etc etc? I was too. So much so that it took me months to buy it and try it out. Maaaan was I wrong to judge it by the graphics alone. Everyone was right! This is an amazing old-style RPG with a great story, lovable characters, unique fight system, interesting concepts, and NO grinding. You don't even have to kill. ACT your way through situations. Learn about the characters, even the minor ones, and take actions to avoid fighting (reassure them, tell a joke, flex, laugh, or even do a sexy jiggle!) while you dodge their attacks. Or, hunt down and kill every monster alive. Your choice. Yes, it's YOUR choice. If you choose to kill, you become the villian of the story. If you choose to spare, you are the hero.
It's short for an RPG, but multiple ways to play leading to different endings, tons of easter eggs, choices that change situations and/or conversations, hidden secrets, and other things make this game one that can be played happily and excitedly over and over again. No side quests, no grinding to level up, and best of all it is hilarious! Buy it. You won't be disappointed.

This is clearly the Shadows of Mordor of this year. Nestled in amongst big ticket releases and published by Warner Bros again infact comes an open world sand box game where the story is really just the threads tying together a well conceived world full of things to kill in delightful fashion.
Mad Max is set in the classic post-apocalyptic world and instantly feels very unforgiving. The resources we are told we need to survive seem very scarce out the box and any real weaponry or ammo also feels somewhat treasured when you find it. The hand to hand combat while not quite as fluid as Shadow of Mordor is still of the standard "press Y to counter" variety, but where it lacks finesse it makes up for with visceral, heavy hits. There is indeed weight behind your attacks and the variety out the box is compelling enough that fighting is pleasing enough. As you pick up melee weapons you have bloody finishing attacks to pepper your standard arsenal of punches and kicks.
But obviously where this game stands out a little is in the car combat. Gaining the grappling hook early on really opens this up being able to pluck foes from cars or towers, the ramming feels very classic to other car combat and actually requires a little bit of technique at times. The other cars especially start out effective enough against you that you do actually need to pay attention somewhat.
I'm only a couple of hours in at this point and there's what seems to be alot of customisation for the car to unlock as the game progresses as well as for Max himself who has ability and stat based boosts you can gain.
In a post-apocalyptic car game, forget perfect handling and blissful power slides and instead expect a rather rough around the edges and unwieldly driving experience. Some would suggest this is insufficient in this day and age for a game about cars, but these are the clunky broken down remnants of cars strung together rather than a brand new Ferrari so it actually works in terms of world building that the cars handle poorly at times. By no means however is it a frustration in my eyes, it's just hard to be as precise as you'd like at times.
The map has a Witcher 3 feel of far too much to do and too little time, with strongholds and other features littering the map. Mad Max also borrows in the watchtower type functionality from Assassin's Creed and similar games, but instead of just adding the markers you can can look out with your binoculars and spot out each land mark. It is unbelievable infact how good the view distance is in this game and how well it performs on my gaming laptop which is far from top of the range.
There's going to be alot of people who will not be happy with a threadbare story of "go here, do this for reasons..." but the game that is here is essentially a very fun sandbox experience that does what it does very well. Releasing on the same day as Metal Gear Solid V was always going to be a very tough sell for many gamers, so this is likely to be a game that people pick up during a lull on sale and for that purpose it is certainly the perfect filler between the massive titles releasing later this year.
With such stiff competition this year, Mad Max will likely be forgotten, but it is a great example that pc versions can release just fine and that movie franchises (just like with Shadows of Mordor) are not the mark of a poor game. I'm enjoying this alot and having picked it up at 50% off initially I feel like even if it lasts only 10 hours before it grows dull I'll have got my monies worth.

Don't be fooled into taking a quick glance at this game and thinking it's a boring half-broken trucking simulator that you'll never play again after 10 minutes.  This game is the complete opposite of those things.

Even with this game being out for over year and a half, the developers continue to provide new updates and DLC that continue to provide new and exciting things to try. In short, you won't be disappointed in this game if you enjoy casual trucking simulators.

This game is a very good truck driving simulator. You can drive many different trucks around the whole Europe, driving logs to London and such. It's very relaxing.
Yes, relaxing.
Just you, the logs, the truck, and the road. All so relaxing.
There's nice scenery outside - there's beautiful sunflowers, windmills, and little huts, all making you feel relax!
And then there are the other commuters on the road. All trying to get somewhere. Because if you're not trying to get somewhere, you're a nobody. You're aimless. Without drive. We all strive for things that are out of our reach, but we forget to stop and think - where are we now? It's the here and now that counts - not where we will be, not where we were, but the now! Does London really need more logs?
No. Probably not. They're bound to have plenty. It's just the everturning cycle of consumerism, telling people that they need more logs. Advertising telling people - younger and younger people - telling them that to have a happy life you have to have logs! And that's why you're delivering the logs.
But happiness isn't in logs, is it? No! That's not where happiness is, in the logs! Happiness is inside yourself! London, you don't need the logs! You don't need trucks! Nobody needs trucks!
Except if you want to relax. Then you absolutely need the trucks of Euro Truck Simulator 2. They're surprisingly relaxing.

I love this first borderlands, i love this game just as much. In borderlands one you played as the prevoius cast , Roland Brick Mordecai and Lilith. Borderlands 2 pretty much follows the same rules as the first game as the story is a dierect sqeual. Borderlands 2 introduces one of the most dickest but the most hilliarous villian every giving even marvel's The Joker a run for his money. Handsome Jack is the primary villan in this game as you'll find out in the first scene of the game. in borderlands 2 you get to see some more personallity from the prevoius cast as the story now revoles around them dealing with the events of opening the vault in the first game. the game spans about....12 hours long give or take wieher you do the side missions or not. and each of the DLCs story missions are about 6 hours each. unlike the first game the number of gun varisations including models have been increased, the new cast are 4 new vault hunters plus 2 DLC hunters. i'll give a review for each character as iv also played them on xbox 360.
Maya as the siren: shes ok being the siren, sadly she only shines as a medic as she lacks all the smg perks and class mods lilth had, her abillity PhaseLock levitates a single mob and puts them in a statis bubble for a few secs. this abillity is good as when its active maya gets a few execllent abillities while its active.  you can play her as a non-medic but you wont acomplish much. 3/10 disapointment
Zero as a number: Zero is a good character having the abillity to Cloack. while cloaked he gains a damage bonus based on how close his cloak is to deactivating. He is also the Sniper and Ninja class of the game gaining a full tree set of skills for both roads. The Sniper tree offers more critical hit damage and an abillity that allows Zero to see enemy weak points while his Decption is active(Cloak) while the Ninja Tree called Bloodshed, allows him to dash when meleeing as well as when he kills an enemy while dectiption is active with a melee attack it allows him to recloak and repeat. 7/10
Salvador as the gunzerker: long story short: a really high Dps and a beef cake, Sally's gunzerker abillity lets him wield 2 guns while its active exchanging ADS and accuracy for the extra power, this abillity doesnt nerf the gun's power either. salvador doesnt get much in terms of elemental bonuses or using a piticualar weapon type. theres alot you can do with him making a versital choice 7/10
Krieg the Psycho: if you thought brick was crazy in borderlands 1 you havnt met Krieg yet. Krieg as his name suggests allows him to become a psycho, using his buzzsaw axe slicing though mobs, Krieg doesnt get much from using accual weapons doing meleeing with him is really the only way to go, 2 of his trees are devoted to melee and the other is for fire, his fire tree allows him to set enemies on fire as well as himself. when Krieg is on fire he gains a varity of damage bonuses and reductions. 6/10
Axton as the Commando: Sadly this isnt roland...so if you planned on using a roland build you're sadly mistakened. Axton lacks both the Medic and Ammo tree roland has but retanded all the damage abillities of the turrent. Axton is mostly about summoning his turrent and letting it do the work for you. the turrent can be equiped with sight lazers rocket pods, a longbow teleporter compent etc, theres alot you can do with it. sadly axton doesnt get much outside of gernades and his turrent with only a select few abillites aiding his gunplay. Lacking the ammo and medic trees axton doesnt have much to offer in the end game. 5/10
Gagie the mechromaner: Gagie...being my favarite character i'll try to be as unbias as possible. Gagie has 3 highly specialized trees. First is aidding death trap, middle is a tree entirely devoted to elemental weapons speficly shock and the last is the anarcy tree which trades weapon accuarcy for weapon damage. When i say highly specialized i seroirsly mean it. most of gagies abillites are good however most of her abillities past the half way point in all her trees are very poor or just not usefull enough. her primary abillity allows her to summon a robot named Deathtrap. Deathrap fights independitly of Gagie using all of his abillites without user input. Deathtrap is very bulk..like..salvador bulky. Gagie gets many abillities that upgrade deathtrap, any deathtrap exclusive upgrade will change his visual appearance such as flurry in the anarcy tree giving him an extra set of claws. sadly Gagie falls short in each tree, Iv had to use abillties in every tree to make her viable. most of Gagies bottom half tree skills are too weak or just outright useless. in my personal unbias as possible review I have to give her a 5/10 due to her skills tree and theyre heavy specialization

This is the first review I'll have written for a game I've purchased on Steam, and most likely the only review I'll ever write for a game I've purchased from Steam. Before purchasing Rust, I thought that due to my age (yes, I'm aware of my Steam username and my profile picture!), I had outgrown video games. Then came Rust; a game that, although in its "alpha stage" of development, is very playable, enjoyable and addictive.
Starting Rust, you're spawned into the world with nothing but two rudimentary tools: a rock and a torch. With the rock you're provided, you can farm stone, wood and other resources, which you can then use to construct buildings and other objects that will aid you in protecting yourself (from the elements, and from other players) and/or raiding enemies' bases. That is the basis of Rust: farming resources to survive the environment (three biomes -- forest, desert and tundra -- each with their negatives and positives), as well as for attacking/raiding other players and their bases.
Although the emphasis is on resource collection and combat, the game is much more nuanced than that -- especially if you're playing cooperatively/role-playing with other players. For example, in the first neighborhood I lived in, comprised of friendly and cooperative players, we moved in next to a player who was antisocial and aggressive. Every time we'd be in the vicinity of his base, which was only several yards from our base, he would "KOS" (Kill On Sight) us. Upon confronting him about his aggressiveness, he countered with: "Rust is not a cooperative/role-playing game. It's kill or be killed." And you know what? He was right. Everyone plays Rust differently. There's no right or wrong way to play Rust. You'll have fun however you play. Which brings me to only complaint about this game: the hackers.
Hacking isn't commonplace in Rust (I could be wrong, as I only play on official servers), in the sense that the majority of players you encounter will be hacking, but given the sheer amount of time you will spend collecting resources, building bases and everything else, encountering a hacker and losing your prized firearm(s), resource(s), etc. -- it can be VERY FRUSTRATING dying to them. It's frustrating dying in a fair fight, from which I've died MANY TIMES (I liken the number of times you'll playing this game, to the number of times you'll die playing Dark Souls!), but you take solace in the fact that you were bested by someone who has out-skilled you, or maybe has thousands of hours in the game.
The small number of hackers aside, this game is definitely worth the price -- whether at full price or discounted. It's also assuring that the developer, Facepunch Studios, is heavily invested in their game and continuing to update it after all these years. One change that I noticed in a recent update was the sound of a blizzard in the tundra biome; it really adds to the immersion of the game! Wonderful. There were several other survival games that I was considering buying, but I went with Rust because of Steam reviews and the commitment of Facepunch Studios to their game. I do not regret my purchase.

Undertale is one of the funniest, strangest, and most compelling games I have ever played. Overall, I give it a 9/10. Here's a list of pros and cons followed by a short blirb.
Pros:
-Fantastic Soundtrack
-Amazing writing
-Compelling characters
-Interesting and fun puzzles
-Spot-on humor
-Well-thought-out and unique boss fights
-Game doesn't hold your hand
-Multiple endings
Cons:
-Missable items, characters, and boss fights (though, that's what multiple playthroughs are for!)
-Some mechanics (especially some boss fight mechanics) are actually so unique that they are confusing and may cause mild frustration
-The random enemy encounters can become repetitive
-Some of the mechanics are so out-there that they make you ask "is this a bug or feature?"
-You'll most likely be confused throughout most of the game, whether it is for the lore reasons, mechanics, or the characters/writing. (Luckily, the top-notch humor is able to off-set this for the most-part).
That's about it. Undertale is hilarious and has amazing characters, puzzles, and boss fights. One complaint is that the game sometimes does such a good job of letting you decide what to do and say that you may be completely confused or stuck as to what to do. There are things you can miss easily if you're not looking (and even if you are, actually). Also, some of the boss mechanics were so confusing that I had to look up what to do. That being said, Undertale is one of the most unique games I have ever played. It takes the old-school RPG format and flips it on its head, resulting in constantly evolving gameplay that leaves you speechless. It is an incredibly well-written game with only a few mild annoyances. Overall, this games gets 9 temmies out of 10. Buy this game so Temmie can go to college!

The game is a huge improvement from the first, if you didn't like the barren enviorment and lack of story from Borderlands one, Borderlands 2 easily fixes this. Going from a chilling tundra, to lush and dangerous highlands, the enviorment is extremely varied. The main villain in particular, Handsome Jack is just as evil and entertaining as Kefka from Final Fantasy who has both very funny and just pure evil moments. The combat is what really shines here where can play how you want to play with over 87 "bazillion" guns to find and the different character classes. Skill trees are more varied than the skill trees from Borderlands 1 where it's not just your action skill with some minor upgrades here and there but also individual abilities. Abilities such as having your health regenerate when your shield is full, or causing corrosion damage when your hitting someone with shock damage. The enemies also have more variety and character, from the goliaths that can actually level up if you enrage them and they kill one of thier teamates, to the badass constructor drones that can spawn enemies and shoot nukes at you. Not only is this a fun game to play alone but also with your friends, because when you are playing with friends not only is there a sense of teamwork but also a greater feeling of reward since the enemies will be even more difficult and the rewards will be even greater. In conclusion, Borderlands 2 is an outstanding game and is probably my favorite game of all time for the reasons I stated and is just a fun and epic time to play with friends. 9.95/10

Now that you have killed your first animal you now must craft some lowgrade so you can make a furnace. Once you have a small 1x2 with a furnace and some small boxes, you now have to find some metal to turn your vulnerable wooden doors to less vulnerable metal doors. Found Undertale to be strange, fascinating, funny, frustrating and brilliant in places. I went in blind in this game, and while I had to look up certain boss fights later on the web (just to be sure of my approach), played the rest of the game without consulting the interwebs.
No doubt, the game (the maker actually) is very smart and ingenious. The game levels and design are excellent. Despite the boss fights seemingly daunting, the game encourages and facilitates the player to win- that part's very well thought out.
And yet, I thought the game did have some major flaws, the primary one being the confusion for the player between killing and defeating. At one point, to my dismay, I killed a character I had definitely not been wanting to, and just the exploration and experimentation while grasping the cryptic nature of conversations led to it. Having gone in blind, there was no way for me to know if there were other endings possible to this particular chapter where the character does not die. Neither was the player offered a choice to spare or not, in this instance. At another point in the game, I was stuck for a while for just the opposite reason. When it turned out (courtesy interwebs) that fighting was the only way out.
The second minor quibble I have is I have no idea about dogs and items related to them. There are some more similar quirks in the game.
Third, the controller thumb stick did not feel reliably responsive during gameplay.
Four, poorly worded questions like 'will you take this item' from a certain setting. When playing a game where ethics matter, one won't just pick up stuff without asking, that could be valuable to them. But the game will punish player if (s)he doesn't.
TL:DR version: The game makers did not clearly differentiate between defeating and killing an adversary. For a game of such refined sensibility, I consider this a big oversight. A 9/10 from me otherwise. A charming, quirky, unusual game. It's heart is in the right place and it deserves applause for it.

M4/FNX: Why are the guns that you could find almost anywhere, are now only found in helicopter crash sites? These 2 guns made dayz, it was reliable, powerful, easy to find, and VERY customizable yet now you can only find them at heli crash sites.
Battle eye: Battle eye sucks. Its main purpose in dayz is to prevent hackers, yet in the last week i have died atleast 5 times only by hackers. very radical changes: When i first started playing i could go to the NE airfield and find an m4, backpack, and plenty of ammo without even needing to server hop. then they took away the barracks and hangers, that was ok because they left the ATC tower, then then they took that away and replaced it with some crappy building that doesnt even spawn loot! wtf! You could loot the tents and be kitted easily, then they took away the tents and for some reason, you can barely find a a jacket at balota! WHY DO YOU HAVE TO CHANGE EVERYTHING? Graphics: the graphics are nice but need to be smoothed out. i have an Alienware Aurora with an i7 clocked at 3.4 Ghz, 30 gigabytes of RAM, dual nvidia 460s and i keep my graphics pretty low and i still lag! this game is very hard to run no matter what.
lag (ping): you spawn in cherno, find a backpack and a gun and some food, you are doing pretty well. you find yourself against a herd of zombies because the slightest noise startlles the whole damn city, but no problem, you went to the fire station and found an axe! you easily kill the zombies but one was able to hit you in the arm. seeing that your arm is now painful, you make a splint since you have no morephine. you add the rags and sticks to make the splint, all is doing well, you click on the splint, and apply it too yourself. nothing happens... you cancel action and try again, nothing happens... for some reason, your splint does not want to function! this is a very big problem if you cant fiind morephine, and if you have broken legs, youre screwed. new senario. This game is a very good truck driving simulator. You can drive many different trucks around the whole Europe, driving logs to London and such. It's very relaxing.
Yes, relaxing.
Just you, the logs, the truck, and the road. All so relaxing.
There's nice scenery outside - there's beautiful sunflowers, windmills, and little huts, all making you feel relax!
And then there are the other commuters on the road. All trying to get somewhere. Because if you're not trying to get somewhere, you're a nobody. You're aimless. Without drive. We all strive for things that are out of our reach, but we forget to stop and think - where are we now? It's the here and now that counts - not where we will be, not where we were, but the now! Does London really need more logs?
No. Probably not. They're bound to have plenty. It's just the everturning cycle of consumerism, telling people that they need more logs. Advertising telling people - younger and younger people - telling them that to have a happy life you have to have logs! And that's why you're delivering the logs.
But happiness isn't in logs, is it? No! That's not where happiness is, in the logs! Happiness is inside yourself! London, you don't need the logs! You don't need trucks! Nobody needs trucks!
Except if you want to relax. Then you absolutely need the trucks of Euro Truck Simulator 2. They're surprisingly relaxing.

Undertale is one of the funniest, strangest, and most compelling games I have ever played. Overall, I give it a 9/10. Here's a list of pros and cons followed by a short blirb.
Pros:
-Fantastic Soundtrack
-Amazing writing
-Compelling characters
-Interesting and fun puzzles
-Spot-on humor
-Well-thought-out and unique boss fights
-Game doesn't hold your hand
-Multiple endings
Cons:
-Missable items, characters, and boss fights (though, that's what multiple playthroughs are for!)
-Some mechanics (especially some boss fight mechanics) are actually so unique that they are confusing and may cause mild frustration
-The random enemy encounters can become repetitive
-Some of the mechanics are so out-there that they make you ask "is this a bug or feature?"
-You'll most likely be confused throughout most of the game, whether it is for the lore reasons, mechanics, or the characters/writing. (Luckily, the top-notch humor is able to off-set this for the most-part).
That's about it. Undertale is hilarious and has amazing characters, puzzles, and boss fights. One complaint is that the game sometimes does such a good job of letting you decide what to do and say that you may be completely confused or stuck as to what to do. There are things you can miss easily if you're not looking (and even if you are, actually). Also, some of the boss mechanics were so confusing that I had to look up what to do. That being said, Undertale is one of the most unique games I have ever played. It takes the old-school RPG format and flips it on its head, resulting in constantly evolving gameplay that leaves you speechless. It is an incredibly well-written game with only a few mild annoyances. Overall, this games gets 9 temmies out of 10. Buy this game so Temmie can go to college!

Mostly excellent feel to the vehicles, playing out that crusty-muck, surviving at the edge of extinction fantasy
- Though I'd like to see a lot of fiddley bits you can tack onto your vehicle that serve no purpose but as trinkets of history - which would be a much better historic relic system than pointless photos;
Wonderful visuals;
A build up system that is mostly effective, pulling forth your vehicle from a mass of kindergarten, saliva-crusted playdough at the start, to an immutable oil-plow of bone and clout and steel.
I'm sure there are more things I liked, though they're being overriden mentally by the things I didn't...
Cons:
Largely broken 4th wall
- Elementary, forced storyline, reminiscent of some first-draft fan fiction, in the annals of the 'innernetz', that I can only guess will be interrupted somewhere with Mad Max and the writer cuddling to a mix-tape of stuck-in-top-gear, endless engine drone
- Transparent main characters and badly-acted secondary ones
-- Especially the trite coupling of Mad Max & Woman #1 (That's cheeky, patriarchal film-speak for female-character-such-an-object-in-story-they-didn't-get-named)
-- Particularly the characters crowbarred in as badly as the story that fuels them
-- It's like Kanye West wrote a story about Mad Max, and somewhere in there is some brilliance and artistry, but you can't help but look at all the chaff around it and struggle little more response than a whimper and a quizzical look;
Boring top-dog fights
- Dodge, hit, dodge, hit some more, dodge, get bored, dodge and hit, eventually grind them down, get anticlimactic reward, wonder why this is some pinnacle to the story line
-- This really should have been a more elaborate system than just beat up some big dudes with big health bars like...80% of other games that shouldn't have done it either
--- why not a complex take-down of a huge camp with some valve/trap puzzles, with several enemies but micro-missions therein, like taking down segments that pull down additional inner-defenses, or saving prisoners, etc.
---- Or perhaps taking down a camp and tacking on an extended mission to build up what remains, something that has you pick up parts around the wasteland to improve that base which allows you to have your own patrols which lowers threat to the same level as the top-dog kill, or allowing it to have some micro-parts built up, like additional food/water that you could help refugees with, and they would give you scrap in turn, etc.;
Scrapping cars in the wasteland that you fought feels anti-climactic to the struggle to take them...10 scrap? For that? When I need 1000 for my next upgrade? (shrug)
- Maybe the scrap but also the random trinket system mentioned before where taking them down also gets you little do-dads, and wiggley things to put on your car as badges? Add some random sauciness, you know.
-- I found some fuzzy dice in there for my mirror? Rock on, put 'em up, buttercup!
-- I found a silver spoon on this guy, add more shiny things - now a dashboard menagerie of cutlery!
-- Culminating like well-travelled people in real life, popping junk around their home to remember where they've been - collecting memories of distant things to forget the local ones you keep...
Snipers with highly-visible glints and indicators all over, ruining the surprise of a 7.25 in your Gludius [Mad] Maximus, a full breakdown of what to find in every camp...no real mysteries here...no reason to explore when you can just pull it all down from a balloon, filled with the theatrical hot-air of a non-sense plotline
The list goes on.
###
A bit more data, if you'd like:
Griffa, for example, could have been a great character that you just bump into, whose quirks might have been amiable and compelling. Instead of sitting in a pictograph filled micro-scene with spooky music and forced dialogue, with the same sense of interaction as if my grandmother tweeted a meme. I mean, they could easily have just been leaned up against a rock, after you'd seen them a couple times wandered by. They'd wave politely and you'd ignore them, because that's what you do. Corner me eventually, in a passive way, wave me in as Mad Max, say hello, sound concernced that I have a clear distance to my gaze, that I've endured much. Offer a bit of advice wanderer-to-wanderer, be a person that also endured much and has run it solo as well - that you don't need to be so distant, try to heal the wounds. Of course you'd decline, but somewhere, well-deep inside, you'd have that enchanting feeling that you might have meant something.
More to the point; if just griffa wasn't enough, the rest of the story goes just the same, with pointless lines up to what writers wanted to happen. From absurdly engineered sniper rifles to "Look guys, a dog! It's like, you can have it, like Max did in the movies, and uh...we didn't know what to do with it, so we jammed in something about minefields, cool...a dog that instantly follows you...because...like...that's what dogs do! What do you mean it feels like some trailing object and not a complex relationship with a domesticated animal, that involves a deeper sense of trust than seems available to any human, let alone a deeply jaded one? Um...but...dog! :ignorant smile from writer, clearly not getting it:"
What about taming it, about proving your worth to it, as it does you? Loyalty is earned.
Extend this even further to being forced to do the story missions to get parts...even though you see them on the cars you destroy...but lo, here be a wanderer that needs to shoot a guy in the distance, beyond the edge of Babylon, to unlock...a bit of twisted metal to bolt onto his car frame? Or that some random person mucking about can give you the full details of all the hidden bits of a camp...spoiler alert? So much for the choose-your-own-adventure form of open worlds.
I suppose, all-in-all, it was interesting to listen to Devs in the pre-release gameplay videos saying how little they liked handholding in games, and wanted an open world, but it all feels so engineered. Must do story to progress, have to complete the first several missions to even be allowed to do side missions, to even be allowed to use all those project parts you had been picking up for hours while wandering, that everything is there, telling you where it all is and how to play it. Sigh.
Car combat makes up for things like this, along with the ambiance of the wasteland and riding about, slamming into things like a neanderthal and clubbing your own sense of diplomacy with 36 inches of spiky-steel. E.g. I loved my first convoy fight in my barely stable vehicle, crumpling like used aluminum foil in the grasp of an underdeveloped toddler. I somehow managed to take the lead down at front, causing an 8-car pile-up of the chasers, leading to a stream out of drivers' seats, likeh I cut them off on the interstate. Course, I jumped out as well for a 4 escort fist fight, and 3 pile-ons that just happened to be driving by...then the awkward game of cleaning up my mess, collapsing all the autos into washers and flaming carbs, to smoldering pitch in the dessicated wild.

After playing for 30 hours, Mad Max is everything I hoped it would be and then some. That being said, I have a hard time understanding why reviews have ranged from the 5 to 8.4 range. 96% positive reviews on Steam means gamers have spoken for themselves. With a cool combination of Fallout, Borderlands, Far Cry, and Just Cause, Mad Max has stunning visuals, engaging combat in-car and on foot, and a great variety of characters.
While I haven't found the story particularly enthralling, it is still fun. The open-world environment, however, is where this game truly excels. As I head towards an objective, I frequently find myself distracted doing other things, such as disarming a minefield with my trusty dog Dinki-Di, clearing out a camp, or being ambushed by a group of enemy vehicles. It is these types of fun distractions that make Mad Max shine.
Everything in this game is upgradeable. Fortresses can be upgraded to give Max refillls on Fuel, Ammo, Water, and Health. The Magnum Opus has millions of possible combinations, from colors and insignia to the body, to engines and other parts. These upgrades make a noticeable difference to the feeling of driving the car, as well as to the way it actually sounds. Max himself can be upgraded in two ways: by visiting Griffa to enhance health or a variety of other attributes, or by adding armor, etc. that gives Max a boost in combat.
I have not found the bleak, postapocalyptic landscape to be repetetive or dull. The graphics are extremely high quality, espcially with Nvidia SLI and AMD Crossfire support right out of the box. The sky and weather visuals are fantastic, especially when a tornado or huge sandstorm occur. Additionally, these storms never seem to be the same, with some looking like the lightning/tornado from Fury Road while others look like a sever haboob in New Mexico.
There are some things I have not enjoyed about the game, and which I feel should have been included right out of the box. Despite his reputation as a road warrior, Max is not able to jump over simple obstacles. While he can jump, he will often need to find the predetermined route into a stronghold, generally marked by yellow paint. Something else that has bothered me is the low quality of graphics in Jeet's stronghold. Avalanche seems to be going for a rising heat effect, but the result is blurry textures. Despite these flaws, the game is still very satisfying.
Driving is an absolute pleasure. As you upgrade your Magnum Opus, you won't want to fully upgrade everything. Putting a heavy ramming bar or armor on your car, for example, will lower your acceleration and handling, making the car less nimble. Upgrading your engine, tires, or suspension will have the opposite effect.
Hand-to-hand combat is both gritty and brutal, with Max using objects in the environment to beat his opponents to a pulp. Fans of the Arkham series will be familiar with the controls, but the combat still has a unique feel to it. Anyone can button mash their way through this game, but there are huge rewards for using the special combo moves available to max. Players who take the time to learn and practice these will find their satisfaction with the combat increases greatly. Additionally, Max can build up a fury meter to unleash Fury Mode, which greatly enhances his attacks and allows for special Fury finishes.
Mad Max doesn't break any new ground in the saturated open-world genre, but it is a rich, immersive game with fantastic graphics and satisfying combat. Reviews have been quite varied, but if you are looking for a new game to play, listen to the gamers themselves and pick up a copy of Mad Max for PC.
Verdict: 8.9/10
A few flaws diminish the experience somewhat, but this is still a AAA title worth investing many hours into.

This was recommended by a friend and I got it in the recent Steam sale. I thought it would be boring but it is insanely addictive. It is a simple concept: drive from one city to another in the time allowed and try not to crash. It is introduced very well as well. Once you have created your company in the menus you can take on quick jobs that provide you with a truck and all of your fuel is paid for. Then once you've earned enough money you can buy your own truck and drive freely to any location on the map. You are constantly gaining experience points that make jobs payout more. You can upgrade certain skills that unlock bigger cargos to haul around. There are quite a few choices of trucks to buy.
The is being updated regularly and new features are always fun to play with. A recent update gave you three extra cities to drive to at no extra cost which I thought was pretty special.
The only dissapointment with the game is that there are no complete cities to explore. When you come off the motorway you have access to a series of roads connecting the different company depots, repair stations and truck dealers.
I would recommend this game to anyone who likes driving games but wants a change from racing. This is more of an endurance driving simulator when you unlock the longest routes.

DayZ is a troubled early access alpha which has spent its 3 year existence in nothing short of development purgatory. After the creative lead, Dean Hall, abandoned his baby the project clearly had a lack of direction given the sparse number of patches and ignorance of community outcry. What's left in its current state is a stagnant mess that will likely never be finished. Feature creep plagues DayZ, while "new" features such as vehicles are being added, the game suffers horribly from poor performance, dated netcode, and myriad bugs.
The game is essentially (and ironically) a slow-paced battle royale, the genre in which DayZ played an important role in reviving with games like H1Z1 and PLAYERUNKNOWN's Battlegrounds, both games sought to copy the DayZ formula but cut out the tumors. The engine in DayZ is extremely dated, Dean Hall himself has previously said that it's "not ideal" but "not as primitive as everyone thinks" ... words of inspiration. Everything ranging from movement to shooting is clunky and unresponsive, as it's basically Arma 2 with some new things tacked on. If you've experienced Arma 2, you've experienced the core of DayZ.
Substantial amounts of time in game will be spent trawling through buildings to find precious loot, with varying degrees of success depending on how many zombies you encounter at the start, how many players you encounter spawn camping, and how fruitful the loot spawns themselves are. Then, providing you don't die to zombies walking through walls as they chase you, begins a cycle of running from town to town and eating/drinking, encountering players if you're (un)lucky, continually building up your arsenal of weapons, attachments, and general loot.
Once you've become an Apex predator in DayZ, with all the best equipment and supplies you've scoured the map for (over a course of potentially several hours per play session), you reach a slump: What next? Well, you can go hunting for other players as you camp popular loot sites, you can go and spawn camp, you can .... actually that's it. Player interaction in game depends on how friendly you want to be and how friendly the other players are.
The ultimate entertainment in game, I found, lies in messing with new spawns in a gang. Forcing 2 players to fight to death in a ring, a single fire axe between them, and letting the survivor continue to live, is better entertainment than the game itself provides. Whether or not the potential 6-8 hours of grind with 0 guarantees of survival to reach that point is worth it is up to you. Personally I don't think it is, I find it to be painfully dull.
Don't bother with DayZ until it's in a better state. It performs too poorly and lacks meaningful content besides an invisible gear treadmill.

Had no expectations for this game, and honestly was not even sure what type of game play it had, but I figured I wouldn't have much to lose at $19.99.  I have to say after about 4 hours of playtime I am taken aback by just how much I am enjoying this one!  I could have easily paid full price for this and not regretted it one bit at this point.
The combat, while very similar to Batman and SoM, is quite satisfying and you can really feel the hits connect, especially on the power moves.  Not long into the game you unlock "Fury Mode" which builds up as you combat the enemies and once filled lets you unleash a variety of fancy moves for a time, from piledrivers to suplexes and so much more!  The vehicular combat is stellar as well, I don't see myself getting tired of harpooning an enemy and flinging him 50 yards across the screen whist shouting "Get over here!" anytime soon!
There seems to be a lot of content to the game as well.  A generous menu of collectibles and skills, weapons, and vehicles to upgrade, and I really like how each area shows you the percentage of items you have yet to discover in that location so the completionist in me knows where to look before moving on.
I know 4 hours is not enough time for a proper review and I'll update this one later once I've had my fill but Mad Max is certainly shaping up to be a great experience that I really hope will not be lost on most gamers in the shadow of MGS:V.

Dayz Standalone is an early access, standalone version of a mod for Arma 2/Operation arrowhead, made with a new engine supporting better enemy AI, weapon models and animations, and performance. Its a standalone version in a similar sense that Tower Unite is a standalone version of Gmod Tower, using this to their advantage to do things the orignal engine wouldn't let thim, and while this might SOUND good for DayZ (and at some point it might) it actually works less in its favor. See, the problem with this is that there is nothing to do. Even with friends. Someone who played the original dayz mod would probably gear up, raid a base, or get missions from NPCs, but in this standalone version, it lacks all of that. But i can see why. They cant just port everything the original dayz had to a new engine, because they were written for almost entirely different engines, so they have to re-build all of that from the ground up, but it is taking WAYYYY to long, and they are even doing things that hinder the game, such as a new hud that doesnt give you any details about your character status, and the details it does give you is miniscule. A broken shock meter where you can get knocked out in 2 punches. And the removal of a useful hud and convenient reload mechanics. Now you have to equip ammo to your hotbar and press that hotbar button with the gun out to reload a new mag, OR go into your menu and drag the item over the weapon, all of which are out of the way. And like i said, there is no amazing content that would cancel this stuff out. There arent even loot containers, so the most interesting thing you can do is just plant potatoes.
In general it is a good game and WILL be a good game, and i would reccommend buying if only to see how the game changes over the years.
However for now, i HIGHLY reccomend just buying ARMA 2 and getting the DayZ mod

Driving a truck through europe.....snorefest much?
That was my first thought when I got this game and most people I know share that thought. There was a huge hype over the game tho so I gave it a shot......
...took me ONE tour to hook me up.
Seriously. Whats fun about this game?
Your truck is a big slow brute, almost everything on the road is faster then you, your acceleration is matching a snails and turning takes hours (felt)...WHAT exactly can be fun about it?
For me.....
- its very relaxing to follow the street and be challenged with realistic physics and traffic rules
- visuals are AWESOME if you take the time to look around there are so many details
- a skill system enables you to evolve and improve your own driver and build up a trucking company
- mostly its about the EXPERIENCE, its not a racer, its not a reaction game....it enabley you to do something most people cannot do in real life ----> commanding 800 horse power at your leasure
I am playing it with keyboard and mouse (for steering and looking around) which works out quite well for me once I adjusted various sensetivities. I seriously consider getting me a steering wheel, camera (to enable me to "look" around with my head) and pedals for better control tho.
It certainly isnt for everybody. I m just saying you dont know if its your game or not if you dont give it a chance. I "thought" this would never work for me and here I am....happily trucking away while my wife watches me shaking her head :)

If I had to review this game in one word, it'd be: good. Okay, great! Review's over, bye! Seriously though, Undertale is amazing. Oh, what's that? Undertale is too expensive? Oh yeah! I forgot how expensive Undertale is compared to any 3ds game! I mean 11 dollars? (Well, 11 where I live) that's barely over a singular bill! Joking aside, I love Undertale. I love it's characters, it's writing, it's humour, I even wrote an essay about Undertale! (Don'tguessmyage) So I guess, sorry teacher? But we'll go through all that slowly.
First off, Undertale's story is perfect in this day and age. Undertale protests against the call of duties of the world, the halos, maybe not the splatoons though. Undertale's message told me that you should never give up, no matter how dire the situation is, to talk to frogs/aliens pretending to be humans, but secretly have only been put here on this planet to torture me. In a world full of 7 year olds playing Call of duty, Undertale tells you violence is never the answer. Which is sad, because when you think about it, Undertale will only be played by the older, never to be found by the younger. The younger people, preferably one old enough to read, but young enough to be not old, I'm guessing will have an experience like mine. (Don'tguessmyage) The sort-of problem is that it creates a boring experience in the genocide route. Wow! I get to attack by timing a button press?! Google doodle did it better. (It was the one with that guy eating peppers if you're interested) But. The genocide route makes up for that in story. The story is consistently good, has feeeeeeels. But I guess there are better games that are cheaper than Undertale. Well, I guess I'll just hit that not recommend but-PSYCH!! What Undertale lacks in how much it cost-though, I still don't see how that's a problem- it makes up in that message. show this game to a younger audience, and this message sticks with them for life. It did for me, at least. Well random person on the Internet, you might be saying. I hear that Undertale's pretty short. A game just for the story? That kinda sucks. Well, I guess you're ri-PSYCH AGAIN!!! Gameplay! Whoosh!
I'm not sure if it's just that I haven't played any games like this, but I found Undertale's battle system.very enjoyable. Both the defence and pacifist "battle" mechanics. I always challenged myself to take no damage, and believe me. That was a challenge. The final boss of the neutral route displays this spectacularly. I am kind of mad that I died like 15 times on the final boss, where my non-gaming sister died ONCE. Buuuut, I'll let it go. What's that? You like the battle system, but don't like how it was implemented? Then look at the many fangames of Undertale, most of them being one off fights. Practically endless fun! The pacifist battle system gets you to choose from a menu what you want to do with the monster. Want to talk to it? Why not! Want to pet it? Why not! Want to look up spoilers for Undertale on the Internet? NO. Undertale has to be a fresh experience. I'd even argue that you shouldn't even look at the characters until you encounter them in the game, but that's your choice, not mine.
There are a lot of small things in Undertale I want to take time in talking about. The humour! Why do I like the humour? Because I love to make horrible puns, and my fairness hate them. The soundtrack. Undertale literally has the best  soundtrack I have ever heard, but than again, I haven't played many games. At the very least, the soundtrack is spectacular. The annoying dog, and tems! Just because. And last but not least, the abandoned quiche. Apparently, Toby Fox found a quiche in real life under a bench. Cool, huh?
Overall, Undertale was a delight to play. It was cheerful, it was dark, it was funny, it was comforting. But in the very end, if you didn't like it, if you think it was trash, if you think I over-hyped it, just remember. It was never about the game. (Well, I guess it kinda was) it was about the message. A message of determination. To wrap it up, I give this game a 9.5/10 score. And remember, when you're out there in the dark and gritty world of video games, or even real life, always remember to show some MERCY.

Dayz Standalone is an early access, standalone version of a mod for Arma 2/Operation arrowhead, made with a new engine supporting better enemy AI, weapon models and animations, and performance. Its a standalone version in a similar sense that Tower Unite is a standalone version of Gmod Tower, using this to their advantage to do things the orignal engine wouldn't let thim, and while this might SOUND good for DayZ (and at some point it might) it actually works less in its favor. See, the problem with this is that there is nothing to do. Even with friends. Someone who played the original dayz mod would probably gear up, raid a base, or get missions from NPCs, but in this standalone version, it lacks all of that. But i can see why. They cant just port everything the original dayz had to a new engine, because they were written for almost entirely different engines, so they have to re-build all of that from the ground up, but it is taking WAYYYY to long, and they are even doing things that hinder the game, such as a new hud that doesnt give you any details about your character status, and the details it does give you is miniscule. A broken shock meter where you can get knocked out in 2 punches. And the removal of a useful hud and convenient reload mechanics. Now you have to equip ammo to your hotbar and press that hotbar button with the gun out to reload a new mag, OR go into your menu and drag the item over the weapon, all of which are out of the way. And like i said, there is no amazing content that would cancel this stuff out. There arent even loot containers, so the most interesting thing you can do is just plant potatoes.
In general it is a good game and WILL be a good game, and i would reccommend buying if only to see how the game changes over the years.
However for now, i HIGHLY reccomend just buying ARMA 2 and getting the DayZ mod

Keep in mind with this review, I didnt pay much for the game, 33% of retail.  So that being said, I might feel better about its quirks than many others reviewing it.
Gameplay Impressions:
So far I like the game, to the contrary of many of the Negative Reviews, I like the controls, but they should have been thought out a little better as defaults.  The game also plays extremely well with the mouse and keyboard, again contrary to many of the -Neg reviews.  I guess I dont blame developers for thoughtless control mapping, but rather blame myself for not picking up on them fast enough.
Character movement and Vehicle movement / Map Navigation.  Both are good, they have the perfect amount of feedback, the cars have very nice weight and slip systems and very easy to control.
Character and Vehicle Combat.  I've never been a fan of the button mash style fighting system, but this feels just as good as any of the best games out there doing it, Including the Batman Series, Witcher 3 and GTA 5.  Vehicle combat is also well thoughtout, but due to odd control mapping it can be challenging.  I was able to figure it out pretty quickly after a few fails.
There is some bad level design decisions you'll discover, for one the character cant climb much and cant jump very high.  This is normally not a big deal, but there are things you'll be trying, logically, assuming you can climb up certain objects, but you cant.  Climbable objects are Designated much in the same way they are depicted in Tomb Raider.  Dont expect Raider'ish control though, and once you've gotten over that, the movement is well done and works well.
The Story seems decent enough, C'mon, these game plots are nearly always crap, and you know it, 90% of gaming suffers from crappy storylines.  Try to base your expectations lower here and you'll have a good time.
Graphics:
Visually, I like everything about the graphics, detailed models, great animations, solid voice acting, interesting locations I dig it.  Would I change certain things, oh yeah.  So much empy open space, yet nothing really to discover.  This game needs tons of lootable caves to explore and gather stuff - (yeah, I'm refering to Skyrim here.)
Performance: The graphics look great maybe I wasnt expecting much, but theyre as good as they need to be.  Simply put, the game looks great, even the wieniest of the graphics cards (in my case the a Stock "2gb GTX 650")  with my settings (mostly Normal, but a few Ultra Settings @ 900p, the game is comfortably sitting between 45-55 fps, a few lower in complex environments and gameplay sections but its never dropped below 35 fps for me.  I'm thinking I can increase the resolution to 1080 and it will sit at 30 fps or more.  Not bad.
Thats it for now.  I have a feeling the game becomes a grind after a few hours, but we'll see.    I'll update this review as I go.

This game is really great, completely blew me away with how perfect this game runs, one of the best pc ports I've played. There's no frame drops or stutters with all the chaos that goes on. It's a constant smooth 60fps even with every graphical setting maxed out. The game is extremely fun too. The combat is really easy and simple (free flow combat from Arkham games) but it's so satisfying to use all these classic wrestling moves and hear the bones of the war boys shatter with each hit. The game shines with it's car combat, the biggest thing they had to nail with a game like this. Upgrading the Magnum Opus with armor or more weaponry to take out vehicles is a blast. Mixing around different upgrades to see what fits your playstyle best. Taking out convoys and war parties feels exactly like George Miller directed them himself and that says enough. The game is also gorgeous. Beautiful lighting effects and skyboxes make the game pop with vibrancy. Even if 99% of the time you'll be looking at a deset. The world hasn't bored me yet, there's planty to do from strongholds to taking out sniper nests to reduce threat in areas (it's a really large map) There's always something to do on your way to story missions or if you just wanna roam around. Overall, I'm very surprised and happy with this game. The story so far is intruiging, with each character voiced very well and just like the movies, Max is set on one goal and kinda just drifts along helping random people and not saying much. But that's all you need for a Mad Max story, and of course the over the top war lords with their unique (sometimes hilarious) names. Avalanche nailed this one, the Mad Max game fans have been waiting for and deserve

From the short amount of time I've played Mad Max I've:
- Had my car stolen
- Murdered several dudes because of my car
- Befriended a hunchback mechanic who's willing to serve my murderous ways
- Saved a dog
- Had my dog blown up
- Started upgrading my car to hopefully make it into a machine that lives off the corpses of my enemies
Mad Max lives up the films pretty well, everyone's out there to murder you for gasoline and just because they want to, Mad has no issues stepping up to the plate and murdering everyone else in turn and you're going to see things blow up constantly. While Mad Max doesn't have the more vivid colors of the recent Fury Road, it does feel like the desolate landscapes we saw in Road Warrior. It's truly a wasteland for you to explore, and an utterly MASSIVE one at that.
The game controls really well, though there's certain things that feel strange if you're playing with a controller; for instance instead of A to be the run button like most other third person titles they made it right trigger. I guess it's to differentiate itself from the recent Batman titles but it seems unnecessary. The only issue I've had with controls so far is ironically with driving, the Buggy and basic car you start with in the beginning fell really, really heavy and sluggish. I want to say that they're meant to be this way since it's the beginning of the game and it's only until later when you have a quicker, more responsive ride.
The game also looks fantastic, I have everything maxed out on an i4790k and GTX 780 with well over 60 frames on average. I initially had thoughts that the game was going to be littered with bugs and playability issues but that is definitely not the case, the game is very well crafted from top to bottom so in case you were haven't any doubts about that don't worry. Also it being somewhat of a movie-tie in (though it doesn't seem to have much to do with them) I'd understand any apprehension.
Mad Max has delivered in spades what I expected and I've barely scratched the surface; I can't wait to see the rest.

If I had to review this game in one word, it'd be: good. Okay, great! Review's over, bye! Seriously though, Undertale is amazing. Oh, what's that? Undertale is too expensive? Oh yeah! I forgot how expensive Undertale is compared to any 3ds game! I mean 11 dollars? (Well, 11 where I live) that's barely over a singular bill! Joking aside, I love Undertale. I love it's characters, it's writing, it's humour, I even wrote an essay about Undertale! (Don'tguessmyage) So I guess, sorry teacher? But we'll go through all that slowly.
First off, Undertale's story is perfect in this day and age. Undertale protests against the call of duties of the world, the halos, maybe not the splatoons though. Undertale's message told me that you should never give up, no matter how dire the situation is, to talk to frogs/aliens pretending to be humans, but secretly have only been put here on this planet to torture me. In a world full of 7 year olds playing Call of duty, Undertale tells you violence is never the answer. Which is sad, because when you think about it, Undertale will only be played by the older, never to be found by the younger. The younger people, preferably one old enough to read, but young enough to be not old, I'm guessing will have an experience like mine. (Don'tguessmyage) The sort-of problem is that it creates a boring experience in the genocide route. Wow! I get to attack by timing a button press?! Google doodle did it better. (It was the one with that guy eating peppers if you're interested) But. The genocide route makes up for that in story. The story is consistently good, has feeeeeeels. But I guess there are better games that are cheaper than Undertale. Well, I guess I'll just hit that not recommend but-PSYCH!! What Undertale lacks in how much it cost-though, I still don't see how that's a problem- it makes up in that message. show this game to a younger audience, and this message sticks with them for life. It did for me, at least. Well random person on the Internet, you might be saying. I hear that Undertale's pretty short. A game just for the story? That kinda sucks. Well, I guess you're ri-PSYCH AGAIN!!! Gameplay! Whoosh!
I'm not sure if it's just that I haven't played any games like this, but I found Undertale's battle system.very enjoyable. Both the defence and pacifist "battle" mechanics. I always challenged myself to take no damage, and believe me. That was a challenge. The final boss of the neutral route displays this spectacularly. I am kind of mad that I died like 15 times on the final boss, where my non-gaming sister died ONCE. Buuuut, I'll let it go. What's that? You like the battle system, but don't like how it was implemented? Then look at the many fangames of Undertale, most of them being one off fights. Practically endless fun! The pacifist battle system gets you to choose from a menu what you want to do with the monster. Want to talk to it? Why not! Want to pet it? Why not! Want to look up spoilers for Undertale on the Internet? NO. Undertale has to be a fresh experience. I'd even argue that you shouldn't even look at the characters until you encounter them in the game, but that's your choice, not mine.
There are a lot of small things in Undertale I want to take time in talking about. The humour! Why do I like the humour? Because I love to make horrible puns, and my fairness hate them. The soundtrack. Undertale literally has the best  soundtrack I have ever heard, but than again, I haven't played many games. At the very least, the soundtrack is spectacular. The annoying dog, and tems! Just because. And last but not least, the abandoned quiche. Apparently, Toby Fox found a quiche in real life under a bench. Cool, huh?
Overall, Undertale was a delight to play. It was cheerful, it was dark, it was funny, it was comforting. But in the very end, if you didn't like it, if you think it was trash, if you think I over-hyped it, just remember. It was never about the game. (Well, I guess it kinda was) it was about the message. A message of determination. To wrap it up, I give this game a 9.5/10 score. And remember, when you're out there in the dark and gritty world of video games, or even real life, always remember to show some MERCY.

It's hard to fault a game that provides this amount of content, in a format that is refreshingly different. This is not a game that jumps on the "simulator" trend lightly, and encompasses different aspects into the game.
You spend your time in a variety of customisable trucks, delivering different shipments across Europe to work your way up the ranks of the trucking business. You can outsource some work to employees you can gain, and even own your own truck which lets you roam free, or access exclusive jobs on the freight market.
For a game where you spend most of your time on the road, ETS2 manages to create brilliant landscapes that run moderately well even on low/mid-range laptops.
Some pentalies the game imposes can be a nuisance at times. For example, a fine is issued if you do not have your headlights on during rain (which is a feature of the game that is executed well). However this is a minor annoyance, and if required the rain frequency can be adjusted (the settings are extremely detailed), or turned off altogether. Most other penalties add a layer of realism and are not too annoying.
I would recommend the purchase of ETS2 to almost anyone, as driving a truck across Europe in this game is enjoyable and a relaxing but captivating change to the fast pace of other games.

Oddly relaxing - put an audiobook or a podcast on (through the ingame radio or otherwise), hit the cruise control and transport your cargo across Europe. Definitely a good time if you want to just chill out.

The characters had some good backstory, which could be viewed by accessing certain parts of the game. But, to be honest, a lot of the backstory is fan-made or implied, and not specifically stated. The game leaves a lot of loose ends for the player to figure out what happened before the events of the game. Not something I particularily enjoy, but it didn't really get in the way of gameplay a noticeable amount.
It was, for the most part, a light-hearted but serious-at-times story, a-la-Disney.
Okay, I'm going to get this out right now before someone stops me.
I think Undertale's gameplay was absolute garbage.
Yes, I think it was interesting to mix the bullet-hell genre with a turn-based RPG. I get it. It's a neat idea. But in execution, there were elements that were underused, overused, or completely forgotten.
No status effects (wat), No blocking, hell, there was only one damaging attack (although I understand that wasn't the point of the game, so Toby gets a freebie on that one.)
My point being, Toby seemed to have forgotten which genre of game he was developing, and messed up the other genre.
This one got me. If you know me in real life, or just know me at all, you should definitely know that I'm a sucker for soundtracks. I listen to video game soundtracks more than I listen to real music.
This game had great music, in my eyes (or ears?). Most of the good tracks were boss themes, and the reason they were so great is that they fit so well with the bosses you were fighting against. You could definitely hear the pang of regret in Toriel's theme, the stab of perseverance in Undyne's theme, and the glamorous narcissism in Mettaton EX's theme.
Overall, the game's soundtrack was well-created to allow you to experience the game in a more enjoyable manner.
Undertale does a great job of mixing Pixel graphics with modern-esque styles. Enemies are all pixellated, but they (for the most part) animate so well. You can see Madgick bouncing around, Undyne holding her spear, bouncing around, Final Froggit... bouncing... around...
Well, you get the point. Toby does a good job of using pixel graphics without resorting to static sprites. Good on you for that, Toby.
Also, don't forget that mind♥♥♥♥ of a pseudo-last boss. Those graphics were like an acid trip.
Not the best game, but certainly not the worst. Play it for yourself and see how you like it!
This games fanbase creeps me out.

I'll be honest, I heard about this game very early when it came out. Before it's community became... Very questionable. Nevertheless, I saw fanart of this game on my Instagram search feed. I came from being part of the FNaF community (a regrettable experience) and I just thought Undertale would be as bad as a game as FNaF turned out to be. I started playing this game as a joke with my friend. I got through a reasonable amount of the
game and I decided to start again and try again, alone and on a different path. I was not disappointed. This is probably the best RPG and story-driven game I have played. No other game has engaged me in a story more than Undertale. The art style gave me that nostalgic 'old-school' style as when I was younger, all I had was the Gameboy games. The soundtrack is probably one of the best video game soundtracks I have ever heard. This game challenges how you've been playing RPGs. It makes you think about the creatures you are fighting as every monster has a character, unlike other games where you just slash them to death with no thought as to if they had any thoughts or feelings. You are morally tested throughout Undertale. Every choice you make is permanent as the game remembers what you've done. Even if you 'RESET' the characters still show vague knowledge of your previous choices. Undetale is meant to be played more than once as you may choose to play differently on another run after you realise the actions you have taken. I've never been a fan of these fantasy RPGs, but this game was one of the greatest games I have ever played and it takes my Game of the Year 2015. I will never forget the wonderful experience I had playing Undertale. Even though the general Undertale community has taken a dark path, I won't let that ruin one of the greatest experiences in gaming I have had.
tl;dr - Undertale is a fantastic story-driven game and anyone can enjoy it if they play it with an openmind.
Sidenote - Be prepared for bullet hell.

The haters are gonna hate, but the simulators are gonna simulate, and the haters are going to miss out on the best PC driving game since Stunts came out over 22 years ago.
Simulation games are all about trying something that you would otherwise not be able to do in real life; its not like most people have ever even met a truck driver before, let alone had the chance to become one, its kinda like being an astronaut: only the best of the best ever have a hope of getting behind that wheel. So if you didn't have perfect grades in highschool, and don't have PHD level degree in engineering, finally here is your chance to haul apples from Munich to Frankfurt in a 40 ft trailer!
But seriously, Euro Truck Sim 2 is a perfect example of a game that really shouldn't work, but does. Lets face it the subject matter is horrible, it simulates a job that I can tell you from experience most people would gladly walk away from and never return if they didn't have a mortgage and 2 kids at home. But somehow the beautifully rendered European scenery, the generally really good physics, the open world gameplay, and the lite buisness sim gameplay provide just enough to make this a really good game. I find that rather than feeling like I am at work when I play it, its always `just one more haul`, so I can do X, and it becomes really addictive.
Players that have played `cargo trading` games before such as Wing Commander privateer or Freelancer will feel right at home here, although instead of getting shot at, its all about safe driving and good route choices.  Strongly recommend it to anyone who wants a good casual driving game with a fun economic rpg built in. If you hate driving games in general, or are generally more action oriented in your game choices maybe take a pass on this one.

It's hard to fault a game that provides this amount of content, in a format that is refreshingly different. This is not a game that jumps on the "simulator" trend lightly, and encompasses different aspects into the game.
You spend your time in a variety of customisable trucks, delivering different shipments across Europe to work your way up the ranks of the trucking business. You can outsource some work to employees you can gain, and even own your own truck which lets you roam free, or access exclusive jobs on the freight market.
For a game where you spend most of your time on the road, ETS2 manages to create brilliant landscapes that run moderately well even on low/mid-range laptops.
Some pentalies the game imposes can be a nuisance at times. For example, a fine is issued if you do not have your headlights on during rain (which is a feature of the game that is executed well). However this is a minor annoyance, and if required the rain frequency can be adjusted (the settings are extremely detailed), or turned off altogether. Most other penalties add a layer of realism and are not too annoying.
I would recommend the purchase of ETS2 to almost anyone, as driving a truck across Europe in this game is enjoyable and a relaxing but captivating change to the fast pace of other games.
