Update: June 9th 2017
Well... They made the environment more lively (grass, trees and debris move with wind), they added new sounds to make the environment more lively (birds, crickets, wind).
The game is still total PvP as there really aren't that many zombies to limit the PvP interaction. There's no reason to not shoot someone if you get the opportunity, since you can easily outrun the few zombies that might be on the area, if there's any at all. Trying to communicate with other players is usually a dissapointment where you most likely will end dead if you have any significant visible equipment to loot (backpacks, weapons, vests...). As a fresh spawn on coastal areas you might survive an encounter with other player(s).
Loot systems seems to be broken to me still. I know they want to force people move to inland from the coastal areas, but sometimes (quite often nowadays) with bad luck you will not have any food to survive the trip to other villages or areas where you might find significant loot to stay alive. Of course this depends on the player count on the server, but who wants to play on empty server?
I hope they figure out how to make zombies a real threat in this game that would unite other players to co-operate more and remove the PvP kill-on-sight element from the game. Of course PvP will be part of survival game always, but PvP seems to be all DayZ is currently.
And the few zombies that you mostly meet around cities or villages are really easy to take down once you have at least a melee weapon. This is why there needs to be hordes of zombies to make them a problem you want to avoid. You can't just walk next to horde and start taking them down one by one or shoot another player if there's hordes of zombies around you. But no, at best there might be like 10 zombies running to you one by one if you shoot another player inside a city. Then it's just up to you if you want to run to get rid of them or just lock yourself inside a house and they lose the aggro and just start wandering around again.
TLDR: The game is still just big PvP sandbox with loot system that most likely starves you to death if the server is full or near full, or someone will just shoot you because zombies really are not the problem in this Zombie survival game. Wait for the reviews to become mostly positive before buying.

This is the first Review I write on steam, so forgive me if it is not the best
First of all, the game is perfectly optimized, and I have yet to encounter a bug, even the smallest one. The atmosphere is great, the voice acting is amazing, and the characters are believeable and relatable. Chumbucket, the crazy blackfinger mechanic, for example, is amazingly animated, well-voiced and overall looks believable in the world that this game is set in.
The voice acting and the animations are smooth, and fit seamlessly.
About the graphics. I myself have a pretty strong machine, but I read that even on low-end computers, the game looks gorgeous. And quite frankly, I believe it. I am running everything on the highest setting and I have yet to have a single frame drop. The game is gorgeous, from the animation of the sand trail behind your moving car to the fight scenes and to gastown in the distance, everything looks and feels gorgeous, while still holding the games theme of a post-apocalyptic world.
The game mechanics are great. How you liberate the land, something we have seen in just cause 2, shadow of mordor and several other games, it feels realistic, and it works, and it's fun, every camp you liberate feels a bit different, which is nice. You have tons of different enemies, and ways to kill them. You can upgrade your car with the help of chumbucket, being able to make your Magnum Opus your own personal War machine. The only thing I might find a bit strange is the entire deal with your canteen being your health potion, but even that is fine.
Overall, even if you have never seen a Mad Max movie, even if you normaly are not a fan of games of this genre, you should pick this up.
Mad Max/10 Guys, buy this game, it's an AAA title worth the title of AAA.

9/10 - Ignore the haters and joke-makers; not every driving game has to be about ripping a Ferrari around the Nurburgring.
This is an amazingly well done sim, doubly so for a Greenlight game. If you've ever wanted to get a feel for driving a semi, this is as close as it gets on a computer. The controls are amazing and the physics of the vehicles and their engines - the power curves, gear shifting, braking, etc. - are better than I've seen in many mainstream driving titles. Full support for keyboard, controller, and/or various steering wheel set-ups. The world is large enough to keep you entertained while still being scaled down enough for you to drive across the continent without it taking all day. You get cruise control. You can take a ferry between England and the mainland. Trucks and cargo take damage if you run into stuff, and it adds up fast, so don't. There are mods like most vehicle games, however the only one I use (and I recommend it) removes the 90kph electronic speed limiter on the trucks so you can actually do 120kph in the 120 zones. Most everything on the trucks can be customized, from mirrors and lights to gas tanks and chassis to engine and transmission (and the engines are actual engines! You swap specific engine A for specific engine B, as opposed to most games where engine upgrades are minor label-less increases to a stat bar titled "power"). The business management system is also well thought out - you hire drivers and purchase garages across Europe, who work while you do, driving trucks that you've purchased and customized and stored, so you don't have to earn all your dollars yourself. The trucks are all licensed from real manufacturers (Renault, Iceni, Man, Scandia, etc.) and they are constantly adding and updating sound effects and other features to make them even more authentic. You and your drivers have an experience and leveling system, which unlocks higher value (and also higher difficulty) loads available to you. Can choose to back your trailer into the delivery spot for extra points, or skip doing it if you can't back very well. The biggest thing I wish they would add/upgrade in a future patch is to include more flavor in each of the cities - apart from the repair shop, truck dealership(s), and job site(s) where you pick up loads, there isn't much to see or do, and there's only a few streets worth of territory in each city. All in all a fantastic sim with an active community and passionate support from developers who really do listen to the players. But if you're looking to put the pedal to the floor and not let up until you reach the finish line, trading paint with your rival truckers and setting a new lap time, then this game is not for you - getting there with no damage is far more profitable than getting there early.

Honestly, after beating the game for 7 hours to have the "happy ending", I cried 3 times because the story is just amazing. It is stunning and incredible. I've never expected to end this way. It started off with some stupid and dumb puzzles. But after that, it drove the player deeper and deeper as the story takes its place and time and affected the players an unprecedented way. That is the factor that makes Undertale a masterpiece. I played a lot of RPGs and this one really makes me turn around and give me an unique story with beautiful gameplay.
*THE SYSTEM OF UNDERTALE
Now, when I first saw Flowey ( dat son of a ♥♥♥♥♥ ) almost killed me, all I think is that this game is stupid because all I have to do is move my heart ( i mean my soul ) around like a little ♥♥♥♥♥. However, after sinking my teeth into the game, I realized it's a lot more and its brilliance lies on its simplicity. Undertale expected me to have played RPGs before and played with those conventions in unexpected ways and that clever manipulation of gameplay mechanics adds weight to a story that couldn’t have been told in any other way or medium. That's what I need from RPG games. Make something new! At first, I thought I got that dodging combat mechanics, but after a while, the gameplay started pushing me and players to a limit with these storytelling from characters to characters as the story builds up. Every monsters in the game has its own unique way to deal with, you can fight them or spare them if you want the true pacifist ending, of course. For me, I wanted the true pacifist ending so therefore, I have to flirt, hug, and pet in order not to kill them so that I can spare them. That's it a cool idea. Not only that, the way that I interact with them feels like we were treating each other from I to I. There are tons of jokes relating to anime and even snail jokes that really know how to set up a crowd. Undertale really knows how to predict the players and that's it a factor that I like about Undertale.
* THE WAY MONSTERS WORK
The way Undertale builds up the story is hilarious and touching. A lot of hidden messages are putted through out the game. Each of them knows how tell a story about humanity and morality. For example, when I was listening to echo flowers in a hallway that recorded a conversation between two people, I was impressed by it. It was about a monster whose greatest wish was to escape this underground lair to see the view, don't want to share it because she(he) afraid that her( his ) friend might laugh at her ( him ). However, after telling the truth, the friend laughed anyway and it was funny until it said: " Sorry, it’s just funny… That’s my wish too. ". And from that I was silenced for how honestly these characters were written. Witnessing the depth of monsters's dreams about freedom really a strength of Undertale. Giving the players the exploration of humanity and morality. Talking to them and discovering about them is amazing. I was amazed for how well-developed these characters were written. It just makes me cry because I have to fight them which I don't.
*THE MOST AND OBVIOUS REASON WHY UNDERTALE IS A MASTERPIECE: DETERMINATIONNNNNNNNNNNNNN

Update: June 9th 2017
Well... They made the environment more lively (grass, trees and debris move with wind), they added new sounds to make the environment more lively (birds, crickets, wind).
The game is still total PvP as there really aren't that many zombies to limit the PvP interaction. There's no reason to not shoot someone if you get the opportunity, since you can easily outrun the few zombies that might be on the area, if there's any at all. Trying to communicate with other players is usually a dissapointment where you most likely will end dead if you have any significant visible equipment to loot (backpacks, weapons, vests...). As a fresh spawn on coastal areas you might survive an encounter with other player(s).
Loot systems seems to be broken to me still. I know they want to force people move to inland from the coastal areas, but sometimes (quite often nowadays) with bad luck you will not have any food to survive the trip to other villages or areas where you might find significant loot to stay alive. Of course this depends on the player count on the server, but who wants to play on empty server?
I hope they figure out how to make zombies a real threat in this game that would unite other players to co-operate more and remove the PvP kill-on-sight element from the game. Of course PvP will be part of survival game always, but PvP seems to be all DayZ is currently.
And the few zombies that you mostly meet around cities or villages are really easy to take down once you have at least a melee weapon. This is why there needs to be hordes of zombies to make them a problem you want to avoid. You can't just walk next to horde and start taking them down one by one or shoot another player if there's hordes of zombies around you. But no, at best there might be like 10 zombies running to you one by one if you shoot another player inside a city. Then it's just up to you if you want to run to get rid of them or just lock yourself inside a house and they lose the aggro and just start wandering around again.
TLDR: The game is still just big PvP sandbox with loot system that most likely starves you to death if the server is full or near full, or someone will just shoot you because zombies really are not the problem in this Zombie survival game. Euro Truck Simulator 2; its often difficult to explain to people what makes this game so immersive and fun to play. You can easily put hours into this game and never realise. After putting 162 hours into the game myself, I figured I should leave a review!
Basically, this game gives you the freedom to travel the roads of Europe, driving any truck you desire, completing jobs from Aberdeen in Scotland to Lublin in Poland and everything in between. The trucks are fully customisable, and there is also a level up system, allowing for longer distance jobs, eco driving, more important cargo and better trucks unlocked.

You may purchase your own garages in the cities you visit across Europe, and hire drivers to work for your company. The more you earn, the more upgrades you can do to your garages and the more trucks you can buy as well.
The devs at SCS are excellent and come out with great updates and DLCs. Also, if you're a modder, this game has a great modding community and awesome scope for mods of all kinds.
It is a great simulation game, if you have a wheel and pedals to use, the experience is even better. But you can also use a normal gamepad if you desire rather than keyboard, it is up to you how you play. The trucks drive like they should do, you can feel the weight of the trailers you pick up.
One of the things I love most about this game is the environment. SCS have done a great job with creating the world of ETS2, and each country has a slightly different feel. I love driving through the Austrian mountains as well as the countryside in the UK. The weather and lighting is also brilliantly done.
I have owned ETS2 since February 2013, and I still enjoy playing. I highly recommend this game!

I recently moved from Xbox 360 back to the PC scene.  In the years that I had an Xbox, I found that I really missed the kind of games that only PC has.  Games where essentially nothing happens. The world won't end if you don't achieve your objective.
This is why I like ETS2.
This is an extremely well-supported game.  The publishers regularly issue free updates (not just bug fixes, but additional cities, road networks, trucks, etc).
I have sunk hours into this game just driving a truck from one city to another, and then another city, etc. It is a great way to while away time with no stress.  Although the roads and cities are very loosely based on the real-life versions, I don't think that you could ever hope to compare game vs. real-world with any degree of accuracy.  Having said that, there are certain roads that I have travelled in-game and in real-life and found myself thinking 'wow, they got that right!', so must be an element of consideration of the real-world road network.
Controls were initially an issue, but a recent update fixed that with proper Xbox controller support.  Performance-wise, the game has never crashed or had any technical problems at all.  It runs at max settings on my PC (which is fairly high-spec, so I would expect that!)
My main criticisms are minor; the graphics can seem a little bleached out / over-saturated (in HDR mode especially), sometimes the AI drivers create a bottleneck where they all block a junction waiting for a vehicle to turn - this causes the lane that the vehicle needs to cross to become blocked (I had to barge my way through the roadside to get past!).  Another minor complaint is that the roads seem very under-populated.  If possible, there needs to be an option to increase AI traffic.
All in all, I love ETS2 and would recommend it to anyone looking for a game to pass time in.

I'm a huge Mad Max fan, and this was a pleasent surprise.
George Miller would be proud of the detail that's gone in, each faction, each enemy, vehicle and stronghold all fit perfectly into the post-nuclear apocalyptic world that has been so well personified in the films, from the jury rigging in household objects to the rusted and battered bodywork of each car, it holds true to the legendary Mad Max films.
The gameplay is good permitted its' limitations, a very good PC port with no CTDs or errors within ten hours of gameplay, fun and challenging on the road; but suffers the warner brothers melee system problem present in Batman, but without a sense of scaling enemies, although improvements to the combat help it feel even more grittier and more desperate as a tail of survival.
The world is suitably large; empty and devoid, how it should feel for such a game, but the small bands of people, warring factions and sidetracking galore as you become addicted to scrap, and just wanting that one more upgrade for the Magnum Opus.
There's a few moderate-to-negligable problems, Max seems to be played by multiple voice actors and oftens sounds completely different in one scene to the other, and unfortunately his voice work doesn't stand up, and I would take Mel GIbson or Tom Hardy over Bren Foster any day. The fortresses and gas pumps become a little repetitive, but that's open world games and multi-platform development for you. And you might as well turn of the near-non-existant music and put on Fury Road's soundtrack as it fails to properly accentuate the full on carnage present.
All in all, after ten hours of non stop gameplay the game is wonderful, but the need for sleep is becoming a problem. If you can get this game at a reasonable price, I'd heavily suggest doing so as you'll be riding the fury road like a true road warrior until you're all SNAFU. (We don't talk about Thunderdome, the kids film).
P.S. Harpoon is OP as ♥♥♥♥.

After driving an impressive 98'000km in game. Being a veteran trucker adds more fun to the game as you begin to understand the fundementals of it all and you become a better player at completing missions and getting out of tricky situations.
The only bad point that needs mentioning: I have found myself, more than once, stuck at a highway intersection (Under a bridge) with nowhere to go due to traffic lodged up from all directions and not being able to move at all. I had to carefully squeeze between the vehicles and the hill, knocking over a roadsign, just to get out of there. The only problem was that I had to do a U-Turn on a tight road, with a long trailer, to be able to get on the correct on-ramp and that caused some damage to the truck and trailer.
Other that that, everything feels real. You feel the difference when you're without a trailer and when you're with trailers of different types and wheight causing different driving techniques. Some trailers allow aggresive driving while others don't. You even have the option to hire drivers that bring you extra income while they drive missions for your ever expanding business.
In short, it's a great game for anybody who loves driving and loves a good simulation. Missions of all types allow you to do a short mission if you don't have plenty time or save in the middle of a long mission and come back to it at a later stage. The autosave function also comes in handy in case there's suddenly a power cut. True story XD

It is hard to explain. It all started when a friend started me on this game called DayZ. It was difficult at first. Basically, it is a game about surviving in a zombie apocalypse. The map is the size of a small country, and you have to find equipment to survive, whether it is guns, clothes, food or water. All of it is necessary for survival.
I can remember my first gunfight so clearly. I was the underdog. I was simply making my way into a parking lot in Elektro, which is one of the most popular locations for people to go to. I was alone, and had nothing but a Makrov pistol with a couple of rounds. I didn’t even have a clip for the gun, so I had to chamber each round individually.
I was in the middle of opening the boot of a car in search of gear, when a bullet hit the roof of the car. As an ARMA player, my first instinct was to go prone and locate where the shot had come from, so I could then figure out what direction to go to stay safe.
The first thing I noticed was that I heard the bullet make contact with the car at almost exactly the same time I heard the bullet leave the barrel of the gun it came from. This much told me that my attacker was close by.
I got up into a crouching position so I could get a better view over the car. It was then I heard a voice. It was the first voice I had ever heard in DayZ, and a mixture of joy and fear pulsated through me.
“Keep your hands behind your head, and you will liv-“his voice was cut off by the sound of a bullet travelling through his skull. Someone had come up behind him with a pistol and shot him in the back of the head. He knew I was behind the car, as he took a few pot-shots at me. I peeked left and took a shot at him. It was a well aimed shot, but his vest took it.
He wasted no time in picking up my first attackers Aug. I chambered a second round and attempted to peek the other direction, but he rushed me. I made my way around the opposite side of the car and stood to take another shot at him. The shot missed, and I ducked in time to hear a bullet whiz over my head.
The only thing of use I had at the time was a flash bang. After chambering the third round, still making my way around the car, I equipped the flash bang, and tossed it towards the attacker. I then made a run for it right after, but as it seems, my attacker had a friend. I spot a sniper on the hill I was about to run to only seconds before he pulled the trigger.
For the first time, those fateful words popped up on the screen. You are dead. Somehow, instead of feeling frustrated or annoyed, I was so happy. That was a rush. One of the best feelings I have ever felt playing a videogame.
After that, I came back to play DayZ every day, but something has changed. Through my experience in the game, (as little as it may be) I seemed to have developed some sort of.... personality while playing the game. I am not myself. Normally, I am a cheerful and carefree person, but when I am in game... I am different. I am what most people would consider a monster. I have made very little friends, and a lot of enemies. Though, there was a pair of people that I felt seemed like good guys, and it turns out they have a hell of a lot of experience, so I could learn a lot from them.
Today, something happened. My full... evolution, has finished, as far as I can tell. I was having quite a moment in DayZ. I was knelt down in a barn, by myself. I had so much gear, but nothing to live for. As I stared down the barrel of the gun for about half an hour, many different thoughts passed through my mind. I didn’t know what I was playing for anymore. That rush in a fight had gone. I was but an emotionless killing machine. I remember hearing someone walk in and scream “wait”. I pulled the trigger anyway... I don’t know what it was, but I felt as if I had come full circle. I started anew, and began collecting gear. I then got in another fire fight, in which I had come to lose. I had come to the conclusion that... well, I don’t really know yet to be honest. I am still trying to figure out what to do next. Isn’t that what we are all trying to do? Figure out what we’re doing means?

I find this is an amazing game to unwind with, it's a great game to turn on a playlist/podcast/internet radio, and just mellow. It is very easy to immerse yourself in the game, especially if you have a racing wheel.
The premise of the game is that you are a truck driver that just started their own long distance transport company. You start off borrowing trucks and doing short deliveries, until you can purchase your own truck, and start doing longer trips, building your empire in the process.
This is one of the rare games where the developer actively listens to their audience, and caters to them. If people want new content, they listen, and strive to make it. I give them a 10/10 on customer service alone, even 2 years after the release of the game, they are still very involved with releasing new patches and content.
The game itslef is a little rough around the edges, using their own game engine, it isn't the most optimized (I can run Skyrim at ultra without AA, but can only run this game on high, with Skyim looking a lot more visualy appealling). That is not to say that graphics are everything, but just expect that if you run games at high settings around 30 FPS, be prepared for some frame drops, especially around cities.
I find that the vanilla game is very fun, but what makes me keep coming back is the constant updates done by mod authors. The Euro Truck Simulator community is very open to new players, and has a very active modding community. Mods typically make the game more immersive, adding new trucks, making new maps, trailers, just about anything and everything that can be modded.
TL;DR
Very immersive game, dev's still improve the game even years after it was released, and mods keep the game fresh. If you are looking to have a laid back gaming session, This game is at the top of my list.

9/10 - Ignore the haters and joke-makers; not every driving game has to be about ripping a Ferrari around the Nurburgring.
This is an amazingly well done sim, doubly so for a Greenlight game. If you've ever wanted to get a feel for driving a semi, this is as close as it gets on a computer. The controls are amazing and the physics of the vehicles and their engines - the power curves, gear shifting, braking, etc. - are better than I've seen in many mainstream driving titles. Full support for keyboard, controller, and/or various steering wheel set-ups. The world is large enough to keep you entertained while still being scaled down enough for you to drive across the continent without it taking all day. You get cruise control. You can take a ferry between England and the mainland. Trucks and cargo take damage if you run into stuff, and it adds up fast, so don't. There are mods like most vehicle games, however the only one I use (and I recommend it) removes the 90kph electronic speed limiter on the trucks so you can actually do 120kph in the 120 zones. Most everything on the trucks can be customized, from mirrors and lights to gas tanks and chassis to engine and transmission (and the engines are actual engines! You swap specific engine A for specific engine B, as opposed to most games where engine upgrades are minor label-less increases to a stat bar titled "power"). The business management system is also well thought out - you hire drivers and purchase garages across Europe, who work while you do, driving trucks that you've purchased and customized and stored, so you don't have to earn all your dollars yourself. The trucks are all licensed from real manufacturers (Renault, Iceni, Man, Scandia, etc.) and they are constantly adding and updating sound effects and other features to make them even more authentic. You and your drivers have an experience and leveling system, which unlocks higher value (and also higher difficulty) loads available to you. Can choose to back your trailer into the delivery spot for extra points, or skip doing it if you can't back very well. The biggest thing I wish they would add/upgrade in a future patch is to include more flavor in each of the cities - apart from the repair shop, truck dealership(s), and job site(s) where you pick up loads, there isn't much to see or do, and there's only a few streets worth of territory in each city. All in all a fantastic sim with an active community and passionate support from developers who really do listen to the players. But if you're looking to put the pedal to the floor and not let up until you reach the finish line, trading paint with your rival truckers and setting a new lap time, then this game is not for you - getting there with no damage is far more profitable than getting there early.

Euro Truck Simulator 2; its often difficult to explain to people what makes this game so immersive and fun to play. You can easily put hours into this game and never realise. After putting 162 hours into the game myself, I figured I should leave a review!
Basically, this game gives you the freedom to travel the roads of Europe, driving any truck you desire, completing jobs from Aberdeen in Scotland to Lublin in Poland and everything in between. The trucks are fully customisable, and there is also a level up system, allowing for longer distance jobs, eco driving, more important cargo and better trucks unlocked.

You may purchase your own garages in the cities you visit across Europe, and hire drivers to work for your company. The more you earn, the more upgrades you can do to your garages and the more trucks you can buy as well.
The devs at SCS are excellent and come out with great updates and DLCs. Also, if you're a modder, this game has a great modding community and awesome scope for mods of all kinds.
It is a great simulation game, if you have a wheel and pedals to use, the experience is even better. But you can also use a normal gamepad if you desire rather than keyboard, it is up to you how you play. The trucks drive like they should do, you can feel the weight of the trailers you pick up.
One of the things I love most about this game is the environment. SCS have done a great job with creating the world of ETS2, and each country has a slightly different feel. I love driving through the Austrian mountains as well as the countryside in the UK. The weather and lighting is also brilliantly done.

If ever there was a game that defined the word repetitive MAD MAX would be it. You move from territory to territory doing the same thing over and over again.
The Driving is not good. It feels slow and sluggish, even with the best engine and handling. Once you've got all the basic car utilites leveled up enough, car combat becomes a rinse and repeat pattern of: blow their armour off and pull their tires off. Even the more leveled enemies become boring to fight once this pattern is discovered.
There are Camps, Scarecrows, Snipers, Convoys and Minefields which classify as the side missions. At first doing these things is enjoyable but once you've done them more than a few times it becomes a chore. There are variations of camps, which have a 'boss fight' at the end. I hesitate to use the words 'boss fight' because you fight the exact same character model just with different colours each time and their attack patterns are exactly the same. The combat is the same as the Batman games and Shadow of Mordor but with less variation. Once you level up your ammo belt and shotgun enough you can pretty much just shoot most enemies and not have to bother with fistfighting.
This game has a lot of stuff to do, but it's of no importance. Completing all the side missions doesn't feel fun, it just results in more stuff so you can get a slightly better this or a slightly better that.
Overall this game has a whole lot of repeating filler content that gets boring after a while. I cannot recommend this game.

Euro Truck Simulator 2; its often difficult to explain to people what makes this game so immersive and fun to play. You can easily put hours into this game and never realise. After putting 162 hours into the game myself, I figured I should leave a review!
Basically, this game gives you the freedom to travel the roads of Europe, driving any truck you desire, completing jobs from Aberdeen in Scotland to Lublin in Poland and everything in between. The trucks are fully customisable, and there is also a level up system, allowing for longer distance jobs, eco driving, more important cargo and better trucks unlocked.

You may purchase your own garages in the cities you visit across Europe, and hire drivers to work for your company. The more you earn, the more upgrades you can do to your garages and the more trucks you can buy as well.
The devs at SCS are excellent and come out with great updates and DLCs. Also, if you're a modder, this game has a great modding community and awesome scope for mods of all kinds.
It is a great simulation game, if you have a wheel and pedals to use, the experience is even better. But you can also use a normal gamepad if you desire rather than keyboard, it is up to you how you play. The trucks drive like they should do, you can feel the weight of the trailers you pick up.
One of the things I love most about this game is the environment. SCS have done a great job with creating the world of ETS2, and each country has a slightly different feel. I love driving through the Austrian mountains as well as the countryside in the UK. The weather and lighting is also brilliantly done.
I have owned ETS2 since February 2013, and I still enjoy playing. I highly recommend this game!

To clear some common misconceptions, this game is mainly about PvP, people who have good awareness, reaction time and teamplay skills (+voice comms!) will succeed, people who wanna play The Sims: Post-Apo or Fallout Online, may get disappointed greatly. Well, you can have your PvE experience and explore the basics of the game in a very low populated PvE server, but I can promise that it will get boring soon enough.
It is also beneficial, if you have a group or 2 or more, like 5 or so, both for strength in numbers and gathering resources faster and in larger amounts - especially in vanilla. And if youre willing to think outside the box while building your base (or outside the square, to be more literal in this case), youre also doing it right - classic fundamentals of architecture as we know it aren't going to work in this game.

If you dont like the idea of that, this game isnt for you. Oh, yes, and stating the obvious, your agressiveness will be rewarded - best defence is good offence! Get yourself aquinted how weapons, ammo and armor work (I'd suggest a practice in Combat Tag server for that), and you save yourself lot of trouble.
Community isnt always the best. When I thought WoW or World of Tanks had rubbish community... After driving an impressive 98'000km in game. Being a veteran trucker adds more fun to the game as you begin to understand the fundementals of it all and you become a better player at completing missions and getting out of tricky situations.
The only bad point that needs mentioning: I have found myself, more than once, stuck at a highway intersection (Under a bridge) with nowhere to go due to traffic lodged up from all directions and not being able to move at all. I had to carefully squeeze between the vehicles and the hill, knocking over a roadsign, just to get out of there. The only problem was that I had to do a U-Turn on a tight road, with a long trailer, to be able to get on the correct on-ramp and that caused some damage to the truck and trailer.
Other that that, everything feels real. You feel the difference when you're without a trailer and when you're with trailers of different types and wheight causing different driving techniques. Some trailers allow aggresive driving while others don't. You even have the option to hire drivers that bring you extra income while they drive missions for your ever expanding business.
In short, it's a great game for anybody who loves driving and loves a good simulation. Missions of all types allow you to do a short mission if you don't have plenty time or save in the middle of a long mission and come back to it at a later stage. The autosave function also comes in handy in case there's suddenly a power cut. True story XD

A great insight and experience into what it is to drive a large combination vehicle over long distances, although these are flatnose pullers which can only compare to early 90s models in North America. Still a great trainer if you are looking into driving the real thing. Though I would strongly suggest dropping down for a decent steering wheel controller, only because the difficulty of controlling said vehicle on a keyboard only justifies the price of getting a steering wheel and shifter combination. If you want to truly immerse yourself, get an Oculus Rift (they just came out with compatible software for the game) and a pair of headphones. Overall, if you ARE training to be a large vehicle freight driver, all this is still cheaper than a school. Unfortunately, most (current) jobs involving this industry will not substitute this for "real" experience.
All in all, still a great program to own and there is a lot of push for far more development into of what is already there.

If ever there was a game that defined the word repetitive MAD MAX would be it. You move from territory to territory doing the same thing over and over again.
The Driving is not good. It feels slow and sluggish, even with the best engine and handling. Once you've got all the basic car utilites leveled up enough, car combat becomes a rinse and repeat pattern of: blow their armour off and pull their tires off. Even the more leveled enemies become boring to fight once this pattern is discovered.
There are Camps, Scarecrows, Snipers, Convoys and Minefields which classify as the side missions. At first doing these things is enjoyable but once you've done them more than a few times it becomes a chore. There are variations of camps, which have a 'boss fight' at the end. I hesitate to use the words 'boss fight' because you fight the exact same character model just with different colours each time and their attack patterns are exactly the same. The combat is the same as the Batman games and Shadow of Mordor but with less variation. Once you level up your ammo belt and shotgun enough you can pretty much just shoot most enemies and not have to bother with fistfighting.
This game has a lot of stuff to do, but it's of no importance. Completing all the side missions doesn't feel fun, it just results in more stuff so you can get a slightly better this or a slightly better that.
Overall this game has a whole lot of repeating filler content that gets boring after a while. I cannot recommend this game.

Mad Max is everything I expected it to be.
It follows, at its core, the same mechanics we've seen through franchises like Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Just Cause to cite some. It promises hours and hours of discoveries, fistfight brawls, car chases, explosions and content overall. I never felt bored (granted I've just played 3 hours tops) because there's simply so much to do and so many butts to kick. First impression is excellent. Here's some brief points:
PROS:
- Huge and beautiful world to discover, play and eat dust in. It's huge and "wide" but it doesn't feel repetitive, monothone or empty at all. Kudos to the developers in both making you feel tiny in a huge and wide desert but still populating it with so much stuff to do without it feeling bloated or unrealistic.
- Fast, fun, easy to learn gameplay. Combat feels fantastic both on your car and out of it. Brawl system similar to Arkham games.
- RPG elements that are actually useful, fun and meaningful at each step of the way, particularly the car customization.
- Amazing storyline so far (yet simple to make your own and drift away for some time before contienueing it).
- Tons of varied and different activities and ways to do them. Huge freedom.
- Amazingly beautiful graphics, scenery and effects. Voice acting and animations are top-notch too.
- Good AI. The world feels alive and challenging. You'll constantly see convoys patrolling, couriers being escorted, raid parties, war bands attacking settlements... They actually try to flee when you're outfighting them and attack you in groups if they have the chance.
- Sound effects and explosions are amaizng.
- All the things "Mad Max". They absolutely nailed the mood.
CONS:
- The sand and the dryness of the world will constantly make you want to drink water.
- Controls could have been better adapted for keyboard and mouse, specially interaction things like jumping in-out of cars, collecting scrap, climb to stairs or sliding down ropes. Combat controls feel good nontheless.
- Controls and hotkeys can't be changed as far as I've seen. I may be wrong because I haven't double-checked.
- I haven't discovered how to drift yet. It may be my car though.
- Small variety of chassis to choose from. I don't know if more are to become available through the storyline or we'll have to wait for DLCs.

The game shows no visible progress in the last two or three years. The developers offer only a lot of air for the minute and insignificant changes. Looking at the aquired budget the company has for the futher development of the game, it is hard to explain why they did not make more headway in finishing the project. The explanation of working on the engine and other vital parts does not excuse the overall cosmetic progress that is largely in the area of items rather than the core gameplay and game stability issues.
Overall I have the impression the staff is getting smaller and smaller. The resent "push" (march 2017) for better vehicles for example was officially schedualed for first quarter of 2015. It was one of the initial bullet points.
My conclusion is either the managers already gave up the project, because they know they will not retreave the attention of the gaming community for DayZ Standalone. They may have realized that there is no way to make more money of the project and every investment in the development is a financial loss. The second possibility is that they simply lack the staff and the talents to finish the job. I doubt this second possibility, because they have the finances to hire people and software projects can be realized from different places around the globe at the same time. They could employ people from Argentina or India or whatnot. And software developers generally have some command of the English language in general.
In may opinion the project appears to have encountered to many problems and the management was probably not willing to spend the needed money early on to try to finish the project in an acceptable time frame. Today the management pretty much gave up to finish the game in an acceptable stable and content rich (base building, vehicles, work shop content, less hacking... etc.) form. They instead employ a rudimentary stuff that nibbles away on a task that is not even half finished and is still fundamentally flawed and most likely will remain so. I feel really sorry for the people employed in the project. It must be a thankless task.
And in addition I am angry that they do not talk plainly about the state of affairs. The developers always talk about progress been made, things introduce and the exiting future of the game which is plainly rubish. They do not talk about real issues and maybe the developers are not allowed to, if they want to keep their jobs.
DayZ Standalone is a negative example for early excess. Crowd funding and early excess is indeed a great way to fund the games we wanna see. The downside is, that the responsible developer/management may bail out if he/it encounters to many unforseen problems. DayZ sold over 3 million copies if I am not completely mistaken. They should have enough money to hire a stuff that could finish the job.

No words can express how much I love this game. It is truly a test of time for the gaming industry, its story so complex and interesting, its characters funny and sometimes terryfying. Everyone has to play this game whether you're young or old, you will always learn something from this game. Whether it be to stay determined to achieve your goals, to always appreciate what you've got, or it could be something entirely different. This game has a different message for every type of person. It's even good for people that don't play games and want to get into it. It's no wonder this game has such a huge following, it always has you begging for more.
Undertale's story takes place in a dystopian future, in a world where monsters and humans are divided. Its set after a devastating war between monsters and humans that killed thousands of lives, in a final stand the humans trap the monsters in an underground system for all eternity with a barrier the keeps the two races seperated. Your character is a human child who has wondered into a cave that leads to the underground, after suffering an almost fatal fall into the underground you find yourself in The Ruins, the entrance to the underground. Where you meet a heartwarming soul named Toriel. This intro sequence acts as a tutorial to the things you'll be facing later on in the underground; including fighting, talking your way out of problems, and how the underground is a very dangerous place for a human to be. After finishing this area you press on to the rest of the underground to begin your journey to find your way home. I wont spoil anything else. This game is best played blind, so that means no looking up spoilers! One thing I do have to mention though is the super unique way the game takes on a fighting system. The fighting system in Undertale is much similar to many other RPG games but features a unique twist: The MERCY option. This option gives players the option to spare their enemies and talk to them during battle. Each character has a different way of being spared though, sometimes you might have to eat something, talk to them about a specific thing, or even just hitting them in the face before sparing them. Another unique thing about this system is how the battle actually plays out, its a turn based system which means you have a turn then your enemy has a turn then vice-versa. You attack with a simple chance type of attacking (that is if you even want to attack your foe) but when you are attacked you take the role of a small red heart that you use to dodge your enemies attacks. I know it sounds weird but you'll know what I mean if you play the game.
Undertale also has an amazing soundtrack featuring 8-bit style retro music with a mix of rock, pop, and even sometimes funky jazz.
Overall I highly recommend this game to absolutely anyone, it is an absolutely fantastic game, and deserves people to play it. So what are you waiting for? Go and play Undertale! :D

I held off this game for more than a year since its release because of its fanbase and daunting popularity where people went "Man, you HAVE to play it" and it was so much pressure and people made it seem like not playing it or not having played it yet was borderline offensive to them. Doesn't help that most of its fandom gets really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and... "meme-y"? about stuff and it really makes everything that transpires in this game rub you off the wrong way (it did to me.)
Simply put, the fandom made it seem like it was all about shallow humor and shallow "emotive moments", shallow themes and a shallow game that people over-enjoyed and it was held in some sort of high pedestal as something that it was not.
Well, about a year ago, a youtuber that I appreciate started playing it, and he never had done it before, so it was purely unbiased views on the game, with decent enough commentary that made me take the game for what it was, and not for what people made it to be. And it seemed actually pretty decent! But alas, that youtuber had contact with a huge portion of the fanbase that berated him for playing it "the wrong way" and other trivial matters, someone went as far as to spoil endgame stuff and it was a big buzzkill for him, so he dropped it.
A few months ago he gave another shot at it and got further in the game, and I was eager to see if it was actually that interesting and generally good. Once he got to the second boss fight I decided I wanted to try it out by myself, and I'm glad I did.
I'm not one to be too turned off by spoilers so I was lucky that the internet didn't ruin the experience too much for me, and y'know? Even though I had watched it prior, playing through everything I had watched didn't water down the experience at all.
So, after recently concluding two of this game's three endings (and having full knowledge about the third one.), I can tell you this:
Undertale is a very charming RPG, who often gets reducted to the fact that you don't need to kill anyone, blablabla, love and peace and all of that stuff but it uses that to greater effect than some "pacifism is good, killing is bad" shallow moral lesson.
It has very endearing characters, a decently thought out lore and world-building, coherent writing and interesting concepts blending traditional RPG mechanics with in-universe reasoning and lampshading for everything, often subverting expectations to one accustomed to such games.
The battles are a blend of bullet hell, some plataforming and other concepts of 2D gaming while keeping the RPG formula of using items, attacking and... getting to know your opponent better. Reasoning with them and whatever rules they appear to play by.
Graphics are simple, but well made and I don't think it could have been done without the 2D pixelated style and still get the point across for many things, and it often relies on it for narrative purposes.
It makes for a fun experience and I don't regret mentioning that it made me care about the main supporting cast so much that I was brought to tears nearing the end of the "True Good Ending".
So overall I'd rate it 9/10, would definitely recommend it and well... I suppose that's about it. Don't let other people dictate how you experience this game, take your own conclusions and it's fine if you dislike it, just don't let other people be the reason of it.

I recently moved from Xbox 360 back to the PC scene.  In the years that I had an Xbox, I found that I really missed the kind of games that only PC has.  Games where essentially nothing happens. The world won't end if you don't achieve your objective.
This is why I like ETS2.
This is an extremely well-supported game.  The publishers regularly issue free updates (not just bug fixes, but additional cities, road networks, trucks, etc).
I have sunk hours into this game just driving a truck from one city to another, and then another city, etc. It is a great way to while away time with no stress.  Although the roads and cities are very loosely based on the real-life versions, I don't think that you could ever hope to compare game vs. real-world with any degree of accuracy.  Having said that, there are certain roads that I have travelled in-game and in real-life and found myself thinking 'wow, they got that right!', so must be an element of consideration of the real-world road network.
Controls were initially an issue, but a recent update fixed that with proper Xbox controller support.  Performance-wise, the game has never crashed or had any technical problems at all.  It runs at max settings on my PC (which is fairly high-spec, so I would expect that!)
My main criticisms are minor; the graphics can seem a little bleached out / over-saturated (in HDR mode especially), sometimes the AI drivers create a bottleneck where they all block a junction waiting for a vehicle to turn - this causes the lane that the vehicle needs to cross to become blocked (I had to barge my way through the roadside to get past!).  Another minor complaint is that the roads seem very under-populated.  If possible, there needs to be an option to increase AI traffic.
All in all, I love ETS2 and would recommend it to anyone looking for a game to pass time in.

Something about this game is addictive... it's indescribable...

The graphics are fantastic, even on medium to low settings, and it won't kill your gpu either. The driving mechanics are great. The AI can be stupid at times, but it somehow adds to the charm of this game. The aspect of customizing your truck keeps you working to get the extra cash you need to upgrade your engine or put on that new coat of paint or even add some lights or horns.
With any good sim, certain aspects of the game can be changed to accomadate your play style, like turning off the sleep simulation or the speed limiter (but sadly traffic fines cannot).
While the vinalla game gets dull after a couple hours, the moddability adds hours upon hours of awesome. There are truck mods, trailer mods (my favorite), and even map mods to freshen the game up.
The one problem you might face with this game is finding the control style that's right for you. Some people like it, but I would strongly caution you to NOT use the keyboard or mouse/keyboard control schemes. The second option is better if you're on a budget, but it's still not great. If you want to get a great experience out of this game, buy a Xbox controller (which I'm stuck with at the moment) or get a racing wheel (strongly reccomended); it will make the game infinitely better.
The game's not for everyone, but I suggest you give it a try; you might like it (I sure do)

Euro Truck Simulator is a very good game, despite how boring it may look on the outside. It has a large exporable map, many vehicles and tons of customization and as such leaves you with an urge to explore and do more to get money and levels. ETS certainly has many things that it could do better, though.
The leveling system is extremely slow and has little reward until you reach high levels, including trucks , which can sometimes make the game boring but is certianly not a game breaking flaw. The money system on the other hand is good and allows you to take out loans for trucks, garages and the like early on without having tons of hours in.
The company system is boring and somewhat useless as the drivers you hire yield little reward and the entire thing is managed from one page. The company aspect has no real effect on gameplay or anything and it seems forced on you.
The A.I. are not the smartest and will often hit you straight on instead of moving out of the way in awkward situations.
And finally the crash physics are not realistic and an accident will not be physically reflected with a dent or scratch. This personally annoys me a lot but there is realistic engine failure when the truck becomes extremely damaged.
I think that if they added a multiplayer or perhaps even online companies it would make the game more exciting and less solitary. The gameplay is great; the graphics are very good and the driving feels good but the game is lacking in some categories. Overall I certainly recommend it though especially if you are bored with your library and looking for new games; it will give you many hours of entertainment. 7.5/10 for lacking categories.

This game has been out for years now and it still has so many issues. This game also crashes for me at least 5 to 6 times within a hour or two of playing. Other than that this game is amazing.

1. Development process
First I want to say that I'm not a fan of preorders or early access. I bought this game after BI released the 2015 roadmap because i thought it will be more or less accurate (+/- one year). Now its 2017 and only a fraction of the mentioned features is in the public version of dayz and most of what is in, is buggy or just a unfinished prototype.
Some people say that the roadmap was written before large technology changes to DayZ were fully realised. The only thing is that the technological changes are part of the roadmap and BI at that time was already aware of what needs to be changed. At this point the scope was clear. As a professional developer you must know that the huge amount of work required to implment all the features and engine changes takes longer than one year.
In this article (
the author mentions the most common factors why software projects fail:
- Unrealistic or unarticulated project goals
- Inaccurate estimates of needed resources
- Badly defined system requirements
- Poor reporting of the project's status
- Unmanaged risks
- Poor communication among customers, developers, and users
- Use of immature technology
- Inability to handle the project's complexity
- Sloppy development practices
- Poor project management
- Stakeholder politics
- Commercial pressures
I think a lot of these points apply to DayZ but i am sure that DayZ will not fail. It will take much longer than expected and we dont know how much of the work is already done. This makes it impossible to estimate when this game will be finished.
2. Game
I have played a lot of DayZ and this game can be awesome. The adrenaline and tension in a fire fight is unique. The map is huge and there are a lot of places to explore. The landscape also looks realy good on high settings.
One the other side, there is not realy much to do in this game and after some hours, you will know almost all important towns, militäry bases or landmarks. It also takes a lot of time to find good gear and loosing it because of a stupid bug can be frustrating. At the moment this game has a lot of bugs and the developers will not fix them until beta.
3. Conclusion
The current state of the game is bad bacause of the bugs, the gameplay and the not existing mid or end game content. The game has now been in development for about 4 years and the visible progress is disappointing. Predictiong when this will change is impossible but i expect at least two more years until release. Therefore, I currently do not recommend to buy DayZ.
TL;DR
The current state of the game is bad and it is unknown when this will change.
NOT RECOMMENDED

ABOUT THIS GAME
Welcome to the world of DayZ, hit by a new and presently unknown infection which has wiped out most of the world's population. You are one of the few that have survived and now you must search this new wasteland in order to fight for your life against what is left of the indigenous population now infected with the disease. Go solo, team up with friends or take on the world, as you choose your path in this brutal and chilling landscape using whatever means you stumble upon to survive.
This is DayZ, this is your story.
DayZ is a gritty, authentic, open-world survival horror hybrid-MMO game, in which players follow a single goal: to survive in the harsh post-apocalyptic landscape as long as they can. Players can experience powerful events and emotions arising from the ever-evolving emergent gameplay. There are no superficial tips, waypoints, built in tutorials or help given to players. Every decision matters, there are no save games, no extra lives, every mistake can be lethal. If you fail, you lose everything and you need to play again from the beginning with nothing but your wits, and your two hands. Fight the hostile environment, where every other player can be friend or foe and nothing can be taken for granted.
KEY FEATURES IN ALPHA
Chernarus - 230 sq. km chunk of post soviet state, featuring deep forests, cities, villages, abandoned military bases, and more..
Up to 50 players per server - Rich server / client architecture developed from scratch.
Persistent player profile - Key player data is persistent across all servers.
Inventory – Combine various clothing items, equipment and carry all of the items that you will need to survive the harsh new environment in the open and intuitive inventory system developed to answer the needs of crafting and character customization.
Crafting - In the apocalyptic world of DayZ, resources are sparse and every useful bit should be utilized. Items or equipment can be improved, turned into something else or fixed using the new crafting mechanisms.
Weapon customization – Use customizable firearms with authentic ballistics and weapon characteristics as well as melee weapons to protect yourself against all the dangers a survivor may face.
Customizable clothing – Customize your survivor with a multitude of new clothing items that can be scavenged from the remnants of civilization, which provide various degree of protection against the elements, infected, and other survivors.

Right, so after having played around 200 hours on xbox, and nearing 50 on pc, I feel it's about time to write a review of some sort about Borderlands 2, I will leave a tl;dr so feel free to just skip to that for a sum up :D
Also as a side note, Im not going to put this into detail, simply because I don't need to, but this game is SO much better played with friends or just general co-op.
I'm not going to delve too much into the story, as personally that isn't what I play Borderlands for, although the story in 2 is MUCH clearer and just generally better than the first. The main antagonist "Handsome Jack" is one of the best antagonists I've come across yet, in that he takes an active role from the start to be an annoyance, but borderlands being borderlands, he does it in a more jokey and "fun" way to start off.
There are 4 characters (6 with dlc) But I'll just be talking about the main 4 as I havent spent time playing the other 2.
The Commando, a class who utilizes auto sentrys in a variety of ways, from sticking them to walls and ceilings, to simply using them as a guard with a shield.
The Siren, my personal favourite, her skill tree can be built around two very different aspects, either an elemental damage beast, or the borderlands equivelent of a healer. The sirens skill "phaselock" targets a single enemy and raises them into what can just simply be put as a bubble, locking them in place for the duration and giving different bonuses depending on the skill trees followed and the progression. I personally prefer to go elemental because.. Well.. Who doesn't like to see♥♥♥♥♥♥explode?
The gunzerker. Now I haven't played too much of the Gunzerker so I don't know a whole lot about his skill trees, but his skill allows him to equip 2 guns at the same time in an akimbo manner, and that's pretty much all I really know, well useful right?
The assassin, Now this class is a TON of fun to play, the whole idea of just popping a decoy, going invisible, and appearing behind a target to deliver a killing blow, is just.. well.. fun! Later in his skill tree you can choose to re-cloak aftet you kill, re-deploying a new decoy and carrying on your little rampage. This class is fairly squishy however, which can lead to some issues if getting caught in a bad place.
Now the gameplay, I've heard alot of people say the start is boring, which, as a huge fan of the game I can agree, until you kill the first boss and leave the Southern Shelf, it is pretty dull, this isn't a huge portion of time, and getting through it to experience more of the game is definitely worth while in my opinion. The game holds a pretty large number of side quests to spend time on but ARE completely optional, and the main game itself is fairly long, a time frame? Well I beat every side quest every playthrough as I'm a maajor completionist, so I don't have one. I highly recommend looking into the game of the year edition, as it just gives.. well.. More, from level cap increases to whole other stories to follow, its well worth the purchase.
It feels great to play on both mouse/keyboard and controller, although I have had some issues on the inventory with mouse, but honestly it's probably me derpin' out.
Another thing I personally love about this game, LOOT, who doesn't love consistent loot? From ammo to cash to guns, the game makes sure to shove loot in your face at every given opportunity, which for me personally, is a great thing, one issue however is other people TAKING the loot you actually need/want CAN get frustrating, and that WILL happen.
That's about all I have to say on the game, I could write for hours about it buuut ohwell, this being my first review, some feedback would be helpful if you've read this far :D I hope to write more so any improvements I could make would be great!
Tl;dr: LOOT LOOT AND LOOT, an incredible game better in co-op,  with 4(6) very different characters to give a go, and an antagonist that may just be my favourite from any game I've played in the past 14 years. Would I recommend? Ofcourse I would!

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is the perfect driving simulator for both the casual non-hardcore sim fan and simulator fans in general. This game offers both nice driving mechanics, basic company/economic management, and a lot of exploring and custimization!

VTC or Virtual Trucking Companies are also really cool. You can create your own online company with your friends or strangers and keep track on earnings and milage, and compare to others.
And then last but not least, the MP mod. This mod gives us all the oppertunity to play together on this huge map and have real time convoys. It can get a little messy sometimes if you meet rammers, but overall, all the players you meet are friendly and won't crash into you.
If you don't already own this game, it's pretty much the first thing you should buy. Even if you don't like this type of game, it's a game all gamers should have in their libery. This is a Indie game that made it BIG time.

1. Development process
First I want to say that I'm not a fan of preorders or early access. I bought this game after BI released the 2015 roadmap because i thought it will be more or less accurate (+/- one year). Now its 2017 and only a fraction of the mentioned features is in the public version of dayz and most of what is in, is buggy or just a unfinished prototype.
Some people say that the roadmap was written before large technology changes to DayZ were fully realised. The only thing is that the technological changes are part of the roadmap and BI at that time was already aware of what needs to be changed. At this point the scope was clear. As a professional developer you must know that the huge amount of work required to implment all the features and engine changes takes longer than one year.
In this article (
the author mentions the most common factors why software projects fail:
- Unrealistic or unarticulated project goals
- Inaccurate estimates of needed resources
- Badly defined system requirements
- Poor reporting of the project's status
- Unmanaged risks
- Poor communication among customers, developers, and users
- Use of immature technology
- Inability to handle the project's complexity
- Sloppy development practices
- Poor project management
- Stakeholder politics
- Commercial pressures
I think a lot of these points apply to DayZ but i am sure that DayZ will not fail. It will take much longer than expected and we dont know how much of the work is already done. This makes it impossible to estimate when this game will be finished.
2. Game
I have played a lot of DayZ and this game can be awesome. The adrenaline and tension in a fire fight is unique. The map is huge and there are a lot of places to explore. The landscape also looks realy good on high settings.
One the other side, there is not realy much to do in this game and after some hours, you will know almost all important towns, militäry bases or landmarks. It also takes a lot of time to find good gear and loosing it because of a stupid bug can be frustrating. At the moment this game has a lot of bugs and the developers will not fix them until beta.
3. Conclusion
The current state of the game is bad bacause of the bugs, the gameplay and the not existing mid or end game content. The game has now been in development for about 4 years and the visible progress is disappointing. Predictiong when this will change is impossible but i expect at least two more years until release. Therefore, I currently do not recommend to buy DayZ.
TL;DR
The current state of the game is bad and it is unknown when this will change.

There are a lot of First Person Shooters out there, and alot are unoriginal and lack style. Borderlands 2, however, re-invents the FPS genre in a new, exciting and comical way.
First off, Borderlands 2's world and map design is like no other. The mysteriously beautiful planet of Pandora looks even more stunning than Borderlands 1, and everything from the way enemies behave, to the performance of the vehicles, makes the presentation of Borderlands 2 one of the most original shooters to date. The strory has you play as one of four Vault Hunters: Axton, the Commando; Maya, the Siren; Salvador, the dual-wielding Gunzerker; or Zer0, the Assassin. As a Vault Hunter, you must compete with Handsome Jack, president of Hyperion, for the alluring ore Eridium.
Borderlands 2 is all about loot. There are containers in every corner, filled with all sorts of goodies like weapons and ammunition. Also, there are a TON of guns in Borderlands 2. Guns are found everywhere. You'll often find them after killing an enemy, opening chests or in huge crates. I have spent so long comparing the stats of these against others, and finding that perfect SMG really scratches that itch.
Although Borderlands 2's gameplay is entertaining, addictive and insane, I do feel that the objectives were often repetitive. Being requested by people to "Go here, kill this bad guy, come back, earn a reward." just gets boring after a while, and was inevitably my biggest problem with the game. What I found enjoyable just seemed to get monotonous.
Overall, there are so many things that are amazing in Borderlands 2. From the hilarious and creative story, to wonderfully presented graphics and game mechanics, it's hard to find imperfections in the game. But, here and there, missions can feel more like a chore than having fun.

So let me start this review with how great this game is. You start naked on a beach, with just a stone and a torch and end up in a metal armour outfit with a pump shotgun and grenades, with everything you have coming from stuff you crafted yourself. The progression from what you have to the next level up feels natural, and appropriate. It is a progressive slide for your armour, weapons and items. Even though the craft is unrealistic, it is kind of intuitive of what you need and where you get your resources from. Also the low and mid level resources required for crafting are easy to obtain, if you are looking for it.
Its not just the concept that is good, I notice that the developers are still active on this project. Not just patches, game balancing or new skins that are coming out, but huge improvements are still being made. New items are still being added and major game mechanics are still shifting. Unlike some other survival games I've played (or observed) this one feels like it still moving toward an actual release date.
Another thing I like, but I assume most people don't, is that other players are the biggest enemy. I remember having to crouch at night walking around rad town, carefully looking and listening to make sure that no one around when I bust open barrels. I'm sort of feeling my way around because I have no light source on me, otherwise I would be spotted and killed instantly. I can't complain about the AI because every enemy in the game (expect bears and wolves) are controlled by other players. If you can get your head around the fact that everyone who you aren't playing with is an enemy then you game will progress much better.
There are also a lot of plug-ins for this game that really add to it, but I won't go into detail about those.
But this game has a few big problems. The first and worst is that the game punishes you for not being online. I assume anyone who has played this game long enough feels the frustration of having your base raided when they were offline. Sure it leads to some clever base designs, but there is not real security in this game. It is a good mechanic for Rust to keep people playing constantly, but you are going to have to leave the game to sleep, eat, work, and hopefully have a life, then (if you're invested in this game) it will be stressful. I have about 20 hours played upon writing this and most of those was within a two week span where I didn't have anything planned and had lots of free time. I don't really get those much, but if I do, that will be the next opportunity I could play this game again.
Another thing I don't like is being quick and early is the most important part of this game. Spears aren't much help against arrows, and arrows aren't great against bullets. Often people with late crafting items will just wander and kill everyone they see. You progress at a decent rate and the time it takes to get to the end game crafting I find is perfect. But if you meet someone who has progressed further then you, then you may have to start from the beginning again or at the very least lose your favourite stuff, which is annoying.
Finally starting a new game of Rust is akin to rolling dice until you get a result you like. You spawn and then die, and this repeats until you can get a base with a lock and sleeping bag setup. There probably should be a way to expedite this. The end result is eventually the same and the people who kill you don't get much. It is pretty much just wasting time until you can start the game.
Like I said, it is a great game, I just wouldn't recommend it to my friends in its current state.

Undertale is a suprisingly detailed and story driven isometric 8bit RPG that took over game of the year lists out of nowhere in 2015. It somewhat uniquely impliments traditional turned based RPG mechanics with bullet hell combat. While the story can sometimes be very predictable, and is often overhyped by zealous spoil happy fans, it is definitely compelling with its branching, multiple endings and sometimes cryptic lore and eastereggs.
This is a dialogue laden game similar to the early JRPGs that it is heavily based on. It is heavily influenced and often compared to the Mother series (Earthbound) for this reason as well as some of its tongue in cheek and self aware humor.
I recomend the game since I enjoy a good story and found the combat challenging and rewarding. The soundtrack is very good and also very reminescent of late 80s early 90s 8 and 16 bit era RPGs and platformers. With that said, realize that this style is not for everyone, and that this is a very hyped game by a broad cult following of devotees. If the type of game described does not appeal to you, attempting to force yourself to enjoy it will not be successful.
Otherwise, play it, and if no one has spoiled the story or some of the  more ambiguous game mechanics for you, try to keep it that way.

Mad Max is an open world third-person action-adventure game that has elements of both a PRG and a Shooter.  I have been watching this game for a long time and of course I pre-ordered it as soon as it was available but I have to admit I was a little worried after Batman: Arkam Knight.  I can honestly say that so far in I am really liking this game.
Mad Max plays great. The controls work well with the exception in the menu where I was forced to use my controller to log into WB.  Now this may only be an issue because I have a controller plugged in, but it was still an issue all the same and I should not have to unplug a controller to play a game with a keyboard and mouse.
They have done an awesome job optimizing this game.  I did have some lighting issues with flickering but after downloading the new Nvidia driver 355.82 it was flicker free.  With Vsync off I am getting well over 200 fps with every setting maxed out.  The graphics are Next Gen and look great.
I really like the story, but then who doesn't like Mad Max. It is the familiar post appopolyptic story where Max has lost everything and revenge.  The open world game with side quests are great.  The environment is easy to immerse yourself in.  I just wish you had choices and consequences.
The game is bug free for the most part although some people have experienced issues with the map, I have found an entirely different issue.  My bug relates to an earlier quest I completed in the first zone unlocking ammo stations in the last two zones.  Unfortunately my ammo stations are not unlocked and of course there is no way to replay the quest without replaying the game so I am unable to collect an achievement I earned unless I replay the game to do so.  The game has been patched several times but my issue remains.  After 75hrs in this game, I still enjoy running around in game, racing, and destroying cars but I am not too excited at the prospect of finding all of the loot objects again.
The game delivers in almost every aspect and I recommend it without any hesitation.

As a big fan of the George Miller movies, as well as games by Avalanche Studios, I felt that a pre-order for this was certainly a good idea. I was right. We return to the Australian wasteland when we join the road warrior on a mission to get his car back that was stolen by the warlord, Scabrous Scrotus.
One thing that stands out to me is how the design of the game world definitely looks Miller-esque. You can easily look at the game screenshots and say "yep, that's a Mad Max game alright". Controls are fluid and responsive, combat is brutal and every punch feels rewarding (is a lot like Shadow of Mordor or Batman games). The car controls take getting used to but will improve over time as you aim to improve it through a detailed and complex upgrades system, meaning you build the car you want to.
Performance is stellar, running at 60 frames per second at 1080p, at least on my rig (i5-4570, GTX 970 with 8GB RAM). This is definitely not another Arkham Knight situation!

A good port to Linux.  It's not unusual for a new port to have various issues--or for a so-so port to keep certain issues for particular, unusual use cases.  That's not the case with Borderlands 2--it's good right out of the gate.
Let's talk about the problems this port doesn't have:
Keep in mind that this is on the dreaded fglrx (buy Nvidia, everybody)--if it works on my card, it'll work on yours.  I even have a friend who's got it working on Intel graphics--and he's got pre-HD2000 Intel graphics.  Or was it on the (Radeon HD) 4830+original A64 rig he's got?  Point is, he made it run on a toaster.  If you're worried that you haven't got enough rig to run Borderlands 2, but you can comfortably eat the cost of the game--buy it and try it out, maybe you've got a chance.
Anyway, bravo to Aspyr for a solid port; they really didn't phone it in here.
As for the game itself--it's Borderlands.  Expect what you've been told--Diablo II with guns.  If you enjoyed Diablo II but struggled with the realization that you were basically just clicking on monster-shaped icons for hours, then this game is for you.  For people who played the first Borderlands:  it's a bit faster paced in combat, the loot is familiar with enough of a changeup to feel fresh, the menus are a bit streamlined, and I've hit level 9 but am yet to see a healing shield--if they're still in, the game is definitely stingier with them.  It's geared even more strongly towards the multiplayer now, so play it with someone if at all possible--if not:  there's still something here for you, but you'll definitely feel the lack of something important.  I recommend it even if you mean to only play it in single player, though:  it's a pretty fun game.
