I have always been a lover of post-apocalyptic themes in both games and movies, and I was extremely excited to learn about the Mad Max open-world adventure game - especially after being a fan of the entire Mad Max franchise (Road Warrior is second only to Fury Road for me). The gameplay looked a lot like the styles seen in games like Assassin's Creed (AC) and Batman Arkham, series that I absolutely adore. I was and continue to be thoroughly satisfied with my gameplay experience.
If you enjoy open-world action and adventure, RPG elements, intense car combat, post-apocalyptic themes, gritty visuals, and the Mad Max franchise (especially Fury Road), then you will love this game.
For full disclosure: my top game of 2014 was Middle: Earth-Shadow of Mordor (SoM), and while I will readily agree that there are much better quality and more in-depth alternatives available, I found SoM to be the most fun; it truly captured the essence of why I enjoy playing games and losing myself to immersion. Mad Max is very similar to SoM for me, in terms of fun factor and enjoyment. I completely understand that people may not like games like this - finding them too repetitive - however, I will do my best to provide an accurate and fair representation of the gameplay you can expect to encounter if you buy and play this title; but please keep in mind that I may still be biased in my review. I would also like to quickly point out that this game is NOT a simple copy-and-paste (or "reskin") of games that I have previously mentioned - such games are definitely formulaic, yes, but they are not direct copy-and-paste titles.
The aesthetics are fantastic - the amount of detail in the environment, character/car models, and special effects is extremely high. Optimization is amazing (so long as your drivers are up-to-date), ensuring that you are receiving the best possible performance while you play (admittedly, I was a bit worried about this PC port following the poor launch of Arkham Knight). The special effects are beautiful - car explosions are massive and bright with pretty fire (moving close to fires will cause the world color to take on a more orange hue), the lighting and shadow effects are realistic (the glare off of your car lights at night time is a sight to behold), and storms are majestic (I implore you to brave a journey into the heart of one once you have a stronger Magnum Opus). The music and sounds are great, however, do not expect to hear any of the tracks from Fury Road (sorry, no "Escape" or "Brothers in Arms" playing while you fight off enemies); the game's soundtrack is still very good. Following the lore established by Mad Max: Fury Road, the story is interesting and engaging - although nothing too special (much like Shadow of Mordor); I will admit that a few times I have skipped cutscenes and/or ignored dialogue.
Controls are not difficult to familiarize yourself with, especially if you use a gamepad and have played game series like Assassin's Creed or Batman Arkham. Unfortunately, you cannot rebind the controller keys, and you can only remap a limited amount of actions on the keyboard - this is definitely something that could have been improved for player convenience. As a result, you cannot easily call up the keyboard controls - in fact, I had to check the discussion boards to find out how to bring up the full map (on the keyboard, it is "Tab;" I thought it was "M"). There is a series of tutorial missions that will quickly get you accustomed to the gameplay. The learning curve is minimal to moderate depending on your experience with open-world adventure games in this vein. You will encounter difficulty with mid-to-late-game main missions if you are not exploring and completing side objectives - this is the "grinding" aspect of the game that helps you build experience and obtain upgrades. This element is seen in other games like the Assassin's Creed and Batman Arkham series (as well as Shadow of Mordor), so if you do not enjoy that style of gameplay, you will probably be dissatisfied with Mad Max. The "boss" fights are fairly easy, especially if you are keeping up with your character/car upgrades.
Gameplay consists of you roaming the wasteland, with your final destination requiring you to first stop by Gastown. The road to Gastown is a brutal, dangerous one, so you will have to first gain more experience and upgrades in neighbouring territories, which are each ruled by leaders that you will meet and help. Each territory is split into smaller pieces and littered with different landmarks like enemy outposts/camps, scavenging areas (for delicious loot), and race meets. Balloons in each territory can be taken into the air to mark important areas, as well as reveal the surrounding land in your map (this is similar to climbing the tall vantage points in SoM and AC). If you do activities that directly affect the enemy - like liberating camps or disarming minefields (the latter being extremely boring) - it will reduce the "threat" level of the entire territory. Reducing threat ratings will result in decreased enemy patrol frequency and presence, making your travel time through the area quicker and less painful.
Main missions progress the story, usually unlocking more of the map and allowing you to obtain better upgrades for your Magnum Opus (your beloved car). In contrast, upgrades for Max are tied to your "Legend" rank, which is increased by doing mostly anything - like destroying enemy vehicles with your shotgun, achieving high combo chains, or killing x amount of enemies; there is no actual "experience points" system. Whenever you complete these "challenges," you will obtain a token that can be exchanged for an ability point, thus allowing you to level up. Each Legend rank (the top being "Road Warrior") is composed of multiple sub-levels, and obtaining a new one will grant you more upgrades for Max like appearance, ammo capacity, and physical damage (all accompanied by nice aesthetics).
Combat is extremely fluid and responsive, albeit quite easy (as is the case in most of Warner Brothers' open-world action-adventure games) because of the counter prompt that appears over the heads of enemies about to attack. Something that balances the ease of countering/parrying is how the button input works - you cannot simply mash the attack button because each attack is a commitment, so if you are already doing an attack animation, countering will probably not work (encouraging you to be patient with your commands). Furthermore, countering right before an attack lands will execute a "perfect parry," which will help build your combos faster and even allow you to disarm an opponent's weapon (further enhanced by Max's ability upgrades).
ABSOLUTELY RECOMMEND!
Cheers,

So let me start this review with how great this game is. You start naked on a beach, with just a stone and a torch and end up in a metal armour outfit with a pump shotgun and grenades, with everything you have coming from stuff you crafted yourself. The progression from what you have to the next level up feels natural, and appropriate. It is a progressive slide for your armour, weapons and items. Even though the craft is unrealistic, it is kind of intuitive of what you need and where you get your resources from. Also the low and mid level resources required for crafting are easy to obtain, if you are looking for it.
Its not just the concept that is good, I notice that the developers are still active on this project. Not just patches, game balancing or new skins that are coming out, but huge improvements are still being made. New items are still being added and major game mechanics are still shifting. Unlike some other survival games I've played (or observed) this one feels like it still moving toward an actual release date.
Another thing I like, but I assume most people don't, is that other players are the biggest enemy. I remember having to crouch at night walking around rad town, carefully looking and listening to make sure that no one around when I bust open barrels. I'm sort of feeling my way around because I have no light source on me, otherwise I would be spotted and killed instantly. I can't complain about the AI because every enemy in the game (expect bears and wolves) are controlled by other players. If you can get your head around the fact that everyone who you aren't playing with is an enemy then you game will progress much better.
There are also a lot of plug-ins for this game that really add to it, but I won't go into detail about those.
But this game has a few big problems. The first and worst is that the game punishes you for not being online. I assume anyone who has played this game long enough feels the frustration of having your base raided when they were offline. Sure it leads to some clever base designs, but there is not real security in this game. It is a good mechanic for Rust to keep people playing constantly, but you are going to have to leave the game to sleep, eat, work, and hopefully have a life, then (if you're invested in this game) it will be stressful. I have about 20 hours played upon writing this and most of those was within a two week span where I didn't have anything planned and had lots of free time. I don't really get those much, but if I do, that will be the next opportunity I could play this game again.
Another thing I don't like is being quick and early is the most important part of this game. Spears aren't much help against arrows, and arrows aren't great against bullets. Often people with late crafting items will just wander and kill everyone they see. You progress at a decent rate and the time it takes to get to the end game crafting I find is perfect. But if you meet someone who has progressed further then you, then you may have to start from the beginning again or at the very least lose your favourite stuff, which is annoying.
Finally starting a new game of Rust is akin to rolling dice until you get a result you like. You spawn and then die, and this repeats until you can get a base with a lock and sleeping bag setup. There probably should be a way to expedite this. The end result is eventually the same and the people who kill you don't get much. It is pretty much just wasting time until you can start the game.
Like I said, it is a great game, I just wouldn't recommend it to my friends in its current state.

there are barely any physics objects anywhere you go, given you never really fight against 6+ enemies (not as far as I went at least).
and what the heck is wrong with the keyboard controls??? How did you mess them up so bad? they need fixing.
EXAMPLES:
Left control to jump?
Space to roll?
E FOR NEARLY EVERYTHING (and most of the time it needs to be a long press, I swear my finger starts hurting after a while and this is the only game that has ever managed that)
middle mouse to QUICK shoot is fine BUT when aiming with RM why the heck is shoot not switched to LM instead of MM?
Basic attack is on mouse roll? wtf?
You can fix some of those but as soon as you change a keybinding the controls kinda break because the keybindings are really weirdly assigned. Like for exmaple there are situations when when you are already pressing on a certain a key, you can presss another one to do another action entirely, now this is fine except it isnt very well defined in the keybindings section.
You could also add that the tutorial is broken on keyboard as the keys it asks you to press for certain actions are wrong. (F1s everywhere when it isnt used at all)
So, clarification here, in fcat the tutorial breaks when you try to change keybindings -.-'
Okay the more I play this, the more I am dissapointed.
Concerning the driving, I find it very sluggish and I find the car unresponsive. Maybe because I use a keyboard, but I dont like using controllers in my video games. So yeah I dont know whats wrong with that. You could argue that its because my car isnt upgraded or whatever but I mean thats not how it should work, the basic car should feel right and then the upgraded ones should maybe turn faster, have better drift or go faster (and of course, have more weapons, armor and stuff). They shouldn't give you a crap car to begin with and expect you to stay with it till you upgrade.
In combat, a lot of times you will click on the parry button but no parry will be done. so it needs fixing too.
Story wise, dont have much to say at the moment, cause the story is pretty much non existent.
No I mean, like, really unexistent. There is NO story in this game whatsoever.
All this game is is a bunch of map completion stuff. and yes, I think it gets boring very fast, very easily.
I dont feel any attachment to max or chumbucket, they are both crap characters because there is no character devleopment.
All in all, I was expecting a lot more from Mad Max.
For the moment I'd give it a 6/10
Play it if you want. it works. but that doesnt make it a great game.
so for me if its 6 or under, its not recommended. A LOT of people dont understand why Id give it a 6 and not recommend it. well thats because its not because a game is good or bad that youll recommend it. I could have given a game a 7 and not recommend it. It's passable. its average. Would you recommend a game you consider average? no. that dont mean its a bad game. I dont even think it's a bad game, I just think it lacks a few things to make it interesting enough to justify a purchase. You cant make a game on car progression alone, and if anything I find this game really boring. This game actually really reminds me of shadow of mordor, which I didnt like either. both had an open world and both had no story at all (well thats a bit unfair to SoM, even THAT had more story than Mad Max). It's not that hard to make a good engaging story is it?

game play::(KB and mouse)
controls have a obvious lag to them but it seem this is by design( adds realisim?), similar to any of the batman games.
combat on ground:: exactly like the newer batmans to a "T", button smash LMB and parry with RMB or roll with space bar, use "e" as a modifer, hold RMB to aim LMB to fire gun while in aim mode. can pick up melee weapons to augment your dmg. cues are on top of targets to help you with parry and when to use modifier button. move mouse to target enemies.
car combat::: actually quiet good, mouse wheel to cycle weapons, wasd movment with mouse as camera, RMB to target, LMB to fire, middle button to quick fire, you have an NPC with you in car that acts as a turret basically with a harpoon(at the moment, can be upgraded). can ram other cars, gates, objects and NPCs

1 air ballons open up map (far cry radio tower style),
2 rigs "free area style mechanic" and friendlies move into rigs once you take over (far cry outposts).
3 Water heals you, you find water in rain collectors and pipes  all over game space.
4 food heals you, find it in world and eat it no hordeing of food.

7 ammo is scarce use it wisely
8 one knife at a time when you use finishing move with knife you loose knife

TL;DR ::: game runs smooth max@4k on win10 pro 64bit, MAD MAX = farcry4+borderlands but more car action less ground. GFX @ max 4k look like elder scrolls online, better than GTA 5 but worse than witcher 3 ( for those who havent played ESO)
ok so only a few hrs in, going to bullet point this
my pc::
AMD FX-8350 oced to 4.8 ghz, 16gb ram, 64 bit win 10 pro, nvidia 980ti g1 gaming oc'ed 1380
resolution: 4k
game runs smooth with everything maxed except AA is off (4k no need)
game play::(KB and mouse)
controls have a obvious lag to them but it seem this is by design( adds realisim?), similar to any of the batman games.
combat on ground:: exactly like the newer batmans to a "T", button smash LMB and parry with RMB or roll with space bar, use "e" as a modifer, hold RMB to aim LMB to fire gun while in aim mode. can pick up melee weapons to augment your dmg. cues are on top of targets to help you with parry and when to use modifier button. move mouse to target enemies.
car combat::: actually quiet good, mouse wheel to cycle weapons, wasd movment with mouse as camera, RMB to target, LMB to fire, middle button to quick fire, you have an NPC with you in car that acts as a turret basically with a harpoon(at the moment, can be upgraded). can ram other cars, gates, objects and NPCs
MAP:: No lie it is fully open ended, the main game area has roads and obvious POI's. TAB is your friend on PC pulls up map, there are air ballons you find that allow you to remove "fog" from map areas just like radio towers in far cry
Over all game mechanics::
1 air ballons open up map (far cry radio tower style),
2 rigs "free area style mechanic" and friendlies move into rigs once you take over (far cry outposts).
3 Water heals you, you find water in rain collectors and pipes  all over game space.
4 food heals you, find it in world and eat it no hordeing of food.
5 fuel makes car go, find fuel in world, win races, when you win a race starting point becomes an unlimited fuel depot, some random spawn points also have full fuel that respawns, fuel is found at rigs (filled fuel once drove around for 1.5 hrs)
6 npc that rides with you auto fixes your car, just stop car and hit "E" or get out of car and he will fix it
7 ammo is scarce use it wisely
8 one knife at a time when you use finishing move with knife you loose knife
9 story mode guides you through the game, but you can do anything at any time except another story line mission while on other missions, keep in mid that you may fail a mission due to time or leaving an area.

First of, this game is just beautiful! I could go on about the sound quality, graphics, mechanics, interaction with the world and everything else but you can’t appreciated it unless seen by yourself.

On the other hand if you expect fast finds, lots of shooting, overpower in later game, pay to win or just fast pace game stile than this is not for you
There is no HUD mini map, compass, health bar, stamina bar there is nothing except indication of hungry, thirsty, cold, not feeling well ect...
You will spawn somewhere and you won’t know where you are for a long time unless you are one of those hard core players that have 1000h or more...

Undertale is a game about a small child of ambiguous gender that likes to avoid fights by flirting their way out of danger and petting all the good little puppies, or a nutcase that greets everyone with a friendly punch in the liver and repurposes good little puppies as something that PETA will no doubt get their knickers in a twist over. Your choice. Basically there are three ways to play the game, two of which are correct, and which you choose will inevitably reflect something of your own personality. Are you a kind hearted individual that wants everyone to get along and be friends, or do you play military shooters to get a stiffy? In technical terms if you're the kind of person who wants me to start making sense sometime soon, there's the Genocide Route, the Neutral Route, and the Pacifist Route. Self explanatory really, though you have to complete a no kill Neutral Route to get a Pacifist Route, so while the game does employ a very well thought out system to ensure your choices in the game actually matter the truth of the matter is that if you go on a Genocide Route and spare anyone or a no kill Neutral Route and kill one monster then you may as well start the entire game over cause you just effed up. Yes, there are many different endings to the neutral route depending on what key characters are still alive when you finish the game, but the simple fact of the matter is anything other than total Genocide or complete Pacifism is basically a nonstandard game over since it doesn't give any true closure.
Combat mechanics? Well, let's just say I feel that the combat mechanics are genuinely the strongest point to this game. This is because when someone is trying to hurt you in this game you are actually expected to put your best effort into
getting hit. When enemies attack you move your "Soul" which is in the shape of a ❤️ (although it may occasionally be a 💙, a 💚, a 💜, or a 💛) on a board using the arrow keys, and try to avoid a variety of bullets of all shapes and sizes. Every enemy has a unique type of attack based on their appearance and personality, such as falling snowflakes and giant bulging biceps that move from the bottom to the top of the bullet board, and when multiple enemies are present they all attack you at once, resulting in combination attacks that are far more difficult to avoid and make you think that these guys just
to have rehearsed this at some point, because no freaking way two random strangers can team up for a fight and have choreography like that nailed down solely on instinct. As far as your attacks go (that is if your attack button doesn't turn black and fall off from neglect) a white bar slides across the screen and you have to hit the select button (Z) to try to stop this as close to the center as possible for maximum damage. Is it truly that simple? For the first and last weapon in the game, yes. Every other weapon aside from that has some kind of attack gimmick that you have to get used to, so every time you get a new weapon things feel a bit more interesting. This variety in enemy attacks and your own attacks manages to keep combat from becoming boring and repetitive as the game goes on, and is truly praiseworthy. If you're one of those people that enjoys frolicking through fields of flowers instead of flames, to spare enemies you use the Act menu and select from a series of options specific to that enemy actions that will pacify it somehow, such as choosing not to pick on the weird eyeball thing that asks you not to pick on him.
As far as the two different Routes go, you're probably thinking this is shaping up to be one of those horrible morality systems that basically ask you two choose between helping a little girl get her cat out of a tree or setting the tree on fire and stealing the little girl's candy just to add insult to injury. Not true. While this game does have you choose between two very basic options like your standard morality system the story and difficulty of the game is actually very different depending upon your choice. This largely hinges on the choice you have to make: kill no one, or kill everyone. Assuming your mother didn't substitute paint thinner for milk can probably figure out the immediate consequence of not killing anyone in an RPG: no EXP, and no base stat boosts, including HP for the entire game. Knowing this, one might naturally think that a Pacifist Route is considerably harder than a Genocide Route. For the most part this is true. I personally found during the first area of the game that killing all enemies was actually harder than sparing them simply due to the fact that for the stronger enemies of the area it took more turns to kill them than it did to pacify and spare them. Who knew becoming a successful child murderer would be so difficult? That is, a child that murders, not a person that murders children. That's terrible for a completely different reason. That being said, once I had a decent amount of EXP under my belt and a new weapon and armor set fights became easier to win, save for two very specific boss fights, and if you don't already know who I'm talking about I must congratulate you with all the sincerity I can muster for managing to avoid those spoilers for this long. Simply put the final boss of the Genocide Route reduced me from a full 92 HP to 1 on his first attack, and I knew exactly what was coming. Of course if you're anything like me you'll just interpret that as a challenge.
The story? Well, on a Genocide Route there isn't much of one, largely due to the fact that once you start successfully purging the immediate area of life everyone decides that perhaps getting as far away from the insane knife wielding sociopath as possible is the best course of action if they want to survive. You want the story of a Genocide Route? Well here you go: you are an insane child that thinks are monsters are unusually stubborn piñatas. Go nuts.
For the rest of you role playing a sane human being, the story is that you are a child that decided to go mountain climbing by themselves—normal kid stuff—and awaken after falling down a hole into a cavern where the entire monster population of the world was sealed away a long, long time ago by♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥I mean humans. You land safely on a flower bed (nature's bouncy castle), and are greeted by a friendly little talking flower and a milf who takes the hand holding tutorial part of the game a little too literally. I shall now highlight specific points of the game out of context, and in no particular order. As you progress through the game you will:
I recommend both paths of the game, but I understand how a lot of people are too chicken to commit Genocide themselves and watch it on YouTube. Just know the Flower will call you out on it.
In conclusion: Undertale has in common with Portal the fact that they are both very good games with unique gameplay mechanics and a well crafted narrative that are overhyped and oversaturated by their respective fans. I do recommend this game, but temper your expectations. Nothing ruins a game like fans teaching you to expect finding the Holy Grail only to find a silver chalice.

Before I had this game, I wasn't completely sure what the fuss was about. I had played UK Truck Simulator and heard that Euro Truck Simulator 1 wasn't even worth looking into, so when this game came out, I wasn't too enthusiastic about it. Then, the internet suddenly burst with so much positive reviews that I had to take a look. So, I bought the game, sat down and played for about 4 hours. And to this day, those were the best 4 hours of my life.
Do I recommend this game? Yes. It doesn't matter if you're 10 or 50 years old. Anyone and everyone can play this game, making it either super easy, or one of the hardest challenges ever. It's a brilliant game to lose yourself in.
Pros:
- Wide range of trucks to buy
- VERY big map
- Real sense of driving a truck
- Oculus Rift AND Logitech G27 support (feels like you're in the truck!)
- Large amount of mod support
- Multiplayer modification (Very nice to play with others, not just AI)
Cons:
- Once company is properly set up, can be very easy to make money and 'beat' the game
- Can become boring after a long drive
Final verdict: Seriously recommended
Final Score: 9.5/10

So back when I was just in my teens I watched 3 random youtubers play this new game I had never heard of before. The game was called "Arma II" and they said it was a "mod" called "DayZ". I didnt know what a mod was, what Arma meant, or why this game was called DayZ. But having watched such shows as "Survivorman" and "Man Vs Wild" I instantly fell in love with the game. It was exactly what I was looking for, something for the hardcore survivor geeks. I quickly learned that not only was this a survivor type game but also a zombie game, I didnt really care for zombies but I saw that it added a certain flavor to the game, a certain mood. But most of all this was my first time being introduced to this type of "MMO PVP" style of game, the unease of knowing anyone could be watching at anytime was something I didn't know could be in a video game.
I came to watch many youtubers play this game and lived through them, sharing in their experiences. I eventually found Frankie's videos and those changed how I saw the game completely. Like many others I found out that DayZ is what you make it. Frankie made it into something worth watching and waiting on, something that had depth and an underelying story but that you could still be silly in.
I wanted this game so bad but at the time I didn't have a Pc that could run anything else besides Lego Island. So I just became content with watching. Until I found out that the man behind the mod had plans to make his own standalone game.
I was so excited, I saved up for almost a year in anticipation of the release. Some people don't undertand why we were so excited at that time, but y'all have to understand that this was the modern day equilivelent of PlayerUnknown releasing PUBG. We wanted to hop on this wagon because of the asured destination, a game that in time would succeed the mod.
I couldn't buy it right away but I purchased it sometime between initial release and when they had fixed the axe positioning (originally the axe was at a weird sideways angle, was playing before the movement update somewhere around there).
Here I was, first time ever playing DayZ, finally ready to make my story. I first spawned in as a black female, not the race or gender I had originally chosen, walked in the first building I found which was the construction layer cake building. Walked up the stairs, fell through the floor and broke my legs, zombie came and ate my face off.
Welcome to the Standalone.
I realized this was not the same game I once had a passion for, it was different. Still though I was determined to see this new experience through, I gave this game a solid chance. For as long as I played this game I've only had a handful of great experiences, but those experiences were absolutely amazing, something that could only happen in this game and the mod. The players were clever, atleast early on, which made for these mini stories to be had.
But after all that waiting and saving up and anticipation, it wasn't enough. I'm glad I had those times but in retrospect it wasn't worth it for the amount of time I invested in. It would be different if the game wasn't riddled with player killing glitches, the game only becomes enjoyable after the first 90 deaths because it takes that long to figure out where not to step, or to test the ground with a can of soda before dropping your weapon so that it doesn't get swallowed up.
To go through with this game you need to have alot of love for it, and some people have invested in much more time then I have and still have advised against getting this game. It would be different if the game had made any forward progress but unfortunately that is not the case. I'm still glad I was initially insterested in this game because it opened the door to learning about this great genre. I now have a love not just for survival games but also for more slowpaced games as well. Games like Arma III, Squad, Miscreated, The Long Dark, Escape from Tarkov etc. And it introduced me to the content creators of such games.
3 years ago I fell through the floor in my first time playing DayZ, 3 years later and it still happens to the most seasoned players.
This game isn't broken, something has to be whole to be broken.

For the most part a game with 'Simulator' in its title is something to avoid, ETS2 is a rare exception and a surprisingly addictive game.
You can chose to play ETS2 as realistic as possible, controlling air brakes and fuel consumption along with a manor of other things I just don't understand myself, happily however you can also play the game with a few automated options which lets you enjoy your trucking adventure with the simplicity of accelerating and braking (you'll still need to refuel though).
As a wanna-be truck driver this fills a gap, I can hitch a trailer and drive from Devon to Italy, earn my money and upgrade my truck - I'm happy, I've got my music playing and the open road awaits. Then I find you can buy a garage and hire other drivers thus creating your own tuck company, I'm addicted! But wait, there is also a multiplayer mod that allows you to join other likeminded truckers? I'm going to quit my job and just play ETS2 all day!
Don't get me wrong, this is still a simulator, there are still bugs (though very few, and even less with each update) and you'll curse at yourself after trying to reverse your trailer into the same damned parking bay thirty times or more and still failing but it does the basics right, it adds a sense of accomplishment to the game from starting out as a driver for hire to the owner of a company. The indicators even work!
I'd recommend this game to anyone who enjoys their driving and simulator games but beware, you'll easily lose many hours of your day to ETS2 - but you'll enjoy those hours!
*The ETS2 Multiplayer mod is still in ALPHA, it's free to download and is fairly stable but I recommend checking out their forums before installing the mod.

SCS's approval of Mod Creations was what really triggered the epidemic of Trucking Online. "When there is Competition in the air, You can bet that just about anyone will be there." Sites like Promods, Modsaholic,ets-2, and Gamemodding were just as competitive producing the mods as the Modders were Creating them.
In today's time it's hard to find a Developer Company to actually care about it's fan base. This is not the case with SCS. They not only improve their Simulation through contstant Updates through their testers eyes, but their fans as well. SCS is known to always keep their Fans updated through their website
If you want to be more a part of the SCS Community, they have set up another website to do just
SCS is always looking for Great Feedback that will help improve their gaming design. So far no update has recived noticeable negative responses. That may do to the fact that they allow Steam users to try out the Beta's of the updates before offically launching them. This Simulation was made in 2012, and is still expanding it's viewers. The problem most people see in this game; is that how can it be fun driving a truck, wasting up to 5 hours a day. You seen the gameplay in youtube, twitch, steam broadcast and thinking "Huh... okay so what"... Here's what, it is not suppose to Grand Theft Auto, there is no cops(weirdly) but there is system that keeps your driving speed and manners in check. It's not about ramming or running over an AI with your truck.
This game is your getaway game if you're seriously sick of gun-shooting, exploding bodies, plane-jihading while trying to waste a good amount of time. To be honest, this is a very good way to relax yourself after rage-quitting ARMA 3/COD-whatever-warfare.
Don't believe me? Try it, hook it up with a 'console' controller(at least, please!) and play up till at one point you are able to afford a garage, by then think back was it worth the money you spend. If you're still not satisfied then....
Mods for this game are plenty but be aware that there are ALOT of outdated mods, with every new patch from SCS may broke some mods. Promods and realistic driving(by KacakTV) is a best way to start your journey. If you have found nirvana, and peace with this game, may i suggest you to "ETS2MP.
Play with REAL players, some purposely trying to crash onto you every corner you turn. A fine challenge to keep yourself calm and be forgiving. Get connected, join in on a convoy or organise a convoy from ETS2MP forums, have a friendly chat at the "Official" ETS2MP teamspeak. A fair Warning though, read the teamspeak rules thoroughly and some particular admins are very power-abusive. Simple Review: Worth it; however be wearily of lack of optimization and prolonged Early Access.
I've put quite a few hours into Rust and figured I should write a review. Firstly, I highly recommend it. However, I play on a lower end computer and only get about 15-20 FPS consistently and with drops to 5. I know that is not most people's experience, yet it is worth noting that it is very poorly optimised, and as much as the team (devs) put lots of work in. The company (Facepunch) doesn't seem to be willing to finalize the game.
That being said, Rust is awesome. You can play it in a huge variety of ways, I put about 250 hours in playing solo, I then put in about 50 hours on battliefield servers, now the past 350 I've done in large groups. It's super enjoyable. Nonetheless, Rust is not for the faint of heart. People tend to descibe the community as "toxic" which it is, but that is because of the game requirements. You have to be willing to stab anyone in the back to gain the upper hand. So yeah, play it. It's a fun game.
** Sidenote: I would say it is worth $20 (I have 600 hours, so about 3 cents an hour). But, for where it is at with optimization it's fair safer to buy in a bundle for $5-$10.**

I spent 3 years playing the original DayZ mod before buying the standalone. I loved traversing the land, and the constant threat of being shot. I enjoyed gathering what gear I could, then  duking it out with other players.

I just spent an hour searching for food while starving to death, wasting my times searching buildings that COULD have had loot but didnt, until I finally found a can of tuna. I opened the can of tuna (and did not drop any, I used a can opener) and after eating the tuna, I was still starving to death.
I used to enjoy spending my time scrambling around enjoying the action of being shot at and shooting others, scrambling around aimlessly just to stay alive is not as fun.
If you like the premise of DayZ, I recommend you install Arma2 and try the mod instead.

After over 20 hrs I'm pretty much sick of MM.  You do the same old boring scrap grinding from zone to zone.  Here's the gameplay:
-Go to an outpost.
-Meet the leader.
-Do something for the leader.
-Find all the parts for the scrap crew (they harvest scrap while you're offline)
-Take over all the camps in that part of the district.
-Go to the next outpost with a leader and rinse and repeat.
The gameplay and narrative is sooo uninspired and drab.  There isn't much of a story and the gameplay leaves alot to be desired.  For one, the ground combat is buttom spam.  The car combat has bad controls at times until you fully upgrade the Magnum Opus.  Then it becomes fun.  Until then, farm scrap by taking over every camp in the game.
Taking over camps is a contest in tedium.  Each one is practically the same.  Kill all the guys in each camp, or torch their oil well (which doesn't make sense, since you would want the oil for yourself) and then your cronies come on in and take it over, giving you scrap over time.

I woke up on a beach.
I look down and realize I am naked.
I notice a rock next to me,
I pick it up and move inland.
I spot a man with a pickaxe smacking a rock with his pick.
I sneak up behind him and drive my rock into the back of his skull.
He falls to the floor, yelling and grasping at his skull.
I end his suffering by once again driving my rock into his face.
It felt good.
It felt liberating
I gather some materials to build myself a house.
I build a moderate looking house with just one floor.
I put a door on it and stick a lock onto the door and craft myself a key.
I hear a knocking at the door.
It's an older guy, sounds like a 19-25 year old.
"Hello? Is anyone in there?"
I don't reply.
I slam open my door and drive a spear that I had crafted earlier into his face.
He falls onto the floor.
No screaming
No pain
Just death.
I pack my things, realizing he or his friends will come back soon.
I run.
I run far away.
Then I arrived at my real home and hopped onto steam and bought Rust.
It's pretty good I guess.

For the most part a game with 'Simulator' in its title is something to avoid, ETS2 is a rare exception and a surprisingly addictive game.
You can chose to play ETS2 as realistic as possible, controlling air brakes and fuel consumption along with a manor of other things I just don't understand myself, happily however you can also play the game with a few automated options which lets you enjoy your trucking adventure with the simplicity of accelerating and braking (you'll still need to refuel though).
As a wanna-be truck driver this fills a gap, I can hitch a trailer and drive from Devon to Italy, earn my money and upgrade my truck - I'm happy, I've got my music playing and the open road awaits. Then I find you can buy a garage and hire other drivers thus creating your own tuck company, I'm addicted! But wait, there is also a multiplayer mod that allows you to join other likeminded truckers? I'm going to quit my job and just play ETS2 all day!
Don't get me wrong, this is still a simulator, there are still bugs (though very few, and even less with each update) and you'll curse at yourself after trying to reverse your trailer into the same damned parking bay thirty times or more and still failing but it does the basics right, it adds a sense of accomplishment to the game from starting out as a driver for hire to the owner of a company. The indicators even work!
I'd recommend this game to anyone who enjoys their driving and simulator games but beware, you'll easily lose many hours of your day to ETS2 - but you'll enjoy those hours!
*The ETS2 Multiplayer mod is still in ALPHA, it's free to download and is fairly stable but I recommend checking out their forums before installing the mod.

SCS's approval of Mod Creations was what really triggered the epidemic of Trucking Online. "When there is Competition in the air, You can bet that just about anyone will be there." Sites like Promods, Modsaholic,ets-2, and Gamemodding were just as competitive producing the mods as the Modders were Creating them.
In today's time it's hard to find a Developer Company to actually care about it's fan base. This is not the case with SCS. They not only improve their Simulation through contstant Updates through their testers eyes, but their fans as well. SCS is known to always keep their Fans updated through their website
If you want to be more a part of the SCS Community, they have set up another website to do just
SCS is always looking for Great Feedback that will help improve their gaming design. So far no update has recived noticeable negative responses. That may do to the fact that they allow Steam users to try out the Beta's of the updates before offically launching them. This Simulation was made in 2012, and is still expanding it's viewers. If that doesn't say something good about SCS, I don't know what does.

The problem most people see in this game; is that how can it be fun driving a truck, wasting up to 5 hours a day. Subterranean Chronicle could probably be nominated for three of these Steam Choice Awards.
A great story with mostly clever writing, a bunch of likable characters, and a fun and unique battle system. This indie game implements player choice better than some AAA games I've played and depending on your choices, you'll either be cracking up or feeling terrible. It also has one of the best 4th-wall breaks I've seen in a game.
If for some reason Toby Fox decides to not make another game, then I hope he continues to make more music, because the game's soundtrack is fantastic. The rest of the sound effects are pretty plain. The "retro" graphics can be underwhelming at times (except for a scene near the end that caught me off guard), but the character designs are pretty unique.
Overall, it's a excellent indie game that I highly recommend, especially if you love surreal games like Earthbound.

Here i am, 28 hours in-game time, half of the main missions are done and i've already unlocked every character customization...
Story is...well...it's Mad Max. It doesn't go up or down from that. If you're buying this game for an emmy award winning scenario, don't. Don't get me wrong. It's still pretty good. However, you should be aware, scenario is not the most important element to this game.
Combat and driving is just awesome. You'll most likely will find a new way to kill someone everyday if you can push your imagination to the limit.
I recommend this game to people who likes Mad Max franchise. This is your game. If not, it's better to watch some videos before you decide whether to buy it or not.

TLDR: 9 out of 10 - Too much sand.
No but seriously, only 3hrs in (could change further down the line, who knows) but I can already say I'm thoroughly enjoying this game, the review embargo thing is always worrying but looking at gameplay and knowing its Avalanche Studios (are they even able to make boring / bad games?) I took a punt and so far its paid off in spades.
The visuals are really striking and something to behold in places, the physics are as awesome and meaningful (got owned by some metal roof plating flying loose in a sandstorm taking a tidy chunk of health) as you'd expect from the team that brought us the awesome Just Cause series, the cars handle well, some of the control conventions are different but you get used to it pretty quickly (tutorials and instructions are easy to find should you forget or need it), they are loads and loads and loads of things to do and upgrade carrots to encourage you to do them.
Performance has been excellent for my setup (rig in profile) with every setting on maximum running at a smooth 60fps (or whatever fps it runs). I've not bumped into any medium or major issues, only very, very minor things like the occasionally graphic pop or UI graphics not going into colour from b+w upon entering them (fixed by going back and in again) but other than that, no need to Warn A Brother with this one.
Now, I just need to figure out what happened to that poor dog at Chum's tabernacle...

Warner Brothers? Warn a Brother.
In this case, you don't need warning. Avalanche Studios have demonstrated their skill as PC developers and delivered a fantastic port. I can Max this at 1440p at 144fps, which isn't usually possible for new titles (SLI 980s, 16GB RAM, 4790k @4.5, not an underpowered rig by any means, but still at the mercy of optimisation).
If you're a fan of Mad Max, then this game is a definite buy. If you're not a fan, then it's about some Australian guy called Max who goes around a wasteland in his car beating up people like he's Batman (the game has the same combat style as Batman), with another guy who resembles the Hunchback of Notre Dame that performs maintenence on your vehicle. You can also customise your vehicle and engage in car combat (which is basically shooting other cars and ramming them).
You scavenge for supplies like fuel, water, ammo, and scrap metal, though this isn't a survival game (mostly because it's not in early access, doesn't have zombies, and doesn't have a crafting system where you make a bow from two tin cans and grass), water restores lost health, fuel is what your car eats, ammo makes your rooty-tooty-point-and-shooty go 'bang' and so on.
As for negatives, the world can be a bit lifeless at times, and there really isn't much here for non fans. The Max in the game isn't based on Mel Gibson or Tom Hardy, so you'll have to use your imagination.
TL;DR:
Great port
Fighting is like Batman
Car combat involves shooting and ramming
Scavenging for items
Looks nice graphically
Max is not based on any of the actors, but he is still Australian, the game bears some resemblance to the recent Mad Max movie.
Sandstorms (not placed by Darude)
If you're a fan, get it. If you're interested in a post apocalyptic open world with cars, shooting and fighting, get it (and go and watch the Mad Max movies, especially the old ones).

This game is a perfect example of why you shouldn't place your trust in early access games. It has been 3 years and it is still in early access, is still very unpolished and offers very little in the way of gameplay and even the gameplay that it offers is lackluster and rather repetitive. The only real thing you can do in this game is PvP, which is rather depressing considering that it is a survival game without any real survival elements. Food is easy to get, there is no reason to start a camp or to hunt, and weapons are very easy to aquire, which I admit is not necessarily a bad thing, but it only fuels the deathmatch mode that this game is put in because of it.
The PvP can be quite exciting and can get you running on a bit of a high for a little while, but it still has its issues. There are a number of bugs that you can encounter and there are issues with hit registration and the way guns work. And although people may argue that the situations you get in are different everytime, there is still a cycle you go through. You get into combat, you kill a guy or two, you eventually die, you respawn and you start running again.
Which leads me to my next point, the game is quite repetitive. You spawn in and you start running. You loot through houses and you start running again. You get geared enough and run to one of the PvP hotspots. You get into a fight and if you die you respawn at the coast and do it all over again. But if you win, you either get to sit and wait for more people to fight, or you start running to the next PvP zone.
Now, there is fun to be had in this game, otherwise I would not have put as much time into it as I have. But the main message I'm trying to send here it is easily not worth getting in the state it's at. But if you do decide to get the game, make sure you have a decent group of friends to play with, playing solo can be boring and frustrating.
I believe that this will always be a PvP based game, but if they were to add more survival elements to encourage cooperation and discourage KOS, and iron out the bugs, it would be the crown of survival games and a very good game as a whole. But as of now it is not worth the time.

Mad Max so far for me and in my little time playing it has shown how a PC game should play.. I have an old sandybridge 2600 i7 @3.4ghz, 16gb DDR3 Corsair vengance ram @ 2133mhz and a single AMD R9 290 on a fatal1ty z77 socket 1150 motherboard. Most games i attempt to play on this rig perform perfectly at 1080p and i run into some issues issues with other games such as dying light  and upon its release mortal kombat X. for once i decided i wasnt going to mess with the settings prior to starting the game... and just plunged myself headlong into the game, After the first hour or so playing the game and remarking on how beautiful it was.. i decided to check what settings the game had "auto selected" for me upon launch.. It turns out it was set to 2560x1440 with everything on High I had been achieving 60-120fps with zero microstutters flawlessly at these settings..
The graphics are beautiful and striking. The art style is bleak and sombre but fasinating and inviting. The gameplay is smooth entertaining and rewarding with a familiar but well testing and working combat system that is similar to the likes of the Batman Arkham series and Witcher 3.
The driving is OK for me at the moment but i put that down to my lack of experience driving on this game.. every game is different, it can be frustrating at times!
The developers of this game should take their hats off at such a marvel of a PC creation and everyone should buy this game. Its just a shame that Metal Gear solid has just come out and this game will lose the attention it deserves.
If you are looking to buy a game that you wont turn on for 10 minutes and say "Meh.. cant be arsed playing this" than this is that game..

I've only played a few hours of this game so far but first impressions are very positive with solid and satisfyingly brutal melee combat, enjoyable car battles and a surprisingly interesting environment to explore. The desert comes across as a desolate, believable place, thanks to an impressive game engine that renders a massive draw distance and runs pretty much flawlessly at 60 fps maxed out on my system. Only the auto-checkpointing and end mission screens cause hitches.
Graphically the game is excellent despite the drab setting. Max is well detailed and he and all the other characters so far are expertly animated. If I have one minor gripe it is that Max feels a little sluggish to control. The Magnum Opus vehicle feels suitably heavy and, coupled with the excellent physics and entertaining abilities (I especially like the harpoon), is a lot of fun to drive. Have I mentioned the explosions yet? No? Well this are fantastic, by far the best I've seen in any game to date and do not appear to be canned. Finally, this game has great lighting and some breath-taking skylines (the skyboxes in this game are stunning). I cannot fault the visuals really apart from some overdone bloom and perhaps weak anti-aliasing.
Aurally the game is fine with meaty engine noises from the vehicles and convincing metal on metal sounds for car crashes. Voice-acting is good, especially that of Chum and Max sounds how I imagined he would. Music is a bit subdued, to be honest I hardly noticed it except on the title screen.
Looking forward to checking out this open world game more over the coming days. As a licensed game, Mad Max had the potential to have been awful (as many unfortunately are) but in the hands of Just Cause 2's great developer, Avalance, I had complete faith that this game would turn out to be good. On the basis of what I've seen so far this game seems very promising and will very possibly keep me going until Just Cause 3 comes out in December.
*UPDATE 7th September 2015*
Having played this addictive game for over 35 hours, I can now say with absolute confidence that I love it! One of the most downright fun, rewarding, entertaining and varied open world games I have played in recent years, Mad Max deserves to do extremely well if only so we get a sequel! Pretty please?

Overall, it's a excellent indie game that I highly recommend, especially if you love surreal games like Earthbound.

How do I sum this whole thing up...
Borderlands 2 is a game where you control one of 4-6 Vault Hunters on the planet of Pandora, a planet where pretty much everything wants you dead, as they set off on a revenge quest. Along the way, you meet up with the PCs of the previous game, join a resistance group, find crazy loot, kill psychotic bandits/rabid creatures/killer robots/midgets by firing off far more lead than you really needed to with said loot, and generally cause chaos as you fight your way across Pandora to stop a man named Handsome Jack (who also happens to be the target of your revenge quest).
It's also, in my humble opinion, probably one of the greatest experiences I've ever had as a gamer.
So how exactly is BL2 so great? Well, it's great because it...
It...
Erm...
...
...Alright, I'll be honest - I really don't think anything I could think of putting down here could really sum up how much of a good time I've had with BL2. It's one thing to write how a game is good, but sometimes the experience can't really be summed up with words.
There's something about the way this game put itself together - with the gameplay, art design, story, variety, and general style - that really just struck a chord with me. I dunno what the specifics of that forumla are, but whatever it is, it seems like one that rarely appears in video games.
The only other game that's struck me like this Team Fortress 2, and even then it didn't strike quite as hard as it did here.
This game is, for lack of a better term. something very special.

I've only played a few hours of this game so far but first impressions are very positive with solid and satisfyingly brutal melee combat, enjoyable car battles and a surprisingly interesting environment to explore. The desert comes across as a desolate, believable place, thanks to an impressive game engine that renders a massive draw distance and runs pretty much flawlessly at 60 fps maxed out on my system. Only the auto-checkpointing and end mission screens cause hitches.
Graphically the game is excellent despite the drab setting. Max is well detailed and he and all the other characters so far are expertly animated. If I have one minor gripe it is that Max feels a little sluggish to control. The Magnum Opus vehicle feels suitably heavy and, coupled with the excellent physics and entertaining abilities (I especially like the harpoon), is a lot of fun to drive. Have I mentioned the explosions yet? No? Well this are fantastic, by far the best I've seen in any game to date and do not appear to be canned. Finally, this game has great lighting and some breath-taking skylines (the skyboxes in this game are stunning). I cannot fault the visuals really apart from some overdone bloom and perhaps weak anti-aliasing.
Aurally the game is fine with meaty engine noises from the vehicles and convincing metal on metal sounds for car crashes. Voice-acting is good, especially that of Chum and Max sounds how I imagined he would. Music is a bit subdued, to be honest I hardly noticed it except on the title screen.
Looking forward to checking out this open world game more over the coming days. As a licensed game, Mad Max had the potential to have been awful (as many unfortunately are) but in the hands of Just Cause 2's great developer, Avalance, I had complete faith that this game would turn out to be good. On the basis of what I've seen so far this game seems very promising and will very possibly keep me going until Just Cause 3 comes out in December.
*UPDATE 7th September 2015*
Having played this addictive game for over 35 hours, I can now say with absolute confidence that I love it! One of the most downright fun, rewarding, entertaining and varied open world games I have played in recent years, Mad Max deserves to do extremely well if only so we get a sequel! Pretty please?

Euro Truck Simulator 2.
What can be said about this game that hasn't been said already. It is quite fun to play. I have approximately 20 hours in the game, and that's about where I'd say most users that would be interested in this, would get to. For someone more casual, and not into the "sim" genre (think... the person that plays flight simulator, and the first thing they do is nose it over into the ground because they wanted to see what the crash looked like)... you're probably looking at about 5 hours.
Pros: The game is good, it's well oiled, and a complete package. You'll have no problem picking it up, driving for miles, and running an RPG style trucking company if you'd like, or you could simply roam about in the countryside racking up speeding fines.
Cons: They types of loads get a bit repetitive, and I think the developers are missing a HUGE opportunity for a CHALLENGING trucking sim. Spin Tires goes further than it needs to (though still a FANTASTIC game), but where Spin Tires is all mud, and challenge... ETS2 is all highway, and cruise control. Adding a variety of loads to carry, and the challenge of mountain trucking, or big city fuel tanker deliveries, etc... would make this game much more interesting.
Still, the mod community is strong. I prefer not to mod, since they're largely just skins, which I find provide nothing more than (no pun) a skin deep experience.
Buy it if: You're fascinated by running a freight business as an owner/operator, and enjoy the long haul aspects of FSX.
Skip it if: You're looking for something that requires you to think your way through something, or do more than remember to indicate properly, and back a big rig into a loading dock. True story, I've fallen asleep while driving on the virtual highway on a longhaul... which is probably realistic... but not the kind of realism I want in a game.
I'm giving it a 7/10 if you don't mod. I wish there was more variety in the challenge of loads (long loads, doubles, triples, oversized, etc.), and the traffic AI seems to leave something to be desired.

TLDR: Decent game, fascinated by the physiological problems, and solutions to such problems. Game seems to be stuck in muddy soil as far as an Alpha Release for years on end. Add more baddies, add some electronics or something. 7/10
I enjoy many aspects of this game. The one I do not enjoy is this:
"DayZ is an alpha game for like two or three years now and one day we're gonna load it up with epic cool stuff and call it finished"
You can do that for a while, but even slow people like me who don't know whether to use a flat head or a phillips get to where we think..."wait just a second here...I think...I think you guys are gonna do this for another two years...maybe ten even"
I do recommend DayZ and admit that I may be biased. I played it with a friend and enjoyed it. It was also the first Alpha Early release game I have played. It's the small things that bug me...like why to this day can I not lock pick a medical box? Everytime I see one I wonder why in God's name I still can't open it for some badly needed antibiotics or something.
If you are looking for a zombie/survival/crafting game this is a good one (among the half dozen or so tht are worth paying money for).
What keeps me from calling it crap is the physiological aspects. Blood poisoning, breaking bones, hypothermia, hyperthermia, and more. What is more impressive are the solutions to such problems. You can make a basic splint for a broken leg. You can take antibiotics to kill an infection. You can even conduct a blood transfusion if you are medically savvy enough (or use a guide) to keep another player (or yourself) alive. You have to do it right though. Can't go mixing the wrong blood type with yours, and you don't want to infect yourself with dirty medical equipment.
The thinking behind that aspect alone is enough for me to recommend it. 7/10. This game could very easily run up into an 8.5 or even 9 with some updates that are not just your usual server maintanence.

I bought this game to laugh at it, I've bought many simluators in the past 'for a laugh', I thought this was going to be no different.
Making the profile was comical. I even found a picture of Ellen DeGeneres which I ended up choosing for my trucker. I called my company something 'funny' like 'Les-Be-Friends'. Just the usual for me when starting a new simulator game...
But then the game started and I was awestruck.
The graphics are beautiful. Very detailed and well designed.
The game physics aren't a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥like they are on usual simulators.
The sound effects are brilliant. No complaint from me.
Now... the gameplay.
When I did my first job/mission, I didn't take it seriously; I caused as much damage as possible. I maybe lasted about 30 minutes before I closed the game and went to bed. The next morning I had an urge to finish it and so I did. That was the moment I got hooked onto this.
I've now started taking it seriously, abiding by the laws of the road, stopping at traffic lights... I've even bought myself a wheel controller just so I can feel even more immersed in the game.
This game is what simulators should be. Euro Truck Simulator 2 and OMSI are the REAL simulators not Farm Simulator 2012, Woodcutter 2013 etc.
I was never interested in trucks or driving but now I love it. If anybody has actually gotten this far in my review, then please try this game because I was just as uninterested as you are and now look at me!
10/10 - I reccomend this game A LOT.
PS: There is currently a brilliant Mod out for this game that enables multiplayer. It takes no time to get it working, you only have to install it... nothing else.
The mod allows you and your friends to truck as one. You will come across a lot of other people too. I just went on multiplayer and there was over 2,000 people playing. It isn't littered with trolls either as they are quickly banned for blocking roads, purposely banging into other players etc etc.
This adds to the game even more. So please, try this game out or forever be known as an idiot!

I don't quite know why this wasn't just a piece of Hungle Bungle fodder that I left running in the background for Steam cards, but for some odd reason, I spent a good portion of this weekend hauling tonnage from Frankfurt Am Main to Rostock in Euro Truck Simulator 2. The experience was... mixed. My first attempt was a rocky one. After setting up my company and picking the driver that most looked like a tiny pope, I started up the tutorial and learned my way around the inside of a big rig. So far, so good, but moments into my first actual job the truck got caught on seemingly nothing and glitched out spectacularly, forcing me to cut power to the computer to get the damn game to go away.
Hesitantly, I ran it again, and thankfully it worked much better this time around. Using my trusty GPS and occasionally checking the Options screen for controls (How do I headlights? How do I windshield? What the hell's an Ausfhart?), I was burnin' my litres of petrol, cruising past countryside, intimidating other drivers with my apocalyptic girth, and agonizingly crawling up steep on- and off-ramps, ignorant of the screams of the jerks in cars around me. The discovery of the radio was delightful; the game offers a default selection of live European stations to run through, all completely indecipherable, all pretty fascinating, and all of which drop F-bombs with cheery regularity. If that's not your style, you can import whatever audio tracks you want and just shuffle through those (because all truckers love haulin'♥♥♥♥♥to One-Winged Angel and Dancing Mad Tier). Admittedly, all I was doing was driving at moderate speed down some fairly low-res highways, but there's something meditative about the experience. The road called, and I answered.
Over time though, things soured. I decided I was done being a mere professional trucker, employed by others and making a fraction of what I could working on my own. I discovered several recruiting agencies and truck dealerships, so technically, becoming my own boss was now an option. Then I saw the price tags. Getting my own truck, even the worst of the worst, would run me upwards of $100k. As I was making a mere $2-3k per job (assuming no Headlight Violations or Vehicular Collisions take a chunk out of the profits), and each job takes a good chunk of real-world time to complete, I could see I'd be grinding for a while. And then another glitch hit, this time simply freezing the game for a good thirty seconds, then unleashing everything I missed out on all at once as the game caught up with itself. So many car crashes. So much fines. I'd managed to completely undo all my hard work up to that point in a single, underwhelming 40 car pile-up.
On top of that, the game had some other less than stellar traits. Rather than being a faithful recreation of the European highway system, everything is shrunken down to scale. You clear kilometers in seconds, and even the biggest cities seem to be composed of a couple industrial sites, a gas station, a hotel, and maybe a dozen odd generic structures here and there. The pastoral scenery fares no better; I'd say it's maybe a touch better than PS2 quality, but that's pretty jarring for a 2012 game, especially when scenery is such a critical part of the game. I was briefly okay with the attention to detail paid to the truck interiors, but there are no personal touches added, no fuzzy dice, no dancing Hawaiian girl, no litter on the floor, no beaded seat cover. A little flair could have gone a long way here. Finally, (and this may be an understandable limitation to keep the game from becoming a demolition derby) all car crashes do is jostle the screen a bit and dock your pay. No matter how much more massive you are than your prey, all you manage to do is bump them, and off they go on their merry way. I'm not out for blood here, but I'd like the repercussions to be a little more significant than that.
There's definitely an audience for this game. I myself came close to finding it worth the time - perhaps not as a source of fun, but as an interesting and relaxing title to come back to now and again. Unfortunately, the bugs and the budget both hamstring it more than I'd like. If you're deadset on buying it, go ahead, and you'll likely enjoy the experience. For everyone else, wait for a bargain or keep your expectations in check; it's a hell of a bumpy road out there.

before he cut off and flossed with their sacks.
Max is not a happy guy. His car gets stolen, and a lot of people want to kill him, his only friend being a crazy mechanic who is basically Smeagol high on Petrol fumes. Walking around a desert with sand in your boots all day would make anyone mad.
This sets Max on a quest to build the perfect car, the Magnum Opus, which draws a lot of comparisons with how the game plays. Like the Opus, the game itself is incredibly well optimised; it runs smoothly, at a very high frame rate, and has clearly been crafted with a lot of care and attention. The downside to this is that I feel like they could have used those spare resources to do more with the game engine, to make the game look better than it currently does - it's not ugly, but there is definitely room for an upgraded "Definitive Edition" later down the road. AA does a mediocre job of eliminating jaggies and it would be nice to have an MSAA option, with higher quality textures.
Using a third-party injector, I managed to improve the colour palette - a desert will never be bright and shiny and colourful, but there's definitely room to enhance and sharpen the existing palette. All in all, it's beautiful to behold, and the night sky is a sight to behold.
I've never been a fan of the films, but I love this game's story. It's clearly explained, I know exactly what's going on at all times, and it's interesting. I also like the upgrade system, which is fairly comprehensive and gives you some great options to customise both Max and the Magnum Opus.
A lot of folks complained that I hadn't spent much time with the game and therefore had no right to judge it, so I'm changing my review to reflect having spent more time with the game - I now give it an 8.5 out of 10. While it may not technically be the best game ever made, for me, it ticks all the right boxes and does a LOT of things right. You won't regret buying this, I can promise you.

Alright so I haven't played DAYZ in a few years now and figured I'd give it a shot, back when it was released it was attrocious to put it in very mild words.
And honestly I think the entire thing was a flop to begin with and should never have seen the light of day but that's biased as I was an avid fan of the mod for Arma 2.
It was overly ambitious and it wanted to continue on the trend the mod had previously created and of course it couldn't deliver, it was porly optimized, riddled with more bugs than the mod had just to name a few of the crushing problems it had. Over the year it's improved quite significantly I might add, I haven't played it but have kept up to date with it, just incase I'd feel the urge to return.
I reinstalled it last night and had a go on a few servers only to find that sure enough, it has improved, stability is a lot better and optimization isn't even remotely close to being as awful as it used to be, but I found a few problems on the 8 or so different servers I had. I died on 7 of them which you might think is normal with this being a survival game and sure enough, 7 of the deaths where due to me not being able to survive but not because I got killed by players, nono. I killed 17 or so players but all of which seem to have the same problem, there's literally no f-ing food anywhere, no apples, no rice, nothing. There was plenty of water to go around but food was scarce to put it blunt and no. It wasn't the lack of server restarts as it was 8 different servers with various population, I even tried 3 servers that had barely anyone on it and that had just restarted. I found 2 canned tuna in my sit through those 8 lives, still alive on the last guy I created but the problem remains.
Tons of weapons, water and clothing/tools.
-Not even remotely close to being enough food however and I figured I'd try and hunt for some food too, or I would if I could find a single animal, wanted to try and grow crops, no seeds...
So can recommend the game in it's current state?
I mean, I could go on and on about what's good about it and all, but at the end of the day.
Nobody wants to waste 30minutes looting up an entire town only to find zero water, food, medical supplies or anything even remotely usefull to your survival besides a fireaxe, then run to the nearest military location only to find 2 attachments after 10minutes of looting, thinking you can reach the other town before dieing only to realize that right, you have no food, you'll die in the next 5minutes anyway, just afk, respawn and hope to god you get spawned next to a major city so you have a chance of survival and if not, waste another 30+ minutes frantically trying your darnest to survive or find nutritions only to die again, rince and repeat.
So YAY or NAY?
Currently?
Still a resounding nay, I'll take the vanilla mod with hackers, lack of players, buggy zombies over this pile of junk any day of the week, not to mention there's better survival games out there now anyhow so this is just a has-been and will never be able to replace it's predecessor.

-The level scaling is all wrong. Need to beat the game twice to get the game to dynamically scale to your level. Complicated work-arounds include not starting missions till scaling starts... new difficulties made this worse. You just can't play the way you want and the dlc you want. You kind-of have to do things in specific orders and that still does not work well enough.  Would have LOVED to have an option to play on 2nd difficulty (TVH) and let that scale PAST the new level cap for a viable endgame (without a few BiS items and lower drop rate of course) so that we could have enjoyed that and geared up for the next difficulty rather than being forced into it..
Careful not to get too many levels before the 3rd difficulty. Combat mechanics and enemies change alot and scale to you. This means that your gear will gimp you pretty badly till you get your footing.
Still love the game and highly recommend. But for the scaling, this would be a nearly perfect co-op FPS game.

When I first bought this I thought to myself "This'll be bloomin' awful"... how wrong I was.
I bought this game to laugh at it, I've bought many simluators in the past 'for a laugh', I thought this was going to be no different.
Making the profile was comical. I even found a picture of Ellen DeGeneres which I ended up choosing for my trucker. I called my company something 'funny' like 'Les-Be-Friends'. Just the usual for me when starting a new simulator game...
But then the game started and I was awestruck.
The graphics are beautiful. Very detailed and well designed.
The game physics aren't a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥like they are on usual simulators.
The sound effects are brilliant. No complaint from me.
Now... the gameplay.
When I did my first job/mission, I didn't take it seriously; I caused as much damage as possible. I maybe lasted about 30 minutes before I closed the game and went to bed. The next morning I had an urge to finish it and so I did. That was the moment I got hooked onto this.
I've now started taking it seriously, abiding by the laws of the road, stopping at traffic lights... I've even bought myself a wheel controller just so I can feel even more immersed in the game.
This game is what simulators should be. Euro Truck Simulator 2 and OMSI are the REAL simulators not Farm Simulator 2012, Woodcutter 2013 etc.
I was never interested in trucks or driving but now I love it. If anybody has actually gotten this far in my review, then please try this game because I was just as uninterested as you are and now look at me!
10/10 - I reccomend this game A LOT.
PS: There is currently a brilliant Mod out for this game that enables multiplayer. It takes no time to get it working, you only have to install it... nothing else.
The mod allows you and your friends to truck as one. You will come across a lot of other people too. I just went on multiplayer and there was over 2,000 people playing. It isn't littered with trolls either as they are quickly banned for blocking roads, purposely banging into other players etc etc.
This adds to the game even more. So please, try this game out or forever be known as an idiot!
