Handsome Jack is the tyrant who "rules" pandora (he doesn't actually rule anything, he's only interested in said planet due to its resources, so while everyone kills each other he mines the eridium out of it). You'd have no business with him if he wasn't the only one between you and the treasures in the vault, so naturally the plot revolves around stopping him.
This first person shooter is incredibly fun, and addicting too. It follows the standard MMO color scheme, so white weapons are basically garbage while pearlescent (cyan) weapons are the best of the best (though you won't see any pearlescents until you're level 60+). The best you'll find in Normal mode will be Legendary (orange) weapons, so make sure to treasure them if you get any!
Gunplay is fun as hell, every weapon has its highs and lows and there's PLENTY of choice, so there's a combo for everyone. Enemies can be tough and bosses too, so updating your gear frequently is recommended... remember, a high-level white weapon is better than a low-level purple weapon! Don't look at the colors, look at the numbers.
The final enemy is a bit disappointing, there are tougher bosses in the DLCs, but I guarantee their intros aren't as epic. Not by a long shot.
Co-op is deliciously well implemented and it can improve your experience, so make sure to try it! After finishing the game you can start again in True Vault Hunter Mode (TVHM), keeping all your gear and perks, so if you felt the first playthrough was easy, you might wanna try it too.
Curiously, this game is famous because of its graphics, but you'll find they're not exactly ultra-realistic/highly-demanding graphics. This gives the game a lot of personality and makes it even more enjoyable.
The soundtrack is a must-have, plenty of songs that can pump you up, even if you aren't even playing (Ice, anyone?).
Completely customizable, 100% left-handed friendly
If you ever want to play this game, make sure to get the GOTY edition, it contains all the cool stuff! Except Sir Hammerlock's Big Game Hunt. I love the guy but his DLC just sucks. And don't play Tiny Tina's DLC unless you've already beaten the game at least once, since there's plenty of spoilers in it.
I'd also like to use this space to openly admit my love for Gaige.
9/10 a must have for all the FPS/loot lovers. The humour can be a bit off-putting (some people just hate memes and pop culture) but I didn't mind at all.

Undertale is a pretty quirky RPG that doesn't actually offer that much. However, what it offers is really good.
The RPG elements are pretty bare-bones and seem kind of gratuitous, however that's not necessarily a bad thing. It's not really a game that would benefit from more complex mechanics. The same with the length. It's rather on the short side, a single playthrough lasts only a few hours, but that's not a bad thing at all. It's just as long as it needs to be.
Gameplay-wise the central element is certainly it's combat system, just as quirky as the rest of the game. Battles don't merely involve dice rolls, but have you actively avoid the attacks of your enemies. Clearly, lots of thought went into making the attacks of any enemy types, and even combination of several ones, as unique as possible and especially the boss enemies have patterns that are very memorable and often feature well-used gimmicks. The "Mercy" mechanic (not just the option, but the entire concept of defeating enemies without killing them) is also very well-done and entertaining. More often than not, it's much more interesting to spare enemies than to kill them, not just enabling but also heavily encouraging pacifist runs.
On the other hand, killing enemies, particularly bosses, tends to be interesting for all the wrong reasons. The game does a good job in making you feel bad about rampart killing sprees, without even demonizing you very much until the end. It's a pity that the end of a particularly violent playthrough is pretty terrible with no real conclusion and semi-nonsensical meta commentary. The good thing is that other playthrough are (mostly) devoid of things like that.
One big reason why killing can easily make you feel bad are the characters themselves. Those are the real star of Undertale. From a motherly goat-like creature, over two odd skeleton brothers, a fish that fancies herself a shounen action hero, to the surprisingly sympathetic king, the game is full of very likeable and amusing characters. Even many random and unimportant NPCs end up pretty memorable. Interacting with them alone makes this game well worth playing.
Presentation-wise, Undertale is a mixed bag, at least when it comes to graphics. They are pretty simple and tend to look "off" at times. This includes the sprites of the main characters. On the other hand, they're overall pretty well-done, especially the many different areas, which are very distinct and sometimes downright beautiful. Character art is much better in battle, although the use of purely black and white sprites might not be everyone's cup of tea.
The music, however, is pretty much unanimously good and often really great. It's very noticeable that the creator is mostly a musician and he put his skills to great use here. Many tracks are a pleasure to listen to, in the game and out of it (and of course, the soundtrack is available separately), and there's no real bad song here (although I'm not so fond of the recycling of a song he used in at least two other projects before). Many songs are building on others, sometimes blatantly, sometimes subtly, creating familiarity without becoming repetitive.
Is Undertale as great as the hype says it is? Well, no. But with a hype that huge, no game ever could possibly be. It is, however, a very good game that's well worth its price and that I can recommend to nearly everyone.

Borderlands 2...what can be said about it that hasn't already been said? Probably a lot of things, but I'm just gonna go ahead and say whatever I damn well feel like. It's a great game. The art style is pleasing to the eye, the dialogue is hilarious, the controls are smooth, the characters are memorable, the story is interesting, the amount of different guns and other loot is overwhelming, and the crate-opening animations are satisfying as hell. I haven't played more than 30 minutes of the first game, but I'd say you don't really need to in order to enjoy the story of this game. Each character (that has a name) has his/her/its own personality that distinguishes it from anyone else in the game, and this just adds to the immersion of the world.
Another thing that pleased me when I played the game was the dynamic soundtrack. It hasn't the smoothness of Banjo-Kazooie, but you recognize exactly what kind of situation you're in depending on what music is playing. It's a nice touch.
TL;DR:
If you want a great first-person shooter with a fun story, buy this game.

Hoo boy, how do you even review a game like this?  Especially when so many of the game's mechanics have some unexpected twist added to them?
Undertale was designed to feel like your typical 90s JRPG, hence the graphics, music, and overall design.  Yet, just as mentioned on the game's store page, you don't have to kill the monsters you fight.  Instead, you'' have to figure out what the opponent wants (or is afraid of) and dodge their attacks until you do.  That little detail essentially results in two different games being playable: one where you fight everything, and one where you befriend everything.
It's a short experience though - the first playthrough will probably only take 10-15 hours, tops, and that's assuming you're the sort who likes to take their time, explore and speak to everybody.  Yet, it is quite replayable, but due to a particular... "reason" within the game, you might choose not to, out of concern of making things worse.
This is near storytelling perfection. The characters, the music, the world is just so well done. Read/watch as little as possible about it, just buy it and experience it for yourself.

Handsome Jack is the tyrant who "rules" pandora (he doesn't actually rule anything, he's only interested in said planet due to its resources, so while everyone kills each other he mines the eridium out of it). You'd have no business with him if he wasn't the only one between you and the treasures in the vault, so naturally the plot revolves around stopping him.
This first person shooter is incredibly fun, and addicting too. It follows the standard MMO color scheme, so white weapons are basically garbage while pearlescent (cyan) weapons are the best of the best (though you won't see any pearlescents until you're level 60+). The best you'll find in Normal mode will be Legendary (orange) weapons, so make sure to treasure them if you get any!
Gunplay is fun as hell, every weapon has its highs and lows and there's PLENTY of choice, so there's a combo for everyone. Enemies can be tough and bosses too, so updating your gear frequently is recommended... remember, a high-level white weapon is better than a low-level purple weapon! Don't look at the colors, look at the numbers.
The final enemy is a bit disappointing, there are tougher bosses in the DLCs, but I guarantee their intros aren't as epic. Not by a long shot.
Co-op is deliciously well implemented and it can improve your experience, so make sure to try it! After finishing the game you can start again in True Vault Hunter Mode (TVHM), keeping all your gear and perks, so if you felt the first playthrough was easy, you might wanna try it too.
Curiously, this game is famous because of its graphics, but you'll find they're not exactly ultra-realistic/highly-demanding graphics. This gives the game a lot of personality and makes it even more enjoyable.
The soundtrack is a must-have, plenty of songs that can pump you up, even if you aren't even playing (Ice, anyone?).
Completely customizable, 100% left-handed friendly
If you ever want to play this game, make sure to get the GOTY edition, it contains all the cool stuff! Except Sir Hammerlock's Big Game Hunt. I love the guy but his DLC just sucks. And don't play Tiny Tina's DLC unless you've already beaten the game at least once, since there's plenty of spoilers in it.
I'd also like to use this space to openly admit my love for Gaige.

Rust is like the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ child of Darksouls and Minecraft. Its an open word survival crafting game in early access. Which for some is an instant turn off, understandably. Well I was naive and got interested and started following it. Needless to say all in I have sunk close to 1300 hours, in this game with 600 being on this account.  My PC couldn’t handle it not to long ago, so I had to play on my friends when I hung out with him. I played pretty evenly legacy(an old and now dead form of this game) and "new rust" as we know it now. The reason this game is difficult isn’t the AI or the environment, its the player base. Its a game that rewards being harsh as much as it does being kind, in fact I would say more so. Being kind is a good way to get and early death or two. It has it's charm though. I love being kind, when able. Its something relatively rare as most people have had it beaten into them with various things from rocks to hatchets Kill on Sight. Overall I do recommend this game, if you can stand some toxicity from its player base and the salt to follow death. The devs push out updates almost every week on Thursdays and fix any bugs discovered asap if game breaking. It’s one of the few games to hold my interest for so long. I have burned myself out on it several times. I always end up coming back ready for more.
Just a tip, I recommend a low pop community server to start. Preferably with someone to teach you if able or a friend to learn together. Otherwise jump into a high pop and learn trial by fire style... Good luck!

I picked up this game a long time ago at Best Buy because it was on sale for about $10. I had heard great things about it and knew it was a great PC game and I had played a good bit of the original Borderlands and liked it as well. It took me over a year to really sit down and play it a good bit (Note: Gameplay was post Destiny release) I've got to say after playing Destiny fairly heavy for a good week and half, beating the current campaign, all strikes, exploring all the maps to the fullest and finding most gold chests, alot of crucible and achieving 3 pieces of legendary gear, for me Borderlands 2 is the better game by a pretty good margin. There is wayyy more variety in the guns and gear you get on Borderlands not to mention how cool the guns and gear actually look. The more you progress in the game, the cooler the guns look obviously. This didnt seem to be the case in Destiny, you could have a level 1 gun beside a level 20 legendary gun and wouldnt really notice any difference other than the stats of the level 20 item. Also the armor ranging from the world and the other five factions had very little variety at all and didnt seem like something I really wanted to work towards. They always claimed the maps to be so massive in Destiny, and they were for the most part, but after playing Borderlands 2 I quickly found out this game was just as much or more ambitious than the new title with tons of different locations to visit and a good variety of weather and terrain it kept the entire game up to the point im currently at very entertaining. Alot of the locations are also very memorable in Borderlands 2, you can remember when you choose to side with either the irish guys from overlook or the rednecks from the dust map each time you pass through the areas and so many more other things. Another thing is the humor and voice acting in this game is some of the best out there, there are some parts that will seriously make you laugh out loud typically with the rednecks in the game they are pretty hilarious. However in Destiny ive got to say the voice acting was awful, probably the worst thing about the game I couldnt believe from a game with that kind of team and budget that the voice acting was so bad and unimmersive, not to mention there was 0 humor in the game (not saying there wernt attempts) Another thing is the story in Borderlands 2 is so fun and action packed and never gets dry because the characters and locations are changing so often, you may do 3 missions here 2 there and 3 for some other guy before you ever even go back and touch a main storyline mission. This is another thing I like is the game doesnt feel linear whatsoever. You can choose however you would like to play it whether that be knock all the story quests out back to back (which may be hard due to having to continously level your character up for certain parts of the game) or do side missions and explore for loot to make sure your character will be fully adept for the main storyline. In Destiny I really dont even know what the heck went on in that game, I ran, I shot, i took cover, fought some boss that took 45 mins to kill and moved on to the next mission on the planet in which I didnt really know why I was there in the first place other than to try and reach level 20 (Which is the current soft level cap) As much as I wanted there to be a cool story, it just wasnt there in Destiny, however you could look at it as you make your own story with your friends as you play through the campaign in co-op, but who really wants that kind of story? Last thing i'll mention is how long and how much playability there is in both games. I know in Destiny I played the game pretty heavily for 2 days before i beat all strikes and missions and reached the level 20 cap. All i really had left to do was the same missions and strikes or crucible to try and find light armor to continue leveling my character. There was no more story, no more xp, no more anything new, just hopes of finding one more piece of better gear after 4 hours of gameplay, and this is only 3 and 4 days after release?? However in Borderlands 2 i've put in 36 hours in the past week and a half and still have not beaten the game and am level 26 (Soft level cap of 50, 72 after all dlc) I like to play alot of the side quest and have done tons of those to make sure i level enough and to get all of the story. There is just so much to do in the base game alone and thats how it should be honestly, not spanned out through dlc over 10 years. There is a ton of great dlc content for Borderlands 2 which i have not purchases or played yet but viewed some gameplay and it looks like alot of fun, Id like to beat the regular game first before i buy anything extra for the game. I know it may have sounded like I bashed Destiny a little in this review, it was a pretty good game overall despite being repetitive and having almost no story but i figured it would be a good comparative for Borderlands 2 since ive seen so many people compare the two already. I was really stoked for weeks about the release of Destiny and went to the midnight release so im completely unbiased, but ive got to say im kinda done with it. I know there will be alot more dlc to come but I dont think it will change things much other than putting you in a new mass location with more grinding for levels and waves of things to shoot. If anyone is looking for a new fps shoot and loot with great replayability, Pick this up right away (Preferably GOTY edition I wish I had) you wont be disappointed.

So yet another review. I want you to be able to understand my perspective from some of my credentials such as: I was in the military. I work as system administrator now and had contact with countless product companies and every imaginable kind of  department in highly successful companies.
So let's start with a few pros:
- highly complex game with a lot of features other game developers can only dream about.
- intense combat feeling
- can also be a quite relaxing game when you walk through the big variety of nature on the map, make a campfire or go fishing.
- care for detail
- no real competing product with the same complexity
Now for the immense problems and why I don't recommend the game:
- Due to the complexity many features don't work properly.
- False statements about time schedules and deceit about added content in the development, which makes one wonder how high the quality of the endproduct will really be.
- Extremly poor costumer service, non existing internal testing, even downright failing to understand what people are criticising
- bugfixing of important bugs has been extremly slow due to poor management, even considering that underlying technologies are developed there are many signs of sheer incompetence and neglegence.
I am aware that this game has alpha status right now but looking at the 17 years of developing history of BI and that there are the same constant problems with games from BI for 17 years I just don't see how DayZ won't have the same problems we had with future titles like the history of neglect and ignoring major problems and plausible critique from the costumer base.

Undertale is a retro throwback to the old RPG where you explore and meet monsters.
The only difference this game is different is that you have an option to give mercy to these monsters instead of killing them.
This game mixes turn base RPG with a bullet hell aspect that lets you dodge your enemy's attacks instead of letting numbers do thing for you like miss chances and those sorts. Undertale also packs alot of nostalgia, references, comedy and hell lot of emotions for me. One of the main reasons why I love Undertale so much is because of the soundtracks this game has that is wonderful done by Toby Fox that really expresses each of the characters really well. The characters aren't strong on their own but it's because of the soundtracks that come with them really make them stand out and flesh them out well. Every monster's bullet patterns also gives out a personality for the character which is quite a smart decision by Toby Fox to not let narrative do all the job.
This game isn't perfect by any chance but is it worth trying it out and finishing it once? Heck yea! If you like RPG, bullet hell and puns this game is just for you.
If anything this game is best to play blind to have the full experience and just play it your way without anyone telling you what to do.

A combination of first person shooter and role playing game, Borderlands 2 is an addictive mix of genres that will suck away thousands of hours of your time. The cell shading art style is different - but beautiful - and can be removed with a minor tweak in the config files if you want to take it off for a small increase in performance. Removing the cell shading does not detract from the beauty of the game, just changing it slightly.
The storyline, voice work, and pace of the game are all fantastic. And I loved the humour and subtle (and some not so subtle) jokes throughout. Not much else can be said about it without giving too much away.
I would highly recommend purchasing the Game Of The Year edition and playing through the game as each of the characters to explore the differing fight mechanics that come with them. Go in guns blazing as a Gunzerker, or sneak in as an Assassin; the choice is yours. There are a few more characters and others ways to deal with enemies, and those methods will keep you busy for a long time in this game as you explore the world anew each time.
Although many of the side quests are not mandatory, they are recommended to be completed to gain experience to be able to progress through the story missions without having to empty hundreds of rounds of ammo into enemies. If you try to run through the story as fast as possible, you will find yourself coming across enemies many levels above your own, and you will die, a lot.
If you like first person shooters, you'll like this game. If you like 4 player co-op with friends, you'll like this game. And if you want a game that provides a lot of content that is good value for money, you'll like this game (GOTY Edition, anyway).

There is only one viable, fulfilling way to play this game. To run across the entire map so you reach the only 2 or 3 real locations that spawn useful gear/weapons, so that you might actually be able to engage in real combat with other players. Aside from police stations, which only spawn low level firearms, the only locations to aquire any real weapons are military bases. Of which there are only 2 sizeable one. The airfield and tisy, with the airfield being located in the northeast, opposite of all spawn locations, and tisy being located in the far northeast corner, bordering the edge of the map.
On multiple occasions, of which I have just now experienced multiple in a row, I have opened the game to find my character reset back to a basic spawn. M4, fully equipped with magpul parts and an acog, few hundred rounds of ammo, suppressors, military clothing, food, miscellaneous items of various uses, all gone.
As anyone who has sunk a couple dozen hours into dayz would know, Dayz requires a fair bit of grinding to gain any considerably useful eqiupment. If you want more than some a 22 or a handgun, let alone everything else that is needed/extremely useful in game, you have to put in some time. Not a massive problem in and of itself, except for the fact that it seems to basically be a gamble as to whether or not you keep what you earn.
Now I understand there instances where chracters may be forced to reset. Server restarts being one. That did not account for the vast majority of the times this has happened.
It also makes it worse that cars are practically nonexistant. I have not seen one in weeks, and any that I have found have all been missing the required parts. The effort, luck, and time required to actually obtain a working vehicle is nowhere worth it.
When dayz works properly, it honestly can be a great game. The grinding makes those few and rare encounters with other players extremely intense. You really do play this game for hours for what is really just a few seconds, or a few minutes of actual pvp action. I would mention zombies but they are broken, awkward, and simply inconvenient, without actually adding anything of tangible banefit to the game.
All in all, the choice is yours. Everybody will have a different experience, and this game is still in Alpha after all, although that in and of itself is laughable. The problems with it are simply too abundent and intrusive to be disregarded as developmental issues when this game has been out for as long as it has.
But ultimately, just make up your own mind. I for one am always going to be on the lookout for a better zombie/apocolypse/survival game, as it wouldn't take much to top dayz in the state that it is in right now.

Fancy driving around Europe with a bloody great big digger on the back of a lorry? Or maybe 20 tonnes of Potatoes? Then this is the game for you! ETS2 is one of those simulators that gets the balance of being too accurate and not accurate enough just right. You know those train or plane sims where you have to do this and do that before you can even start moving? not here you just hook up a trailer with a single button and off you go. No checking your oil, doing a full vehicle safety check, attaching all the trailer electrics etc. blah blah. Just get trucking out on the huge map. Works nicely with mouse and keyboard but even better with a controller. Loads of customization, parts, paint etc. A calming, enjoyable and strangely addivtive game.

Truck trips around Europe, delivering cargo preferably in time and undamaged is what you are going to enjoy playing this great SCS game.
Good graphics with cool landcapes, wide highways or narrow curvy roads, hearing the game music or, much better, FM streams you can choose.
You begin working with companies trucks but can buy your first truck quickly, with bank loans. The truck dealers are DAF, Iveco, MAN, Majestic, Renault Trucks, Scania and Volvo. You can also improve performance with lots of different parts and, of course, change the visuals. There are many skins to choose from and also some country inspired DLCs.
Then you start to buy more trucks, expand and buy more garages, hire drivers and get rich!
There is a skill system that improves the payment for delivers, for your character and your drivers too.
The developers are constantly adding new trucks and areas, usually via a new DLC.
Great game, highly recommended

First of all I have a lot of hours in this game and have had many different experiences within the game throughout my time playing. One thing I have to warn you about is the pure amount of time you spend running from place to place to get gear or just to meet up with friends. That brings me onto the next thing is that you have to have map knowledge if you want to know where you are going or else you are going to get lost and eventually die. It is also extremely hard to meet up with friends unless you both get a very lucky spawn where you are in the same place.
You will also come across hackers later on up north which kill you in an instant and all that time you spent getting the gear is all gone in a few seconds. The game is also very risky when you go into a "high pop" server and head up north to the military installations. However I didn't run into people as often as my friends did.
Losing gear is so annoying espically when you lose it in an instant when you spent all that time getting it and you can just lose it in a few seconds to very little things like hunger and dehydration or a zombie that made you bleed and you had nothing that could get rid of the bleeding.
However you can get some amaxing moments in the game that I and friends were lucky to experience such as becoming allies with a random stranger that could turn around and shoot you in whenever he/she wanted and take all your gear. Or you could hold someone up and take all theirs. If you look on my scrennshots you can see you get held up a lot and it is very frustrating when it happens.
Overall I do reccommend getting this game but do be prepared to spend a lot of your game time running and walking around. If you have friends that have this game it is a lot better but it is not bad without them and you can still play the game.

Rust is a survival game with a lot of strategic thinking involved, when it comes to PvP survival this game is definely the best out there, but when it comes to PvE this game is seriously lacking. The monthly wipes are extremely demotivating you from playing the game. Once you've figured out to set up a strong defensive base you manage to defend from raids, the game simply decides to wipe everything and lets you start all over. Some people may dislike the fact there aren't any vehicles, or that Rust may be missing some other features they would like to see in survival games, but there's a lot of things they are still planning to add, so keep that in mind.
Only recommended if you are into PvP survival. If you are looking for a PvE survival game I would recommend you to play 7 Days To Die.

You drive a truck for someone else until you make enough money to buy your own.  Then you drive it and make more money which you can use to buy more trucks, hire drivers, and expand your garage. Some additional clothes (we had plenty of clothes in 2014).
Some additional towns (we had penty of towns in 2014).
Zombie hoards? No, and the zombies there are have got worse.
Dogs? No.
Predators? ...Ah, yes! ...De-sync wolves.
Expanded hunting? Nope.
The complex player health system...?  Noo.
Dietry requirements? Non.
Character aging? Nein!
Vehicle Customisation? Nada.
That contagion system kinda thing...? Negative.
Base building? ...Wait... An additional tent. Well whoopy-fricking-doo.
The big change? ...Two additional road vehicles. We had a truck in 2014, they added a bus and a 4x4...There's sea round half of the map, airfields. There's so many possibilities and we've got 3 vehicles which only someone doing a no-lifer has any real chance of getting. I'm about the most tedious gamer out there as far as long-winded missions go but even I can't be bothered looking for a vehicle - running miles to a single spawn point for a slim chance at a find whilst, all the way, trying not to poision yourself by drinking from the jerry can you have to carry in order to fuel it. Yes, the menu makes 'drink' the default action of a can full of petrol. ...In a perma-death game.
Yeah, aside from a few trimmings it's the same game they released over three years ago, gameplay development is non-existent. The team just doesn't seem to have any ideas, imagination, vision... Not the kind needed for a game like this anyway. I think, somewhere along the line, the community got a bit confused (including myself) and thought Bohemia were going to do something amazingly creative with the standalone - push that passion and inventiveness exploding out of DayZ mod further... harder. ...But, no, the truth is it was the modders that made DayZ mod so exciting, Rocket was just the first of them.
So, I think, the Standalone isn't going to be DayZ until the Modders have it, I do though hope it stays alive long enough to reach them. Buy it for the map if you'ew interested, put it to one side when it gets frustrating and then wait for the modders to make a game of it.

A combination of first person shooter and role playing game, Borderlands 2 is an addictive mix of genres that will suck away thousands of hours of your time. The cell shading art style is different - but beautiful - and can be removed with a minor tweak in the config files if you want to take it off for a small increase in performance. Removing the cell shading does not detract from the beauty of the game, just changing it slightly.
The storyline, voice work, and pace of the game are all fantastic. And I loved the humour and subtle (and some not so subtle) jokes throughout. Not much else can be said about it without giving too much away.
I would highly recommend purchasing the Game Of The Year edition and playing through the game as each of the characters to explore the differing fight mechanics that come with them. Go in guns blazing as a Gunzerker, or sneak in as an Assassin; the choice is yours. There are a few more characters and others ways to deal with enemies, and those methods will keep you busy for a long time in this game as you explore the world anew each time.
Although many of the side quests are not mandatory, they are recommended to be completed to gain experience to be able to progress through the story missions without having to empty hundreds of rounds of ammo into enemies. If you try to run through the story as fast as possible, you will find yourself coming across enemies many levels above your own, and you will die, a lot.
If you like first person shooters, you'll like this game. If you like 4 player co-op with friends, you'll like this game. And if you want a game that provides a lot of content that is good value for money, you'll like this game (GOTY Edition, anyway).

No checking your oil, doing a full vehicle safety check, attaching all the trailer electrics etc. blah blah. Just get trucking out on the huge map. Works nicely with mouse and keyboard but even better with a controller. Loads of customization, parts, paint etc. A calming, enjoyable and strangely addivtive game.

Truck trips around Europe, delivering cargo preferably in time and undamaged is what you are going to enjoy playing this great SCS game.
Good graphics with cool landcapes, wide highways or narrow curvy roads, hearing the game music or, much better, FM streams you can choose.
You begin working with companies trucks but can buy your first truck quickly, with bank loans. The truck dealers are DAF, Iveco, MAN, Majestic, Renault Trucks, Scania and Volvo. You can also improve performance with lots of different parts and, of course, change the visuals. There are many skins to choose from and also some country inspired DLCs.
Then you start to buy more trucks, expand and buy more garages, hire drivers and get rich!
There is a skill system that improves the payment for delivers, for your character and your drivers too.
The developers are constantly adding new trucks and areas, usually via a new DLC.
Great game, highly recommended

Many people face the problem with outstanding gameplay bugs and the fact that the game has and still currently been in alpha for the past three-four years, but despite this DayZ is a unique and overall amazing game.
With the setting of a foreign country, during a zombie apocalypse and the fall of mankind, you spawn in an unknown location with nothing but the clothes on your back. Through following your natural instincts to survive by seeking food and water and more loot you face the challenges of hunger, thirst, zombies and other players. While eventually working inland and finding more loot, players and zombies and the risk gets higher but so does the reward of gaining better loot and getting into more PVP. You soon come to realise that you will choose a path of either being a hero or bandit or maybe somewhere in between, the way you play the game differs. You can either choose to be a lone ranger or meet up with either friends or random people and encounter many other players during your experience. You will face many deaths, and go through fits of anger and frustation because of unfair bugs or simply just being killed after working so hard the simple art of the game is to just have fun and stay alive.
Although there are countless bugs in the game that give certain players advantages or even disadvantags in certain circumstances, the game is still highly enjoyable if you can put up with it. Many dislike the game due to these reasons but if you're a survival game enthusiast this is a great game to play.

This game was much better than I thought it would be. Originally I bought ETS 2 to have a relaxing alternative to the racing games I normally play, but at times I found myself playing it more than them.
Graphics are quite detailed and there is quite a bit of scenery to explore. This variety and detail makes long trips fun and interesting. The trucks themselves look good too and there are quite a few customization options available. Gameplay-wise, the trucks are fun to drive. Each truck offers a different driving experience and you will end up finding one that matches your style of driving eventually. Weather effects are solid and day/night transitions look very good.
Creating your own trucking company is fun though I didn't feel that it added that much to the overall experience. At the end of the day this game is simply a truck driving sim, whichever part of your "career" you're at.
I've never driven a real truck, but the ones in this game feel as heavy and reactive (or not) as you expect them to be. Using a wheel is a must for this game. It's just more enjoyable to steer across Europe's highways with a proper wheel in your hands.
Overall, I highly recommend ETS 2 to people who are looking for a slow paced driving game as opposed to the more frantic competitive ones.

I came across this game, like many others, from memes, references, covers of the music ands videos online.
It has such a high rating that I was expected something amazing from this game. Instead I got a boring tedious game with a very childish sense of humor. It was a struggle to make it a half-hour into the game just to leave the ruins. The rest was nearly as bad (with the occasional good character or easter-egg). Maybe it would be different if it wasn't so overhyped for me.
The mechanics are rediculously boring. Many are simply knowing where to position yourself rather than figuring out a pattern, this means it's mainly about wrote memorization rath than any test of skill or pattern recognition. It honestly doesn't feel like a game half the time, but a interractive movie I can't just try to enjoy and focus on. Some of the forth-wall or "established norm" breaking interractions are cool, but not worth playing the game through alone.
The story feels pretenious and pushing morals on you that don't make any sense half the time. The different endings all push you to play the game over again in this meta interraction (which in itself I find really cool), but all towards a "desired" best ending that I feel is the worst by far. There is no real story pregression and every ending except the "right" one pushes you into playing the game again or accepting a loss-condition. This presents in my mind a rediculous linear game that only pretends to allow you to make any choices.
It's like this is supposed to teach you something, but I didn't get it. I don't get why others enjoyed it so much.

Borderlands 2 is primarily a multiplayer experience; while the game can be played single player, and I have done so, it simply is not as enjoyable as when you are playing with another person.
Why? I think the ultimate answer to this is that there is a lot of garbage in the game, and it is easy to get side-tracked and spend a lot of time exploring the (ultimately not that interesting) environment rather than actually playing the game and killing enemies. Ultimately the best part of the game is the various humorous dialogue dispersed throughout the game as you make your way through, and as a result, the faster you go through the game and the less time you spend doing stupid stuff, the more time you actually spend enjoying yourself and the less time you waste on stuff which isn't ultimately that fulfilling.
There is a lot to do in the game, but ultimately the real fun comes out of the humor and out of getting various wacky guns and using them on enemies. The actual game mechanics are fairly mediocre, and only some of the enemies are all that interesting to fight - mostly, the mechanics of the game are just not interesting enough to really pull your interest over other FPS-type games, especially games like the Crysis series.
It's  immature, mindless, juvenile and highly offensive and yet strangely quite fun.

Pretty good game.  Excellent story.  Don't pay any attention to its awful fanbase, or read any reviews or anything about this game.  It's best to go in blind into this game and pay no attention to anything outside of it.

One of the most important morality narratives in games since Bioshock or Spec Ops: The Line, Undertale is the rare breed of game that makes you question why you kill in videogames. It's also charming and fundamentally optimistic, challenging you to be a good person and empathize with your enemy.
The combat system is a frantic, ever-mutating bullet hell that's constantly redefining it's own rules and flipping the script to keep you guessing how to play it. Every enemy is a puzzle to figure out how to make friends and "win". You'll cheer up ghosts that fight you with their tears, and sinister turnips that want you to eat your veggies. It's weird, disarming, and puts a smile on the face of a cynic and softens a hardened heart.
Adding to the feelings-fest is an expansive soundtrack that keeps you tapping your foot or wiping tears from your eyes at many of the games critical moments. Honestly, the soundtrack is an achievement in itself. It's filled with distinctive leitmotifs that are tied to characters and themes, with familiar motifs weaving in and out at just the right time. It's beautifully rendered, and part of the reason I bought the game at full price (which I never do).
All in all, if you want to meet some fun characters who you'll slowly grow to love, and reconsider violence in videogames, Undertale is a must-buy.
Cons: the walk speed is very slow, some of the jokes can be grating, and the enviroment art is basic and/or ugly.

I wish I could say good things about this game but I can't think of anything positive to say. When this game was released in 2013 it was amazing. I spent days playing it with friends, sure it had its quirks but it was honestly enjoyable. Then things went down hill. Every single update now breaks something. It just gets worse and worse. The game has always been "clunky" to play like most arma games but when you add broken mechanics and glitchy enemies on top of a clunky system you get nothing enjoyable. The physics and mechanics of movement are greatly broken for both human players and zombies (but the broken mechanics greatly favor the zombies). It is still nearly impossible to find decent ammounts of food 4 years later, which used to be balanced by easily finding weapons (making the game enjoyable because pvp was actually easy) but now it's also nearly impossible to find guns and ammo too. On top of that your character doesn't retain food and water well either so the difficulty to pleasure ratio never really pays off. It just keeps getting worse. The menu and inventory system used to work flawlessly. Recently they changed the inventory UI and it's terrible. If you're not exact in the menu it doesn't work, and all the great features for helping you manage your inventory don't work anymore either (for example its very easy to accidently drop items now).
I've been trying to give this game a second chance for years now but I'm dissapointed every time. Please save yourself the trouble and don't buy this game. You can litteraly get more enjoyment from burning $35 instead of spending it on this terrible excuse for a game. (Seriously, how is this game not even made it to beta in 4 years?!)
Want my advice? Spend your money on an early access game where the developers are actually listening to the community and care more about the game than the money they're making on it. Rust is a great survival game and the devs actually listen to their players as well as push weekly updates instead of every few months like DayZ.

First and foremost, the game is pretty well polished. Most "Simulator" games come off as pretty cheap and lazy, but you can tell SCS Software really put a lot of time and thought into it. I've never run into any serious glitches, and everything just works the way it's supposed to. My only complaint is the lack of full controller support (I still have to bind a couple of things to keys), which I think they've been working on adding.
The driving itself just feels great. It's very realistic, and the physics are the best I have ever seen in a driving game. The AI of the other drivers recently got an update, so the traffic behaves in a very realistic behavior, and having to account for things like sleeping, fuel, and even using your turn signals properly provides a really satisfying experience. On top of that, the world it gives you to drive around in is absolutely massive. I've played for around 50 hours and have only seen less than 20% of it (I also have the Going East DLC which expands the map).
The actual "game" part of it is actually very well thought-out and fun. If you can make your delivery quickly and without any damage, you'll get more money and XP, and you can level up. Leveling up grants you a point in a handful of different categories, such as the ability to take on longer driving assignments, decreasing your fuel consumption, or earning more money for successful deliveries of different classes of shipment. You can use your money to buy trucks, upgrades, and eventually garages that can accrue their own new truckers that you can send out on driving missions to earn you some extra money.
Perhaps the most brilliant feature is an in-game radio station that can play any music on your hard drive, or any online radio station, while you drive. This makes the experience of the driving even more enjoyable, as you can just sit back, relax, and drive along to your favorite music. It's an excellent idea that I wish more games incorporated.
The visuals are very nice as well. There's a lot of variety in the environments, and they all look beautiful. Everything is very nicely defined with a lot of detail, and the great-looking environments help make the driving feel more like an exciting exploration than a chore. Considering it's one of the most important aspects of the game, SCS really nailed it and made sure the experience never gets boring or tiresome.
The modding community is great. There are a wide variety of mods (My favorite has been a winter mod that made the environments snowy, which I used when I played in winter), and SCS fully supports the community. Mods range from truck skins and sounds to visual and physics enhancements to entirely new areas to drive on the map. I haven't delved too far into the modding scene, but there is a lot of really great stuff the community is doing with the game and they can add a lot. They've even added an online multiplayer component, although I have not gotten to try that out yet.
Last but not least, SCS Soft's continuing support for the game is excellent. More than a year and a half after release, they're still releasing updates that improve the physics, graphics, environments, AI, controller support, and many other things (The next update includes seat adjustment, which is a really crazy thing to think about), all for absolutely free. You can beta test all of the updates before they're out, and the new things that they add in each one are for the most part all very exciting changes, no matter how small. They've added official Oculus Rift support, which I can't wait to try out once I get one of those.
All of these things add up to make Euro Truck Simulator 2 a really special game. It's beautiful, rewarding, satisfying, and most of all - just fun to play. I've put a lot of time into it and I can't wait to put a whole lot more in. Most games don't really hook me anymore like they used to, but starting up ETS2 is an exciting and addictive experience every time. I simply can't recommend it enough.

So I've had this game Since about a week after it's release and played it on multiple accounts racking up 1000's of hours and I reckon it's high time I posted my indepth review so here goes,
Legacy Rust was a huge part of this games charm, the combat system and overall feel of the game and although it's a distant memory way it will always hold a special place in the hearts of the veterans of Rust.
Now for the curren't build you spawn naked, alone on the beach, confused, and here your adventure begins, it is what you make of it and nobody but you decides what you will do as you walk towards the mainland, unless of course a hungry bear decides that you are going to be his next meal if you can't run fast enough.
Rust is a unique game like no other, there are many, many other sandbox games each with their own unique charm that you can almost guarentee that Rust has had some kind of influence on, clones and copies aside it really is a special game, no wipe is the same, one wipe you might build a huge base with all the loot in the world and be the kingpin of the server, other wipes you might find yourself harveseting the dead and cooking it over your campfire to stay alive, Rust's replay value is huge which is why I come back week after week.
Pros:
- Great with friends or solo (although solo can be more challenging)
- Very adaptable mechanics, you can learn quite quickley but there are still little things that improve your gameplay
- Reasonably balanced PvP, all things considered
- Base building and making land yours is incredibly fun
- Multiple ways of raiding other peoples hard earned loot at all ends of the resource scale
- Extremely unique player interactions (Some trash talk but mostly just funny remarks)
- Procedural map generation so no two wipes are the same
- PvE events like the airdrops and Helicopter battles
- Weekly updates from a VERY active and engaging developer who really use the early-access title as it was intended
All things considered Rust has a lot of positive attributes about it that make it a fun and interesting game to play, many of which contribute to why people keep coming back week after week and enjoying the game.
Cons:
- Quite lengthy loading times on lower end machines
- Animal pathing is a bit wonky (This is being adressed in a coming update)
- Lack of Rad animals and other micro-level PvE events (Rad animals being a great feature of Rust Legacy)
- Zerg clans can be a bit frustrating if you are a solo or small group (although this is not a reason to detract points from the game)
- Lower end systems may suffer lag spikes due to the large maps and player-built structures
- New players might feel a bit overwhelmed as the game has no real tutorial
All games have their negitives and drawbacks and Rust isn't perfect by any stretch of the term but Rust really does justice to the term early access, in my opinion if there is a game in EA that you could get behind Rust is that game, weekly updates and very supportive and active developers alongside a fun and banterous community really make this game fun to be a part of, sure there are times I get frustrated and lose all my hard-grafted gear and base but you can guarentee I'll be back on the beach bloodthirsty for revenge come the next wipe.
I couldn't reccomend a game more than Rust to sink hours-days-weeks-years into, and for £15 it's a steal, Grab your rock and torch and let's start our journey.

Cons

Overall if you have friends to play this with, it can be a heart pumping fun experience. BUT by yourself it lacks replayability i think.

Too little too late here.  I "REALLY" wanted to like this game.  I've done everything possible to like this game.  The game is fundamentally flawed at the core when it comes to client server interaction.  The networking mechanics need to be completely ripped out and start over.  There's no excuse for a game like this to have the lag and desync issues 4 years into alpha when you have games like Miscreated that have none of these issues.
The community on Twitch that loved and supported this game has moved on.  All the streamers I used to watch who loved DayZ and were hyped at release and struggled with getting in on day one when the game was released have moved on to other games.  There's nothing more depressing than spending 2 hours running around a huge, empty map and getting geared up only to find one person and die (or trade) due to networking issues.  When you pump 5 rounds into someone's chest at point blank range and they keep firing at you and you die, it's incredibly demoralizing.
The concept of the game is fantastic -- there is no other "survival apocalyptic" game like this anywhere.  But, if it's not fun, it's irrelevant.  And, quite bluntly, it's not fun.
You had a THRIVING and PASSIONATE community that has whithered away to nothing but people getting excited when they find a wolf to fight because at least they found something.  I watched a streamer yesterday who has played since day 1 (and continues to play) say that he was EXCITED when he died because that meant he could switch to another game.
Sorry guys but you released this too early with too many bugs on a too flawed engine and you won't man up and admit that the fundamental framework is a steaming pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥  Take the concept and start over with solid networking code and maybe, just maybe, the community might come back.
But I fear it's still too late for this game.  Wish I could get a refund but I was one of the suckers who bought it day one.

Borderlands 2 is a great fps/rpg hybrid game, and if you like one or both of those game genres you ought to give it a try.  It's fun single player, and more fun multi player.  The only significant problem with multiplayer, in my opinion, is the leveling structure.  If you don't have a character of similar level to the host's, there isn't anything to balance things out.  Maximum level in the version I bought is 61, and you would think the balance problem would be resolved at level cap.  Unfortunately, I don't think either of my kids is likely to ever hit the level cap.
Borderlands has a much bigger world and story than other fps hybrids I've tried, such as Sanctum, Orcs Must Die, and Dungeon Defenders.  It's also got a sense of humor, though occasionally a rude one.  The huge variety of guns available is interesting, but occasionally anoying.  Guns become obsolete as you level, so you're always on the lookout for something useful.  If you outlevel a favorite gun, you can pass it on to a lower level toon.  One of the things I'm looking forward to now that I have one max level toon is getting to actually keep my favorite guns.

Oddly engaging and meditative.  You drive a truck around Europe (well, a greatly reduced imitation of Europe) delivering all sorts of random goods, level your driver up, then head out to deliver more stuff.  That's pretty much all there is to it.  On the surface it sounds incredibly boring and like something that would only appeal to a niche audience, but oddly enough it works.  While the game can be modded to satisfy the hardcore sim fan, the vanilla game is very simple and not at all the kind of in-depth driving sim you might expect.  Once you get used to the controls, driving becomes much easier and eventually you're just sort of "in the zone."  Listen to a podcast or an audio book.  Just chill.  really if I had any complaints about the game it's that there are no in-game guides of any kind on what exactly certain traffic laws are in certain places, so there are occasions where you may find yourself getting tickets for things you weren't expecting.  Maybe this is a glitch, but it seems like driving around central Europe you would have to be a psychopath to get a fine, but the second you set foot (or in this case, set tire) in Britain, you get speeding and lane-change fines up the♥♥♥♥♥♥ yet it is not entirely clear what limits you are breaking.  The only future improvements I would like to see would be maybe tuning up the NPC car AI?

One of the best open world games I've played. This game has a lot of things in it that make it really enjoyable. The characters are well done, especially the voice acting which I think is this game's main selling point. The missions themselves aren't really boring, though at times it can get a little repetitive. The way the missions are introduced make you think of them as objectives. They're practical, unlike some games. If I was to compare it with other games, I would compare it to Dishonored, simply because you have people telling you what to do, and the missions aren't straightforward, if they tell you to do something, you have to find other ways of making it work, which leads to a longer mission.
Compared to Borderlands, this game has visibly better graphics and offers a smoother experience. The leveling system is strange, much like skyrim but only come into effect once you play multiplayer. The perks in skyrim are like the skill points in Borderlands, the main difference is, you automatically get more health.... Don't get me wrong, I think the levelling system rocks! The DLCs are worth buying too, they offer a different experience that feels refreshing.
I found this game pretty addictive, playing it for hours non-stop ever since I bought it. So, even if this game has flaws that you might notice later on in the game, the way the missions are constructed are pretty well done. Borderlands 2 really did make me laugh at times! The simple things count the most, including the little one-liner jokes. Did I mention this game is also violent? Not in a bad way, I think it will fill you with adrenaline and sometimes frustration, as the missions are seriously difficult.
I would rate it 8.5/10.
P.S. Play it with your friends! It's more enjoyable since the missions are lengthy.

This is my first review of a game so far and I can proudly say that I've reached 340 hours on DayZ SA. I have the mod to so I know were DayZ originated from. Lets start from the beginning. DayZ was a mod for Arma 2. Arma is a military simulator game were you're fighting with new military weapons and vehicles. It has large open maps which is mostly based on real life places eg. Chernarus is based on the Chezec republic. DayZ was made by Dean Hall. At the time of Arma 2 it had sale problems were if it wasn't for DayZ. Arma would not have made it to what we now play as Arma 3. DayZ dramatically increased Arma's sales through the roof. Playing DayZ you would have found yourself in a infected world were you struggle to survive, you'll fight infected and other people. I was hooked when I first saw one of Frankieonpcin1018p's videos. I played the Mod up until the gamespy shutdown. I then saw DayZ Standalone and was fascinated by it's more complex survival system and possibilities to do more than just survive. I had high hopes before I got this survival game as some of you also had/have. My hopes were crushed when I saw it wasn't what I was expecting but I didn't give up on DayZ. To say the least, DayZ is just starting and there will be much more to come in 2017 and in the future. There are many negative tags on DayZ and the time it's taking to hit Beta. DayZ has no rules except if you join a private server. You can be a survivor, hero or bandit. They choice is yours and the interactions between players are memorable. DayZ for me is all about how I interact with others and how they interact back. I play the friendly but cautious player.
Pro's: DayZ has a unique survival system with the best interactions between players. You are sometimes forced to do what you wouldn't think you're capable of in real life. It sometimes the things that keep you up at night thinking of that poor soul you lured into a trap and made him do something against his will then killed him, but it's mostly that type of interactions which gives DayZ its silver lining.
Conn's: Its unfinished and is taking long with lots op promises with no rewards. We all get frustrated with the game and want it to be complete without any errors or bugs.
It can't be what we want it to be if we don't give our feedback and full devotion to the DayZ dev team because they got us this far and I don't think that they're gonna drop us just like that. I see potential in DayZ so I hope that you see the light as I do

Been playing DayZ since the mod came out many moons ago (2012), and I'll never forget what it was like the first time I tried it. The feeling of crawling around avoiding the zombies and not knowing what to do or how to defeat them, and slowly mastering how to play the game and fearing neither zombie nor player.
Between all the mods that essentially turned DayZ from a survival-type game into a Arma 2 Wasteland w/zombies game, I lost interest in DayZ. Standalone came out and because of the extremely limited content, I stayed away for quite some time. Every once in a while, I would come back to see what improved, but never really came back for any length of time. When .61 came out, I got back into it. I've found a renewed interest in playing, and playing it now is very fun.
First, you'll see the parade of 12 year olds trotting out to talk about how bad the game is now because they get killed by zombies. THAT'S KIND OF THE POINT. Zombies have been added back in and are once again a threat, just like they were in the early days of the mod, before people added servers where your character starts with a 100rd belt mag and an M249 that shoots completely accurate full auto.
The real star of this game, however, is the stellar survival mechanics they've added. After fumbling around for a while, struggling to find food and with no weapon to defend myself, I figured out that if you can find a rock to make a knife, you can survive for any length of time in the game. I remember a recent character start, where I spawned near a camping ground. I found a stone, crafted a stone knife, and proceeded to make an improvised bow, sharpened sticks for ammunition, and killed a chicken for food and to craft a spear for melee attacks. In fact, most of the time a bow is better than most guns in the game because it's quiet. The struggle to survive is by far the most fun and most important part of this game, and the mechanics added by the devs have fleshed those out into a challenging and entertaining experience.
Has this game been in alpha for almost 4 years? Yes. Have there been a lot of promises the devs haven't fulfilled? Definitely. Was this game really un-fun and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fairly recently? Absolutely.
But, is it fun now? Yes.
Here's hoping that after this turning point back to a fun game, that the devs continue to expand upon what works.

Oddly engaging and meditative.  You drive a truck around Europe (well, a greatly reduced imitation of Europe) delivering all sorts of random goods, level your driver up, then head out to deliver more stuff.  That's pretty much all there is to it.  On the surface it sounds incredibly boring and like something that would only appeal to a niche audience, but oddly enough it works.  While the game can be modded to satisfy the hardcore sim fan, the vanilla game is very simple and not at all the kind of in-depth driving sim you might expect.  Once you get used to the controls, driving becomes much easier and eventually you're just sort of "in the zone."  Listen to a podcast or an audio book.  Just chill.  really if I had any complaints about the game it's that there are no in-game guides of any kind on what exactly certain traffic laws are in certain places, so there are occasions where you may find yourself getting tickets for things you weren't expecting.  Maybe this is a glitch, but it seems like driving around central Europe you would have to be a psychopath to get a fine, but the second you set foot (or in this case, set tire) in Britain, you get speeding and lane-change fines up the♥♥♥♥♥♥ yet it is not entirely clear what limits you are breaking.  The only future improvements I would like to see would be maybe tuning up the NPC car AI?

Borderlands 2 is somewhat of a "generic" FPS game with little care for the story in the sense that you hardly lose anything by muting the game and listening to your favorite choice of music. The game focuses primarily on entertaining you with a cartoonish style of gunfights and a focus on loot and things that go boom.
If you want a visually stunning game with a deep, engaging story (for example, Skyrim) Borderlands 2 is NOT your kind of game. In order to enjoy this game, you need to forget the subpar graphics and any demand for story. The proper use for this game is to relax, let go and shoot stuff.
Borderlands 2 improves on several of the aspects of the original Borderlands that felt lacking. From the simple things like a minimap to different game balancing, Borderlands 2 differentiates itself from the original by having a much greater focus on equipment rather than level.
In the original Borderlands, your level was very, very important in terms of damage output vs. [Insert enemy here]. Going up even a single level had monumental effects on gameplay, to the point where the game felt like you had to go back for that extra level simply because the game didn´t allow you to proceed otherwise. This has been fixed in Borderlands 2 where your power comes mainly from keeping your weapons relevant and up-to-date. This is of no great concern untill the very endgame, so you should have little trouble having the tools required to proceed through the game as you play.
If you are an "average" gamer who just wants to play through the game once or twice, perhaps with your friends, then you will enjoy the experience. The game is semi-supposed to be played in Co-op, and you will find good challenges and the chance to build your characters towards helping each other out (For example, the Siren character can be a healer character, and the Gunzerker can take on a tanking role). If this is your plan, I warn you to stop after the second playthrough unless you and your friends are enjoying the game and prepared for the endgame grind.
Should you now wonder what the "endgame grind" means, let me explain: 1 playthrough is designed to let you reach level 30, and unlocks a higher level of difficulty. This new playthrough aims to leave you at level 50, unlocking yet another difficulty. This third playthrough (This is where it might feel rather tedious) is designed to leave you at level 61, yet you need to reach 72 to be maxed out level-wise. This means you can either reset the story mode and play through it 1-2 times again, or spread it across the DLC packs (Which I reccomend getting by the way!) with some farming for gear towards the high 60s. At level 72, you then have the option of unlocking another 8 levels of difficulty, called "OP Levels". These require almost constant farming to replace gear, as each level ramps up the Health and Damage of enemies by far more than the former difficulties ever did.
In terms of grinding and farming aspects, Borderlands 2 has upped Borderlands by a very large amount. This is largely due to the very long life span of the game compared to the original; Where Borderlands only demanded 2 playthroughs and some endgame farming to reach the max level, Borderlands 2 requires several playthroughs at endgame because the game has had so many more expansions than it has actual content. If you are the kind of person who wants to complete your game by getting to the highest level, both in terms of character, difficulty and equipment, you will find that Borderlands 2 is a game that is in for the long haul. I would personally find a friend who is already max level to help powerlevel you towards the high 50s, as that will probably be when you´ve completed the game a third time and have ~12-15 levels to go before you can begin to unlock the true endgame difficulties. These last "OP Levels" 1-8 especially require a lot of farming for new gear between the levels, with the intensity of the regearing depending on which character you happen to be playing.
All in all, if you need something to enjoy for a week(end) or something to have fun with along with your friends, buy this game and have a buttload of fun. If you can, I reccomend getting the Game of the Year edition, which gives you all the DLCs and level upgrade packs, which you will find are well worth the slight price increase.
Slight edit: I realise this review is semi-short compared to all the things can be discussed. This review is mainly aimed at a potential buyer who is on the fence, not for someone who wants to know exactly what they are buying.

I haven't been playing this game for very long, but I am really enjoying it so far and can definitely see many more hours ahead of me soon. ETS2 is a very relaxing, enjoyable, challenging and therapeutic game with so much to do and so many things to achieve. The concept is incredibly simple but as an actual game it works so well, it is difficult to explain why it's so fun, but just is!
You start off as a cargo truck driver for hire, doing small or large jobs for money so that you can form your own business with your own fully customisable trucks in a beautiful realistic environment. The cities and routes are not 100% accurate and not as long (that would be ridiculous) but it doesn't matter. There is still hundreds upon hundreds of hours of game play on offer and fantastic scenery all around the developers vision of Europe in this amazing simulator.
This time last year, I would have said that I do not understand how a truck simulator could be any fun as ever since I was a child I have questioned the fun factor of simulation games, but I am so glad that I spent £7.50 for the collection (ETS, ETS2, Bus Driver, Trucks and Trailers, Scania Truck Driving Simulator and plenty of DLC for ETS2), an absolutely amazing bargain.  Some of the best money I have ever spent and I have only played the one game of the collection so far!
ETS2 is worth every penny, so if you see it even cheaper than it's full retail price pick it up and you won't regret it. For the sake of £3.75, you should just buy it anyway!

Borderlands 2 is a great fps/rpg hybrid game, and if you like one or both of those game genres you ought to give it a try.  It's fun single player, and more fun multi player.  The only significant problem with multiplayer, in my opinion, is the leveling structure.  If you don't have a character of similar level to the host's, there isn't anything to balance things out.  Maximum level in the version I bought is 61, and you would think the balance problem would be resolved at level cap.  Unfortunately, I don't think either of my kids is likely to ever hit the level cap.
Borderlands has a much bigger world and story than other fps hybrids I've tried, such as Sanctum, Orcs Must Die, and Dungeon Defenders.  It's also got a sense of humor, though occasionally a rude one.  The huge variety of guns available is interesting, but occasionally anoying.  Guns become obsolete as you level, so you're always on the lookout for something useful.  If you outlevel a favorite gun, you can pass it on to a lower level toon.  One of the things I'm looking forward to now that I have one max level toon is getting to actually keep my favorite guns.

Been playing DayZ since the mod came out many moons ago (2012), and I'll never forget what it was like the first time I tried it. The feeling of crawling around avoiding the zombies and not knowing what to do or how to defeat them, and slowly mastering how to play the game and fearing neither zombie nor player.
Between all the mods that essentially turned DayZ from a survival-type game into a Arma 2 Wasteland w/zombies game, I lost interest in DayZ. Standalone came out and because of the extremely limited content, I stayed away for quite some time. Every once in a while, I would come back to see what improved, but never really came back for any length of time. When .61 came out, I got back into it. I've found a renewed interest in playing, and playing it now is very fun.
First, you'll see the parade of 12 year olds trotting out to talk about how bad the game is now because they get killed by zombies. THAT'S KIND OF THE POINT. Zombies have been added back in and are once again a threat, just like they were in the early days of the mod, before people added servers where your character starts with a 100rd belt mag and an M249 that shoots completely accurate full auto.
The real star of this game, however, is the stellar survival mechanics they've added. After fumbling around for a while, struggling to find food and with no weapon to defend myself, I figured out that if you can find a rock to make a knife, you can survive for any length of time in the game. I remember a recent character start, where I spawned near a camping ground. I found a stone, crafted a stone knife, and proceeded to make an improvised bow, sharpened sticks for ammunition, and killed a chicken for food and to craft a spear for melee attacks. In fact, most of the time a bow is better than most guns in the game because it's quiet. The struggle to survive is by far the most fun and most important part of this game, and the mechanics added by the devs have fleshed those out into a challenging and entertaining experience.
Has this game been in alpha for almost 4 years? Yes. Have there been a lot of promises the devs haven't fulfilled? Definitely. Was this game really un-fun and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fairly recently? Absolutely.
But, is it fun now? Yes.
Here's hoping that after this turning point back to a fun game, that the devs continue to expand upon what works.

if you like emergent gameplay, endless replayability, mmo, survival horror all in a huge open world then this is your game. its been a long time coming, the game is still in EA after 4 years and probabaly not even close to finished, but the game is unique and immersive as is. From the beginning player interaction has been the core element of this game, but as of .61 and the implementation of the new spawn system and AI, the infected are finally a force to be reckoned with. Along with the addition of wolf packs and a revamped temperature system, the survival aspect of the game is finally catching up. There are few other games that can put youy on the edge of your seat like this one. whether its creeping through a backyaard hoping the zed standing a few feet away doesnt turn around, dodging bullets from a bandit posted up on a rooftop, or going on an adventure with some good friends, this game will draw you back again and again, and every playthrough will bring something new. Alot of people who try the game will quit because of the stiff learning curve, the bugs, or just because they really suck at the game and cant handle dying 5 times in a row as a bambi from KOS (we have all been there, suck it up). the game is harsh, especially as a fresh spawn, but once you sink some hours into it and get the hang of keeping your head on a swivel and always staying on the move, the rest falls into place. I highly suggest you get this game, and if you fail miserably dont be discouraged. when you do get the hang of it i promise you an experience you woint find anywhere else. I hope we bump into each other in the wasteland, just be on your best behavior because ill see you before you see me

A extraordinary game. I doubt anyone could've predicted what kind of amazing journey they started when they first played the game, a game that, on first sight, looks like any other 2D pixel game, and would more likely remind you of pacman or snake than the kind of adventure it turns out to be, wich is, simply put, astonishing. The soundtrack, oh yes that soundtrack, completely composed by a singular mind, and it's absolutely beautiful, the music of this game is just as important as the story behind it. I don't think there's a way to verbally explain how good this game is, the only way for someone to understand is to buy the game themselves and go on this amazing journey in the underground.
A truly astonishing perfectly made game, 10/10 recommend you play this, and that fills me with...
D E T E R M I N A T I O N.

People at first may see this game as a horrible, cruel, violent, psychopathic, rage inducing, sleep preventing, pornographic, time inducing game. But really, it's a fun environment for the whole family to enjoy from the age of three upwards!
Don't be thrown by reviews and videos of naked men and women running about with rocks, for this is only part of the fun. Plus, if you like (which I doubt you would) you can enable a blur to be placed in front of the naked men and women's genitalia.
Of course there will be the occasional hacker, just like with every game out there; but Facepunch are doing their best to eliminate these people from the toxic rust community with weekly updates. Did I just say toxic? I meant friendly.
This game takes a lot of time to master, it also takes a lot of time in general to do anything within the game. So this game is for people with a lot of time on their hands and have reached the patience equal to that of a monk.
The base building is also a pain to master also, ranging from a twig material to an armoured one. Over time you'll find yourself being raided a lot, but also being able to learn from where you went wrong and how to improve on your base design. The base building in this game is literally a trial and error but there are some very good tips for new players on YouTube.
The optimisation of this game isn't the best, but what can you expect from an early access game? Besides, even at the most basic graphic settings, the game still looks beautiful.
Did this game make me rage? No.
Did this game cause me to break things I own? No.
Did I die a lot? No.
Did I make new friends? No.
Did I have fun throughout the whole Rust experience? Of course.
Overall, this game is not for the faint hearted. You will die, a lot. You will rage, a lot. But this game is honestly, in my opinion, a 1/10 and I can't get enough of it.
