Journal Entry 1
Its my first day running my new company "Marauder Trucking" I took out a huge loan from the bank scored myself a sick looking Volvo truck, im ready for action.
Journal Entry 2
I'm new to driving a vehicle with this many gears and new to shifting manually with a clutch but I think I got it under control.... then I back up straight into the side of a small van... so no im not under control.... I've now damaged my truck to 8% and cost myself a pretty penny for the accident..... But hey we all gotta learn sometime right?
Journal Entry 3
After driving around my small property parking lot and learning my gears I decide to venture to the populated streets! I backup (this time checking my mirrors) and carefully pull onto the street. I'm now happily driving among the traffic of Europe! The drivers a slow and waiting at lights is a pain in the rear...but... alas this is my life now ...
Journal Entry 4
I have picked a mission to haul a load of heavy machinery across the countryside. I drive to my location, which happens to be a nice little farm with very tight corners and fences. I see my load waiting between two other loaded trailers, this looks like a tight fit. I attempted backing up several times not getting it right, I'm sure the farmer and his wife were either giggling inside their house or regretting not hiring a better driver. I finally get latched on and give a sigh of relief, I pull out of the space and very gently make my turns while trying not to stall out. Although its tight maneuvering I am able to escape Vincent's Smoked Meats!
Journal Entry 5
Now on the road I get to enjoy the beautiful countryside and shake my fist at the slow and dangerous drivers around me.... it begins to get a bit darker and a light rain starts, I almost drive my truck off the road twice trying to turn on my headlights and windshield wipers but were all good. I'm now cruising down the road at a gentle 70 and things are good....uh oh.....I can see a line of cars piling up behind me so I better pick up the pace... This was a poor decision on my part...
Journal Entry 6
Now thinking back... in the best interest of other drivers I should have just stayed the speed I was going.... but I did not. I got far to generous with the gas pedal and shifting, ended up pumping my truck up to around 120. This speed was great, I was making good time, I didn't have a line of cars behind me.... but I didn't account for sharp corners in my equation. I came whipping up to a corner thinking... ok ill just tap the brakes and slow down a bit.... well its wet on the road.... its a sharp corner... I got it down to about 98 when i hit the corner and suddenly my world started to become slightly off center...
Journal Entry 7
Now that my truck is laying on its side I've learned a key element about gear reduction to control speed as well as "when to" and "when not to" apply the brakes. I had missed my corner by lots...I had not taken into account the grade % of the road and I rolled it and slid for a long distance... it was quite scary......After my truck is up righted from the long skid on its side im now looking at 72% damage, the truck sounds like a blender full of ball bearings and the lights flicker.... that's totally normal right? ...
Journal Entry 8
Ok the truck sounds terrible but it still drives... Its got horrible turning now and 3 of my gears are non existent... I'm still about 2 (game hours) away from my destination. I am able to drive for about 45 mins before the truck really starts to have...issues... I was driving along at my new cautious speed of 50 and suddenly my truck turns off.... great no power steering so my wheel locks up and its like trying to steer a dead whale with a pool cue....not working well.... but I'm able to get it to the side of the road safely.
Journal Entry 9
I am able to start the truck again and drive another while before it turns off again. I'm now only 20 mins away from my destination and im not giving up... if its the last thing I do im getting this load to its destination. I've now cranked this thing over enough times that I could probably forge a blade on the starter.... but luck has it that the final stretch into town is all down hill....yay!..... throw it in neutral and coast into the city... I blast my horn and coast powerlessly through red lights, dodging traffic and jumping curves. I look like a boat without a crew heading directly for the shore.
Journal Entry 10
I can see the building! I'm almost there! .. I'm coasting much much slower now that the terrain has leveled out, The truck won't even start now its toast, im about 30 feet from the buildings entrance and moving at a speed of about 5-7... Old ladies with walkers are getting better torque ratios then my truck. I finally land right next to the door, Unable to start the truck im not going to be able to back it in manually so we will take a gimme on this load.... this may be bad for my business but I can personally suggest you don't hire anyone from "Marauder Trucking"

If you haven't played Undertale yet - I would love to know why.
In a flurry of fanfare and support, this game really has taken the heart of everybody who has played it.
But if you're not familair, you might notice it's exact predecessor - Earthbound.
Toby Fox, the creator of Undertale, previously made a Earthbound Halloween mod, a whole new story using the world of Onett and Twoson.
This would be the prototype to what is clearly his magnum opus - Undertale, a clever and thoughtfull little game that eschews the normal mechanics of RPGs, not only commenting on the games we all play - but subverting those ideas to move you.
I am a sucker for meta-joke, meta-narrative and all things that reference themselves.  But this uses all those clever tricks behind the scenes to really punch home a narrative about connection, love and trust.
I don't want to ruin the game, but I reccomend you give it a try. It's a short and cheep game - but I garuntee these characters will stay long after you've deleted your save file and moved on to kill the next batch of electronic friends.

I got Rust after reading about it, and I wanted to see if it was as much a sociopathic experience as I had been led to believe.
Oh, it was.
The fact is, Rust is typical of games like 'Day Z' and other 'Open World Survival Games' that have promoted early access and have yet to establish groundwork, evolving between server wipes. There is a great deal of Rust which focuses on resoruce gathering and that stuff, but it really boils down to your ability to find a group (preferrably large) and then murder the hell out of anyone else during raids. Yep, you learn how to build, etc, but it doesn't matter - You cannot go it alone in Rust for very long, and even your allies will eventually either get fed up and quit or you will.
There are good things about Rust - I said it was familiar to Day Z, but I think it takes those elements and builds in more survival and on one level it forces you to cooperate in situations you wouldn't want to. Rust's receipe system is okay, I've seen better, but Rust handles it well. Combat is attrocious and cheating remains a big issue. Aimbot city at some points, reminding me of the aborted APB launch on how many people at one time or another use aimbots or a few other cheats. This is the biggest issue - It's never about survival or combat, and neither matter when you're dealing with the uncertainty of what you do and people whose only goal is to eat you....which actually happens with surprising frequency.
So, until Rust is fully supported and released, I can't really recommend it. I like a lot of the ideas about it, but I get frustrated with the combat system, the survival mechanic, and the cheating in it. You're better off with something else, but hey, that's my opinion

This game has a lot to offer, it is good in so many vital aspects that I was willing to overlook the miniscule flaws that the game had.
Pros:
1) VERY VERY customizable - This isn't one of those games where there is an "optimal" build or "best" weapons that everyone should follow. Every skill and character has its pros and cons and every weapon is different. You will find yourself ACTUALLY looking for a character, build, and weapon that suits your playstyle. I emphasize this a lot because I know for most games out there, theres always that one dominating class with a specific build and specific best weapon. But Borderlands 2 is different, you WILL NEED to find a path that suits your playstyle.
2) Good storyline - Characters are pretty well made and storyline flows smoothly. I also like that they implement a big humor factor in the storyline so it doesn't feel so serious. However, there isn't much character development, but that isn't really what Borderlands 2 is about and it never bothered me. Plus, the voiceovers are very impressive and well done.
3) Online play is fun, most the Borderlands 2 online community is helpful (from my experience) and overall enjoyable to play with. It also flows smoothly so lag was never an issue for me.
4) Lots of fun sidequests to do if you're bored.
5) Huge amount of weapons, plus they are fun to obtain and compare. When i first started this, I thought it would be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥to be constantly switching weapons and stuff, but no, I found it very enjoyable to actually pause the game a lot of compare items and shields and etc.
6) Large collection of enemys, you won't be fighting the same things over and over again so that isn't a problem.
7) You might think after the first playthrough "wow I have to play the same game again? That sucks", but no, even though the storyline is the same, everything else is different, the weapons, the enemys, etc. I had no problem enjoying the second playthrough.
Cons:
1) After getting very far into the game (like near end of 2nd playthrough and 3rd playthrough) the enemys get REALLY tough and playing alone isn't that enjoyable anymore, you'd pretty much HAVE to play with friends.
2) The level system is very flawed in my opinion. Basically, your power level as well as the enemys power level drastically alters for every level gap. For example, if you're level 40, a level 43 enemy would be VERY difficult to kill, and a level 40 mission would be way to easy for a level 43. Also, you have to CONSTANTLY change weapons due to the fact that the weapon level gaps are drastic as well. For example, at level 20, your level 18 weapon is pretty much completely useless. I know I said I liked switching weapons but this flaw has a huge impact on the replay value of the game (I don't really want to start a new character because I know i'll spend most the time switching weapons around. It would be cool if weapons can level up with you, so you don't have to constantly change weapons as you level  (especially at the early levels).
3) Minor flaw with death, for example, i've killed bosses, but died afterward because it charged an attack right before I killed it and the attack killed me and because I died, I wasn't able to listen to the characters speak because the death ended the voiceovers. This is pretty much a very minor flaw but it did ruin some parts of the game bigtime for me.
Overall
A must buy for people who enjoy fps and co op games, even great for people who just want to play alone. I'd say even if you just want to play the storyline out once, it's still worth the money. You definitely get the bang for your buck in this game (especially if you get it on sale, it's pretty much a steal).

Let's get this out of the way right away; I don't think Borderlands 2 is a bad game. I do, in fact, think I got my money's worth of enjoyment out of it.
The problem is that the enjoyment doesn't actually last. The first time through the story, it's thoroughly-enjoyable. The twists are a genuine surprise and get you thoroughly-invested in the goal of "smash in Handsome Jack's ugly face". The problem is that the game expects you to be equally-eager to go through the exact same story a second time on a harder difficulty. Let's be perfectly honest, a story that depends on surprise twists can't possibly be as enjoyable when you already know the twists, but Borderlands 2 seems to have skipped that session of Storytelling 101. The cathartic pleasure of mutilating Handsome Jack isn't worth going through all of that effort a second time. And then it expects you to do it all again a third time. And if you make another character, then a fourth time, and a fifth, and sixth. And the story just isn't compelling enough to enjoy a second time, never mind a twelfth.
This isn't helped by the fact that on the harder playthroughs, enemy health and damage scales exponentially-faster than yours, such that even with a combined total of nearly a million health and shields, you can be killed in about five hits while every single enemy soaks up bullets like a redneck soaks up cheap whiskey.
Even with the DLC packs, you still have to be on your third playthrough before the "loot" part of the "shoot and loot" part of the game kicks in. Actually, scratch that; I'm not sure the "loot" part ever really kicks in. Compounding the problem of "linear players, quadratic NPCs", nearly every single item that drops can only be classified as "vendor trash", perhaps only worth keeping because of a marginal improvement over the vendor trash you're already equipping for lack of anything else to use. Occassionally you'll get your greasy mitts on something that's worth keeping on its own merits - maybe a grenade mod that homes in after you throw it and melts victims with acid - but you have to kill thousands upon thousands of Jason Voorhees'es before that happens.
If you can get the entire game, DLCs included, for about £20 or your local equivalent thereof, and you liked Diablo back in the day, then you'll probably find enough here to give you your money's worth. Otherwise - avoid.
I'm making an edit here to include something that I hadn't considered before; all of the above is based on my experience playing alone. Sometimes I did get to play the game with friends, and when that happens it's a lot more enjoyable - I can't explain why. If you can reliably set up a group, then the game should be fun for you. If your ability to play multiplayer with friends is sporadic, though, then the game is just a grind.

Borderlands 2 is the sequel to the popular first-person co-op action adventure game Borderlands. Developed by Gearbox Software and published by 2K games, it uses the formula which made the first game good and expanded it in astronomical proportions. The game promises larger maps, expanded co-op play, new classes and most importantly, procedurally generated items resulting in an almost infinite weapon & item variation.
The story picks up after the events of the first game. Hyperion Corporation headed by Handsome Jack has arrived on Pandora, stolen the Vault Key and is driving the inhabitants to near extinction. The Vault Hunters from the first game (Roland, Lilith, Mordecai, & Brick) has gathered what was left of the Crimson Lance and reorganized them into the Crimson Raiders to stop Handsome Jack. The player takes control of a new set of Vault Hunters in their quest to help the Crimson Raiders stop Hyperion from opening a second Vault and unleashing a sleeping monster within.
+ Cell-shaded textures that works well with the art style of the game
+ Great voice acting and characters, most notably, Handsome Jack
+  Expanded world which is almost 3 times larger than the first game
+ New classes with new skills that are fun to play
+ Entering and inviting for Co-op play is simple and easy
+ Improved story from the first game with well paced missions
+ Re-playability. The fun does not end after the final boss! There are new unlockable modes and expanded  adventure with...
+ Quality Story DLC that adds several hours of game time per DLC campaign
+ A lot of guns. “87 Bazillion Guns” as claimed by Gearbox
+ Improved enemy AI that goes well with...
+ Enemy Variety. Fight of bandits, robots, worms, armoured spiders, flying monsters and a whole lot more, each requiring the player to adapt by changing play-styles.
+ Substantial amount of unlockable Character customization
+ Good use of Physx for the benefit of PC gamers
- Texture pop-in. Mostly noticeable when entering the game or entering a new area
- Loot sharing needs to be improved since ninja looting is a concern for most players
- In-game voices and messages, even story related ones, can overlap each other. New messages will cancel out any playing messages which is very annoying if your trying to immerse yourself in the story.
- No ECHO (in-game voice message) replay like the first game. Once a voice-over message given by an NPC is overlapped, there is no way to listen to it again, aside from starting a new game plus.
- Some DLC maps have glitches
and with a good blend of first-person shooting action, coupled with the progression and quest system of an RPG and all the fun and excitement of co-op play.
I RECOMMEND this game to anyone looking for a fun coop experience with their buddies or story oriented gamers who likes an immersive experience.
Although the game is well worth it's full price, I would still recommend this to be bought on SALE because of how often this title get discounted and by the sheer amount of DLCs available.

Here is my review of Borderlands 2. In all honesty this is my opinion and you shouldn't be take this too seriously. This is from my experiences with the game.
Borderlands 2 while being a "Loot em up" is surely a LOOT EM UP. With over 100+ hours of gameplay the game will surely give you tons of playtime, but here are the downsides.
Gameplay: 7.5/10
While the game is fun, it does get tedious (boring) after a while, constantly running back and forth between missions is a hassle, and if you are even 2 levels higher than other players, then be prepared to have a rough time. The game is balanced if everyone is the same level but if you have a level 23 going into a level 25 lobby, then the level 23 will get floored a lot. Speaking off of levels, the loot system in this game is alright, while you still have the essentials such as: the weak pistol, the OP rocket launcher, etc. But after a while its the same loot you got in that crate an hour ago, so then you proceed to run to the nearest store to sell your garbage weapon.
Music/Audio: 9/10
This game provides a great soundtrack and one of the funniest dialouge lines ever. Borderlands 2 trys to take itself seriously, but the humor is too much, leaving you laughing for a while. Every area has its own unique dialouge line that maybe different everytime you play.
Presentation: 8/10
The game still has the cartoonyish graphics frrom Borderlands 1, but it can still be breathtaking. While at some moments you may have a rendering issue, this is due to either moving to fast or a small glitch.
Overall score: 8/10
While I enjoyed Borderlands 2 for some time, it didn't appeal to me once its flaws showed up, however if you look past these you can see Borderlands 2 has a lot of potential, and while being nominated for GOTY a couple of times, there is no reason why you shouldn't buy 3-4 copys and play with some friends.

I have never played the original Borderlands. I decided to play Borderlands 2 to see what this franchise is like. I first noticed the cel-shaded graphics and a diverse number of characters to choose from. After I chose my protagonist (Gunzerker) I had to get used to the skill trees, the wacky characters, the large number of side missions in addition to the main story missions. One of the wackiest characters is Claptrap, a robot with something to say all the time and is quite delusional.
The story is set in Pandora, a planet filled with vicious creatures of all kinds. The planet is control by Handsome Jack, the main antagonist of the game. As you progress through the game you will regularly hear Handsome Jack’s speak sarcastically about your goal to bring him down. There are many Echo recorders that will help flesh out the story and who Handsome Jack really is.
The script and voice acting in Borderlands 2 is nothing short of superb. The voice actors and script writers should be highly commended for making the characters such as Scooter, Moxxi, Claptrap and others very entertaining. The only problem I found with the voices was that some conversations can be interrupted by other conversations before you can hear them completely. However, it’s not such a bad thing for the game overall.
There is plenty to explore and if you’re into exploring as much as possible, Borderlands 2 will entertain you for 100+ hours. Each sector of the map has its own environmental feel and its own creatures. The DLCs add even more content for you to explore, but you are best advised to advance your character to at least level 20 because the enemies are much tougher than those enemies in the main story. The DLCs are divided into chapters and side missions while the battles with tougher creatures will reward you with lots of experience points. The side missions in the main game are definitely worth pursuing, as they include puzzle elements and some very simple goals such as simply shooting someone in the face in the side mission titled “Shoot This Guy in the Face.” Other side missions require you to find certain items to receive a unique weapon such as the side mission titled “The Lost Treasure”, a mission that requires you to find different parts of a treasure map. The parts can be anywhere in a region, but the payoff is huge in the form of a very powerful pistol.
Part of what makes Borderlands 2 great in gameplay is the diverse availability of weapons, shields, grenade mods, class mods, and relics. Class mods and relics have ways of enhancing your character’s combat abilities. The inventory feels a little clunky, but once you get used to it you can navigate it pretty quickly. The inventory is important for using in the various vending machines for buying ammo, selling ammo and streamlining.
Respawning is an integral part of this game, as enemies will respawn when you return to the same sector. It may feel tedious after a while, but it can be rewarding because these are opportunities to gain more experience as you try to reach the level of 50. To max out your character you will have to complete the normal mode in order to open up the True Vault Hunter Mode. It is important to know the strengths and weaknesses of enemies so that you know which weapons and ammo work best against them. For example, the loaders (mechanical bots) are vulnerable to corrosive ammo. Therefore, it is best to use a corrosive weapon to kill them faster. The crystallisks are hulking creatures with shins that are made of brittle crystals. Shooting their brittle shins is the only way to bring them down.
This game encourages cooperative play, so it can be fun playing with friends. However, it is better to play with friends who are at a level close to yours, although the game automatically balances the difficulty according to the levels of the players. It is a great feeling trying to heal fellow players in dire times. The unusual feature of death is interesting because there is a chance to achieve a second wind if you get a kill while you’re dying and the red meter is going down to zero.
I found the save system awkward since it saves everything that happens. If you leave the game while in the middle of a mission, you will have to pick up where you left off and the enemies you killed will respawn. In essence, the save system consists simply of save and quit.
Borderlands 2 is one of the most entertaining role-playing games with so much to explore. The gameworld is thriving with loot and opportunities to reap the rewards of doing favors for other townsfolks. I highly recommend this game to anyone as it will take many, many hours of your time and those hours will feel worth it.

UT things, like Urinary Tract Infection, are mostly bad (yes, I know it's a UTI thing, but shut up). Then a special man brought us a good UT thing. This man is called Toby Fox. Toby Fox began with a question, a question that ruptured the very fabric of RPGs. "What if there was a RPG," Toby thought, "that allowed you not to hurt a soul?" Then it was built up, through code and thought. Think of it as a child, they could be innocent but also become vile, like a bully. This "child" was Undertale. Undertale is a RPG where you don't have to be a hunter and a deer trying to live it's life. Like a hunter, they try to kill the deer, but maybe you thought the hunter would leave the deer alone. Think of yourself as a hunter, hunting different deer, and you're guided by Undertale. Undertale, as a child, would say that you should leave the deer alone. That is your choice, you may think, but it's a child. Let me ask you personally, would you kill the deer or will you listen to Undertale and give in to the innocent child's nature? I think I mostly hear you claiming to spare the deer, I mean, think of it's characteristics. It's peaceful, and you shouldn't bother it. That's just an example, and it's not over. In Undertale, you meet a variety of characters, and the first two you meet are clear definitions. You know who I'm talking about. Sans and Papyrus are skeletons, and they're brothers. Papyrus is a fun, spaghetti-loving fan favorite. Sans is a fan favorite too, and if you dare go bad but spare him, well, he prefers his Dunkin Donuts with a little sweet flavor. Although if you're going to bag the deer, you shouldn't forget how funny Sans is. Really, Sans seems to be a little COMICal, right?
. Sans also has a knack for helping his brother out with puzzles, and he thinks his brother is cool. Whether or not he thinks Papyrus is cool, you can't forget how Papyrus constantly fails but constantly tries to get you captured from his puzzling traps. However, these characters can die if you decide to paint yourself red and get all HORN-y. Now, I believe I'm finished with characters, BUT we're just getting started on the book. So, to briefly describe the game's story without spoilers, I think this will be legit. So after a war between the locked-up monsters and the victorious hoomans, a child with a name falls and meets different characters from Flowey to the King. The child decides to go evil/good by sparing/killing monsters which is fun. Then after some funtime, the child makes it to the surface after facing some bosses. END!!! Now that you heard that, let me tell you Undertale's overall. Undertale is one of those games that will be remembered throughout time, and that's why I nominated it for the "Most Heartwarming Game" Award during the Steam Award Nominations. What I ask of you, if you enjoyed the game, is to also nominate it for "Most Heartwarming Game". If you don't, then that's your choice. Think of this as a favor between fellow strangers on the internet united by god-like Undertale over here. Also, if you agree with this entire review, comment any Sans pun down below. I bet you, these puns will sure be a PUN-ch to the FUNNY BONE.

I feel this game has received many UNFAIR negative reviews.  The reality of those reviews is this: those people bought this game expecting a finished product.  This product IS STILL IN ALPHA.
I bought this game when the pre-release was first issued.  I can tell from experience that at that point in the build it was atrocious and unplayable.  I got back into it 2 months ago, and MAN HAS THIS GAME GOTTEN GOOD!!
At this point, the game is about ready to enter the Beta testing period (which is the point when I would have access to a "pre-release" game in the past...  This is the first "alpha" I've ever been involved with).  During the Alpha they've focused primarily on gameplay issues, when the beta starts they will begin to refine other bugs in the game.
The reality is, most games are too simple and boring to keep me interested.  This one is not..  It's complicated.  It's EASY TO DIE, and not from players...  This is a survival game.  It's not fast paced.  The map is HUGE, and currently there are no vehicles... but I believe they will be back in one or two updates (and they will make the experience much more pleasureable... being able to actually get somewhere in a reasonable amount of time).
New players will find the zombies and environmental obstacles a deadly challenge..  but as you play, you will realize the only real threat are other humans in the world.  They are smart, they will kill you for your stuff.  They are OTHER PLAYERS.  They are also just trying to find stuff to survive.
This game represents a great framework for a really open-ended roleplay type environment.  Most public-hive servers do not represent this gameplay mechanic... Too many "CS:GO" or "CoD" types are in the environment, making this for the most part a FPS.  It is MUCH MORE INDEPTH than just an FPS...  but many of your experiences in highly populated servers will be PvP with other players...  if this is not your style, you may have to join a private hive server that has rules and regulations that can be enforced by server admins.
Really, IMHO, the biggest drawback of this game is the incredible limitations placed upon server administrators by Bohemia Interactive.  You can ONLY purchase server hosting through an approved provider, and due to the agreement BI has with those providers (basically, they have to host 50 public servers free to be considered a hosting provider...) the costs for "public" infrastructure are absorbed by individuals who are interested in renting their own servers...  Servers that you can't ban people from for being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥or not following administrative rules for the server...  As far as I'm concerned, IF I'M paying for a service I should have the authority to restrict access to those I see fit; period.
If you decide to get this game, feel free to join my public hive server "Bittercup's Domain" if you're looking for a "friendly" place to play ;-).  The regulars are friendly anyway, the clans and kiddies just jumping in to loot high value military targets will probably just KoS lol.

Here is my review of Borderlands 2. In all honesty this is my opinion and you shouldn't be take this too seriously. This is from my experiences with the game.
Borderlands 2 while being a "Loot em up" is surely a LOOT EM UP. With over 100+ hours of gameplay the game will surely give you tons of playtime, but here are the downsides.
Gameplay: 7.5/10
While the game is fun, it does get tedious (boring) after a while, constantly running back and forth between missions is a hassle, and if you are even 2 levels higher than other players, then be prepared to have a rough time. The game is balanced if everyone is the same level but if you have a level 23 going into a level 25 lobby, then the level 23 will get floored a lot. Speaking off of levels, the loot system in this game is alright, while you still have the essentials such as: the weak pistol, the OP rocket launcher, etc. But after a while its the same loot you got in that crate an hour ago, so then you proceed to run to the nearest store to sell your garbage weapon.
Music/Audio: 9/10
This game provides a great soundtrack and one of the funniest dialouge lines ever. Borderlands 2 trys to take itself seriously, but the humor is too much, leaving you laughing for a while. Every area has its own unique dialouge line that maybe different everytime you play.
Presentation: 8/10
The game still has the cartoonyish graphics frrom Borderlands 1, but it can still be breathtaking. While at some moments you may have a rendering issue, this is due to either moving to fast or a small glitch.
Overall score: 8/10
While I enjoyed Borderlands 2 for some time, it didn't appeal to me once its flaws showed up, however if you look past these you can see Borderlands 2 has a lot of potential, and while being nominated for GOTY a couple of times, there is no reason why you shouldn't buy 3-4 copys and play with some friends.

I have never played the original Borderlands. I decided to play Borderlands 2 to see what this franchise is like. I first noticed the cel-shaded graphics and a diverse number of characters to choose from. After I chose my protagonist (Gunzerker) I had to get used to the skill trees, the wacky characters, the large number of side missions in addition to the main story missions. One of the wackiest characters is Claptrap, a robot with something to say all the time and is quite delusional.
The story is set in Pandora, a planet filled with vicious creatures of all kinds. The planet is control by Handsome Jack, the main antagonist of the game. As you progress through the game you will regularly hear Handsome Jack’s speak sarcastically about your goal to bring him down. There are many Echo recorders that will help flesh out the story and who Handsome Jack really is.
The script and voice acting in Borderlands 2 is nothing short of superb. The voice actors and script writers should be highly commended for making the characters such as Scooter, Moxxi, Claptrap and others very entertaining. The only problem I found with the voices was that some conversations can be interrupted by other conversations before you can hear them completely. However, it’s not such a bad thing for the game overall.
There is plenty to explore and if you’re into exploring as much as possible, Borderlands 2 will entertain you for 100+ hours. Each sector of the map has its own environmental feel and its own creatures. The DLCs add even more content for you to explore, but you are best advised to advance your character to at least level 20 because the enemies are much tougher than those enemies in the main story. The DLCs are divided into chapters and side missions while the battles with tougher creatures will reward you with lots of experience points. The side missions in the main game are definitely worth pursuing, as they include puzzle elements and some very simple goals such as simply shooting someone in the face in the side mission titled “Shoot This Guy in the Face.” Other side missions require you to find certain items to receive a unique weapon such as the side mission titled “The Lost Treasure”, a mission that requires you to find different parts of a treasure map. The parts can be anywhere in a region, but the payoff is huge in the form of a very powerful pistol.
Part of what makes Borderlands 2 great in gameplay is the diverse availability of weapons, shields, grenade mods, class mods, and relics. Class mods and relics have ways of enhancing your character’s combat abilities. The inventory feels a little clunky, but once you get used to it you can navigate it pretty quickly. The inventory is important for using in the various vending machines for buying ammo, selling ammo and streamlining.
Respawning is an integral part of this game, as enemies will respawn when you return to the same sector. It may feel tedious after a while, but it can be rewarding because these are opportunities to gain more experience as you try to reach the level of 50. To max out your character you will have to complete the normal mode in order to open up the True Vault Hunter Mode. It is important to know the strengths and weaknesses of enemies so that you know which weapons and ammo work best against them. For example, the loaders (mechanical bots) are vulnerable to corrosive ammo. Therefore, it is best to use a corrosive weapon to kill them faster. The crystallisks are hulking creatures with shins that are made of brittle crystals. Shooting their brittle shins is the only way to bring them down.
This game encourages cooperative play, so it can be fun playing with friends. However, it is better to play with friends who are at a level close to yours, although the game automatically balances the difficulty according to the levels of the players. It is a great feeling trying to heal fellow players in dire times. The unusual feature of death is interesting because there is a chance to achieve a second wind if you get a kill while you’re dying and the red meter is going down to zero.
I found the save system awkward since it saves everything that happens. If you leave the game while in the middle of a mission, you will have to pick up where you left off and the enemies you killed will respawn. In essence, the save system consists simply of save and quit.
Borderlands 2 is one of the most entertaining role-playing games with so much to explore. The gameworld is thriving with loot and opportunities to reap the rewards of doing favors for other townsfolks. I highly recommend this game to anyone as it will take many, many hours of your time and those hours will feel worth it.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 puts you in the shoes of a.................. truck driver. You start out as any regular bloke being a hired driver and delivering various things with a given truck.
After a few jobs you have the option to get a loan from the bank to buy your very own truck. This is where the game truly opens. With your own truck you can drive around anywhere in the map and explore it as you please. Jobs give a higher pay so you can profit something while also paying off your debt. After some jobs the bank will offer you another loan, so you can start your very own trucking company. You use that money to buy a few trucks and hire drivers to work for you.
There is no objective in the game, you're free to do anything, but you could say the objective is to have the biggest trucking empire.
The game does a very good job at keeping you driving, if you don't pay off your debts, it's game over, but that's not all. You need more experience levels to be able to customize your truck to the max and also acquire better trucks.
There many trucks in this game. Iveco, Scania, Volvo, Mercedes-Benz, MAN and Renault; all with different models and configurations.
The world extends from Aberdeen to Budapest, but there are mods that expands the map even more, such as TSM, which will open up parts of Italy, France, Spain and Northern Africa. Or the Scandinavia Promod, it opens up Denmark, Sweden and Norway.
This game will probably never die all thanks to the modding community who make mods and the players who play them and the developers who never stop developing.

A year or more ago I had the same thoughts as today, that I give dayz another try. Maybe things have changed a bit, improved. I didn´t expect much improvement as this title was, is and will be alpha for a long long time.
First impressions were satisfying as the interface changed and it ran with a decent framerate.
But at my first encounter with a zombie, using an axe, I was shocked. The physics worsened, there is NO way to swing the axe to land a hit. I had to aim away from the body, so that hitting was pure luck. The zombie on the opposite was far away, but I was hit.
The last action was falling off the hospital, when I was not that near to the edge, that you would fall off in any other game.
My conclusions are devastating. Before you ever think of changing the interface, graphics, whatever - fix the interaction with objects and enemies. Otherwise it is totally useless.

Melhor simulador da categoria na steam, sem dúvida alguma, seu maior ponto forte além de possuir o modo multiplayer é com certeza o suporte para mods da comunidade, deixando assim o jogador com uma liberdade imensa para configurar o jogo ao seu gosto.
A comunidade brasileira é imensa desde mods de mapas do Brasil, até mapas que simulam estradas altamente perigosas. o primeiro mod que instalei e que foi recentemente foi o do mapa brasileiro, o nome do mod é Mapa EAA, os produtores tem até o canal no youtube e são bem simpáticos e carismáticos.
A física do jogo é fantástica, enquanto você sobe uma ladeira ou morro, ou como queira chamar, você estando fora do jogo consegue sentir o peso das toneladas em cima do seu caminhão, no menu também tem a possibilidade de você ativar a simulação de freios a ar e muitas outras opções desde da linguagem a tipo da moeda no jogo, mas uma que achei bem interessante é o "Consumo de combustível real" o jogo é realmente fantástico.
A trilha sonora do jogo deixa a desejar mas não perde notas por isso, com um sistema de rádios ingame podendo você por até sua rádio favorita e jogar ouvindo sua estação predileta, também possuindo suporte para suas músicas pela pasta Meus documentos, simples prático e fantástico.
Bom é isso, lembrando que o jogo sempre está atualizando a cada patch adiciona algo novo, a compra das dlc's "Going to East" e "Scandinavia" são essenciais, mas também pode jogar só com o jogo base, pois o mapa é realmente imenso.

The fact that you can play music from a HELL of a lot of radio stations from Europe also add to the vivid and realistic experience. Since it is just an indie game, I cannot really fault the graphics that much, there is quite a lot of detail to the massive open-world gameplay, with just about everything you would expect from a properly made simulator. What's so fun about pretending to drive a truck around Europe? I honestly don't know. I can't figure out why this game is so entertaining, but it is. Maybe it's the empire building aspect, combined with exploration, and trucks. Regardless, even though I am not able to pin-point why this game is hours of entertainment, it is a lot of fun. I was surprised when I kept loading it up to play more.
That said, there are a few quirks to the game that bug me, but they are all minor enough as to not really take away from the overall enjoyment factor. AI traffic is mind bogglingly stupid, but that's just realism. The interaction between the clip planes and the working components of the truck don't always want to work together. That is to say, the trucks are rigid, and don't allow for the tires to drop to meet the contours of the ground, which gives you a high centered effect, but it's rare.
I don't have a whole lot more to add, but if you're into sims, give it a try.

This game is awesome. Simply put.
The graphics, while cartoonish, are great. The gameplay is great. It's the continuation of Borderlands. And they improved it.
A Role playing first person shooter. The story is superb. It's well developed while making you laugh. The Co-Op is well made.
It's great to play, but better with 3 more friends. The items are made by a random generator (like Diablo's items), so you'll never get the same weapon twice.
As a plus, in the main city called Sanctuary, you have a chest that needs "Skeleton keys" to open. That chest gives you (with luck) high valuable weaponry of your current level. To get the keys, you need to create a special account inside the game (Extras >> Redeem Codes), and special codes. Every week, Gearbox gives, on Facebook and Twitter, codes for their fans to redeem them for keys (usually 3-5 per code).
About the story: The vault is a legend, and it's said to bring power and wealth to the one who gets it. You start as one of 4 vault hunters (6 if you buy Krieg, the psyco and Gaige, the mechromancer... they are DLCs); a 'Siren', a Gunzerker, a Commando and an Assassin, and you are all gathered there because of the Hyperion Corporation (a weapon manufacturer), who wanted vault hunters to find the vault with them. But their true motive is to kill vault hunters. You survive, and fight back. (I told it this way to avoid any possible spoiler)
Although it has some minor bugs (some walls are not actually walls, and the inventory doesn't move down [literally] well), it is a great game to play.
The DLCs it offers are awesome. The best of them all is Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon's Keep, where you are in the magic world of Role Playing (Dungeons and Dragons kind of Role playing). But Captain Scarlett, Torgue's Campaign and Sir Hammerlock's game hunt are all great DLCs.
The downside is the many DLCs it has. Cosmetics, upgrade of max lvl, characters, scenarios, etc. All of this makes it very expensive.
Other thing is this: the Headhunter packs are short. They can be done in no time. Sure, this separate stories are fun to play (excepting the Mercenary Day, which is MEH), but being that short makes you regretting your decision of buying it.
Word of advice: Buy the GOTY edition (it has all the max lvl upgrades, the major dlcs, Creature Slaughterdome and Gaige and Krieg) and the headhunter packs on 75% sale. It saves you money, and you can play the entire game (which is a must have).

Lets start off saying I've played the first one. Now, comparativly speaking, this game is much better in a variety of ways.
I picked this game up only because it was on sale and because it was also on free weekend. i was able to try it out and see for myself what the game was like without reviews. Now on to reviewing the game.
This game has much more content and a really nice story line. i'm not going to give anything away for those that have not played this game, but i think this game needs more hours into the game to finish every quest in the game. full completion will take a while.
The characters. I havent played this game enough to know all the characters well, but with what i've done so far, everyone is roughly equal in ability level and game play. unlike Borderlands 1 where the action skill is mainly your bread and butter of the class, in BL2 its become more of a utility. I especially like that they added 2 characters on with DLC, i hope more will be released but i wont get my hopes up.
Weapons. This game has a huge weapon variety just like the original but weapon scaling is much better. there are new weapons and there are a few left over from the first game that made its way into the second one.
Locations. I dont believe there are any locations from Borderlands 1 inside the BL2 map except Fyerstone. its under a different name though and i wont spoil it for others. just be aware that its there.
Vehicles. you still have the basic car, but as you make progress into the game you unlock a vehicle similar to the big SUV like truck in the BL1 DLC. (dont recall the name of either the car or the DLC right now) there are also 2 more vehicles that are only available in the DLC zones, sad. :( i still wish that i could use the DLC cars in the main game.
Game Mechanics. The Weapon Proficiancies no longer exists. nor do elementally charging your action skill with relics. claptrap is still annoying. wait thats not a mechanic... There are now 2 seperate storage areas. a BANK and a TRANSFER LOCKER. self explanitory.
For people that played Borderlands 1 and liked it this game is much better.
For people that played Borderlands 1 and didnt like it, this game has many differences that you should give it a try anyways.
For people that have not played Borderlands 1, why are you even here? i'm just kidding, This game is a wonderful game to play. if you enjoy shooting bandits and having them explode, this is the game for you.

Borderlands 2 fits easily in my top 5 games list. The game is funny, enjoyable, beautiful in its terrain, characters, enemies, and allies alike. It takes place on a dangerous, feral planet called Pandora and its areas range from desert wastelands, icy glaciers, flying cities, polluted underground caves, firey volcanoes, as well as man-made fortifications that house robots made by Hyperion, a company that seeks to profit from the opening of an alien vault, opened around 5 years ago. There are 4 main characters, Axton the Commando, Maya the Siren, ZER0 the Assasin, and Salvador the Gunzerker, and 2 DLC characters; Kreig the Psycho and Gaige the Mechromancer. The characters all have different skills, abilities, skill TREES , and play-styles. I believe this game to be easy for FPS newbies and on harder difficulties, challenging for veterans of the first-person shooter. The weapon system includes incredible combinations of different parts per weapon, making the game have trillions upon trillions of weapon combinations. The game is playable online with up to 4 players, and each added player increases the enemy difficulty as well as the rarity of the loot dropped by defeated enemies. There are many pop-culture references, easter eggs, you name it. This game features mature humor, some animated blood and gore, general cruelty, things that will make you laugh, cringe, and even let a chill run up your spine. I absolutely love this game and would recommend it to every gamer who hasn't played it yet.
5/5 Graphics (Animated, somewhat like a comic book)
5/5 Plot (The plot does NOT rely heavily on that of the first game, though previous knowlege will increase your enjoyment)
5/5 Gameplay (Fun, challenging, nearly endless, tremendous replay value)
At the moment, I can not really think of anything that I don't like about the game, but I will add it to this review if I think of any.
*I have also purchased every DLC pack and expansion, (not including some of the character skins) and this is the only game I have done this with. I highly recommend each piece of downloadable content.*

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is that rare thing, a strong sim tethered to a strong game. Where other vehicle-obsessed devs seem to take player motivation for granted, Czech studio SCS understand that a pleasingly modelled steed needs a pleasingly modelled environment to shine.
On this occasion that environment is a swathe of Europe stretching from Plymouth in the west to Wroclaw in the east, from Aberdeen in the north to Milan in the South. The tangle of motorways and major roads is stylised and condensed, but feels massive. After a splendid week of non-stop trucking the stats screen tells me I’ve still only seen 50% of it.
There’s satisfaction in exploring new routes, seeing new golden been-there-done-that squiggles appearing on the in-game map, but it tends to be the promise of cold, hard cash that gets you out of bed in the morning. Like Farming Simulator, ETS2 has a simple yet resonant economic sandbox at its centre.

I just installed it and opened it up for the first time in 1.5 years. I set all the graphics options on max (I have a GTX980 w/4GB RAM + Core i7 @ 4ghz). Under "video memory" the max was 2gb. I set it to auto.
I started playing the game, ran for about 5 minutes and found a town. The movement is still as jerky and choppy as it always was. I pressed V to step over 2 fences, then there was an even shorter concrete wall (2ft high). I pressed V but he wouldn't step over it. I found some canned tuna, ate it; I found a bottle of vitamins, but it wouldn't let me take one; it also said the bottle of 21 tablets weighed "about 2kg". 6lbs for 21 tablets? Really?
I entered 3 more buildings, and on the 4th building I entered, the game crashed because Microsoft said "Your computer is low on memory. Close programs to free memory."
I have 8gb of RAM. As someone with a small knowledge of C++, memory loss of this caliber so early on in the game, with 8gb RAM and 4gb video RAM, this is caused by what's called a Memory Leak. This is a problem (basically) exclusive to C++ when pointers (the feature that make C++ so powerful) are not handled correctly. Pointers allow you to pass segments of memory as though they are variables. This is both very powerful, and very easy to mess up.
In other words, the game is coded poorly.
The graphics were almost horrible as I remember, except the developers implemented a massive amount of HDR bloom to try and make things look better.
I vividly remember seeing a "puddle of water" with leaves in it that looked like it was made in MS Paint.
The draw distance was terrible. Even with everything on max, I could see trees gaining limbs and foliage when they appeared to be 20ft in front of me in-game.
That was 10 minutes of play time. I will not be coming back to this game for another 1.5 years.

What's so fun about pretending to drive a truck around Europe? I honestly don't know. I can't figure out why this game is so entertaining, but it is. Maybe it's the empire building aspect, combined with exploration, and trucks. Regardless, even though I am not able to pin-point why this game is hours of entertainment, it is a lot of fun. I was surprised when I kept loading it up to play more.
That said, there are a few quirks to the game that bug me, but they are all minor enough as to not really take away from the overall enjoyment factor. AI traffic is mind bogglingly stupid, but that's just realism. The interaction between the clip planes and the working components of the truck don't always want to work together. That is to say, the trucks are rigid, and don't allow for the tires to drop to meet the contours of the ground, which gives you a high centered effect, but it's rare.
I don't have a whole lot more to add, but if you're into sims, give it a try.

3 years in development. Yeah it's been a slow process and yeah it's still in alpha. Things were promised, promises were broken. But the progress that IS being made shows a lot of potential for the game's future, the beta and full release.
I just think many people are not being patient, that they feel "betrayed" since many promises were broken, but for someone like me that appreciates every little update for a game that I truly enjoy, I am glad to see progress is made, even if it's a very slow one.
Mechanics are clunky, but not incomprehensable, and with a bit of learning and knowledge or real life survival methods and knowledge about weapons you'll be surprised how much fun it is to play a realistic Zombie survival game unlike 7 Days To Die, H1Z1 and other survival games such as Rust and Hurtworld.
PVP combat sure still is a problem with people obting to use a "Kill on Sight" approach to eliminate potential threats. I personally play by this as well as not many players seem to listen to your beggings of not shooting you and yelling "FRIENDLY! FRIENDLY!" on mic. But also go for retreats if a situation is not giving me and advantage.
The game is still a buggy mess and a lot of things still need to be worked on, that I won't lie about. But the development really seems determined to fixing as much as they can. Smaller less gamebreaking bugs that still can be annoying are not dealt with till many updates later as they focus on the larger issues first. Which is a good approach of course!
This is why I think a lot of people just have a wrong view about this game. Bugs exist, the game is still in alpha but getting closer to beta (in fact update 0.63 will be the first beta update and will be a huge one and the game currently is on 0.61).
So I'd recommend, if you are not already a DayZ fan, come back when beta is released. It may take a while but I believe it will be worth it! If you still don't like it then come back with the game's full release. If you THEN don't like it, it's completely justified. Taste differs and I am not holding my opinion against someone else's.
I just think people are not giving it a proper chance since the game hasn't even hit beta yet and are just too impatient with it's slow development.

Borderlands 2 fits easily in my top 5 games list. The game is funny, enjoyable, beautiful in its terrain, characters, enemies, and allies alike. It takes place on a dangerous, feral planet called Pandora and its areas range from desert wastelands, icy glaciers, flying cities, polluted underground caves, firey volcanoes, as well as man-made fortifications that house robots made by Hyperion, a company that seeks to profit from the opening of an alien vault, opened around 5 years ago. There are 4 main characters, Axton the Commando, Maya the Siren, ZER0 the Assasin, and Salvador the Gunzerker, and 2 DLC characters; Kreig the Psycho and Gaige the Mechromancer. The characters all have different skills, abilities, skill TREES , and play-styles. I believe this game to be easy for FPS newbies and on harder difficulties, challenging for veterans of the first-person shooter. The weapon system includes incredible combinations of different parts per weapon, making the game have trillions upon trillions of weapon combinations. The game is playable online with up to 4 players, and each added player increases the enemy difficulty as well as the rarity of the loot dropped by defeated enemies. There are many pop-culture references, easter eggs, you name it. This game features mature humor, some animated blood and gore, general cruelty, things that will make you laugh, cringe, and even let a chill run up your spine. I absolutely love this game and would recommend it to every gamer who hasn't played it yet.
5/5 Graphics (Animated, somewhat like a comic book)
5/5 Plot (The plot does NOT rely heavily on that of the first game, though previous knowlege will increase your enjoyment)
5/5 Gameplay (Fun, challenging, nearly endless, tremendous replay value)
At the moment, I can not really think of anything that I don't like about the game, but I will add it to this review if I think of any.
*I have also purchased every DLC pack and expansion, (not including some of the character skins) and this is the only game I have done this with. I highly recommend each piece of downloadable content.*

3 years in development. Yeah it's been a slow process and yeah it's still in alpha. Things were promised, promises were broken. But the progress that IS being made shows a lot of potential for the game's future, the beta and full release.
I just think many people are not being patient, that they feel "betrayed" since many promises were broken, but for someone like me that appreciates every little update for a game that I truly enjoy, I am glad to see progress is made, even if it's a very slow one.
Mechanics are clunky, but not incomprehensable, and with a bit of learning and knowledge or real life survival methods and knowledge about weapons you'll be surprised how much fun it is to play a realistic Zombie survival game unlike 7 Days To Die, H1Z1 and other survival games such as Rust and Hurtworld.
PVP combat sure still is a problem with people obting to use a "Kill on Sight" approach to eliminate potential threats. I personally play by this as well as not many players seem to listen to your beggings of not shooting you and yelling "FRIENDLY! FRIENDLY!" on mic. But also go for retreats if a situation is not giving me and advantage.
The game is still a buggy mess and a lot of things still need to be worked on, that I won't lie about. But the development really seems determined to fixing as much as they can. Smaller less gamebreaking bugs that still can be annoying are not dealt with till many updates later as they focus on the larger issues first. Which is a good approach of course!
This is why I think a lot of people just have a wrong view about this game. Bugs exist, the game is still in alpha but getting closer to beta (in fact update 0.63 will be the first beta update and will be a huge one and the game currently is on 0.61).
So I'd recommend, if you are not already a DayZ fan, come back when beta is released. It may take a while but I believe it will be worth it! If you still don't like it then come back with the game's full release. If you THEN don't like it, it's completely justified. Taste differs and I am not holding my opinion against someone else's.
I just think people are not giving it a proper chance since the game hasn't even hit beta yet and are just too impatient with it's slow development.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 puts you in the shoes of a.................. truck driver. You start out as any regular bloke being a hired driver and delivering various things with a given truck.
After a few jobs you have the option to get a loan from the bank to buy your very own truck. This is where the game truly opens. With your own truck you can drive around anywhere in the map and explore it as you please. Jobs give a higher pay so you can profit something while also paying off your debt. After some jobs the bank will offer you another loan, so you can start your very own trucking company. You use that money to buy a few trucks and hire drivers to work for you.
There is no objective in the game, you're free to do anything, but you could say the objective is to have the biggest trucking empire.
The game does a very good job at keeping you driving, if you don't pay off your debts, it's game over, but that's not all. You need more experience levels to be able to customize your truck to the max and also acquire better trucks.
There many trucks in this game. Iveco, Scania, Volvo, Mercedes-Benz, MAN and Renault; all with different models and configurations.
The world extends from Aberdeen to Budapest, but there are mods that expands the map even more, such as TSM, which will open up parts of Italy, France, Spain and Northern Africa. Or the Scandinavia Promod, it opens up Denmark, Sweden and Norway.
This game will probably never die all thanks to the modding community who make mods and the players who play them and the developers who never stop developing.

Melhor simulador da categoria na steam, sem dúvida alguma, seu maior ponto forte além de possuir o modo multiplayer é com certeza o suporte para mods da comunidade, deixando assim o jogador com uma liberdade imensa para configurar o jogo ao seu gosto.
A comunidade brasileira é imensa desde mods de mapas do Brasil, até mapas que simulam estradas altamente perigosas. o primeiro mod que instalei e que foi recentemente foi o do mapa brasileiro, o nome do mod é Mapa EAA, os produtores tem até o canal no youtube e são bem simpáticos e carismáticos.
A física do jogo é fantástica, enquanto você sobe uma ladeira ou morro, ou como queira chamar, você estando fora do jogo consegue sentir o peso das toneladas em cima do seu caminhão, no menu também tem a possibilidade de você ativar a simulação de freios a ar e muitas outras opções desde da linguagem a tipo da moeda no jogo, mas uma que achei bem interessante é o "Consumo de combustível real" o jogo é realmente fantástico.
A trilha sonora do jogo deixa a desejar mas não perde notas por isso, com um sistema de rádios ingame podendo você por até sua rádio favorita e jogar ouvindo sua estação predileta, também possuindo suporte para suas músicas pela pasta Meus documentos, simples prático e fantástico.
Bom é isso, lembrando que o jogo sempre está atualizando a cada patch adiciona algo novo, a compra das dlc's "Going to East" e "Scandinavia" são essenciais, mas também pode jogar só com o jogo base, pois o mapa é realmente imenso.

If you’re looking for a gritty, realistic game about survival in the apocalypse, then DayZ is for you. If you’re looking for a fast-paced instant gratification PvP lobby, then move along because this rustic end-of-the-world gem is not for the CoD kiddies or the faint of heart.
DayZ is not something to jump into blindly. My recommendation to those just starting is to review several of the fanmade DayZ beginner’s guides while you wait for your game to download. DayZ has a great fanbase and there is plethora of excellent guides out there for just about any DayZ topic under the sun. DayZ  Wiki and DayZ TV’s map are also helpful to any beginners looking to dive in.
You begin hungry and cold and must scavenge to survive, having to find water sources and supplies. That being said, the difference between having a difficult time starting out and an easier one comes from simply having the right knowledge. There are key items that survivors can craft after fresh spawning, using stones, wood, and chickens that will make initial survival much easier as survivors acclimate to the map and discover key locations on the coast for initial gearing. (The Stone Knife, Spear, and Improvised Bow are must haves for any fresh spawn looking to survive to his next water pump or apple tree.) Teaching oneself how to make fire and most importantly ‘where’ to make fire when it’s raining are essential fundamentals, as the cold can be as lethal as running afoul of cannibals or wolves.
In addition to scavenging from a ruined world, survivors can grow their own produce, hunt wild game, and craft an assortment of handmade clothing, equipment, and gear. Vehicles can be repaired and put on the road, and survivors can band together in their own tent cities, working together for mutual advantage in a world of horrors.
For a game in alpha stage, there are the expected glitches and bugs—but DayZ is surprisingly polished and highly functional despite its alpha process. I highly recommend DayZ to anyone looking for a game that is truly about survival and exploration in a gritty world where you are as likely to die of cholera as you are to a mob of infected.

The appeal of this game is strange. On the surface it seems more like just "driving trucks," but no, the game goes much deeper than that. This game is not about driving trucks, it's about building an empire. Either way, driving trucks in this game is still an incredible experience. Though the physics was thrown a little off in v1.9, and the traffic AI is kind of stupid, that doesn't make it any less enjoyable. This game is surprisingly relaxing and enjoyable. It's also extremely detailed: SCS Software's recreation of Europe is absolutely stunning. The countryside, that is. Cities are extremely tiny and leave a lot to be desired, but modded maps make up for a lot of that. Speaking of mods: this game is extremely moddable. There is a mapping team which has created absolutely stunning maps for anywhere from Northern Africa to Southwest France and Spain to Scandinavia and (coming soon) Iceland. The graphics (especially with anti-aliasing) leave a bit to be desired but that doesn't generally detract from the experience. Aside from anti-aliasing this is a model PC game, especially with the absolutely grand scale (an entire continent!) and capabilities of the engine. I certainly wouldn't pay full price for it, but if you can find it on sale, it's worth every penny and has almost infinite replayability.

EARLY ACCESS REVIEW POSTED: 30 DECEMBER, 2016
Is this game mind blowing? No. Is it fun and worth 5 bucks? Yes. Overall it is a decent survival/crafting game for the cost.
While it doesn’t break new ground, Fragmented hits all the right marks in the survival game genre and at the sale cost of 5 dollars, you get a decent amount of game per dollar. I would recommend it for the person who has never tried a first-person survival/crafting game before and wants to dip their toes in one that works relatively well and isn’t overly complicated.
Most the negative reviews here are from people who are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ about the devs previous early access project, The Repopulation, which is going through some very painful delays. As a backer myself of that game I am also bummed but this review here is focused solely on Fragmented gameplay itself.
Pros:
-Somewhat unique hybrid alien/earth world setting with nice graphics
-Large variety of cool weapons and armor, much more than most survival games
-Overall solid implementation of the standard survival /crafting game aspects
-Very good gamepad support
-Only 5 dollars
Cons:
-Limited features since it’s early access
-Low player base makes multiplayer a bit lonely and the game is mainly PVE for the moment
-Combat is on-par with other early access survival games, meaning it’s rather clunky
-While it implements the survival game basics well, it does feel rather repetitious to similar games and doesn't add much new to the genre
-A few poor UI and inventory management designs
Longer review:
Fragmented joins the fray of the numerous Steam Early Access survival/crafting games. At its core it seems inspired by what I consider to be the original and one of the best survival games, the Arma II mod DayZ (not the standalone version).
You start alone on the planet which you appear to have crash landed on. You then need to proceed to try and survive by staying fed, staying hydrated, staying warm, and of course staying alive. The graphics in Fragmented are nice and having played many early access survival games, it is better than most.
The one unique thing about Fragmented is the setting. It departs from the usual post apocalyptic/zombie environment found in many similar games. While much of the gameplay terrain looks very earthlike, there is a decent variation of alien looking plants and some rather interesting looking alien creatures you will be encountering and fighting. You can even get some as pets to help you.
You do all the basic things you would do in a survival/crafting game. You chop wood, mine stone, gather plants and then combine it all to make better stuff and keep surviving. The base building is modest so far and to clarify this is NOT one of those voxel based games where you can literally modify everything in game and make minecraft-like bases.
The combat is decent but nothing to rave about. Most survival games seem to have bad combat mechanics in general and even 7 Days to Die, which I own and is one of the best selling survival games, has combat that is pretty clunky and jarring. Combat is actually a bit smoother in Fragmented I think but could still use quite a bit of improvement. On the other hand Fragmented has the best variety of weapons and armor I have seen in this genre. From the plain ole stone weapons to sci-fi electro swords, flamethrowers, and laser rifles. It is a nice change of pace and gives you something to aim and progress toward.
I personally am big on gamepad support and Fragmented has done it well. Like many adult gamers I have a real job where I am in front of a computer all day. I want to be able to relax and game on my couch when I get home, and not keep hunching over in front of a desk. This has true gamepad support with inventory management, UI navigation, and hotkeys mapped to gamepad controls. It is almost 100% playable from a gamepad except for a couple functions you still need the mouse for and the radial wheel selector which glitches out occasionally requiring you to reset it with a mouse. Additionally the aiming and settings aren't quite optimized, but overall much better gamepad support than most games like it.
There is one feature most survival crafting games have which this one doesn't that threw me off a bit: the ability to craft or see info about crafting directly from your inventory. Inventory management is an issue in this game and unfortunately you can’t easily see what items can be crafted from the things in your inventory without closing it and opening the crafting menu and finding it in the recipes list there. This makes it more annoying than it should be when you are trying to make more room and figure which things are valuable for crafting and should be kept, and which aren't and can be ditched.
This game also has an annoying hotkey bar “feature”. The things you put on your hotkey bar still remain in your inventory, unless you are actually holding it in your hand. This can often result in the situation where you are holding a melee weapon, you kill something and pick stuff up, then you switch to another tool or weapon on your hotkey bar and your char tries to put his melee weapon back into inventory. But if there is no room since you picked stuff up in the meantime, he just throws it on the ground without warning. I died more than once when this happen since I got attacked right after my char inadvertently threw his main weapon on the ground. Seems like there is a better way to handle this, like just making the things on the hotkey bar their own separate inventory.
The biggest issue right now is the low playerbase. What makes survival games great is the moral dilemmas it puts you in with other players. Do I say hi to this other player I just met or kill him for his berries because I’m starving? Should I work with him which might be better in the long run or take his stuff for a short term one-time gain? Right now there isn’t much of this due to the low player base. Hopefully that will improve with time or you should consider playing it with a friend as I can see coop being rather fun.
Overall, if you have played other survival/crafting games there really isn’t much new here. If you haven't though this is probably one of the more decent games in the genre that has a low learning curve and which you can start playing and having fun surviving and/or dieing immedietly. While the overall game is limited due to its early development stage it has all the survival/crafting gameplay basics one would expect and at its current sale price is worth the cost. Given how early access this is and the unique sci-fi setting, there appears to be a lot of room up for this game to go. So at minimum I think you easily get your 5 dollars worth with the game in it’s current state, and at maximum you get something much better as it develops.

Addictive and funny Diablo-style RPG with first person prespective and gun-focused combat. This game doesn't improve much on the original formula, specifically on the quality of combat. It is still rather shallow, the only reactive enemies are robots (which change attack style after you shoot off the limbs), and ultimately requires zero skill to play.
Success of combat depends entirely on quality of your loot (unless you count being able to aim as a skill, in which case you must be new to gaming), and this is often extremely annoying. I really hate how you have to tank most of the damage, because they didn't put a dodge move into the game, wheras a lot of enemies look like they were designed with a dodge in mind -  a lot of well-telegraphed attack patterns that would be fun to skillfully avoid without breaking damage output... But alas, all depends on your stats like in first game.
However the game still has excellent sense of humour, good loot system, this time the characters are a bit more explored(although story and animation quality could definitely use more attention), which is a good addition from the first game and this time we actually have a proper port. So grab a GOTY edition on sale and you will have a lot of fun.
Something should be said about it's DLC though. Borderlands lore basically always portrays greedy companies as the ultimate evil force. However ironically enough Gearbox don't fall far from the very evils they show. The game is plaigued by meaningless DLC that adds some guns (that you will use for 1 hour and replace as with all equipment in this game) and raises level caps by a few %, which in total costs far more than the actual good DLC included in GOTY edition.
