As of now I have over 400 hrs on Dayz and as much as it pains me to say the game is awful. I have tried to love this game for so long but in the end it is a mess of poor development, lies from said development, and a massive amount bugs. We have been told of many great things to come but have yet to see any of it, such as base building...we were told in 2015 that  both predators and base building were to be added by the end of the year but in 2015 what was added in the place of building was lockpicks. As for predators we did get those but at the end of 2016.
Now lets fast forward from 2015 to the start of 2016, this is where many of the bugs that still plauge the game to this very day. These bugs range from random despawning to players clothing being unrendered. Too many time have I go to bandage and realized that my rags disappeared from my bag, or I try to fire my mosin after loading it and the chamber being empty. There were actualy many less bugs in 2015 than 2016. I know that many have said that it is the progress that they have made with the game that has caused a majority of the bugs, but to this I ask what progress?
Asking "what progress?" may at first come off as just me bashing on Dayz but lest take a moment to look at the "progress" of 2016. To start with check how many updates that there were in 2016, there were 2. But please don't take my word for it, do your own reserch to verify what I say. To me there is no excuse for this. Truth be told I see no reason for the lack of updates in 2016 reason other the the developer laziness and failure. I wish it was not this way but its clear that time after time the developers have failed both the game and the community.
I have repetedly seen it said that the game is early access so its ok for it to have all of these issues and shortcomings, but why does that justify any of them? Dayz has been early access since the end of 2013 and it has yet to leave alpha. I feel that this should be the cut off point to the leniency for it being an "early access title". I am not saying that we should judge it as a full released game but what if every game developer used "early access" as an excuse?
Now that we are in 2017 lets talk about the new update .61. .61 brought with it several nice things such as the wolves that we were promised so very long ago as well as dynamic shadows and updated audio for weaponry. However, it also brought many new issues.
The first of the issues I find to be quite odd. As I have been playing on the new patch I notced that both my face and the faces of others have at times become a complete black blank slate. What I mean by this is the head is pitch black and has no features such as hair, eyes, or mouth. At first I found it is a touch funny but the more I see it the more it annoys me.
The next issue is somewhat like the first. On about one third of the players that I have seen their shirt (or whatever they are wering on their chest) or helmet is following them around on the ground as thought that have not picked it up and either their torso or head is invisible. The reason that I have sepreated this from the first issue is that this one can actualy effect the game for other players. If say, someone is sitting in a bush they normaly can still be seen because of the color of their shirt showing between the leaves but if their torso is clear than what is there to see before the rush out of the bush and bash in your head with a bat?
Third is one that personally annoys the hell out of me. This one is an issue with the zombies, specifically the way the zombies move. There are two things I have seen, one is that sometimes zombies will run incredibly slow yet be doing an extreamly rapid run animation. When this happens its almost as though there is a slow moveing invisible wall in between them and you. The second issue with them is that sometimes they will run nearly as fast as two times a player. I am not sure if it is a bug or not but I have a issue with this espicaly as playes can not escape a normal zombie if it is after them while they are moveing up any form of incline, where as zombies can do a full sprint up any angle. This is already a pain but now that they can move so fast it is just plain unreasonable.
The forth and last big issue is the new auido. several times when both I and someone else have fired our guns instead of gunshots all that is heard is static. This one seems to be reather rare but I still feel that it should be mentioned. Even if this issue is annoying I can atleast understand that it is abit expected as they have greatly changed the gun audio in this update.
At the point that I am at in this I feel that there is no need to go on as it would be more of the same, all of the issues that I have had with the game. Since the release of Dayz I had great hopes for it and yet every patch has fallen short even so I stayed with it untill now as there were still some good times to be had on it, but I feel that it is time for everyone to wake up and see Dayz for what it is, a failure and empty promises.

Forgive me for using a Shrek analogy, but Undertale really is like an onion. It gets stronger and more intense the closer you get to the core and it'll make you want to cry your eyes out if you don't properly prepare yourself.
Undertale somehow manages to offer something for everyone without feeling disjointed. You'll find a riveting story, innovative game mechanics, lovable characters, absurdity and silliness, tension and drama, hideously difficult tests of skill, moral dilemmas, a soundtrack you'll want to play on a loop for days on end, and even frickin' memes. Most importantly, Undertale offers you choices that actually
. The effects of your decisions begin showing up immediately, which really forces you to think about what you're doing and the consequences of your actions. For such a seemingly benign retro game, it's astonishingly complex and more than happy to put you through the wringer.
In short, this game has changed my life -- mainly in the sense that I'm now less bothered by skeletons but more bothered by flowers.

I've been playing Rust for a while. Not as long as some of the guys who reviewed. But since the blueprint system.
Let me say that most of the playerbase now just doesn't know what they're missing. There was a time in Rust where it was pure survival. It wasn't so much of raiding and mindless pvp combined with excessive grinding. The chances of a raid weren't as high. As most people weren't able to make c4 and satchel charges were not in game yet. Just to share, i've been through the bp system, xp system, and now the component system. I enjoyed the BP system the most.
The Dev's are doing a bang up job with this game. They're really on top of things and are trying to gear the game towards its playerbase. This is in no way even close to the Dev's of DayZ or other "in development games". They are very committed to the game.
It is unfortunate at this stage in the game this is where we have come. With satchel charges being so readily available and gears being close to impossible to find. It really puts the raider at an advantage. Also, to get c4 or an AK-Bolty all you have to do is pass through a rad town a couple of times. They really made things too easy and that is not what this game was made for.
Overall you will enjoy this game. You missed a great period where you learned a lot from mistakes and became a better player. Now this game is gearing itself towards any other simple minded multiplayer shooter. Hopefully they at least throw a few blueprint servers in here and there. Many others including myself would be happy.

Where do I start to review a game as massively packed with content as Borderlands 2? I guess the best way to describe something is to tell you where it comes from.
Borderlands is a series of First-Person Shooters mixed with tradtional Action RPG's. You pick a class, level up your skills, and shoot your way through hordes of baddies. This specific formula was also used by the Blizzard's critically acclaimed "Diablo" series and "Torchlight" by Runic Games.
The unique thing about these kinds of games that gives it so much replayability is the loot system. Weapon pick-ups are generated randomly from a list of possible statistics; each base type has a few different ways it be be created, with specific stats and visuals to each. For example, you may load up the game, find an assault rifle made by Torgue, with a sight made by Hyperion, the grip made by Vladof (and each part follows these lines) and a weapon level depending on where, when, and how lucky you were when you got it. It all turns out to literally tens of thousands of possible weapons to find.
As for the story, it is a direct sequel to the original. The Hyperion corporation has become extremely powerful selling a new type of element called "slag", which in game causes those affected by it to take extra damage from other sources (Hint: It's great for co-op, which I will get to briefly). The young new President of Hyperion, Handsome Jack, has practically claimed the planet of Pandora as his own little mining facility. And let me tell you, Handsome Jack is one of the meanest, funniest, most interesting villians I have seen in a long time. He makes Sephiroth look like butt, Duke Nukem look like Baby Mario and Master Chief the Wimpy Loser (If you do not get this reference, please uninstall right now.) He also has a bright side, too - he bought a living solid diamond horse to show off how rich he was, and even named it after you! Buttstallion is such a pretty name.
As for the visuals of the game - it may look odd at first glance, but it's about time the gaming world moved past how many pixels a game has and start looking at how the game plays. Notably, like The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker, it's art style was critized for it's use of colour and texture. And know how that turned out? Wind Waker still looks just as good today as it did back in the day, while games like Halo: Combat Evolved and Final Fantasy VII have not aged well at all when it comes to visual feedback. This game looks wonderful, and I'm sure it will still look appealing to the eye 5 - even 10 - years from now.
As for the shooting, it's fun and zanny, just like before. One complaint I have however is the number of non-traditional shooting patterns the guns have really take away from the whole "Desperate rebellion on a desert planet against a highly trained, well equiped mega corporation that basically runs the world." (AHEM! HUMPH! WAL-MART! COUGH!) Nothing really seems rag-tag like it fittingly did in the original.
"Well, DTB... tell us about the writing." Well, dear readers, if you thought the humour in the original was good, it's basically like comparing Robert Downey Jr. to Adam Sandler. One is wel scripted humour, the other a 90's-esque hobo joke mixed with the same stereotypical character. Borderlands 2 takes a much more serious approach at the dialogue. Before you were likely to hear a joke about pages in a magazine stuck together. While entertaining, doesn't fully satisfy my needs, and leaves a guilty pleasure and room for another big one.
...
Nobody?
... fine.
THAT'S WHAT SHE SAID.
Ahem. Anyways, Borderlands 2's humour is full-frontal and downright halarious at times. I especially love the characters Handsome Jack and Tiny Tina. Tiny Tina was a minor character, but she was so popular with fans she actually got her own DLC. Well done, Gearbox. You made me choke on that one...
So basically, the game turns out to be worth it's hype. I believe Will Ferall said it best when he shouted "I'M IN A GLASS CASE OF EMOTION!"
Final Verdict for Borderlands 2 is a 8.5/10 for the average person, 9/10 for fans.
Speaking of HYPE... Pre-Sequel set to release October 18th, 2014. Who's ready for some anti-gravity bandit-killing?

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).

I adored the first Borderlands; the mixture of a space-cowboy setting with FPS and RPG blended together so perfectly. I myself normally do not like pure FPS, games like Call of Duty, I need something supernatural, (e.g. fighting aliens in Halo), to make it interesting and as such borderlands fit the bill for me. The loot system was great, basically every gun that's dropped is randomly generated from several lists of gun models and effects. Everytime you play the game you will never get the same weapon, it will always be slightly different; this allows for a high replay value. The classes, action skills and skill trees added quite a bit of depth to the game and allowed you to focus your character to a certain role. Another great feature was elemental weapons, having trouble with an enemy with a shield? Shoot him with lightning. Want to get rid of those shieldless enemies faster? Shoot him with fire.
Borderlands 2 had all these features and more, and improved on every feature it had before! Better graphics, new playable characters, better story, more guns, more elemental effects, more in depth skill tree, more guns, more complex action skills, and did I mention more guns? The graphics are suped up while still preserving the charm of the original, 6 new classes, more dialogue and a more complex story line, more guns than the original which had 17,750,000 different variations. That's 17 million, 750 thousand different guns; and borderlands 2 has more than that! New elemental effect, slag. Big skill tree that adds things like action skill augments and melee augments. Awesome action skills like using two guns at once, becoming invisible and summoning a death robot to name a few.

Early Access Watcher Reviews DayZ
Update Version: 0.61 Experimental
Disclosure: The game copy was bought by the reviewer.
This will be the shortest review I write, but it will also be the most beneficial. As I stated in my curate, very little progress has been made on the game and it is very unlikely (now highly impossible) that the game will reach release by the end of 2016 (though the developers have stated the goal was early 2016).
Technical difficulties, terrible rendering, frame rate issues and crashing/loading freezes are just some of the issues that have gone unresolved over the years as they attempt to cram more in with little to no optimization.
My wholesome advice is to avoid this proof of concept completely and buy Arma II. You can purchase it along with downloading the DayZ mod for way less than this and have so much more content available to you. I cannot stress it enough. Avoid this disaster.
Edit: It seems the Early Access information has changed the projected completion time from early 2016 to mid 2017. Let's see what happens.

First off, The game is in ALPHA, this means that it's basically running on the framework. Despite this, the game is doing some major progress and in comparison to the DayZ Mod for ArmA 2, It's pretty decent. The second plothole seems to be unnoticed by all, so I may be the only one to notice it. Luckily, it is not a spoiler issue, as it is offhand knowledge you can find early in the game. The plothole is caused by the fact that Humans sealed the Monsters under the Barrier long long ago. The problem is that this is entirely impossible. Humans simply did not have the technology to make a giant super barrier under a mountain many centuries or longer ago. You might claim that perhaps the barrier was made by some form of magic, but this too is impossible as explained in the game's own text. You see, in the early game town of Snowdin, there is a library where you can read some books. In one of the books it says the following: "While monsters are mostly made of magic, human beings are mostly made of water. Humans, with their physical forms, are far stronger than us. But they will never know the joy of expressing themselves through magic." This clearly states that the barrier could not have been made with magic. So how DID the Humans create the Barrier? Maybe tobyfox will tell us when he gets up off of his money pile...

Undertale is an choice based RPG, that has a seemingly endless amount of choices, so much so that it is very hard to get two of the same game on a second play through.
So the story is very basic (or so it seems). Long ago, the world was shared by humans and monsters. One day, war broke out, and the humans sealed all the monsters underground with a magic spell. Many years later, a human climbs up Mount Ebott, and falls down into the underground. Now, they must make their way out and back home. In the game, you have encounters with monsters, much like the turned-based battles from Pokemon, and much like Pokemon, you have four classic options: Fight, where you lay your best attack on your opponent; act, where you make an action (usually not Fight related); and Mercy (running away, or stopping the fight). Based on these buttons, there are different play styles. The game has three play styles, each has a name, but the name hints at which ending you get, so I won't say it. You can, Spare everyone you meet, kill everyone you meet, or kill and spare as you please (I recommend either of the “extremes”).  As you play, the game is very (and I repeat, very) clear which style is the intended one. The visuals aren’t really that good, because they aren’t supposed to be. The graphics come right out of the 16-bit era. But the music certainly hasn’t.
As I’ve noticed, the music starts out like the graphics, 8-bit, but it grows less and less so as the game progresses. And as the story reaches it’s climax the soundtrack has no “beeps” at all. The soundtrack is also one of the best parts of the game. It literally has the “Great Soundtrack” tag on steam. But enough about superficial things, now about what really makes this gem shine: it’s characters and story.
I freaking love the characters in Undertale. My favorites being Toriel (the tutoriel NPC)… someone you meet at the end… And Sans (the skeleton, named after his text font: Comic Sans). Something just hit me as I was writing this, they’re NPCs. NPC means “non-player-character,” for those who don’t know. But it was strange to me, because they are so well written, you can forget sometimes that they’re just characters in a game. Each one has so much “life” to them. I accidentally killed one of the main characters, and felt really bad about it. Yes, I know it’s just a game, and that they’re not real... but that didn’t stop me gasping as she (like all monsters when they die) turned to dust. But the nail in the coffin, was that her soul (a little heart) hovered in the air, trembled, and shattered. Then, (when guilt tripped about my mistake by another character) I reset, and did things differently.
So that’s Undertale, one of the best games I’ve ever played, and won't soon forget.
(PS, I can NOT click reccomend enough!!!)

Euro Truck Simulator was a fun and relaxing game where you drove cargo around central Europe. It was suprisingly compelling to do so, but the experience also felt very bare bones. There was only the slightest semblance of actual progression and the experience felt very sparse and unpopulated at times. While the experience for part 2 has not changed drastically, the game now feels more like a legitimate trucking sim and not just a driving simulator. There's more terrain, a GPS, European streaming radio stations at your fingertips, and a much more fleshed out career mode. If you suspect you might be interested in Euro Truck, Part 2 is the way to go. If you're an insane person with a crazy driving wheel setup, this game also supports that.

Where do I start to review a game as massively packed with content as Borderlands 2? I guess the best way to describe something is to tell you where it comes from.
Borderlands is a series of First-Person Shooters mixed with tradtional Action RPG's. You pick a class, level up your skills, and shoot your way through hordes of baddies. This specific formula was also used by the Blizzard's critically acclaimed "Diablo" series and "Torchlight" by Runic Games.
The unique thing about these kinds of games that gives it so much replayability is the loot system. Weapon pick-ups are generated randomly from a list of possible statistics; each base type has a few different ways it be be created, with specific stats and visuals to each. For example, you may load up the game, find an assault rifle made by Torgue, with a sight made by Hyperion, the grip made by Vladof (and each part follows these lines) and a weapon level depending on where, when, and how lucky you were when you got it. It all turns out to literally tens of thousands of possible weapons to find.
As for the story, it is a direct sequel to the original. The Hyperion corporation has become extremely powerful selling a new type of element called "slag", which in game causes those affected by it to take extra damage from other sources (Hint: It's great for co-op, which I will get to briefly). The young new President of Hyperion, Handsome Jack, has practically claimed the planet of Pandora as his own little mining facility. And let me tell you, Handsome Jack is one of the meanest, funniest, most interesting villians I have seen in a long time. He makes Sephiroth look like butt, Duke Nukem look like Baby Mario and Master Chief the Wimpy Loser (If you do not get this reference, please uninstall right now.) He also has a bright side, too - he bought a living solid diamond horse to show off how rich he was, and even named it after you! Buttstallion is such a pretty name.
As for the visuals of the game - it may look odd at first glance, but it's about time the gaming world moved past how many pixels a game has and start looking at how the game plays. Notably, like The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker, it's art style was critized for it's use of colour and texture. And know how that turned out? Wind Waker still looks just as good today as it did back in the day, while games like Halo: Combat Evolved and Final Fantasy VII have not aged well at all when it comes to visual feedback. This game looks wonderful, and I'm sure it will still look appealing to the eye 5 - even 10 - years from now.
As for the shooting, it's fun and zanny, just like before. One complaint I have however is the number of non-traditional shooting patterns the guns have really take away from the whole "Desperate rebellion on a desert planet against a highly trained, well equiped mega corporation that basically runs the world." (AHEM! HUMPH! WAL-MART! COUGH!) Nothing really seems rag-tag like it fittingly did in the original.
"Well, DTB... tell us about the writing." Well, dear readers, if you thought the humour in the original was good, it's basically like comparing Robert Downey Jr. to Adam Sandler. One is wel scripted humour, the other a 90's-esque hobo joke mixed with the same stereotypical character. Borderlands 2 takes a much more serious approach at the dialogue. Before you were likely to hear a joke about pages in a magazine stuck together. While entertaining, doesn't fully satisfy my needs, and leaves a guilty pleasure and room for another big one.
...
Nobody?
... fine.
THAT'S WHAT SHE SAID.
Ahem. Anyways, Borderlands 2's humour is full-frontal and downright halarious at times. I especially love the characters Handsome Jack and Tiny Tina. Tiny Tina was a minor character, but she was so popular with fans she actually got her own DLC. Well done, Gearbox. You made me choke on that one...
So basically, the game turns out to be worth it's hype. I believe Will Ferall said it best when he shouted "I'M IN A GLASS CASE OF EMOTION!"
Final Verdict for Borderlands 2 is a 8.5/10 for the average person, 9/10 for fans.

There are titles in the simulation market which can be sold on the novelty factor alone, but tend to be disappointing games.  Euro Truck Simulator 2 is not one of them, it is strangely cathartic, engaging and relaxing. Unlike other niche games, there is a smaller barrier to entry and features a simple control scheme for newcomers.  There are some reservations such as an infuriating penalty system and a lack of vehicles on major highways but these are outweighed by the positives.  Overall, for the fee of 20€, I would highly recommend this driving experience even if it’s not something that would usually be on your radar.

After spending almost 600 hours into the game, I can say that, this is a fantastic trucking simulator. I have all the functional DLCs and they certainly live up to the value.
Pros:
-- Fantastic driving experience.
-- Really good texture and modelling.
-- Variety of cargo and trucks.
-- Very little to no bugs.
-- Economy system can be challenging at the beginning.
-- Challenging cargo and good range of truck customization.
-- Fantastic support for driving gears.
-- Superb geometry and physics. You will not find hidden hit boxes or go through objects.
Cons:
-- AI is really poor at decision making.
-- Not much in terms of building your trucking empire. You basically can hire a limited amount of drivers and select their skill gain focus, but that's about it. It will not interest you when you already own all the possible garages and recruited all the available drivers and almost all of them are already level 10.
-- Lack of endgame goal. I literally have nothing more to do in the game after reaching level 90. Now I drive like GTA and get to the destination even without a scratch or a fine because I even memorized all the speed checkers.
-- Not enough scope to spend your in game earning. They keep piling up and you have nothing to do apart from buying and selling trucks repeatedly, which is pointless.
-- Why release a new game (ATS) which is basically the same game? Could be a DLC for ETS2 like "Connecting America" or something.
-- No damage models.
-- No realistic impact of tandem axles.
-- Not enough drivers to fill up all my garages.
-- You have to pay fine if AI hits you wrongly.
What I would like to see:
-- Improved AI.
-- Realistic axle physics.
-- More recruitment interaction, for example, recruiting a driver far from his home city will put negative impact on the earning.
-- More economical interaction (I know this is about driving, but other components would be a great attraction).
If you just like driving by following rules, enjoy the beautiful landscape, hauling various cargo on routes of various distances, this is a great game for you. You will not find end game content or much challenge at all. I enjoy the game, so I will recommend you to try it.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of those games you'd expect to only cater towards hardcore trucking fans and alike, and that it would be a rather boring experience to everybody else. Somehow the SCS Software managed to make a trucking game that doesn't feel that boring (unless you play 8+ hours a day every single day, then it might start to feel slightly boring) and is actually quite relaxing and enjoyable. The game is solid with little to no bugs in the core game and there are tons of mods available for it if you know where to look. I'd love to see this game have its own Steam Workshop for easy mod installation and to ensure that mods are up to date and compatible with the latest version of the game at all times, but sadly this isn't the case just yet. The game looks beautiful on high settings and features the possibility of using Oculus rift or TrackIR to make the immersion even higher. The only real complaints that a full blown assburger such as myself can muster up is that the immersion hasn't been taken far enough. I'd like to be able to get out of my truck and walk around it, inspecting it, or to pull up to a gas station and walk in and order a coffee and a donut, or buy a can of energy drink to give me a 30 to 60 minute boost so I can drive that last stretch and deliver my stuff. An animation of the driver getting out of his drivers seat and crawling behind for a few hours of sleep would also be nice, but sadly none of these things are in the game.. yet.
To put it short, anyone can enjoy this game, not just hardcore truck enthusiasts, and it's actually quite relaxing to just drive around and deliver stuff from A to B. Gameplay is solid and there aren't any bugs that I have encountered (unmodded that is). Stunning visuals and quite immersive especially with Oculus Rift or TrackIR.

If you are interested in driving, like me, or are interested in running a buisness related to driving car or truck, then this game is for you. Overall the game mechanics are great, each job pays well enough to make you want to keep playing but doesnt pay enough to make the game too easy. The buisness owning aspect of the game is fantastic, you can plan to start a company asap by taking out a loan, or you can save up for a while to avoid being in debt, there is so many possibilities. Overall I love this game, you should too, What are you waiting for?

It's very hard for me to describe why this game is so great, especially when you factor in all the bad reputation it has thanks to it's terrible community. Overall the game has a certain charm to it that many games tend to lack these days. The only way to understand why so much high praise has been given towards the game is to play it for yourself. Here are some of my personal pros and cons...
Pros:
-Excelent music. Probably one of the strongest points in the game. Every song feels unique and is used to describe each situation and character.
-Amazingly funny, clever, and surprisingly emotional writting. The comedy in this game is not at all just silly one liners (though those are definitely part of it). The game will often mess with you and break the forth wall. This makes you the player feel a lot more involved in what is happening in the world.
-Characters that you can never forget. I have no clue how they were able to make 2D pixelated characters that aren't even voice acted or have many facial expressions feel so real. They are all unique in their own way.
-Multiple ways to play. If you want to go through this game mindlessly killing everything in your way cuz you really don't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥ then you can do that. If you want to go through the world killing and sparing who you chose, that option is available. Or if you want to be everyone's friend and save everyone that choice is up to you. It's choices like this that make you feel important in the world you have been dropped into.
-The fast paced bullet hell combat. I've never been a big fan of this kind of combat, but after this my mind has been changed. Fights have your heart racing at times. The game mixes RPG elements but instead of just sitting there taking turns and hitting "fight", you actually have to fight for your life. The combat is difficult, but not to the point where it feels imposible. Unless you're fighting Sans, that's a whole other story.
-The addition of the "Act" option in combat. It adds a whole new dynamic to the game, allowing you to "talk", "pick on", "complement", etc. It's a small addition to the game that creates all kinds of different interactions.
Cons:
-The visuals at times can be seen as ugly because everything is so pixelated. At many points the game is impressively beautiful in certain settings, but I can understand if some dislike it.
-THE COMMUNITY (Im not counting this as a negative towards the game itself). The community has seriously hurt this game's reputation, so much so that it causes many people to avoid it. They are fanboys to the extreme. I like the game a lot but these people will attack anyone with even the slightest criticizm about the game. It makes people hate the game, hurting it's reputation. My advice is to just avoid googling or looking up anything about undertale related altogether
The only other cons I could think of would be nitpicking and would give away too much. I would recommend anyone to play Undertale as soon as they can. Other reviewers that highly recommend the game and/or give it GOTY for 2015 is TotalBiscuit, The Escapist, and VideoGameDunky. I personally see it as one of my favorite games out there and couldn't recommend it more.

I adored the first Borderlands; the mixture of a space-cowboy setting with FPS and RPG blended together so perfectly. I myself normally do not like pure FPS, games like Call of Duty, I need something supernatural, (e.g. fighting aliens in Halo), to make it interesting and as such borderlands fit the bill for me. The loot system was great, basically every gun that's dropped is randomly generated from several lists of gun models and effects. Everytime you play the game you will never get the same weapon, it will always be slightly different; this allows for a high replay value. The classes, action skills and skill trees added quite a bit of depth to the game and allowed you to focus your character to a certain role. Another great feature was elemental weapons, having trouble with an enemy with a shield? Shoot him with lightning. Want to get rid of those shieldless enemies faster? Shoot him with fire.
Borderlands 2 had all these features and more, and improved on every feature it had before! Better graphics, new playable characters, better story, more guns, more elemental effects, more in depth skill tree, more guns, more complex action skills, and did I mention more guns? The graphics are suped up while still preserving the charm of the original, 6 new classes, more dialogue and a more complex story line, more guns than the original which had 17,750,000 different variations. That's 17 million, 750 thousand different guns; and borderlands 2 has more than that! New elemental effect, slag. Big skill tree that adds things like action skill augments and melee augments. Awesome action skills like using two guns at once, becoming invisible and summoning a death robot to name a few.
All in all, I loved the first borderlands, and borderlands 2 just took a great game and made it better. They improved almost every aspect of what made the first game great. I'm hoping for the pre-sequel to do the same, but it will be difficult to top this one.

As a child and still recently I have always wanted to drive big vehicles: Lorries, Vans, etc.  To be honest this is the closest I'm likely to get without spending a grand and the rest on Class 1 lessons that I'd probably never then use.  After playing the demo I decided to buy the full game as simulation plus management element not only satisifed the excitement (I'll get to that) element I wanted but also the endless, endless desire for fettling I have.
I really was unconvinced that driving an articulated lorry in a game could be exciting until I discovered how much concentration and application of logical thought it requires.  Judging how to take tight corners and negotiating the motorway at high speed are a real challenge which keeps you constantly occupied and I feel something which I haven't in other driving games; a destinct compulsion to obey the rules (whatever they may be - in this case of the road).  I think this is because unlikea lot of games, you are actively rewarded (or rather, not penalised) for driving sensibly; drivers will let you out at junctions ocassionally and they stop in the right places (Get too close to a driver and he brakes to a halt, make a bad overtake and cars coming the other way will attempt to stop).
I think what the game tries to acheive through simulation it does brilliantly.
In terms of management, this is really fun too.  Upgrading your garage(s) and managing your drivers and vehicles is exactly the right blend of depth and simplicity,  you don't have to spend hours decoding the stats of each driver before making a hire and you're kept pretty well up to date through your in-game HUD as to how your hires are doing.  Money also seems to come in at a balanced rate and in sensible chunks - you don't end up scratching around for cash but neither are you swimming in it.
The trucks themselves are beatifully represented and the models fantastically detailed, I've only diven two so far but differences between the two are destinct.  I started with the Iveco Stralis and quickly got quite use to this, so I bought another and hired a driver.  I finally hired a third driver, gave him my Stralis and then bought the most powerful truck I could afford at my level (10 at this point).  A Volvo FH16 classic.  As soon as I pulled away I noticed the difference, with nearly twice the power and almost 2.5 times the torque it was rather difficult to drive at first.  The way it should be, a game should continually test and this scenario mimics real life.  You don't go from a Polo to a Ferrari without noticing the difference.
Ok, a couple of gripes; they aren't deal breakers but things that if were included at a later stage would be really great.  The first one I think is a bit lapse however.
1.  There's no training mode.  Really?  As a result of my latent interest I was probably more prepared than most when going into this game, but still some stuff I had NO idea.  Let's forget for a moment that fact you're trying to drive something approaching 80ft long and pivots 20ft from the front  (Just wait till you come to back it up for the first time) and concentrate on a few key words.
Retarder, Exhaust Brake and 12-gear gearbox.  No idea?  Not surprised.  I really think this game needs a training mode as for me part of the fun of simulation games is doing things properly and there are lots of things that need explaining even if you drive a car, like for instance the fact that if you pull away from the lights in 1st you'll be in 4th or 5th before you've crossed the junction.  Pull away in 3rd or 4th.
2.  The fettling element with your trucks is great, you can change almost every part in and out to your heart's content but there's little in the way of guidance or much pay-off.  Upgrading the engine is obvious; more power, more torque but apart from allowing you to go a bit faster I'm not sure what the real benefit of it is.  Perhaps if there was a maximum permissible load per engine size so upgrading meant you could pull bigger loads?
I also have no idea why I would upgrade to a 6x2 chassis other than the fact that it looks the dog's.
3.  I'm not really into the whole posting photos thing but I do like posing a good shot to admire the rig I've spent time agonising over the pait job for. Can we please have a mode where you can assembled all or selected trucks from your fleet for a group photo?  One which perhaps allows you to reposition them within the shot, at a choice of some locations?
Right, sorry.  I know it sounds like nothing but whinge but there are a few bits I'd like to see added or improved.  That said I absolutely love this game, it's brilliant.  Buy it, seriously.

Things I like about ETS 2 is a wide selection of trucks, rainy weather, no speed limit that you can change in options and the whole game itself. The disadvantages, in my honest opinion, are medium graphics of the game that is inconsistent in nowadays. It is hard to explain what makes this game so addicting. On paper it looks like the most boring thing in the world. Driving a truck from one city to another for hours, but like Civilization has its "just one more turn" this game has a similar thing. Just a little further, just get to the next city, just one more one more trip.
I don't really have any interest in trucks, but I have still put alot of hours into this game. Both relaxing and rewarding. You level up with each trip, so there is a good sense of progression and even a basic RPG element as well. With many other games today having a very open world and tons of possibilities, there is something appealing about something utterly simple like getting from point A to point B. No real choices or stragies to make, just do it. Probably not a thing for everybody, but give it a try even though it looks boring on paper.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a different kind of game. It's a relaxing low-pressure game, and still quite entertaining. My only real gripe with the game is the lack of American-style trucks. I've got nothing against a good European cabover truck, but it just feels wrong to play a trucking game without Peterbilt, etc. I'd love for the game to be set in the US, as well, but admittedly that'd probably get boring quick, with all the IRL-trucking friendly straight/wide roads.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 turns the excitement levels up to 11; out of a possible 5.

Thinking about buying this game?  Do it.  I was actually quite impressed with it, it includes some overall meta-game elements (like managing a trucking company with several trucks and hiring drivers to drive them) but also does a fantastic job with an expansive open world that I've barely had a chance to explore.  Keep in mind that time is sped up significantly (because it's a game, I don't actually want to simulate what it's like to drive for 16 hours on a single haul) so some of my short hauls only take around 5-10 minutes and some of the longer ones can take 20+ (and I have barely scratched the surface on leveling up long-haul delivers).  The level-up system keeps newer and more challenging (and fun) jobs right around the corner (with better rewards!) and also allows you to customize your truck, or buy a better one.
All around, Euro Truck Simulator is way more fun than driving a semi truck actually sounds like it would be.

I like the ideas in this game, but I do have some things to point out. It might be a bit of a long one.
Firstly, what is typically used is something called subsonic rounds. This is a round with a significantly lesser powder load. This is intended to lower the velocity of the round to, well, subsonic speeds. This means that it goes slower than the speed of sound, because a great deal of the sound that comes from a gun firing is from the sonic boom created by the bullet. This would mean that the bullet drop would in fact be greater, because it would take longer for the bullet to get to its target, allowing more downwards acceleration by gravity.
However, this makes your second point far more accurate, as a lower powder load always means less recoil.
Their third point about damage is also not strictly incorrect. Yes, the barrel would give it more time to accelerate, but with the lower powder load, it would not be significant enough to counteract it. This would overall give it less energy, but this is not necessarily a bad thing. An often used round for stealth operations in special forces is a .22 caliber subsonic round. The reason it is used is due to the fact that it has such a low velocity. At close enough ranges (a few dozen meters) it has enough energy to pierce the skull, but not enough to exit out the other side. This causes it to bounce off the other side of the skull, and further tear up the brain, ensuring a quick and quiet kill. In addition, bullets with lower velocities are more likely to remain inside a person's body, causing more damage in the long run.

It is hard to explain what makes this game so addicting. On paper it looks like the most boring thing in the world. Driving a truck from one city to another for hours, but like Civilization has its "just one more turn" this game has a similar thing. Just a little further, just get to the next city, just one more one more trip.
I don't really have any interest in trucks, but I have still put alot of hours into this game. Both relaxing and rewarding. You level up with each trip, so there is a good sense of progression and even a basic RPG element as well. With many other games today having a very open world and tons of possibilities, there is something appealing about something utterly simple like getting from point A to point B. No real choices or stragies to make, just do it. Probably not a thing for everybody, but give it a try even though it looks boring on paper.

I have a love-hate relationship with this game.
While having its faults it does not deserve the oversaturated hate it is getting.
Does it have short comings? Sure. But it is still one of the best, if not, the best survival game out there. No other game comes close to the experiences that you'll have in this game, even though a lot of them do try. The ammount of adrenaline you get when shots are fired, or when you hear footsteps is something that almost seduces me to come back. No other game puts me through these emotions of hate, fear and joy.
A lot of people are quick to call the game dead while the blood isn't even dry, and the body warm. It still has a very active playerbase and the BETA should be released within a few months or so. You can check the changelog and website for this, as it does get updated frequently. I believe it can fully redeem itself if given the oppertunity, but a lot of these people seemingly don't even want to give it a chance. I do agree it's been a while, but I do think you should cut the developers some slack, as they had to pretty much start from scratch after Dean Hall's departure.
A lot of people have been talking about getting blocked on Twitter. Which is odd to me. Not that I don't believe them, but they all seem to have a thing in common. None of them believe in the product they used to play so often back in the day. I don't really know what happened with these people as they don't really tell you. It's just something they speak of and laugh about and then further critisize the game for in negative reviews or videos calling it dead in the water.
Something that has also been happening, is they call the game flawed because of the community it has. Same thing happens with games such as Rust or Garry's Mod. While this can be frustrating, it is not the fault of the game.
Dayz does seem to have a serious community problem. Most of the people that play have a severe bloodlust, shooting new spawns, camping loot places and just being a total tool.
I do hope the people that were so negative before will all come back and play when the game reaches the beta phase. A lot of promises are made for the beta, and a lot of mini-updates were made also.
I believe that this is still a good game, and one of the best survival games out there. Don't allow yourself to be scared away by negativity and cloned arguments regarding its livelihood or the original creator.

All the things you have done in the main game can be done in the DLC content from customizing your routes or trucks or drive freely to explore the vast world of the game. This is definitely a must get for anyone who is looking for a nice relaxing game to play that will suck you in for many hours.

As a child and still recently I have always wanted to drive big vehicles: Lorries, Vans, etc.  To be honest this is the closest I'm likely to get without spending a grand and the rest on Class 1 lessons that I'd probably never then use.  After playing the demo I decided to buy the full game as simulation plus management element not only satisifed the excitement (I'll get to that) element I wanted but also the endless, endless desire for fettling I have.
I really was unconvinced that driving an articulated lorry in a game could be exciting until I discovered how much concentration and application of logical thought it requires.  Judging how to take tight corners and negotiating the motorway at high speed are a real challenge which keeps you constantly occupied and I feel something which I haven't in other driving games; a destinct compulsion to obey the rules (whatever they may be - in this case of the road).  I think this is because unlikea lot of games, you are actively rewarded (or rather, not penalised) for driving sensibly; drivers will let you out at junctions ocassionally and they stop in the right places (Get too close to a driver and he brakes to a halt, make a bad overtake and cars coming the other way will attempt to stop).
I think what the game tries to acheive through simulation it does brilliantly.
In terms of management, this is really fun too.  Upgrading your garage(s) and managing your drivers and vehicles is exactly the right blend of depth and simplicity,  you don't have to spend hours decoding the stats of each driver before making a hire and you're kept pretty well up to date through your in-game HUD as to how your hires are doing.  Money also seems to come in at a balanced rate and in sensible chunks - you don't end up scratching around for cash but neither are you swimming in it.
The trucks themselves are beatifully represented and the models fantastically detailed, I've only diven two so far but differences between the two are destinct.  I started with the Iveco Stralis and quickly got quite use to this, so I bought another and hired a driver.  I finally hired a third driver, gave him my Stralis and then bought the most powerful truck I could afford at my level (10 at this point).  A Volvo FH16 classic.  As soon as I pulled away I noticed the difference, with nearly twice the power and almost 2.5 times the torque it was rather difficult to drive at first.  The way it should be, a game should continually test and this scenario mimics real life.  You don't go from a Polo to a Ferrari without noticing the difference.
Ok, a couple of gripes; they aren't deal breakers but things that if were included at a later stage would be really great.  The first one I think is a bit lapse however.
1.  There's no training mode.  Really?  As a result of my latent interest I was probably more prepared than most when going into this game, but still some stuff I had NO idea.  Let's forget for a moment that fact you're trying to drive something approaching 80ft long and pivots 20ft from the front  (Just wait till you come to back it up for the first time) and concentrate on a few key words.
Retarder, Exhaust Brake and 12-gear gearbox.  No idea?  Not surprised.  I really think this game needs a training mode as for me part of the fun of simulation games is doing things properly and there are lots of things that need explaining even if you drive a car, like for instance the fact that if you pull away from the lights in 1st you'll be in 4th or 5th before you've crossed the junction.  Pull away in 3rd or 4th.
2.  The fettling element with your trucks is great, you can change almost every part in and out to your heart's content but there's little in the way of guidance or much pay-off.  Upgrading the engine is obvious; more power, more torque but apart from allowing you to go a bit faster I'm not sure what the real benefit of it is.  Perhaps if there was a maximum permissible load per engine size so upgrading meant you could pull bigger loads?
I also have no idea why I would upgrade to a 6x2 chassis other than the fact that it looks the dog's.
3.  I'm not really into the whole posting photos thing but I do like posing a good shot to admire the rig I've spent time agonising over the pait job for. Can we please have a mode where you can assembled all or selected trucks from your fleet for a group photo?  One which perhaps allows you to reposition them within the shot, at a choice of some locations?
Right, sorry.  I know it sounds like nothing but whinge but there are a few bits I'd like to see added or improved.  That said I absolutely love this game, it's brilliant.  Buy it, seriously.

Lets see... Where to start, Ahh I got it.
I was originally gifted this game in (Early) 2015 as I played and loved the Arma 2 mod and they thought I would love it.
I originally hated the game as the Melee combat was clunky (Still is but it got a lot better) and the Ranged combat was primitive as hell.
Fast forward to Early September 2016 the game is a lot better in ever aspect!
- The Ranged combat is very smoothe and relies on knowlage and bullet drop isntead of just "Oh point and shoot ahaha I killed you!"(Rating: 8/ 10)
- The melee combat, While still clunky is actuially not bad if your ping is very low, Other then that zombies tend to teleport around.  (Rating: 5 / 10)
- The zombies are a lot different then in the mod, You dont just sit in a pine tree for a few seconds to lose them. You can lock them inside buildings or lock yourself inside them. (I do that often) Or You can try and break line of sight in the forest (Keep moving, They can easily keep up with you.) (Rating: 6 / 10)
- Last but not least: The players. Most players will try to outright kill your or stab you in the back making trust a very very deadly thing to have. But, When you constantly kill on sight (As♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥do) you also start to develop a certain mindset that you are getting closer and closer to being invincible due to your end-game gear or your large group. None of this is true of course. (Rating: ??? / 10) (You cant rate a whole player base to be honest, Just dont trust anyone.)
Now, There are many ways to play DayZ but each one had its own set of Highs and Lows, Here are the biggest three.
Hero - A player who goes out of there way to help and defend players, Even when said players may not deserve it at the time. They will be the first ones to get you up after you are knocked out from a bandit or a Hoard of Zeds. Now most heros are not idiots, They wont run in the open to save your sorry♥♥♥♥♥if your knocked out but they will try to find other ways around. Often found on the coastal cities.
Neutral - They dont care about you, But they dont wat to kill you either, They will keep their distance and stay out of sight to avoid people. They only want to survive and they will ensure that one way or the other. These people are often found in the far north due to the lack of people and the higher survival rate in general.
Bandit - These people hate humanity and they will kill anyone and everyone in existence if they can. They will kill Freshspawns for the fun of it and wound others because it gets there rocks off. Found in groups (Some small and some large) around or inside most major cities.

I like the ideas in this game, but I do have some things to point out. It might be a bit of a long one.
Firstly, what is typically used is something called subsonic rounds. This is a round with a significantly lesser powder load. This is intended to lower the velocity of the round to, well, subsonic speeds. This means that it goes slower than the speed of sound, because a great deal of the sound that comes from a gun firing is from the sonic boom created by the bullet. This would mean that the bullet drop would in fact be greater, because it would take longer for the bullet to get to its target, allowing more downwards acceleration by gravity.
However, this makes your second point far more accurate, as a lower powder load always means less recoil.
Their third point about damage is also not strictly incorrect. Yes, the barrel would give it more time to accelerate, but with the lower powder load, it would not be significant enough to counteract it. This would overall give it less energy, but this is not necessarily a bad thing. An often used round for stealth operations in special forces is a .22 caliber subsonic round. The reason it is used is due to the fact that it has such a low velocity. At close enough ranges (a few dozen meters) it has enough energy to pierce the skull, but not enough to exit out the other side. This causes it to bounce off the other side of the skull, and further tear up the brain, ensuring a quick and quiet kill. In addition, bullets with lower velocities are more likely to remain inside a person's body, causing more damage in the long run.

I have over 3 million miles in real world semi's in 3 countries. I have driven just about every type of truck, hauled most types of loads, and did so for nearly 18 yrs. Since being forced into early retirement for medical reasons. I have tried every truck simulator out there, looking for a means to keep my skills sharp. Though this is based in Europe and it's primary focus is on COE's. This is the most realistic semi/ truck simulator out there. The world dynamic's are the most true to life I have ever seen. The shifting actually behaves like it should in a real truck. This is by far the best truck simulator out on the market. Can't wait for one to be done for America and Austrailia.
In no other truck simulator out there, could I drive from the 1st person view. This one I haven't had to take it out of it. The views are spot on, the feel that comes thru is fantastic. All you need is a real truck cab mockup, a vibrating device tied to the engine noise, rumble strips and with a large enough screen, it's doubtful you would realize this was just a game enviroment. The only downfall I have found, the engine noise level inside the cab is way too low. I'm used to being able to drive by the sound without gauges, because of this I have to look from time to time. Generally I find this to be a worthy value and a great trainer aid. I am glad I found this simulator here on Steam. I'v also added some DLC mods as well as other mods that expand the map, trailer types and cargo. Makes it much more to life. But ETS2 is still a great starting point on its own.  Highly recommend.

My review of Borderlands 2
Borderlands 2 provides a lengthy adventure, and one that gets better when you play it with friends. As before, online games can accommodate up to four players of any character class. A small icon denotes how well you are matched with potential players, and though the difficulty attempts to scale appropriately, it's best to play with someone close to you in level. If you accomplish later missions while someone else is hosting the game, you'll be given the option to skip those missions when you reach them on your own, which helps minimize the redundant play that was often the result of joining online games in Borderlands. A new item trading mechanic, tougher enemies, better rewards and playing the game cooperatively is the absolute best way to experience the game.
Borderlands 2 is an amazing and heart-stopping game. Both singleplayer and multiplayer options in the game are excellent, but its always better to play with some buddies! Then there's the loot, the loot is extremely obsessive and I spend a lot of time comparing my guns to see which is better. I even think I spend almost as much time in my inventory than actually playing the game!
I do have two complaints though, occassionally it does feel that the combat is a tiny bit repetitive, I do wish that they would add a bit more variety to the enemies The best shoot and loot of all time in my opinion. Also, there are no difficulty options to choose from which is slightly annoying as some players like to play on easy mode or other ones like playing on hard or if you're like me and like to play on medium difficulty. Although, these can be looked over as the positives definitely beat the negatives  A near perfect game.
This concludes my review of Borderlands 2

I think when I first saw this game on steam I chuckled to myself, thinking "Pfft, seems like the worst game ever, who wants to drive a truck for hours?"
15 hours in, I'm not chuckling any more.
This game has a strange, addicting appeal I don't quite understand. I'm currently hauling a load of forklifts (my specialty these days) from Brussels to Amsterdam and I'm almost out of time. My Volvo FHS (not the best truck but she's all mine) is rumbling away underneath my feet, and I'm scrolling through the job listings to find a new truck driver for my small trucking company (I had to let Mario go, he just wasn't cutting it). This game is a bona fide RPG, simulator, tycoon game, and driving game all in one. There's a lot of depth to how the trucks operate, although it's up to you how authentic you want to make the experience. You can level up your character to be specialized in hauling certain loads. You can upgrade your truck after you've made enough money to purchase one. Too poor? Take out a loan from the bank! Eventually, you can open your own company and slowly buy up more garages across all of Europe to become the best trucker of them all.
There's nothing quite like kicking back and listening to the in game radio, streaming live from actual internet radio stations in Europe and driving through a lush countryside as the sun rises. I never knew I wanted to be a truck driver so bad!
Way of the road, buddy.

The idea of driving a semi (or lorry, if you're English) around Europe seems rather bland and boring, but for me, it was a chance to learn the geography and cities of Europe.  You can start in any city on the map, whther it be Aberdeen, Scotland or Paris or Olsztyn, Poland.  It works on an experience system, and as you level up, you can increase attributes that give you better jobs that pay more, so you can buy garages, more trucks, and workers to drive them to do jobs and make you even more money.
As such, there is no end-game on this, so for you, it might be making a billion Euros (this game supports any currency used in the countries featured in the game, like the British pound or Polish zloty, which also come with exchange rates), or exploring the whole map (be sure to stop at recruitment centers and small truck dealers if you're a cartography addict like me, passing by won't turn them from grey to yellow on the map), or just buying, upgrading, and filling every garage in every city.
Since this is a simulator, you still have to stick in your lane and do the speed limit.  There are no cops, but if you break a law, you face an immediate fine (red light offence, vehicle crash, speed offence, etc.), but you won't be fined for not using a turn signal or switch lanes on double-solid lane lines.  I've also experienced several glitches, like running a red light didn't fine me, some cars and trucks go through turns without slowing down, and in the biggest case, having everyone stop at a railroad crossing (complete with red lights and bells) for a train that never came.  This game doesn't have as much Europe as some would like, stopping as far west as Paris, north as Aberdeen, south as Milan, Italty, and east as Poland, Slovakia, and Hungary.  Also worth noting is that the game using the native names for cities for authenticity while in that country, like Praha, Czech Republic (Prague), Munchen, Germany (Munich), or Geneve, Switzerland (Geneva).  If you're up for all this, then take a job, and start truckin.

Ignore all reviews posted before December 20th, 2016. 0.61 was a major update.
The game has gone from almost unplayable to highly playable and maybe close to release. Getting over 60 fps all the time in 1080P, everything on very high, playing on an i7-6700K, GTX 1070, and 16GB RAM. I should note that my laptop, i7-4720HQ, with GTX 970M and 12GB RAM needs most settings on low to keep FPS high and gets a CTD per hour if I turn things up. The hardware reqs are pretty high.
---
It's an incredibly fun and unique game, but it does have a learning curve, especially in the first hour after spawning, so I'll offer a bunch of important tips. Use the map at
. Read street signs and study major landmarks ASAP to figure out your initial location. You are born starving, so eat lots of apples as soon as you can get to them. They are the green dots on the map. You are only maxed on food and water when your status bars (pressing tab) read "stuffed, hydrated, and energized." At this point, you could probably sprint for an hour before needing to arrive at new food and water sources.
After eating or while traveling to your first apples, with your hands empty, try to search non-grassy, rocky-looking ground for stones by pressing F. When you find one, right click the stone in your inventory to craft it into a stone knife. If you find any pristine clothes while looting houses, put the knife in your hands and right click the clothes to tear them into rags (you can do this to the shirt you spawned with). They have to be pristine clothes because you use these rags as bandages if a zombie causes you to bleed by right clicking a rag in your inventory and clicking use. Damaged clothes make damaged rags which will cause infections when used as bandages. Always punch heads to kill zombies rather than using a melee weapon (unless brass knuckles) and never run away from them because they are hard to lose and you'll probably attract more.
Your stone knife can also harvest wood from trees and bushes. If your character falls and complains of hurt feet, ankles/legs, etc., put a rag in your hand and then right click some wood in your inventory to make a splint and use the splint. Don't eat raw meat unless you have charcoal tabs to cure sickness. Apples contain some water, but for more water, find wells on the map and never drink from other water sources (blue dots on map) unless you have a container and water purification tablets. Get out of the rain ASAP and dry yourself off from being "damp" by sprinting around indoors (also makes you "hot"). If you are "completely drenched," you will die of hypothermia, even indoors, unless you make a fire which requires matches, a rag, and some wood. You may not find matches before the first rain, so you may need to just find shelter and wait out the rain.
Later on, you will find rain gear that make rain not so dangerous. When you have satisfied your hunger/thirst and have some rags for safety, begin looting nearest towns/cities until you find a backpack (or craft one from rope, wood, and a burlap sack). Fill backpack with apples. Run northwest for better loot. Turn up your brightness and gamma a little for basic night time visibility. Happy looting.

My review of Borderlands 2
Borderlands 2 provides a lengthy adventure, and one that gets better when you play it with friends. As before, online games can accommodate up to four players of any character class. A small icon denotes how well you are matched with potential players, and though the difficulty attempts to scale appropriately, it's best to play with someone close to you in level. If you accomplish later missions while someone else is hosting the game, you'll be given the option to skip those missions when you reach them on your own, which helps minimize the redundant play that was often the result of joining online games in Borderlands. A new item trading mechanic, tougher enemies, better rewards and playing the game cooperatively is the absolute best way to experience the game.
Borderlands 2 is an amazing and heart-stopping game. Both singleplayer and multiplayer options in the game are excellent, but its always better to play with some buddies! Then there's the loot, the loot is extremely obsessive and I spend a lot of time comparing my guns to see which is better. I even think I spend almost as much time in my inventory than actually playing the game!
I do have two complaints though, occassionally it does feel that the combat is a tiny bit repetitive, I do wish that they would add a bit more variety to the enemies The best shoot and loot of all time in my opinion. Also, there are no difficulty options to choose from which is slightly annoying as some players like to play on easy mode or other ones like playing on hard or if you're like me and like to play on medium difficulty. Although, these can be looked over as the positives definitely beat the negatives  A near perfect game.
This concludes my review of Borderlands 2

I've started playing DayZ back when it was a mod for Arma 2 and remember being really into it and looking forward to each new update. As a result I was pretty exited when the "stand alone" version came out and bought it at launch.
Unfortunatly the game itself wasn't nearly as developed as the mod had been and was riddled with bugs, such as zombies clipping through walls or randomly falling off of ladders and similar issues, but the developers promised that updates in future months would fix all that.
Over the following 3 years I regularly checked on the progress the developers made would summarize it in one sentence: Nothing changed.
Sure, there are a few new crafting options and apparently there now more animals running around in the wild, but the core problems like broken zombies or ladders, as well as too sparse spawn of food and water still persist. New crafting or hunting options or any gear in general has no meaning if you can't live long enough to see any of it. roughly 75% of my deaths have been to starvation or dehydration, even though I was walking for hours from town to town looting every house.
The other 25% of death goes to players, since the zombies have become so rare at this point that they might as well not be in the game.
Back when the game launched the developers justified the low spawn rate of the zombies by pointing out that various glitches in their AI (such as the clipping through walls) would make the game unplayable if there where too many zombies around, therefore the spawn rates on zombies being lower than ever should tell you everything you need to know.
The mod was miles ahead of this game.

Euro Truck Simulator is the "Football Manager" of trucking simulators. Not only can you bid on and drive your own routes, you eventually buy new garages / bases, hire personnel, send them on routes, buy trucks, and so on - eventually building your transportation empire. One of the two minor negatives is that this is a /simulator/, there's nothing here for anyone interested in blowing up aliens or slaying dragons. Otherwise the only caveat is that this game does NOT include any kind of tutorial or free driving range to practice driving skills. The developer, SCS, believes gamers should have to buy their older (but still very competent) games Scania Truck Driving Simulator or Trucks & Trailers. Scania TDS should be on Steam sometime in the future, but I doubt Trucks & Trailers will be. Trucks & Trailers is truly the best starting point for truck / combination vehicle simulation, which is only $13. Scania TDS is a "spirtual successor", if you will, because it features much more difficult challenges. At $25 it's a worthwhile purchase for anyone that beat all of the challenges in T&T - but not worth the purchase otherwise since T&T is better for beginners and it's only half the price, and ETS2 can often be found on sale for less than Scania and has much more going for it.

Ladies and gentlemen, I present to you the definitive cure for insomnia.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a fine simulator that mimics enough physics and visual splendor to immerse you into the world of roads and heavy goods vehicles. Unfortunatly, there isn't much in the form of gameplay. You get a lorry, pick up some cargo, drive a few hundred miles and you get paid. Rinse, repeat. It is a seemingly endless process with barely anything worth mentioning. There are no cyclists to avoid. No looters to fight off when you're resting by the roadside. No police chases. No drug and alcohol checks. Nothing but your truck and the other robots that fill a world dictated by traffic lights and speed cameras.
The sim does a good job at making you feel like a trucker. You even have to take the mandatory rest every 10 hours, or face a penalty. However, this is horribly obsolete feature because I fall asleep behind the wheel faster than the game can black out the screen.

This is a game you should not buy if you are not intrested in trucking or chauffeuring, but if you are you might wanna pick up a copy at a sale.

text:
The original Rust was a simple, clean and basic game which was fun to play, especially considering that it was so fresh and new. You could forgive it's faults because at it's core it was good, and you knew they would improve the lackluster outer shell of the experience with regular, consistant updates.
Then they screwed everything up with new Rust.
Rust is basically the video game equivilant of Coca Cola. It was a'ight, and beloved by all. But someone up in the headquarters had a brain anuerysm and said "Hey, let's release a NEW, practically unfinished overhaul of Rust!".
You know the saying, "If it ain't broke don't fix it"? These guys had something that was partially broken, and smashed the part which worked to peices in an attempt to build something bigger. The only problem was that when you try and build something that big with such little time and resources, you realize you've bit off way more than you can chew and the new product, while objectively better, sucks eggs.
And new Rust was born.
Basically, Gary and his team has been spending the last few years trying to fix the monsterous and bloated overzelous moneypit that is New Rust, and while they have improved it a little, it still is not as good as the original. They apparently haven't head of quality over quantity over there, and they just recently realized that they should stop adding frivolous add-ons to the game when the core gameplay is still broken.
There have been several half-baked attempts to make it more like coke classic, but it still tastes like crappy new coke. And I think it will for many years until they get back their original formula.
My advice is as follows:
If you're looking for your first multiplayer survival game, don't get Rust. Get The Forest, which I've found has everything I liked about old rust and more, and it's on a fast track to get even better.
If you already have a handful of good multiplayer survival games, get Rust when it's on sale. It's up to you, but if you want to join the long haul of waiting for the game to be good again after a couple years of work, go ahead, as I feel it will eventually become a rewarding and fun investment. Someday.
If you already have Rust, and you're eligable for a refund, my advice is varied. Again, if you don't have The Forest, get a refund and buy that ASAP. It's everything rust could have been. However, if you already have one or more perfectly functional and enjoyable multiplayer survival games, just wait. It'll go back to coke classic eventually.
(Also, be warned. The community is kind of the worst I've ever seen and will KOS you no matter what. Facepunch's idea of players working together to survive went down the crapper as soon as players realized they could kill and raid each other. There's a game where this formula works better, though. It's called the Forest.)

I have no idea why, but driving a virtual truck across a virtual Western and Central Europe is so much fun. Maybe it's the truck upgrades, maybe it's the greed of building a super-rich truck empire. I dunno, but I love it. All except for the fact that the radio feature (which lets you listen to internet radio from all the countries featured in the game) decided to pack its bags after an update. But aside from that, I love it!

Simulators tend to be hit and miss, but this is no doubt a hit. This is a game where you can chill, as though you are indeed driving through Europe. When you do the larger missions, completion is fabulously rewarding, as is the excitment the game manages to give when you purchase your own truck.
They have managed to get the scaling down of Europe and the speed of time spot on in my opinion. The perfection means that it's not too slow going from one country to another, but there is a certain marathon of time to fare in driving. I think this plays an important role in how much satisfaction the game gives you; getting 20,000 virtual pounds has never felt so good after an hour's drive.
I'm not going to pretend this game is bang on though. Things do end up being repetitive; for example the locations for a company are exactly the same style of building no matter where you are. There are limited AI cars (themselves a bit dim-witted), the motorways could do with being a little bit busier (like rush hour), and the turn off junctions on motorways are extremelly inaccurate.
My suggestions for an update would be to allow the driver to skip a track whilst driving in music, and for the fuel prices to be updated through the internet to match the current prices. Surely that's not too difficult?
That may sound like a proper moan, but these are tiny issues that can't overlap the fact that this is a very well designed game with jaw-dropping physics on the trucks. Just don't tell your friends that this is a more enjoyable game than most action games out there...

Those who enjoy hardcore survival games will fill with joy playing this game. Players aren't bullet sponges and real life combat mechanics (bleeding, broken bones etc) are in the game. If you've played any Arma games this game has an identical feel and style to the combat. This game is definately not the casual player. You can spend hours looting and someone can end those continuous hours of hard work with one shot. That's the type of gameplay in this game and for me not many games do this right, which is why I personally play the game.
Nowhere near as many bugs in the game currently as there used to be a couple of years back. Zombies don't clip through every model in the game, i've never experienced any deaths by door or rock and I haven't any unexplained character wipes. From my experience bugs are definately not an issue in this current stage of development, however this may not be the case for other people. Keep this into consideration.
Just recently specifc sounds such as firearms and melee weapons have been tweaked, to sound a lot more realistic. When firearms are shot now they can be heard correctly with factors determining the loudness and direction of the shot. Like I stated previously the game has realistic combat mechanics which created a whole new level of difficulty in the game. Loot is very scarce in the game, you have to spend a decent amount of time getting decent clothing, food and tools. Depending on where you're looking you will find specifc gear in specific places. If you're looting an military compound, you're going to find military gear. Hunting, fireplaces and cannabilism are in the game. Touching back to sounds you will hear birds, trees and the sound of footsteps while playing. Overall yeah, the game has a lot of immersion and realism.
Multiple playstyles are used in this game. How I see it there is three types of players.
