RUST is a multiplayer, Open world survival game with great core building system and generally good ideas, but it has several flaws, lack of content and an ultimately shallow and empty experience.
The game is in development since 2013 (3 solid years) but it feels like if it was just released yesterday in Early Access. While the core experience is fun and there are quite a few things one can build, it is heavily limited after 10-15 hours of gameplay value. After reaching the end of the “tech tree” with all the assets, the game provides little interest after on, except the hunting of other survivors.
This causes RUST to have a generally very hostile player base whose primary purpose to raid player compounds and kill on sight. Since the game does not provide literally any PVE experience, exploration value and have limited building options every game turns out (after 10-15 hours) a Deathmatch.
To list the issues
The Positives
I would have expected much more from a game in Early Access for 3 years, but it seems RUST have the same level semi-abandoned state just as Day-Z. They had the time to implement micro transactions (via Steam marketplace) tho. ARK and even the newly released (in Early Access) Conan Exiles have so much more content than this game.
While the core content is fun, you will only get so much from it and realize the heavy limitations. I would suggest looking elsewhere, since in this current state I cannot recommend this game.

BUILD AT TIME OF REVIEW: 0.61.13 (please rememeber this review may become outdated if my lazy self fails to update it with future updates)
~A review by a guy whose girlfriend gave him a deeply dissapointed look when she saw how long he'd played DayZ
Well here it is, you've found it. The legend, the myth, the loved, the hated, the one and only (except for those 8 trillion Arma 2 and 3 mods) DayZ. First off I'm gonna give a bit of a disclaimer- DayZ has a real nostalgia factor for me, my friends and I used to play the original mod together back in the day- that being said I will attempt to keep this as unbiased as possible. Hopefully this will help you decide if DayZ is for you.
THE BAD- Let's get the worst out of the way first shall we?
-Fourth year of early access, give it up for year four!
-Performance is dissapointing. You're reading a review by someone who plays battlefield 1 at ultra but sturggles to push 30 fps in towns at high settings in DayZ.
-Buggy as that creepy bug room at the zoo but this is getting way better.
-You will go through entire phases of your life between updates and the devs will act like it's all good
THE... WELL.... I MEAN IT COULD BE WORS- THE "MEH", THIS IS THE "MEH" SECTION
-Zombies no longer walk through walls, in fact they have pretty good pathfinding. Otherwise they're quite basic.
-Vehicles as of the last patch were buggy but functional (currently vehicles have been removed for polishing)
-Melee combat as a whole is very basic. Great variety of weapons however, from scredrivers and hammers to longswords and chainsaws.
THE CONTROVERSIAL: You ever seen one of those rubber band balls? DayZ is like one of those- except the rubber bands are controversial gameplay aspects...
-The player controler is perpetually wonky. It feels a bit clunky which some people like, others don't. It makes every action require more thought.
-The community is at worst annoying and full of deathmatching bandits and at best full of noble heroes and devilishly clever evil geniuses, Very mixed bag there.
-Plentiful PvP will keep you on edge. Some people think there's too much of it.
THE GOOD: don't worry, this sections pretty big...
-Awesome variety of gear and methods. Become a businessman turned survivor, and elite soldier, a paramedic, a warlord bandit, a canibalistic lumberjack, a psycho wearing nothing but underwear and a clown mask chasing terrified players through the woods laughing maniacally... yeah I've seen it.
-Chernarus is huge and becasue I'm a loser I still know it better than my hometwon.
-Gunplay feels like it should, feels very much like Arma still. Also the game sports a wide variety of firearms and attachments.
-Survival can be demanding. Stay warm, dry, fed, watered, healthy, oh and don't get eaten by wolves or zombies (or shot)
-Immersively immersive immersion is quite immersing. Between cluttered city streets and ambient noises, coastal fog and thunderstorms, this can be a very immersive game. (I suggest very quite dark ambient music in the background too)
-You will feel both lonely and watched all the time and yes it will get to you.
-This is a game chalk full of choices. Look for food in town, or hunt in the woods, be a sane survivor or a complete psycho- it's up to you.
-When you see there's been an update you will want to sprint home at mach 6 (sanic fast) to check it out.
DayZ is a mixed bag... You'll have to be patient and willing to shell out the steep price for it, and overlook more bugs than you'd ideally like to and put up with the seemingly perpetual state of early access... and it's understandble if you don't want to. But if you do you'll get a survival experience like none other, full of anxiety, exploration, brave moments, terrifying encounters and you'll gather plenty of stories to share with your gamer friends and no two of your characters lives will be quite the same. In many ways, DayZ is what you make of it. The adventure is yours to craft, so craft it well.

The idea of driving a semi (or lorry, if you're English) around Europe seems rather bland and boring, but for me, it was a chance to learn the geography and cities of Europe.  You can start in any city on the map, whther it be Aberdeen, Scotland or Paris or Olsztyn, Poland.  It works on an experience system, and as you level up, you can increase attributes that give you better jobs that pay more, so you can buy garages, more trucks, and workers to drive them to do jobs and make you even more money.
As such, there is no end-game on this, so for you, it might be making a billion Euros (this game supports any currency used in the countries featured in the game, like the British pound or Polish zloty, which also come with exchange rates), or exploring the whole map (be sure to stop at recruitment centers and small truck dealers if you're a cartography addict like me, passing by won't turn them from grey to yellow on the map), or just buying, upgrading, and filling every garage in every city.
Since this is a simulator, you still have to stick in your lane and do the speed limit.  There are no cops, but if you break a law, you face an immediate fine (red light offence, vehicle crash, speed offence, etc.), but you won't be fined for not using a turn signal or switch lanes on double-solid lane lines.  I've also experienced several glitches, like running a red light didn't fine me, some cars and trucks go through turns without slowing down, and in the biggest case, having everyone stop at a railroad crossing (complete with red lights and bells) for a train that never came.  This game doesn't have as much Europe as some would like, stopping as far west as Paris, north as Aberdeen, south as Milan, Italty, and east as Poland, Slovakia, and Hungary.  Also worth noting is that the game using the native names for cities for authenticity while in that country, like Praha, Czech Republic (Prague), Munchen, Germany (Munich), or Geneve, Switzerland (Geneva).  If you're up for all this, then take a job, and start truckin.

First of all I have been playing Rust for over a year and would say I have a good amount of time on the game to really review it.
When you first play Rust you will probably die within the first 5minutes and it may happen multiple times within the first hour of playing the game. I find this is usually what makes people hate Rust.
Rust is a very good game in the sense that it allows you to build bases however you would like (to a degree) and that you can craft weapons, ammo and resources in order to defend your base or use the resources to raid other bases. The community is Rust is savage and that is just something you will have to get over in order to like Rust, treat everyone as a threat but that doesn't mean you need to shoot everyone you see.
Decide what sort of person you are, are you someone who will shoot anyone you see? Or are you a player that will only shoot people who are a threat to you and your base? Rust can be frustrating when your base gets raided by other players or when you die and lose your stuff. But that is just part of the game and if you can't handle that then you should'nt be on Rust in the first place. Don't hate the game because someone else is better than you.

If you have never played a simulation before, or if you generally do not like them (for reasons of stigma or otherwise), ignore pretty much all of the other reviews.
I see a LOT of posts about how fantastic the simulation aspects are and how accurate everything feels. While I agree, only expounding on the qualities that make it a good "simulation" is NOT a good way to sell this game to the countless number of people who would never touch a simulation even if you paid them. Yes, it is a simulation, but it as much an open world driving game as NFS Undercover, Burnout Paradise, or many others. When many people think of "simulation", "boring" quickly comes to mind. This isn't that, not at all. I love the game, and I find it difficult to describe what is so captivating about it. I would liken ETS2 to less of a Lunar orbiter simulator and more of the Sims series. Not in style, but in terms of in-game entertainment and playability. I implore anyone who reads this review/plee and is hesitant to buy the game, download the demo and give it a try. You might just forget that you are playing a dreaded simulator!

My name is Jsn1981 and I'm... Wait, this isn't a meeting.. It's a review... Here we go:
So.. After some time spent on Rust, I have developed an opinion. Not about Rust, but about survival games in general.
If it is a multiplayer survival game, then the community is often salty and/or toxic. That's not as bad as most people seem to think. It adds rivalry and bitterness towards other players, which, games of this nature were designed to nurture.
You have nothing to do but become the best. And, everyone else is in your way.
Rust is an excellent game with a terrible community. It's fantastic.
Rust has excellent graphics with arguably even beter graphical glitches. Every time I kill a bear, it's head spins around like it was the stunt double for Linda Blair in The Excorcist. My bandaids looks like agave plants.. Water sometimes does not render...even with the graphics all the way up. None of this bothers me at all.
Rust has excellent gameplay. Wether you like to solo it or group up. Farm or kill other players. There is something there for you to excell at. Hell, even if you like to just randomly surprise friends with a bout of gunfire for no reason, you can excel at that.
I would sell milk forever in order to make sure every pc gamer in the world has a chance to own this game.
If you don't agree with this review, I don't care.
This is not satire. This is how I honestly feel about this game. Thank you.

Undertale, at the time of this review, has sort of lost its spotlight. Upon it's release, it drew in a huge amount of fans, and for good reason. The game has some amazing positives to it, many that will outweigh the negatives. Personally, I never much got into the game. I liked the innovative game play, but I got bored of it's repetitiveness rather fast. The fan culture grew tiresome as well. For me, it just seemed like the game grew old a little too fast. Granted, for it being a relatively short game, it held my interest much longer than most of it's kind.
Now, let's get into the part everyone actually likes to read.
Pros:
-Comedic, though not to the point of turning the plot into a joke.
-Speaking of plot, it's a very inspired one. It is one of the game's most praised feature. A short and deep sort of tale.
-Innovative and distinct battle system. Turn-based, but with moments of intense action that you might not expect.
-Interesting and lovable characters. They each have very distinct personalities.
-There is a high replay value. Depending on your actions in the game, you can change the outcome of the plot entirely. In fact, a main mechanic in the game has to do with starting over.
-There is a lot of fan support, and it's easy to find other fan content of the game.
Cons:
-The game can feel rather grind-y at times, mostly due to random encounters.
-The plot is short, and though some may appreciate that, it means that many of the characters and aspects of the game seem underdeveloped. However, for what the game is meant to be, this isn't the worst con.
-Not very appealing aesthetically. Most of the game keeps a rather simplistic sort of design, but it doesn't look as nice as other simplistic designs I've seen.
-The fanculture surrounding this game has been deemed annoying as of late. Be prepared for skeleton porn and bad OCs.
Overall, I'd say this game is worth buying, if not for the game play and innovative game mechanics, then for the plot.

So yeah, this game is really, really, REALLY good.
Its shmup-inspired battle system is just easy-but-fun enough to end up working well, even in a game that blatantly advertises itself as the "RPG game where you don't have to destroy anyone". Which is cool, but more importantly, it has one of the best soundtracks of...pretty much any video game ever. Mostly because Toby Fox is actually a musician and this game is a miraculously functional bundle of spaghetti code, but that's not really stopping him. (No, that wasn't hyperbole, the soundtrack actually is that good.)
Undertale also has a remarkable ability to make people attached to its characters. Like, unless you have pretty specific tastes, there aren't any unlikable characters in the game. It also pulls off the JRPG staple of humorous cutscenes very well, better than some games that rely solely on it.
The only problem is if you already know everything about it. In which case it's still pretty good.
But seriously, if you're in the rare category of people who still don't know what DIO's Stand does—I mean, who haven't had Undertale spoiled for them yet, be warned that enough spoilers CAN ruin this game. And as tempting as it may be, try not to touch the soundtrack.
As an additional warning, this game assumes that its audience plays JRPGs, a genre that generally requires a lot of time investment and the ability to empathize with fictional characters to enjoy. Undertale isn't a long game, but if you can't do the latter, you're probably going to have a bad time. Outside of that, I'd recommend it to anyone who likes video games, even if they haven't touched a JRPG in their life.

I don't quite understand why a game about obeying traffic laws and making sure you get enough sleep and don't run out of gas is so engaging, but it really is. I bought my first racing wheel thanks to ETS2, which further enhances the experience. It's an odd game that I feel strange recommending, since I suspect it could be a certain neurosis that causes people to enjoy playing it, but I will defend Euro Truck Simulator 2's merits wherever and whenever my friends give me suspicious looks about it.

Euro Truck Simulator is the "Football Manager" of trucking simulators. Not only can you bid on and drive your own routes, you eventually buy new garages / bases, hire personnel, send them on routes, buy trucks, and so on - eventually building your transportation empire. One of the two minor negatives is that this is a /simulator/, there's nothing here for anyone interested in blowing up aliens or slaying dragons. Otherwise the only caveat is that this game does NOT include any kind of tutorial or free driving range to practice driving skills. The developer, SCS, believes gamers should have to buy their older (but still very competent) games Scania Truck Driving Simulator or Trucks & Trailers. Scania TDS should be on Steam sometime in the future, but I doubt Trucks & Trailers will be. Trucks & Trailers is truly the best starting point for truck / combination vehicle simulation, which is only $13. Scania TDS is a "spirtual successor", if you will, because it features much more difficult challenges. At $25 it's a worthwhile purchase for anyone that beat all of the challenges in T&T - but not worth the purchase otherwise since T&T is better for beginners and it's only half the price, and ETS2 can often be found on sale for less than Scania and has much more going for it.

12-31-2016 Alpha Review
DayZ has been in development for awhile now, and has been available to purchase for 3 years to experience the game in early development.
Hopefully the reviews get wiped once the game is released, because it's bogus reading these negative reviews, most of these people don't even know what they are talking about and seem to of not even played the recent version.
I diffiently recommend this game.  It's not for everybody, but if you're the type that likes to come home and sit down on the computer and be fully immersed in a virtual world, this game is for you.  The good thing about this survival game that is different from other competiting titles is that it doesn't require you to be on HOURS AND HOURS a day to save your progress. Character wipes barely happen unless there's a new big update, and when you log out you log out; there's no "sleeper" state like from Rust, and there's also anti-combat logging (logging out when getting attacked).
Here's the pros and cons I can say right now for the current state of this magnificant entertainment product:
-Beautiful world filled with clues and objects that tell a little about the lore
-Infected are an actual threat; they can indicate your position to other players and can really mess up your day if you decide to shoot in a risky area, attracting many of them.
-Every structure is enterable except the occasional 1 or 2 out of atleast 5000 on the world.
-Neat nutrition system and medical (however, it's still WIP and not the greatest, just like everything in the game)
-Huge, huge world. 225km squared.
-Modding support is coming in the future.
-You're always gonna remember all the interactions with players you encounter.
-Extremely fun with friends.
-Persistence; you can find tents and barrels to store loot and they stay on the world unless they are left untouched for 12-45 days.
-Ballistics. Bullets actually travel
-Wolves are scary
-FPS is amazing.  It use to be some sort of meme to make fun of dayZ's FPS back in the day but they fixed it and there's no more complaining unless your on a potato.  Sometimes FPS can go a little below 60 in areas with lots of models.
-Gestures.
-Many more things.
-Clunkyness.  This is going to be amazingly fixed however in a future update with the new player controller, which should be version 0.63. Right now it is 0.61.
-Lack of detail for some things.  For example, there's no blood decals when you shoot someone, the only blood is a crappy particle effect. This however is changing in the future for sure.
-Very annoying bugs can sometimes occure but nothing too gamebreaking, such as; bodies can sometimes go invisible but you can still loot them, you can become out of sync with the server and have some realy weird desyncy movement, zombies collide with the player very weirdly sometimes, server performance can cause dumb bugs such as zombies going through doors (THIS BARELY HAPPENS.), etc.
-Renderer can be kinda wonky sometimes, objects sometimes "pop in" but it's not too noticeable.
-Players as of right now collide weirdly when they run into other players, you kinda get pushed and teleport.
-Some other things I mentioned.
-Everything I mentioned is going to be improved and fixed.
-there's really not much of an "end game" element right now, it's fun setting goals for yourself.  Personally I think it'd be cool if they added a fairly sized island somewhere in the ocean that you could "escape" too, absent of infected, with a good place to build a shelter/base at.
Overall, I recommend this game, but like I said it's not for everybody.  Beware of these crappy negative reviews, like I said most of them are just random hate with kids not knowing anything about making a product.  Making something good takes time, everyone should know this, it's why we're not on Mars yet.

I feel like a hipster about this game (Nominated for the "I thought this game was cool before it won an award" award) because I had anticipated it's release, bought it the day of release, and spent the next week doing nothing but playing and talking about this evident passion project.
This game manages to take a very simple concept and pack as much detail into this idea as it can. The game feels like it captures something "new" using previous gems (Earthbound) as inspiration for it's core mechanics, a unique combat system that differs significantly from a normal RPGs combat. The branching story gives reason to play through the game multiple times in multiple ways in order to find every single secret the game has to offer.
The story is pretty good too, although it leaves most of it open to interpretation.
The characters have fairly strong personalities, too. Everybody is unique and loveable in their own way. Everybody serves a purpose in the story too.
Words can't describe how much I cared about this game on release. I felt it was one of my sworn duties to make sure to spread the word about this game.
So I did.
I made sure to convince as many friends as I could to give this game a chance, and many of them fell in love with it. I had friends who I barely talk to saying that just from seeing me play it they wanted to take a look at it themselves.
You can tell Toby Fox put his heart into this game and that's something I expect to see from game developers if we're gonna call video games an art form.

I actually got this game because I had heard some of the soundtrack being played at a friend's place. This soundtrack is very well done and notoriously catchy at times - I'm very partial to "Mad Dummy".
As for the game itself, as others have mentioned, if you haven't played this game and know little to nothing about it, just pick it up and play it. Reading walkthroughs or reviews will very likely ruin a good portion of the story for you and that would be a waste. Most of the characters are at the very least unique or funny and at most relatable or sympathetic, and the story paces itself well - you get pieces of the story through character interaction.
The game is an RPG/dungeon crawler with slight puzzle elements, and the interesting bit is that you do not have to kill anyone, but you can if you want; it's your choice. Gameplay is similar to olderThere is a slight learning curve to gameplay, but almost anyone can pick it up and understand what needs to be done. It is fairly linear, but I believe this was intentionally done as to keep the overall story unknown until the climax.
The art style is reminiscent of older RPGs utilizing sprite art and basic color pallette and really pulls at the nostalgia strings. It also lends to the humor and drama of the characters and story without overwhelming you with stylistic tropes.
Overall, I loved this game, and the soundtrack is a great addition to those that enjoy chiptunes/8-bit style music.

So yeah, this game is really, really, REALLY good.
Its shmup-inspired battle system is just easy-but-fun enough to end up working well, even in a game that blatantly advertises itself as the "RPG game where you don't have to destroy anyone". Which is cool, but more importantly, it has one of the best soundtracks of...pretty much any video game ever. Mostly because Toby Fox is actually a musician and this game is a miraculously functional bundle of spaghetti code, but that's not really stopping him. (No, that wasn't hyperbole, the soundtrack actually is that good.)
Undertale also has a remarkable ability to make people attached to its characters. Like, unless you have pretty specific tastes, there aren't any unlikable characters in the game. It also pulls off the JRPG staple of humorous cutscenes very well, better than some games that rely solely on it.
The only problem is if you already know everything about it. In which case it's still pretty good.
But seriously, if you're in the rare category of people who still don't know what DIO's Stand does—I mean, who haven't had Undertale spoiled for them yet, be warned that enough spoilers CAN ruin this game. And as tempting as it may be, try not to touch the soundtrack.
As an additional warning, this game assumes that its audience plays JRPGs, a genre that generally requires a lot of time investment and the ability to empathize with fictional characters to enjoy. Undertale isn't a long game, but if you can't do the latter, you're probably going to have a bad time. Outside of that, I'd recommend it to anyone who likes video games, even if they haven't touched a JRPG in their life.

Day Z is a perfect example of how NOT to do Early Access. When DayZ standalone was first announced, I was a bit surprised and interested in equal amounts. I was a bit skeptical how it would work on its own, but my interest remained none the less. Once I eventually decided I would dish out 30$ and buy it I figured it would entertain me and provide me with a survival experience, which at that point had yet to be wide spread, with no equal. However, you knew that "however" was coming, the game started out as a complete and total mess. Poor optimization, and that's putting it mildly, bad UI, horrible player base, and a developer that seemed to be further distancing themselves from their fanbase. I stopped playing, disgusted with the product and refused to play for a time. I'd occasionally come back and test the waters before promptly hopping off again.
Now don't get me wrong, there were plenty of fun and memorable moments. From getting held up, to being enslaved, and even having drawn out stressful gun fights. I got my money's worth out of it. That being said though, the developers have failed in every aspect  they could have possibly failed in. The optimization took nearly 3 years to iron out and it is still not perfect. The gameplay is still buggy and while patches could be released remedying these issues, the developers opt to introduce more features and items, which promptly become broken as well, instead.
DayZ is the sole reason I am cautious about ANY Early Access game. I take every "Alpha" or "Beta" game with a huge grain of salt, because of how poorly DayZ was and still is handled. Oh and DayZ has been out for many years now and is still in Beta. So there.

I actually got this game because I had heard some of the soundtrack being played at a friend's place. This soundtrack is very well done and notoriously catchy at times - I'm very partial to "Mad Dummy".
As for the game itself, as others have mentioned, if you haven't played this game and know little to nothing about it, just pick it up and play it. Reading walkthroughs or reviews will very likely ruin a good portion of the story for you and that would be a waste. Most of the characters are at the very least unique or funny and at most relatable or sympathetic, and the story paces itself well - you get pieces of the story through character interaction.
The game is an RPG/dungeon crawler with slight puzzle elements, and the interesting bit is that you do not have to kill anyone, but you can if you want; it's your choice. Gameplay is similar to olderThere is a slight learning curve to gameplay, but almost anyone can pick it up and understand what needs to be done. It is fairly linear, but I believe this was intentionally done as to keep the overall story unknown until the climax.
The art style is reminiscent of older RPGs utilizing sprite art and basic color pallette and really pulls at the nostalgia strings. It also lends to the humor and drama of the characters and story without overwhelming you with stylistic tropes.
Overall, I loved this game, and the soundtrack is a great addition to those that enjoy chiptunes/8-bit style music.

Rust.
Hm, Trying to be as objective as possible.
As an Alpha, It has its problems, that I am without a doubt will be fixed.
I'll start with the cons: Huge learning curve with the rifles and pistols and such. The shooting, in general, is much more difficult than other games, which in turn makes it feel much more realistic and rewarding when you get a kill.
Another con is probably the toxicity of the younger fan base. Most of the adults aren't so much, but the younger ones are. (That isn't so much a "Con" on the game's behalf, But a reflection on the community games like this create.)
Pros are too much to list:
One of the most fun and rewarding survival titles I've ever played. I'm 32 and started playing Zelda titles and stuff as a kid, so I'm not new to gaming, but this game will, like ARK and Zelda, always have a place in my memory!
The building system is stellar, compared to ARK. (Minus the fact that there is a time on how late after placing you can demo misplaced items)
The PvP is crazy intense. I mean heart pumping, adrenaline surging fight or flight moments that grab at that Darwinian instinct to run after you've spent an hour farming materials to build with and you don't want to die and lose it!
Addendum: With the addition of the tiered map system, scrap introduction, use of tiered benches and several other highly convoluted systems rapidly implemented with seemingly no forethought given to brand new players I have totally given up Rust altogether.
During XP I managed to have loads of fun, during components I had a lot of fun, but with this new system, your "Fun" is locked away. You're totally screwed if you're a newer player, too. I had a friend join me and he left from me simply explaining the "new mechanics" to him.
I suppose I should have added or talked about the addition of an even heavier RNG system into the game. It's terrible and one of the worst thought out systems for a survival game. Google "Skinner box" and that's basically exactly what the RNG based weapons drops are.
Imagine a survival game where you can randomly find a better weapon, not through hard work, not through skill, but random luck and that's the system that's currently running in Rust. You then have to research the weapon, collect the components and scrap to craft the BP in a research bench, THEN craft it. And let's keep in mind you could walk out your front door and lose that item instantly from a guy who got a slightly better RNG dropped weapon who decided to camp your door.
It further increases the already widening gap between solo players and even duos or trios.
Now if you can control a monument or town you have zero competition, whereas before this wasn't an issue.
I have to commend the devs for trying, though. But I fear what they're trying will fall into this category of "Highly innovative, but trying to reinvent the wheel for no apparent reason". It's a great system for Veterans of the game but takes almost no consideration into account of how a newer player will cope. (Considering most of the mechanics have literally never been seen in a game before)
So, for all the aforementioned traits and much more that I frankly don't feel like typing out, I'm sorry. I can't in this current iteration recommend Rust anymore. It's complicated for the sake of complication (Or "Progression") and trying to reinvent the wheel, when the wheel was working just fine and I am afraid most of the community are too biased to see or admit this and in the end it will hurt the game beyond repair because the Devs aren't getting honest feedback.

When you start off, you will not have your own truck, and you will have to take jobs using company trucks, after building up enough moolah, or building up some, and taking out a loan from the bank, you can purchase your own truck. This is where the fun truly begins. You get more deliveries, with lots of different types of cargo. You can also hire a driver to build up your company, you can get jobs with longer distances, and instead of delivering nothing but wood shavings over, and over, you can deliver fragile cargo, such as cars, or gasoline.
This simulator is fantastic, and even though it has a few troubles, I would definitely  say that you should pick it up.

Take a FPS add a dungeon crawler, take most of them away and add an open map. Take the ratchet and clank gun technology, with ES:IV drops, And halo co-op. Add great voice acting, and guess what you get? BORDERLANDS 2.
If you liked halo you'll feel right at home with it and you'll easily adapt to the different playstyle. If you like offline dungeon crawlers you'll know that most of your equipment will be useless in a few levels and what to sell at the slightest glance. Quests are fun, co-op is perfect, and you will enjoy it to any extent no matter what.
Playing alone is like elder scrolls, as in you'll advance just once and you'll get the drops and quest rewards one time unless there are special circumstances. But on co-op, you can relive absolutely every story and event your host has. want to see Lilith beg for eridium twice for no reason? grab a new player.
The level system is akin to an mmo, but more forgiving. so for example, running into lower levelled enemies will give you a god mode feeling, as they'll be useless and dr5op nonsense that all you'll want to do is sell. Which is good, because you wont fly through the challenges simply by grinding through it. Though if the quest system matches it, you may want to do everything you want before hunting quests with rare rewards. As that was a very annoying case in Oblivion.
Grab a few friends and try it out, it's pretty fun and interesting, And in my opinion it will last you a long time for entertainment. Though you may want to find a few fiends who understand how dungeon crawlers work, so they dont get stuck on equipment that obviously needs to be sold or dropped, purple or not. And the game has that message as a load screen.
Levelling, is very exponential in my opinion, so like some of the broken rpg games out there, if you're struggling on something, better try to level up or buy a good shield before anything else, because shields and normal health have their pros and cons.
After you understand the system, It'll be even mor fun to play and teach others how the system works, and you'll all e3njoy abusing the enemies in unison. Which is pretty perfect seeing as halo was insanely easy when you had a focused team.
It's a pretty unique experience. So if you really want to try a fun shooter with friends, you should give it a go.

HUGE THUMBS UP!!!!  One of the most ADDICTIVE simulations I've ever played... period!  Drive your lug nuts off making big money traveling across Europe, England, and Scotland by yourself while increasing your various skill levels (and $$$), then when you've saved enough money, buy your own rig, and be your own boss.  You'll then be free to explore every nook and cranny of this gorgeous virtual world.  As your own boss you can optionally hire and personally direct training of novice drivers to become an elite team with the specialized skills that you decide.  Don't worry... it's very easy.  With more money you can buy new garages to host more drivers, and you decide which cities to buy garages that offer the most potentially profitable routes.  With each new driver that you hire your virtual bank account will keep growing and growing as your drivers gain more skills and driving experience.  The only downside is that we're not paid in Bitcoins!  Oh well...
Since this is all about trucks there are a variety of European big rig brands and models to suit your budget and they're all massively upgradeable and customizable, including fancy paint schemes.  The more you drive the more bonus features are unlocked in the game.  Buy more garages, trucks, and upgrades, hire more drivers, and become a gear jammin' Euro-redneck tycoon rolling in the dough as you traverse the beautiful scenery while cursin' those danged 4-wheelers for holdin' you back.
One tiny hint... turn off the speed limiter in settings as there are many stretches of the Autobahn highway with NO speed limits so...  HAMMER DOWN!!!!  Also a couple of warnings... watch out for speed traps and be careful as the weather is subject to deteriorating rapidly so don't hesitate to switch on those windshield wipers and be ready to slow down for fog!
Did I mention this game is sooooooooooo ADDICTIVE?!  Gotta admit this is a good one.  It's multifaceted approach keeps it interesting.  The hiring and management of AI drivers is strictly optional but quickly draws you in as each driver has unique characteristics that you decide how to make the best use of by keeping track of his/her driver's log and selecting future driving skills to maximize performance.  And speaking of AI the quality of the AI traffic in the game is so very good that it also quickly draws you into the virtual world.
Oh, one more thing... don't forget to drive on the left side of the road when you arrive in the UK or things could get messy quickly.   Enjoy!

You know what, I've been absolutly addicted to this game and by this point have played for over 55 hours after just 8 days of getting the game. It's not your typical simulation management game and it's not your typical driving game. For some reason it is just good fun.
It's not the absolute best game in the world, the scenary is a bit samy and the cities do not really look like the cities they represent, although Bratislava is represented by the Novy Most tower, but you can't drive across it. The lack of petrol (or, "gas") stations in the actual cities feels a bit unrealistic too, the weather in the UK is 90% NOT raining which isn't realistic and at night the NPC cars lights don't show a beam in front of them. At least, though, when you get fined its only a small amount and I believed that getting tired didn't mean anything really except a small fine, until my driver dozed off just an hour from his destination, but I had to keep going otherwise I'd have missed the deadline.
The thing that mainly disappoints me with this game is that there are no explosions nor do you get simulated damage and engine smoke when it begins to malfunction. I crashed a truck and rolled it by mistake while carrying 22 tons of fuel. It never exploded or spilled or anything. That would have made it more fun than it already is.
With this game, you set up a business, but you don't have to sit back and wait, wait, wait for the money to start rolling in, you get your hands "dirty" and drive. This is a brilliant game and I fully recommend it for people who want to try something completely different.

I wasn't sure when I bought this because the premise sounds kind of corny.  I thought it might be crap, but it isn't it's great if you like driving sims!
The sim part of the driving is great.  You definitely don't want to play with keyboard / mouse (though you can).  It was much easier for me to use an Xbox controller, and I suspect a steering wheel would be better.
The other half of the game is a business sim.  You earn money by delivering goods across Europe.  WIth that money, you can upgrade your rig, buy other trucks and hire other drivers to expand your business.  This adds a lot to the game because there is a purpose and goal to your driving whereby you can fulfill goals.
A must-have for driving sim fans.

Take a FPS add a dungeon crawler, take most of them away and add an open map. Take the ratchet and clank gun technology, with ES:IV drops, And halo co-op. Add great voice acting, and guess what you get? BORDERLANDS 2.
If you liked halo you'll feel right at home with it and you'll easily adapt to the different playstyle. If you like offline dungeon crawlers you'll know that most of your equipment will be useless in a few levels and what to sell at the slightest glance. Quests are fun, co-op is perfect, and you will enjoy it to any extent no matter what.
Playing alone is like elder scrolls, as in you'll advance just once and you'll get the drops and quest rewards one time unless there are special circumstances. But on co-op, you can relive absolutely every story and event your host has. want to see Lilith beg for eridium twice for no reason? grab a new player.
The level system is akin to an mmo, but more forgiving. so for example, running into lower levelled enemies will give you a god mode feeling, as they'll be useless and dr5op nonsense that all you'll want to do is sell. Which is good, because you wont fly through the challenges simply by grinding through it. Though if the quest system matches it, you may want to do everything you want before hunting quests with rare rewards. As that was a very annoying case in Oblivion.
Grab a few friends and try it out, it's pretty fun and interesting, And in my opinion it will last you a long time for entertainment. Though you may want to find a few fiends who understand how dungeon crawlers work, so they dont get stuck on equipment that obviously needs to be sold or dropped, purple or not. And the game has that message as a load screen.
Levelling, is very exponential in my opinion, so like some of the broken rpg games out there, if you're struggling on something, better try to level up or buy a good shield before anything else, because shields and normal health have their pros and cons.
After you understand the system, It'll be even mor fun to play and teach others how the system works, and you'll all e3njoy abusing the enemies in unison. Which is pretty perfect seeing as halo was insanely easy when you had a focused team.
It's a pretty unique experience. So if you really want to try a fun shooter with friends, you should give it a go.

Too alpha. I've put in enough hours to know every single bug in this entire game, and it's just too alpha. It's a game about PVP, but the PVP is broken. The hit detection is really good, but the desync is garbage. I can shoot someone and it will be a full 3-5 seconds before they die. Most of the time in close quarters battles, I can see the delay between my weapon firing and the projectile hitting the wall. The desync has always been a problem, even in vanillla ArmA 2 and the DayZ Mod. The developers need to slow down on expanding the map and AI, and work on the PVP aspects of the game. The real meat of this game is fighting other players and fighing for survival, but it's nearly impossible when the bullets take a full 150+ ms to find their target, even at ranges less than 100 meters. I really enjoy this game, but it's really hard to recommend a game that's been pre release for too long. They should have been working on the PVP aspects from the beginning. I really appreciate how much effort has gone into the game. The wolves are awesome, being able to lock doors, being able to maintain gear. The game is extremely immersive, and I really like PVP, but the delay between firing and hitting a target is just unbearable. I won't be playing this game until there has been some noticeable improvement in the PVP aspects. I'll take opening gates and breaking my legs over poor PVP any day.

Unamaginable desync, GREAT. A recent influx of hackers, AWESOME. Maybe in three years and 6 updates later, they will make a cool new looking gun, and add in a bear that is about as harmless as the new wolves. Great(horrid) Game, Great (handicapped) developers. Hicks should feel bad about how much they haven't accomplished, and Dean should feel bad for giving the game its own title instead of sticking with what worked, the mod.

I bought this in the last two months where legacy was the only branch available. It was magical. I played with a couple of friends and we had an absolutely amazing time. The community was amazing, the single map was well built and it forced player interaction because everyone knew where the hot spots for resources were. Almost every time you came across another player, it was a funny experience. I can not describe how incredibly fun legacy Rust was (and it's scary to think that a large portion of the community now may have never even played it) This was my favorite game for a small while.
So you may be asking, why the negative review if it was so great?
Well that's just the answer, it WAS so great. Now however, it is not. The game now, lacks heart. I get a hallow feeling while playing it. The game is supposedly more streamlined now but performance is still worse than legacy. The gunplay is clunky and unrewarding ever since they got rid of hitscan. The game is a chore now, and it isn't even worth it unless you are part of a big clan. In legacy, a small group or even a solo player could be on par with a clan in anything except numbers of course, but now a large clan is needed for any type of real end game content. Otherwise you are just progressing to be killed and have to restart. The progression is a lot slower, and it feels like a job rather than a game. The community has grown more distant and aggressive, though I have no clue if it is because of the removal of legacy rust or if it is just the natural progression as to how the community would have gone.
Now, I would be completely fine with the new Rust as long as I could actually play the older version, but I can't. You used to be able to choose between launching Legacy or Experimental, and when they felt like Experimental was complete enough they put Legacy into the betas options. Despite this, Legacy still had a playerbase (though it was being taken over by hackers but that's because it wasn't getting any support from the devs and it was hard to find out how to play it).
But that wasn't enough, so they took out the ability to play it altogther.
This last paragraph is just going to be about one of the developers, Garry Newman. Garry Newman has made two games, GMod and Rust. He likes to think that even if an entire playerbase (exaggerating here) disagrees with his ideas, they all must be wrong because he couldn't possibly be (just look through his Reddit posts and tweets and see what a massive egotist this guy is). He seems to have some sort of pride issue about Legacy, because he knows people want to play it (even if there wasn't any development on it) but he won't let us. He hates the idea that people could somehow like the prototype more than its result, or at least that's my best guess. He is acting like Blizzard is about not letting people play Classic WoW. This guy supported paid mods and readily called the modding community a bunch of c***ts
he deleted the tweet later) when his entire success is based on the modding community. I hate the direction he has taken the game and so do a lot of people, I could care less about the development of new Rust as it will probably never have the same feel to it as old Rust and I wish we could just play the legacy again.
TL;DR: I liked Legacy, don't like how the game is now. I also don't like Garry Newman.

If you are the type of person that enjoys listening to music the most while driving, then this is the game for you. The radio interface includes dozens of real radio stations, or you can listen to your own MP3 files, nothing better than listenting to Real Radio Manchester classic rock while driving in simulated Northwest England. Licensed real world trucks means that every truck model has its differences, as in real life, do you like horsepower? go Volvo, do you like handling? go Majestic(Mercedes), do you like a vehicle that is undeniably French in its weirdness? go Renault Magnum or if you like a huge windshield, go MAN.Travel a simulated version of Europe hauling cargo to expand your business. Every country has its own differences:you drive on the left in the UK, Switzerland has many mountain roads, France is loaded with toll plazas, Hungary has the most evil speed zones ever, Poland has the most country single lane roads. Experience points allow you to unlock vehicle upgrades, the most important being engines and axles, but cosmetic changes can be unlocked as well, and unlock more profitable jobs. Once you have enough money, you can buy more trucks and more truck yards, hire drivers and let them make money for you. The enemy in this game is careless driving, it is very easy to flip the truck if you take a turn too fast. Speed cameras are an enemy too, you will have to learn their locations and the speed limits they have, 90kmh in Germany, 80 in Austria. This is a more of a passtime than a game, just relax, listen to your favorite tunes, you are bound to find a favorite station, Mine are Real Radio Manchester, Hotmix radio 80's and Belgrade radio 1, and travel the roads of Europe. If you do buy this game, get it with the Going East expansion, as it opens up Poland, Slovakia, and Hungary, making even more profitable jobs available.

Too alpha. I've put in enough hours to know every single bug in this entire game, and it's just too alpha. It's a game about PVP, but the PVP is broken. The hit detection is really good, but the desync is garbage. I can shoot someone and it will be a full 3-5 seconds before they die. Most of the time in close quarters battles, I can see the delay between my weapon firing and the projectile hitting the wall. The desync has always been a problem, even in vanillla ArmA 2 and the DayZ Mod. The developers need to slow down on expanding the map and AI, and work on the PVP aspects of the game. The real meat of this game is fighting other players and fighing for survival, but it's nearly impossible when the bullets take a full 150+ ms to find their target, even at ranges less than 100 meters. I really enjoy this game, but it's really hard to recommend a game that's been pre release for too long. They should have been working on the PVP aspects from the beginning. I really appreciate how much effort has gone into the game. The wolves are awesome, being able to lock doors, being able to maintain gear. The game is extremely immersive, and I really like PVP, but the delay between firing and hitting a target is just unbearable. I won't be playing this game until there has been some noticeable improvement in the PVP aspects. I'll take opening gates and breaking my legs over poor PVP any day.

The Long and Short of it: I DO reccommend this game. AND, I reccommed the Season Pass content. And I reccommend checking out the two other classes.
Borderlands 2 is fun. But it's fun ONCE. The gun play is all there, the classes are fun, as well as the two DLC classes, though I'm not going to buy the Psycho. It's all well and good. BUT, it's also all well and good ONCE. See, after you play through the story content, it feels like a slog. Especially since you have to do it twice just to get to the FIRST max level. That doesn't include the stupid decision to increase the max level not once but TWICE. They could have created better ways to progress characters, but instead just caved and gave players 22 extra unneeded levels. And THAT'S when the game stops being fun. It's a boring grind. It's the worst of the worst grind. Pick something you like and do that OVER AND OVER, because that's what you're going to have to do. And it's a bummer. It's a bummer to NOT like playing this run and gun fun game, but it really depreciates into monotony very quickly.
Not to mention, imagine wanting to play another character? Then you have to do all that motonony of max leveling AGAIN. Play through the game and all the dlc 4 to 5 and even more times, grind the raid bosses, it's the WORST end game content of any game. And it's sad to say that, because I love the game and I don't like hating the content.
Play it once, enjoy the story. Have a BLAST with all four DLCs. And then, either give into the grind or put it down. When the GOTY edition is on sale, it's a worthy price. Heck, even when it ISN'T on sale, it's a worthy price. But, after playing once, you'll see the motonoty. Unless you can find some mod for an endless randomly generated dungeon or perhaps user missions. But other than that, the game gives you nothing better to do when you beat it. I really wish the game would have just said "The end" rather than letting me grind my brains out until the game lost ALL luster.

Rust, what to say about it... It's an interesting game to say the least. in all honestly we've only scratched the surface of Rust. Why you ask? Cause it's still being refined, molded, and shaped into the best game it can possibly be. And hopefully at the end of it all I will still enjoy it as I do now, HELL I hope I will enjoy it even more so! However even with that there are a few things that I'd like to point out which could be better.
Positive:
1: Rust is ever changing, ever evolving. There is always something new to discover.
2: The Developers listen to the players and include some player ideas into the game, fix the bugs we find pretty quick and are usually really good at surprising us with newer and better things to discover and create(Ways to kill each other and survive!)
3: This game unlike so many out there gives you the ability to make and host your own server for free! As long as you have a powerful computer/server rack and are willing to keep it online 24/7 of course.
4: With all the different ways you can mod Rust, it's amazing to see what people can build and how fast they can build what they do! I love playing on modded servers when I just want to chill and play less seriously, or play solo and have a fighting chance cause it's been a while and I need to get up to speed and quick.
Negitive:
1: The Developers need to focus more on optimizing game preformance instead of adding so many more iteams and sounds to the game. I know they did a little bit of optimization, but the game has been getting a bit laggy and it's taking a bit longer to load into any server now. I have a very powerful gaming computer that I hand built with custom parts, Hell I even upgraded it just so I could play RUST better. But with all of the updates I am now starting to have problems with RUST again! Come on Devs, get your act together!
2: You don't need much to get started in this game. Except luck and to stumble across someone that's not paying attention to their surrondings. or a complete noob. It does not take long before you can start raiding and destroying someone's base who has been working on it for weeks. Especially on a modded server. Why is this a negitive you ask? well that means someone who is a griefer can hop onto the server, kill a couple of people and grab their stuff, then raid you in a hour or two while your offline all in a few hours. And all your hard work over the last 2-3 weeks is gone in less then 1 day.
3: This game can bring the worst of the worst crowds and bring out the beast in all of us. You will learn fast that some people and servers just don't give a fling F about you and what others are doing to you. Granted some servers are "Noob" friendly and if your are new player I would recommend you to one of those servers. If someone is being "Toxic" I'd report them to an admin and leave well enough alone. If the admin(s) could care less just log off of that server and join another one. It's not worth the effort of trying to find an admin who cares enough, and don't give them the satisfaction of staying and becoming their prey. Quit while you can and be the bigger person. While you're at it report them to FacePunch. At that point that server should not be up if they encourage Cyber Bulling. I've run into that problem before, and it's not a pretty site.

Rust is a very interesting and entertaining game. For any of you who are into open world survival games such as minecraft or tarraria, this is a good game. Same for people who like Non-strategic FPSs, like Garry's mod (Face Punch developed both Rust and Gmod!). If you are into more strategic games then this sould be for you if you are okay with dying... A lot. It is a simplistic game, but has dificult gameplay. It is fun to play with friends on servers alone, or with tons of other people. At the same time though it can be a cruel, or just difficult and have you spawn near bears or pro players. It is very interesnting, the gameplay, it does have bugs and glitches, but they get fixed quickly. I do suggest this game to Open World Survival players or to Casual FPS players, otherwise it should just be a game to test out and try.

An MMO survival game which is actually good. I do not care about the jerks who also play the game only to raid and ruin other people's day, I play the game for the mystery. Jerks can only terrorize a person for so long before they decide to either give up or move along. That's where I have my fun. I get revenge. I grind to get rockets and C4 and raid their house when they are sleeping. Do not mess with me (I have fun with this). Besides the combat the music and environment helps set a creepy tone and helps showcase the mystery of what happened. "Why are you a naked person with only a rock and a torch on a deserted and irradiated island with airplanes and helicopters coming to kill you, and what is with all the deep military encampments?" At the point I am writing this review, There is no reason for any of this. You have no idea what is going on or what happened in the past to trigger these questions. For people with imaginations this game is a playground for more than just gaming, there are many people who who write articles and stuff like that on what they think happened. All are amazing reads and makes you think yourself, "what happened here?" For a game in early access, Rust does a very good job of filling that void  of an incomplete game.

I have to give DayZ some credit for getting me back into gaming a few years back. I enjoyed the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of this game back then, even calling in sick for work a few times so I could run free over the apocalyptic Chenarus landscape. I had so much fun it was bordering on criminal. I made enemies and allies. I joined teams and raided towns. I won and lost intense firefights. I geared up time and time again, always excited when I found that rare item (even if half of them were practically useless).
Man, those were the days. This was just before the whole community adopted Kill On Sight as the primary method of play. After that play got a lot more serious and challenging. The fun encounters stopped. It was a slug fest. I played on and slowly the problems I had with the game wore me out. Eventually I fell out of love with DayZ and stopped playing.
I just reinstalled DayZ recently to check out where this game is at. Oh boy... DayZ really is a steaming pile of garbage. I now question why I ever had fun with this game. Here is my shitlist (in no particular order):
Character movement is fast and glitchy and hard to control. Forget trying to win a melee fight with anything resembling skill. How hard is it to copy Arma3 in this regard? Are you ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥?
I LOATHE the fast moving zombies. Always have. The zombies have always been part of the general environmental threat - not the primary threat in this game. It's never been a "running from zombies" game. They have responded to calls for more dangerous zombies by making them faster and more annoying. Now you just run forever and can never lose them. For ♥♥♥♥s sake just make the zombies old school George Romero SLOW MOVING ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and really dangerous in close quarters.
The lack of loot is tiresome. Loot used to be everywhere in the old days. Now I can run around for hours starving to death and find NOTHING. Like, actually nothing. ♥♥♥♥ you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s for wasting my time.
Kill On Sight as primary method of play. This is a design and balancing fault based on all the above nonsense. Fix that and maybe you can salvage a game out of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
This game should have been so good. The premise is awesome, the setting is fantastic... the execution however is ♥♥♥♥ing horrible. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.

This is a poster child for bad early access game purchase decisions. I really wish I could get my money back for this.
I keep coming back periodically to see if all the game-breaking bugs, terrible graphics, abhorrent interface, poor itemization, and unintuitive mechanics have been improved. And nope.
While there exist similar games in a COMPLETE state with a BETTER PRICE and a BETTER EXPERIENCE there is no reason to ever consider this.

See below for the reason of my recommendation.
pros:
+ Co-op is fun
+ interesting death system, gives you a chance to recover (and can be a bit suspenseful :P )
+ Respawn dialog was entertaining
cons:
- hunter-gatherer with endless amounts of opening crates everywhere. Perhaps an "auto-open" (and auto-collect for crates) option would help here
- Class options get boring at times/not enough diversity in class (this is purely subjective, as I was playing as a siren - and it seemed that the only way to assist others in co-op was to use the phaselock. I was hoping for other ways besides phaselock; but then again it could be just lack of knowledge)
- story isn't very interesting (again subjective. Good examples of stories are things like Portal, which I know is shorter, but the way they distribute information throughout the game was done well. Here, information is just dumped all over me that I barely even remember the general purpose of the game.
Why do I not recommend the game?
Believe it or not, but I started getting bored - the missions, although they have a different objective, mostly involved the same enemies nearly all the time. I get bored of playing games that involve the same enemy bots over and over again... because it seems like it's more of a time-waster than it is of a challenge. Also, even for the discount it is right now, I don't feel that this game is worth $5 - yes, I know the devs did a lot of work on it, but it certainly isn't something for me. I do enjoy some aspects of the game though - the death system is a new concept to me, and really adds suspense, fighting to save your life. TLDR; Imagine No Mans Sky, but in zombie mode - full of broken promises, missing content, and repetitive gameplay.
Longer Version: They nailed the survival part of the game. Your character gets thirsty, hungry, wet, and sick, inso that you have to deal with these issues if you want to stay alive. Along the way you find things that help you survive. Things like meele weapons, firearms, bullets, mags, backpacks, and armor.
Thats all they did right. The actual zombies in this game are mostly broken. Either they stand around, waiting to be killed, or they are some kind of superzombie that goes through walls, floors, stairs and entire buildings. They don't die easily either.
There is also limited player interaction. In a full game server (40/40 people), you might not run into one. And even if you do, they might kill you on the spot. BANG. All your gear, hard work, and sweat gone. People might enjoy the permadeath component in this game.
However, the game doesn't exactly reward you anything for staying alive and killing other players or zombies.  You'll have to want to do just that, because the only actual progression this game has is better gear (marginallt better, if you find the necessary mag and bullets for it), and staying alive in itself.
VERDICT: This game is mostly a hollow zombie survival/walking simulator/bugfest/no mans sky-like game, where the developers have lost intrest. So have many of its players. It might be fun for the first 2 hours, but after that you'll start to see the repeating patterns and that is all it has to offer.
I don't recommend it for the pricetag vs content vs broken promise quota. I'd say around 5€ worth of content in this game, but I'd also recommend taking your money elsewhere, to other likeminded games on Steam.

If you are the type of person that enjoys listening to music the most while driving, then this is the game for you. The radio interface includes dozens of real radio stations, or you can listen to your own MP3 files, nothing better than listenting to Real Radio Manchester classic rock while driving in simulated Northwest England. Licensed real world trucks means that every truck model has its differences, as in real life, do you like horsepower? go Volvo, do you like handling? go Majestic(Mercedes), do you like a vehicle that is undeniably French in its weirdness? go Renault Magnum or if you like a huge windshield, go MAN.Travel a simulated version of Europe hauling cargo to expand your business. Every country has its own differences:you drive on the left in the UK, Switzerland has many mountain roads, France is loaded with toll plazas, Hungary has the most evil speed zones ever, Poland has the most country single lane roads. Experience points allow you to unlock vehicle upgrades, the most important being engines and axles, but cosmetic changes can be unlocked as well, and unlock more profitable jobs. Once you have enough money, you can buy more trucks and more truck yards, hire drivers and let them make money for you. The enemy in this game is careless driving, it is very easy to flip the truck if you take a turn too fast. Speed cameras are an enemy too, you will have to learn their locations and the speed limits they have, 90kmh in Germany, 80 in Austria. This is a more of a passtime than a game, just relax, listen to your favorite tunes, you are bound to find a favorite station, Mine are Real Radio Manchester, Hotmix radio 80's and Belgrade radio 1, and travel the roads of Europe. If you do buy this game, get it with the Going East expansion, as it opens up Poland, Slovakia, and Hungary, making even more profitable jobs available.

The voice acting is superb, and the game is hard enough at times where I know I have to buckle down and use some strategy in order to move past it, but the game is also set up so that if you're feeling frustrated by not being able to take down this one guy, they are side missions that could possibly give you loot and XP to help power you up enough.
Another fun thing is that all of the crates, dumpsters, port-a-potties, boxes, and chests are replenished by themselves, usually after you've died. So there is absolutely no shortage of ammo or money or cheap pistols that you could junk and sell for more cash to buy even more stuff! Since I play everything on a laptop, the sucker gets a little winded easily with the graphics and movement, and only having the option to change the FPS, the resolution, and window/fullscreen mode is a bit suprrising considering how much detail is put into the display. I'd totally be able to deal with ugly graphics if I could play it just a little bit smoother, but that's neither here nor there.

This is a pretty simple game and in my opinion, it really shines if you're using it to just relax. It is what it says it is, a truck driving simulator. There's no catch to that, you're just driving trucks across Europe. The gameplay is solid, it retains its title as a simulator but isn't as tedious as other simulators in my opinion. Driving is only a fraction of the in-game time, like 100 KM in-game is really only going to take you like 10 minutes.
There is a variety of trucks to choose from once you get enough money to buy your first truck. There are real brands like Volvo and Scania, but also some made up ones like Majestic that is meant to be Mercedes. Upgrades for the trucks are also plentiful, but besides engine, transmission, and bed size, they are all cosmetic. Upgrades can get expensive and although you don't make much money early on in the game, you start making a lot more when you start hiring more drivers for your company. Also, as you level up, you can upgrade your own driving and are able to take higher paying jobs.
The world itself is quite large and the expansion pack also extends the map a good amount. The world is pretty nice but most of the cities look very similar with the same general buildings in every city. Apart from that, it has some very nice and scenic views especially things like bridges and mountain roads.
It also boasts a built-in internet radio function which is nice, but adding your own stations can be a pain. You can also use your own music library(I would recommend making shortcuts to your music folders if you want to do this, it saves space), but the music controls are fairly simplistic and not really meant to be played with during driving.
This game also has a fairly active modding community which means that there are mods for all sorts of things in the game, such as changing the AI traffic, adding new trucks, hi-res textures, and other smaller things like camera and weather tweaks that add to the game.
As for controls, mouse and keyboard work alright, but using the WASD keys to drive can get cumbersome and buying a steering wheel, which is the best option for this game, is a bit too pricey for some people. I would recommend an Xbox 360 controller for this game as it works quite well, you will need to configure it yourself in the settings though.
Overall, it was designed to be a relaxing truck driving simulator, and it does a very good job of that. This game isn't for everyone; however, and if you're not sure if this is the type of game you would enjoy, I would recommend checking out the demo(I believe it's the whole game up until level 5) and seeing if you enjoy it. I would recommend everyone at least try it and it drops in price enough to justify a purchase if you find the game interesting.

It takes every ounce of your energy to not take this game at face value, but is imperative to this sublime simulator that you don't.  Yes, it is a game about driving trucks.  Yes, the hauls get to be long distance.  If you're looking for something that keeps you on the edge of your seat, with non-stop action, this is not your game.
However, if you're looking for one of the most true to life, masterfully done, in-depth simulator you've ever sunk your teeth into, you've come to the right place.
I remember joking with my buddies "LOL who wants to drive truck".  Then a few weeks later, I find myself bored on a Saturday, lo and behold, ETS2 has a demo.  I'll give it a shot, what do I have to lose?  Just my entire Saturday.
I can't quite put my finger on the exact thing that kept me playing this game for an 8 hour marathon session (I had stand alone before the Steam version).  Beautifully, accurately crafted European countryside is a brilliant start.  I plopped my trucking company down in London, as I wanted to tour the UK.  I buy my first truck, and jump right into my first haul.
Well, the minutes turn into hours, and suddenly I'm the owner of a successful trucking company, myself and 2 employees with my own fleet.  As you progress, you level up and can spend points on hauling more dangerous/fragile cargo, longer hauls, more economic hauls (gas/wear and tear), and more.  As your employees complete more hauls, they also level up and start bringing in more cheddar.
My only gripe are the punishment systems.  I was expecting active traffic police, aka being pulled over for breaking the law.  However, the only punishment system is a series of fines.  A fine for running a red light, for driving in the wrong lane, for hitting other cars, and traffic cameras (which I'm told are quite common in Europe) for speeding.  No lost time in accident investigation or being pulled over, just a popup fine.
The only other punishment system is a damage system to your truck and trailer.  Damaging the trailer results in a poor score for the haul, and damaging your truck ends up costing you hefty repair bills.  It's also worth mentioning that it seems you get to a point where you make enough money that any punishment is negligible.  You make enough money on the haul where a few $500 tickets don't phase you, nor does a small repair.
This game is a perfect getaway when you're looking for a lazy escape.  Throw on your favorite tunes, and get to haulin'.  ETS2 gets a 4/5.

15 hours in: The man with no pants is ovbiously afk and I've spent hours admiring his succulent dong.

17 hours in: the man has started moving again. He points a gun at my head. At this point I regret not killing him. He points the gun down at my feet and pulls the trigger. He clearly did not intend to kill me, but I was bleeding and close to death.

THE END

This is a pretty simple game and in my opinion, it really shines if you're using it to just relax. It is what it says it is, a truck driving simulator. There's no catch to that, you're just driving trucks across Europe. The gameplay is solid, it retains its title as a simulator but isn't as tedious as other simulators in my opinion. Driving is only a fraction of the in-game time, like 100 KM in-game is really only going to take you like 10 minutes.
There is a variety of trucks to choose from once you get enough money to buy your first truck. There are real brands like Volvo and Scania, but also some made up ones like Majestic that is meant to be Mercedes. Upgrades for the trucks are also plentiful, but besides engine, transmission, and bed size, they are all cosmetic. Upgrades can get expensive and although you don't make much money early on in the game, you start making a lot more when you start hiring more drivers for your company. Also, as you level up, you can upgrade your own driving and are able to take higher paying jobs.
The world itself is quite large and the expansion pack also extends the map a good amount. The world is pretty nice but most of the cities look very similar with the same general buildings in every city. Apart from that, it has some very nice and scenic views especially things like bridges and mountain roads.
It also boasts a built-in internet radio function which is nice, but adding your own stations can be a pain. You can also use your own music library(I would recommend making shortcuts to your music folders if you want to do this, it saves space), but the music controls are fairly simplistic and not really meant to be played with during driving.
This game also has a fairly active modding community which means that there are mods for all sorts of things in the game, such as changing the AI traffic, adding new trucks, hi-res textures, and other smaller things like camera and weather tweaks that add to the game.
As for controls, mouse and keyboard work alright, but using the WASD keys to drive can get cumbersome and buying a steering wheel, which is the best option for this game, is a bit too pricey for some people. I would recommend an Xbox 360 controller for this game as it works quite well, you will need to configure it yourself in the settings though.
Overall, it was designed to be a relaxing truck driving simulator, and it does a very good job of that. This game isn't for everyone; however, and if you're not sure if this is the type of game you would enjoy, I would recommend checking out the demo(I believe it's the whole game up until level 5) and seeing if you enjoy it. I would recommend everyone at least try it and it drops in price enough to justify a purchase if you find the game interesting.

In reality, there probably would have been an explosion, fire, the truck would not be drivable, or at the very least more than 6% damage.
Aside from the lack of realistic collisions and damage, the game is well designed, and very enjoyable. It supports actual steering hardware, but I do not own any, so I cannot vouch on the programming and feel of those features.
It has a few missing features that would enhance gameplay, such as showing the speed limit on the GPS nav. Also, you will be driving through areas that change between MPH and KPH, but my odometer only shows MPH.
Overall, I would recommend this game, it is still fun. Just remember it is not Grand Theft Auto or Saints Row. It may feel that way with the open world.

The humour and interactions that you have within the game is second to none, the jokes can be understood by all-ages and personally I consider it to be original. I normally play racing games & bought Euro Truck 2 for a bit of fun and something different. I was not expecting to play much more than about 10 hours in this game, but so far I have managed 39 hours & still enjoying it.
You start off doing quick jobs until you have enough money to purchase your own truck & start doing the freight market which is much more profitable.
You can purchase different trucks & upgrade different elements such as the chassis, engine, interior and the look of the truck. You can visit the paint shop to customise the exterior. It includes most of the manufacturers such as Volvo, Scania, Iveco, Man, Daf & Renault.
There is a management aspect to the game where you can employ drivers who will then start earning more money for you. You can expand your trucking empire by purchasing more depot's.
The driving is fun & handles as I would expect a truck to. The roads can be challenging & include a variety of junctions & road types to keep it interesting.  I have mine setup with a Logtiech G27 which makes the experience much more involving. You have to haul various load types of loads to different European cities. The cities are representative of the cities but not an exact replica, so don't expect them to look like your local roads. Once you get to the destination you have the challenge of reversing your trailer in to the bay, which take a bit of practice. You can use a quick park if you find this difficult as the cost of XP points.
The game also has a large modding community to make the game more realistic such as physics & branded trailers.
If you like driving games & you feel like a change then give Euro Truck a try.

A very fun but poorly named game.  It isn't really anything like a simulator and a better name would have been Euro Truck Tycoon.  The 'tycoon' aspect of this game is very good and I hope for the next version that they expand upon it by possibly letting you hire & manage mechanics, dispatchers, etc.  To improve the simulation aspects I would suggest adding insurance and drivers license consequences for accidents, make accidents visually realistic (visible damage) and more catastrophic.  To further improve the immersion more diverse weather is needed (where's the snow in the mountains?), and consider improvements to the wear & tear mechanisms as well.  To expand on the arcade aspect of the game, adding police who pull you over rather than just auto-tickets would go a long way but also adding some sort of bidding-for-jobs against competitors or a race aspect (bonuses for early delivery?) would be fantastic.
The driving aspect of the game is good and can be challenging, however if you are looking for a simulator then Euro Truck Simulator may not be the game you want.  The scenery in this game is gorgeous, and if you like working toward expansion goals you will enjoy hiring & managing drivers, buying garages and trucks, and building skills.
