After playing the mod back when the mod first came out and now moving on to this stand alone version, I have a clear understanding of how to rate this game.
Coming from the mod, I loved the tense moments where you might lose all your gear in a firefight against one man or a group of many. I also loved the aspect of surviving and keeping your character alive and making sure you don't die from hunger, thirst, zombies, or other survivors. All of these aspects plus more are in this game now.
This game brings those tense, heart-pounding moments when you see a player or begin to get shot at. This game is not a game where everyone is balanced with the other person. I mean that by one person will most likely have an advantage over the other at any point in a fire fight. Take Call of Duty games for example; you have time to turn and shoot at a player if they are shooting you in the back. Not the case here. You get shot at from behind and somehow get away, then you are one lucky man. To not go into a lot more detail about this I will just say that in the moments of a gun fight, or soon to be gunfight, there is no fair playing field. This makes you have to adapt to this hostile environment and set yourself up for success all the time. You have to think always as the prey in this game, always looking around for threats even when you are hunting someone.
Now the environment isn't forgiving either except for the many apple trees you can eat from and the many water pumps you can drink from. Basically everything in this games wants to kill you, and they can all do it in their own ways. The temperature in the game, kind of a winter cold out right now in the game, can kill you. Yes, it's slow to do so but it's still something you have to counter. Better clothing like jackets are a good way to stay warm during the cold and the rain coats are good for when it's raining and cold out so you don't get hypothermia. Then there's hot climate which dehydrates you and so on. Zombies are now a big threat in this game as compared to the non-dangerous ones in the mod. They can easily knock you out and kill you in groups. Stealth, a bunch of ammo, or some form of melee is your only way to counter this. Basically what I am trying to get across is that this game is not a forgiving one and is for people who like battling for survival so if you like games like Rust, Ark: Survival Evolved, 7 Days to Die, and many other survival games, you will enjoy this.
All in all, the game is great: Graphics are stunning (still needs optimizing though), gameplay is intense and heart pounding, sounds are on point, and the survival aspect is realistic. If you enjoy survival games and fighting zombies and other players, you will enjoy this game. The only draw back as of today is that it is still in development. It has its glitches every now and again but are worked out by the devs with quick fixes and these glitches aren't game-breaking. It isn't fully optimized yet, seeing that inside cities my frames go from about 30-50 FPS in certain cities and in the wilderness and small cities I get about 55-120 FPS. Those are the only down sides to this game but they aren't game breaking. All taken into account, this game is highly enjoyable.

This is a pretty simple game and in my opinion, it really shines if you're using it to just relax. It is what it says it is, a truck driving simulator. There's no catch to that, you're just driving trucks across Europe. The gameplay is solid, it retains its title as a simulator but isn't as tedious as other simulators in my opinion. Driving is only a fraction of the in-game time, like 100 KM in-game is really only going to take you like 10 minutes.
There is a variety of trucks to choose from once you get enough money to buy your first truck. There are real brands like Volvo and Scania, but also some made up ones like Majestic that is meant to be Mercedes. Upgrades for the trucks are also plentiful, but besides engine, transmission, and bed size, they are all cosmetic. Upgrades can get expensive and although you don't make much money early on in the game, you start making a lot more when you start hiring more drivers for your company. Also, as you level up, you can upgrade your own driving and are able to take higher paying jobs.
The world itself is quite large and the expansion pack also extends the map a good amount. The world is pretty nice but most of the cities look very similar with the same general buildings in every city. Apart from that, it has some very nice and scenic views especially things like bridges and mountain roads.
It also boasts a built-in internet radio function which is nice, but adding your own stations can be a pain. You can also use your own music library(I would recommend making shortcuts to your music folders if you want to do this, it saves space), but the music controls are fairly simplistic and not really meant to be played with during driving.
This game also has a fairly active modding community which means that there are mods for all sorts of things in the game, such as changing the AI traffic, adding new trucks, hi-res textures, and other smaller things like camera and weather tweaks that add to the game.
As for controls, mouse and keyboard work alright, but using the WASD keys to drive can get cumbersome and buying a steering wheel, which is the best option for this game, is a bit too pricey for some people. I would recommend an Xbox 360 controller for this game as it works quite well, you will need to configure it yourself in the settings though.
Overall, it was designed to be a relaxing truck driving simulator, and it does a very good job of that. This game isn't for everyone; however, and if you're not sure if this is the type of game you would enjoy, I would recommend checking out the demo(I believe it's the whole game up until level 5) and seeing if you enjoy it. I would recommend everyone at least try it and it drops in price enough to justify a purchase if you find the game interesting.

This game is oddly addicting. Very stable, have not had the program crash on me.
Gameplay wise, it seems the focus of this game goes into simulating the experience of driving the truck, and not much else though. Crashes are extremely unrealistic, and I have not found any options in the settings to raise the difficulity. I accidently T-boned a bus at 55mph, and only 6% damage occured and I kept going. In reality, there probably would have been an explosion, fire, the truck would not be drivable, or at the very least more than 6% damage.
Aside from the lack of realistic collisions and damage, the game is well designed, and very enjoyable. It supports actual steering hardware, but I do not own any, so I cannot vouch on the programming and feel of those features.
It has a few missing features that would enhance gameplay, such as showing the speed limit on the GPS nav. Also, you will be driving through areas that change between MPH and KPH, but my odometer only shows MPH.
Overall, I would recommend this game, it is still fun. Just remember it is not Grand Theft Auto or Saints Row. It may feel that way with the open world.

This game cares too much for simulating at the expense of fun. Sure it is good to have it simulating how it is like to drive in the real world, but there is no allowance to have you just wanting to let your hair down and have some fun. You get fines for everything it can notice, speeding (even if questionably given), crashing, being crashed into, going on the wrong side of the road, having headlights not on the exact setting wanted. But then at the same time don't pay attention to if the roads tell you not to overtake etc.
Overall the game seems like it cares only for simulation, but with that said it still misses doing everything it should if that is the case.
The turning point for me was when I decided to mess around by taking up the road on both sides on a train crossing, the game stopped the train from coming anywhere close, and then invisible walls prevented me from exploring the train track. The game just limits freedom which would be wanted in an open world driving exploration game. In the end it ONLY wants you on the desginated roads, and as such really cuts down on the fun allowance.
The reason I don't recommend this is because all the reviews that do exist are deceptive, I went into this game thinking from the reviews that it would be fun to play around with, but it isn't, it is fun to play strictly, not to mess around inside. People need to know what they are actually getting into with this game and get it for the right reasons, not to get it because they are just told one side of the story. In the end of the day this wasn't for me as much as I wished it could be, and so I don't recomend it to others who want to mess around while simulating.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is just what it sounds like.  It simulates driving a semi-truck around Europe.  When you start the game, you create a driver, name your company and choose its logo.  Once you have finished that, you are behind the wheel.  The world is huge; it is a scaled down version of Europe.  Even though it is scaled down, it is absolutely massive.  You can buy trucks, property and hire employees to work for you.  You can even paint your truck some ridiculous paint schemes.
The options are great.  When I open up a game for the first time, I always tweak the options.  You can have the truck automatically shift for you or have it so you can shift from reverse to neutral and neutral to drive.  You can even crank it all the way up to manual with clutch.  There are many graphics settings to tweak or max out.  The game even has the support for: keyboard, mouse, gamepad, or steering wheel steering.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 shines in many areas.  It feels as though you are actually driving a truck.  You have a cabin view, and the world comes across as realistic.  The game isn’t top notch graphics-wise, but it still does look amazing when you are driving down a back road with nothing to do but look around. Most of the time when I play, I relax and catch up on some podcasts while driving throughout Europe or I can create a playlist of music I have on my PC.  In my opinion, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is completely addicting. You keep trying to drive better, arrive faster and upgrade your truck to drive better and look great.
There are some areas in which Euro Truck Simulator 2 is lacking.  There doesn’t seem to be an end goal to the game.  You find yourself trying to get more and more money, but you can’t figure out why.  The other cars on the road seem to have some basic AI missing.  For instance, in real life, if a car 400 feet away from you makes a turn, you would slow down or stop if needed.  Sometimes the cars do stop, but you will find times where they don’t even slow down and they will hit you, causing you to need to make repairs to your truck and have road rage at something that isn’t even real.  One thing that could help this would be if SCS software made it so the horn on your truck actually made the other drivers react differently.  The horn seems more like a fun audible sound rather than a game mechanic.
To wrap things up, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a worthy purchase.  There is no greater feeling than turning off the speed limiter and speeding through Europe, dodging cars and not realizing how fast you just took that turn until your truck is on its side.  It’s satisfying when you back up your truck to the bay on your first try while going full speed.  Even with the game’s flaws, I would definitely recommend this game to many people.

This is a fantastic game and well worth the money. There is an extensive campaign with an insane amount of sidequests. The four basic classes have three skill trees themselves which allows for a lot of variation. The addition of two classes as DLC expanded gameplay quite a bit. Borderlands 2 also encourages and in some cases demands multiplayer. Unlike many games the multiplayer in Borderlands 2 is primarily cooperative. The AI difficulty is ramped up slightly to make the multiplayer combat more challenging but still fair. There is also an ridiculous amount of weapons and gear to be found. The DLC packages added later added huge value to the game but the base Borderlands 2 is still a great buy.

Once I bought this game, my quest for finding the ultimate gun has begun. Sadly, it has not ended and probably never will. In Borderlands 2, players have a huge arsenal by their side. The game has a system that mix & match different gun parts and features and creates totally brand new never before-seen guns. I guarantee you'll never get the same exact gun twice. Even if the model is the same (highly rare), the features are always improved. This is the only game where I take more time to decide which guns to use/keep instead of choosing how to take down my enemy. This is a fast-paced game and should be treated as such. Quests never become dull or tedious, enemies are always different each time, and the guns.. Well, let's just say you'll find a favorite one later on (Sorry, no spoilers!)... I can honestly say that this game will never get old and that when you do get bored of it, you'll find yourself coming back to it very soon. The variety of the guns, armor, and equipment will keep you wondering how on earth Gearbox can make up a system like this. And I thought Skyrim had variety. >__>
I definitely recommend this game to my friends and the public. You will not regret buying this and I swear on my Psycho character's life that you will have one of the best times of your life playing this game. Also, if you want to FULLY experience the game, buy ALL THE DLC'S. I'm not saying this game is a Pay To Win game, but the DLC's adds extra fun to it (Yes, even the skin packs!). I don't like rating games but I would give this game a 10/10.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

Euro Truck Simulator 2 from Czech developer SCS Software follows a series of previously-released truck and driving simulation games with a reworked and highly-improved engine that foremost focuses on realism, yet while also incorporating entertaining and rewarding gameplay. As most simulation games often suffer from lackluster gameplay, I was most surprised with with the game's wide variety of content in addition to the stellar gameplay and presentation.
I enjoyed the game's simple introduction in how it teaches players the basics of transporting cargo from one destination to another. Even the game's control setup is highly-intuitive in how it explains the various methods such as mouse and keyboard and also the option to opt for an automatic and manual truck setup.
The amount of customization options for trucks is staggering from parts like the engine and exhaust pipes to additional cosmetic tweaks such as paint jobs and placement of lights. From scenic countrysides to tunnels curving through mountain hills, driving your truck to and from each destination is always an opportunity to see more of the many included countries. The game's world is often vibrant with life from cars, buses, and trucks going about their business.
The diversity of each country's landscape ensures that each trip is paired with an addictive incentive to explore every city and road in the game's world. Not only was I surprised by the varied amount of content and realistic gameplay mechanics, the game surprised me yet again with beautifully-rendered landscapes and cities. The most noteworthy aspect of the game's presentation is the highly-detailed truck exterior and interiors. The truck's dashboard interiors with dynamic speedometers and digital screens, which are even unique to each vehicle model, are some of the best I've seen in any simulation game.
As someone that has always been interested in the simulation genre, I was continually surprised by the new standards set by Euro Truck Simulator 2. The developers at SCS Software have proved that the often lackluster simulation genre can be brought back to life with games that deliver both realistic and entertaining gameplay. Elements of the game's design ranging from the varied content to the customization ensure that beginner players and simulation enthusiasts will discover their desired virtual trucking experience. the majority of content is presented with the utmost polish and detail that few games are able to achieve. Put simply, Euro Truck Simulator 2 sets a new standard for the simulation genre.

This is both a good simulator and a good game
First, the simulator, it is both fun and challenging to drive around without crashing, and keeping within the confines of the law (speed, side of road) which change from street to street, it takes into account different country’s correctly (as far as I can tell) and it is HUGE for a simulator. When driving each specific truck you feel slightly different in the way you drive, having a trailer makes the driving slower and steering harder in a very realistic way. The scale of the game is massive, as you can go from one side of Europe to the other, and it will take a fair few hours. It is, compared to other simulators, a good simulator.
BUT WAIT, THERES MORE!
It’s a good game as well, as you start just driving a lorry with the trailer from point A to B, then taking out a loan to buy a truck, each day paying off a bit of it. as you expand and pay off your debts you hire drivers and buy them trucks gradually going from a small time driver to one of the biggest trucking companies in Europe. It is so progressive but it doesn’t require micro managements like choosing jobs for all your other drivers (fun for one or two, but not for the 100+ you will end up with)
It is a good game, full of detail like roads you can’t drive on having cars on them and the best rain on glass i have ever seen, the graphics are nice and it doesn't take a whole lot to run it (i can play on max settings at 1080p on a £700 pc and get 60+ fps).
However it isn't perfect, it’s a driving game for PC, so I wold defiantly recommend a controller for it. It feels like a huge grind after about 15 hours (which is when I gave up) as it is the same thing of driving over and over again.
If you want a good, large scale business and driving simulator, defiantly go for it, but try the demo first to make sure you both can run it and you like it. If you just want to drive around in a realistic way in a lorry, this is good for you as well. If it’s on a cheap steam sale for less than £10 I would at least give it a look.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is just what it sounds like.  It simulates driving a semi-truck around Europe.  When you start the game, you create a driver, name your company and choose its logo.  Once you have finished that, you are behind the wheel.  The world is huge; it is a scaled down version of Europe.  Even though it is scaled down, it is absolutely massive.  You can buy trucks, property and hire employees to work for you.  You can even paint your truck some ridiculous paint schemes.
The options are great.  When I open up a game for the first time, I always tweak the options.  You can have the truck automatically shift for you or have it so you can shift from reverse to neutral and neutral to drive.  You can even crank it all the way up to manual with clutch.  There are many graphics settings to tweak or max out.  The game even has the support for: keyboard, mouse, gamepad, or steering wheel steering.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 shines in many areas.  It feels as though you are actually driving a truck.  You have a cabin view, and the world comes across as realistic.  The game isn’t top notch graphics-wise, but it still does look amazing when you are driving down a back road with nothing to do but look around. Most of the time when I play, I relax and catch up on some podcasts while driving throughout Europe or I can create a playlist of music I have on my PC.  In my opinion, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is completely addicting. You keep trying to drive better, arrive faster and upgrade your truck to drive better and look great.
There are some areas in which Euro Truck Simulator 2 is lacking.  There doesn’t seem to be an end goal to the game.  You find yourself trying to get more and more money, but you can’t figure out why.  The other cars on the road seem to have some basic AI missing.  For instance, in real life, if a car 400 feet away from you makes a turn, you would slow down or stop if needed.  Sometimes the cars do stop, but you will find times where they don’t even slow down and they will hit you, causing you to need to make repairs to your truck and have road rage at something that isn’t even real.  One thing that could help this would be if SCS software made it so the horn on your truck actually made the other drivers react differently.  The horn seems more like a fun audible sound rather than a game mechanic.
To wrap things up, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a worthy purchase.  There is no greater feeling than turning off the speed limiter and speeding through Europe, dodging cars and not realizing how fast you just took that turn until your truck is on its side.  It’s satisfying when you back up your truck to the bay on your first try while going full speed.  Even with the game’s flaws, I would definitely recommend this game to many people.

I enjoyed when things go right. Killing large amounts of enemies, attaining a nice item or discovering something new and interesting. But these good things seem to be 'islands' between a sea of dull grinding and disappointment.
The majority of the game will be spent going from one objective to another, killing trash mobs and searching for rare items. And all three seem to be a drag, almost a punishment for exploring. This can appear in the form of annoying enemies that corner you and stagnate the flow of the game or long, winding pathways that eventually lead to a dead end.
The core gameplay feels like filler content that pads out the real highlights, which are the cinematic moments, the unusual quests and the entertaining narratives of each character.
As I was playing this game (as the Commando class) I found that at some point, I stopped caring what I was doing or why I was doing it. There's something strangely alluring about this game. I didn't think I'd like it. First off, I hate trucks and the idea of truck driving. I even tried the demo, then put it back down. But there it was, for months, popping up everywhere I looked saying "Yes! You want this." Finally I read a "Games of 2013" article in Eurogamer talking about it and I was convinced. I'm also fascinated by Europe and the U.K. and I wanted to learn a bit about the geography there, where the towns are and things like that. I never knew until playing this that there's something called the Chunnel, or the "Channel Tunnel" connecting England with France. That's just one example.
Okay so you have those space trading games like Freelancer, X, etc. where you go from station to station buying and selling cargo to make money and buy upgrades so you can haul more cargo and buy more upgrades? Well this game is like that, except it's set in Europe and you're driving a truck. Oh, and you're not actually buying the cargo, you just get paid to haul it. There's empire building too, as you can upgrade your garage, buy more trucks, and hire drivers. There's a leveling system with perks and bonuses, and the trucks are upgradeable too. Bigger engines, more lights, better transmissions, etc. Unfortunately a lot of the descriptions of what you're buying aren't there. There aren't enough tooltips or feedback - the shopping interface could use some work. As you level you can unlock the ability to haul more and different types of cargo with bigger payouts and more interesting routes.
But it's a fun game, mastering how to take corners without tipping over, learning where you can go fast and where you need to slow down, navigating traffic, avoiding bumping into guard rails or other vehicles, etc. I play with a 360 controller and it works fine. You do have to map everything and tweak the sensitivity a bit but it works well.
If you like open world driving games, and the idea of those "space trading" type games except on land and with a few differences, and if you're interested in the sights and geography of Europe, check this one out. It's actually quite fun!

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is hands down one of the grestest simulations ever developed.
This is one of the few games out there that run great out of the box. You don't need to mod the game to oblivion to be able to enjoy it unlike a lot of other titles out there. If you are an nVIDIA user and really picky about having good anti-aliasing you will need to make a few anti-aliasing tweaks due to the engine lacking FXAA and proper anti-aliasing support (only MLAA supprt is included), but it's not too big of an issue, as a lot of the post process affects seem to counter most of the jaggies. Out of the box it provides an amazing experience and I recommend playing it out of the box to get faimilar with how the game works. However, once learning the game I recommend downloading the Truck Sim Map mod. Just Google "trucksim map" and you'll find it right away. It adds a whole slew of extra cities and is even compatible with the expansion pack "Going East!"
It's a European game... so that means you're going to be driving cabovers. You can download American trucks, but the American trucks use the European axial setup, I'd assume due to limitations of the game's engine. Some people don't mind it, others like lyself prefer to stick with the European trucks for immersion since the game does take place in Europe afterall. Don't fret Americans, there is an American version of this simulation coming out soon. SCS has already started posting screenshots and it looks like they're even refining the graphics engine. But this is about ETS2, not ATS - so let's talk about ETS2!
I purchased this simulator I believe last summer during the Steam Summer Sale. I believe I got it for $10. I had been eyeballing this game, watching some YouTube videos, and it always looked impressive to me. Getting a truck, picking up freight, carrying it cross country and dropping it off at the destination -- it was just something that looked interesting to me. I just didn't want to pay full price for it. Once it went on sale both myself and my buddy picked it up. We both love it! Now after playing it, I would even pay full price for it. A developer I had never really heard much of making a simulation had me skeptical... but a mistake I did not make when I purchased this simulation! I was really impressed with how polished everything feels. The graphics engine is solid. It is pretty obvious the development was tailored toward AMD users with MLAA support built in but no FXAA support, but there are tweaks out there to get around this for those with high end machines. I just leave anti aliasing off all together, and at 1920x1080 it looks perfectly fine to me! If you are an anti-aliasing nazi and own a high end NVIDIA card, then
tweak is for you! Beware, you may experience significant slow downs. My GeForce GTX 650 Ti has a bit of input lag when I use this tweak, and that was before I got my 1080p monitor running at 1360x768.
The physics are decent out of the box. Optionally, you can download the realistic physics mod (just Google realistic physics - there are many mod sites out there for this game). It adds a lot more roll and bounce to the physics and just makes the game feel a lot more realistic overall when going over bumps and jumping on the accelerator and watching the chassis twist as your massive engine struggles to pull 21t of pesticides. The only complaint I have is sometimes when you touch with other trucks on the road the physics seem to act a little... odd. The other day I barely touched with another truck and that truck instantly stopped. I believe this was more of an issue with AI, and of the however many hours I've played this game (lost track), I've only seen it happen once, so it's not a big deal to me. Overall, you feel like you are driving a massive rig, and it feels good. Acceleration feels right, gearing feels right, turning feels good... it all just feels like it should. My only complaint really is the AI appear like they are on rails. But this simulation is about deliverying goods... not racing. So it doesn't bother me much. They focused on what they needed to focus on, and in the end, this game just feels right.
The engines are pretty hard to hear from the cabs. I've never driven one of these trucks in real life so I'm not sure if that's how it really is, but you can hear the engines nicely if you look out the driver window. Some of the sounds are kind of derpy, but they have been improving a lot of the sounds as of late. It's definitely not bad enough to make you not want to play the game ot ruin the experience.
The graphics are decent. It's not over the top, but it's decent.  The trucks look nice. The other AI vehicles can look a little meh at times, but again... that's not really what this game is about. The good thing is with all the updates they've done they have been adding more and more different types of AI vehicles. There are also of course like anything else, tons of mods to add different types of AI vehicles.
Now... the important stuff. The simulation itself. It does everything you really would expect it to do exclude having cops that pull you over. They do however have fines in the game. If you speed you get fined. If you ram another car, you get fined. There are bank loans. You are expected to pay these banks back... don't press them. There are gas stations. There are rest stops. What else can you ask for in a trucking game? There is resting... yes, the resting. If you don't rest, you will get penalized. Make sure you rest. There is brake simulation. Don't overuse your brakes... or you will regret it. There is a jake brake... there is e verything you could ever think about having. There is fuel consumption. All of these simulation features can be toggled on and off. So if you're a hardcore sim fan you can turn it all on and play it the way it was meant to be played. Or if you're a casual player, just turn all these functions off and play it as a casual game. Whatever your play style you can tweak it for YOU!
So, you start off in a loaner. You'll soon be able to take bank loans and buy your own truck. From there, you can buy additional trucks, hire drivers, fire drivers, trade in trucks, upgrade them, customize them. You name it, you can do it. You're given a starter garage and you can choose from a healthy selection of cities to start from, as well as your truck preference. So if you've ever dreamed about having a business stationed in Koln, Germany like myself... You. Can. Do. It! Oh, and the radio feature. It's awesome. I love it! This game makes you feel like you're on a road trip. Also it has that dynamic weather! Don't get caught up in those rain storms... sometimes they can be pretty vicious.

If you're looking for a real driving simulator I cannot recommend this.
A truck driving simulator sort of!
The game does not provide any realistic simulation as far as driving goes.  90% of the dashboard does not work, trucks do not have real world physics.  Driving is boring, because your truck drives like a toy, because there's no skill involved to do it. Truck has horn lights and turn signals, but they don't matter, the Ai don't see or hear them. There is no visual damage, dirt or tire wear.
The trailers/equipment you pull has no weight to them, you look in your rearview mirror and they are going all the road because there is no physics attributed to the trailers.
It rains but you cannot slide, and it doesn't change your driving.  Rain on the windshield is the only thing that changes, there is no physics so your truck is not going to slide or slip.  There is no snow.
Sound is laughable in the game, there's hardly any, trucks sound OK outside, but inside they are muffled too much. No city or freeway sounds, it's so bad there are several mod's for sound.  As much as the developers keep recording they don't seem to get it right.
AI of course is stupid and their behavior will cause you to get in several accidents. Things you will notice right away, there are no police in Europe, or ambulances or fire trucks, in fact all of Europe only owns about five different cars.  And no motorcycles.  You can get tickets for speeding or running a red light, a little bell goes off in a popup that says you just paid for your infraction.
Your business, you're able to hire employees, who you will never see, you must purchase trucks for them. No reason for that company logo you'll never see your driver's trucks on the road.
There are mod's that help with some of the games shortcomings, unfortunately you have to go looking for them because for some reason the developer will not form a nexus for mod's even though the community has asked.  Make sure your antivirus is up to date when you go mod's hunting.
A lot of people voted to green light this game, to bringing it mainstream because it had a lot of potential to be a real world truck simulator, but the developer has just just sat on it. He wants the game more assessable to the younger players but still wants to call it a simulator for some reason.
Good game for little kids, but not for someone looking for a real driving simulator.

I started playing this game only because I could not find many multi-player PS3 games. When i actually got in to it though, it quickly became my top favorite FPS RPG of all time, along side Skyrim. The general graphical design is unlike any other game and allows Borderlands 2 to have unique style all of its own. The humor is constant and always good - very sarcastic and sometimes dry - but always hilarious. The primary Antagonist, Handomse Jack, truly makes the game worth it all on his own, but other minor characters like Tiny Tina and Moxxie, for example add to the top-notch dialague in their own unique way.
Its not all about the dialogue though. The high-octane action that you get from either running the main quest or side missions will always keep you thrilled and excited to finish the next mission and defeat the next boss. Not to mention the extremely huge and unique collection of firepower and items you can collect throughout the game that makes looting a full-time, fun job.

In conclusion; If you are a fan of Skyrim, Fallout 3 or just love to blow s*** up! Play this game. Its well worth putting life on hold. And I REALLY recommend purchasing the download content. All of them are worth it.

There's something strangely alluring about this game. I didn't think I'd like it. First off, I hate trucks and the idea of truck driving. I even tried the demo, then put it back down. But there it was, for months, popping up everywhere I looked saying "Yes! You want this." Finally I read a "Games of 2013" article in Eurogamer talking about it and I was convinced. I'm also fascinated by Europe and the U.K. and I wanted to learn a bit about the geography there, where the towns are and things like that. I never knew until playing this that there's something called the Chunnel, or the "Channel Tunnel" connecting England with France. That's just one example.
Okay so you have those space trading games like Freelancer, X, etc. where you go from station to station buying and selling cargo to make money and buy upgrades so you can haul more cargo and buy more upgrades? Well this game is like that, except it's set in Europe and you're driving a truck. Oh, and you're not actually buying the cargo, you just get paid to haul it. There's empire building too, as you can upgrade your garage, buy more trucks, and hire drivers. There's a leveling system with perks and bonuses, and the trucks are upgradeable too. Bigger engines, more lights, better transmissions, etc. Unfortunately a lot of the descriptions of what you're buying aren't there. There aren't enough tooltips or feedback - the shopping interface could use some work. As you level you can unlock the ability to haul more and different types of cargo with bigger payouts and more interesting routes.
But it's a fun game, mastering how to take corners without tipping over, learning where you can go fast and where you need to slow down, navigating traffic, avoiding bumping into guard rails or other vehicles, etc. I play with a 360 controller and it works fine. You do have to map everything and tweak the sensitivity a bit but it works well.
If you like open world driving games, and the idea of those "space trading" type games except on land and with a few differences, and if you're interested in the sights and geography of Europe, check this one out. It's actually quite fun!

Having spent 6 years in Germany as a military brat now I'm a CDL truck driver in the midwest US so I thought it would be interesting to see what it's like to drive a truck in Europe so I voted thumbs up to Greenlight this title last year. Others did too apparently and when it released we were rewarded with an unexpectedly addictive game, a simulation as accurate as you will find anywhere that will have you traveling all over europe. In fact It looks and feels like a professional sim one would find in a truck driving school. You will learn the European road signs and general rules of the road.
You start out as a freelancer taking jobs to gain experience and money as you try out different makes and models of trucks supplied  and maintained by your employer. Later you will visit dealerships of the trucks that you enjoy driving and buy your own which gets you more money for upgrades but you will have to pay for fuel, maintenance and repairs.
Some jobs will take you across the English Channel either by ferry or "Chunnel" to England. If you ever wondered what it would be like to drive on the left side of the road you will get that along with a change of scenery, signs and traffic.
If you hesitate to pick up this title because you think of the hours you will spend on the road between deliveries you will find that time is cleverly compressed 19:1 and you can tune in European radio stations in-cab. This it turns out is the K-Y of the long trips and I now have several new favorite radio stations I might never have found otherwise like Radio Energy in Bulgaria, Radio Fresh from Paris and Antenna Radio Stuttgart. It's live web radio and you could just use
to listen whenever you want but driving on the Autobahn listening to German radio is an experience.
A reality mode minimizing the time compression would be nice as would the ability to test drive the trucks you are thinking of buying at dealerships and a rental car option so that you can tour the many cities you will visit in something other than your truck or a company's truck with loaded trailer. But overall this game is a complete and enjoyable experience.
I nominated this game for the "Just Five More Minutes" award since it kept me up late playing.

Be a truck driver and drive your way across Europe!
This game starts you out as a contract driver. You take on jobs hauling freight from one city to another, driving different trucks owned by various companies. Eventually, you'll save up enough money to buy your own truck and, if you so wish, hire your own drivers to make your company grow.
ETS2 is a very relaxing game and it's very easy to learn the basics. The graphics are quite realistic, which is something you want in a game like this as it helps with immersion. The game can also be played as simply or as detailed as you want. For example, when you reach your destination, you can choose to off load the freight easily by pulling into the company lot and pressing "Enter" or you can up the challenge by properly backing the trailer into the loading bay.
Each job done gives you experience, which eventually causes you to level up. When you level up you get to choose a perk - very similar to RPGs. The higher your level, the better the jobs pay.

Driving trucks in traffic for hours on end doesn't sound like much fun, but this game balances things nicely. First, there's the business side of things, where you can take out a loan, buy extra garages and trucks, and hire other drivers to earn money for you.
Next, the actual driving is condensed. Cities and towns are little more than a handful of streets, and time acceleration ensures you're not spending hours in real time travelling between jobs.
Finally, the penalties for speeding and damaging your truck (and other vehicles!) ensure you drive properly. A small amount of damage costs a load of money to fix, eating up profits and making that loan much harder to pay off.
As for driving, I have a Logitech G25 wheel but I don't bother setting it up. Keyboard is fine, although I recommend setting left and right mouse buttons to activate the left and right indicators.
In all, highly recommended, and a lot better than the original Euro Truck Simulator.

If you're looking for a real driving simulator I cannot recommend this.
A truck driving simulator sort of!
The game does not provide any realistic simulation as far as driving goes.  90% of the dashboard does not work, trucks do not have real world physics.  Driving is boring, because your truck drives like a toy, because there's no skill involved to do it. Truck has horn lights and turn signals, but they don't matter, the Ai don't see or hear them. There is no visual damage, dirt or tire wear.
The trailers/equipment you pull has no weight to them, you look in your rearview mirror and they are going all the road because there is no physics attributed to the trailers.
It rains but you cannot slide, and it doesn't change your driving.  Rain on the windshield is the only thing that changes, there is no physics so your truck is not going to slide or slip.  There is no snow.
Sound is laughable in the game, there's hardly any, trucks sound OK outside, but inside they are muffled too much. No city or freeway sounds, it's so bad there are several mod's for sound.  As much as the developers keep recording they don't seem to get it right.
AI of course is stupid and their behavior will cause you to get in several accidents. Things you will notice right away, there are no police in Europe, or ambulances or fire trucks, in fact all of Europe only owns about five different cars.  And no motorcycles.  You can get tickets for speeding or running a red light, a little bell goes off in a popup that says you just paid for your infraction.
Your business, you're able to hire employees, who you will never see, you must purchase trucks for them. No reason for that company logo you'll never see your driver's trucks on the road.
There are mod's that help with some of the games shortcomings, unfortunately you have to go looking for them because for some reason the developer will not form a nexus for mod's even though the community has asked.  Make sure your antivirus is up to date when you go mod's hunting.
A lot of people voted to green light this game, to bringing it mainstream because it had a lot of potential to be a real world truck simulator, but the developer has just just sat on it. He wants the game more assessable to the younger players but still wants to call it a simulator for some reason.
Good game for little kids, but not for someone looking for a real driving simulator.

That time I runned as soon as I could in to a secluded aisle into a corner, to be exact right

Came to the church, about 5 or more dead bodies all over the place filled with ruined gear, and a single freshspawn with an M4 in his hand. I asked how could I help. He told me to pick up a mosin that was on the ground, I did since I had a crossbow. We were watching the church door for about 3 minutes, then he decided to bandage, and I was covering the door alone. Right after that a freshspawn, (Bandit that came back after death) with a sledgehammer, rushed in and targeted the guy I so recently teamed up with. After that we went to pick up a V3S and drove to meet his other friends and hunted bandits for the rest of the play, which was awesome.

In this review, I don't touch bases with in-game morality, the lack of goals and objectives, the known glitches in the environment that kill you at random, or the fact that this game is basically vaporware.
DayZ Standalone is a very ironic game. It is supposed to be a "zombie apocalypse", but the zombies serve only as a pest between you, your destination, and other players. Killing zombies in DayZ is neither rewarding or enjoyable. There is no incentive in the game for you to do so, and they are so buggy that it's just best to avoid them entirely...and you can because the zombie population is so low. Zombies in DayZ Standalone don't overwhelm you with numbers as much as they overwhelm you with ignoring walls, warping, and glitchy melee range. The few updates that still come out do not address this main feature of the game and they probably never will.
The real magic of this game is your interaction with other players in all manners friendly and violent. Unfortunately since the vehicle department is lacking, the amount of interactions you have with other players is significantly less than the mod. Not to mention that since zombies no longer spawn near players who have been occupying a certain area for several minutes, it is nigh impossible to know where other players may be. In my opinion, the game is incredibly boring when you cannot find anyone.
Most of the time in DayZ is spent walking around. Do yourself a favor and spend that time going on an actual hike. I can guarantee it's a whole lot more fun than this snoozefest.

The sheer terror this game can cause you is unique as you really really don't want to die. Fire fights are relavtivly rare (depending on server and playstyle) which makes them all the more terrifying, especially now because of the new audio system in 0.61; guns are MUCH louder and you can tell roughly from where they were shot and how far away. They also brought in new sounds for all of them, making them all sound a hell of a lot more punchy. Also wolves are in now and are scary af to have stalk you and attack you.
Desync/item loss/random dieing is much more rare now than it was 6 months ago. The frame rate is acceptable after the .60 patch in early 2016. It has brushed up amazingly over the past year, development progress as far as I'm concerned is solid and fulfilling, given I never played the original mod nor Arma and have owned it for 14 months.
The reason people need to cut a little slack on the devs and their pace is simply that the scale of this project is ABSOLUTELY HUGE, there are billions of things that all have to work in harmony not to mention the fact their completely overhauling certain systems and there cant be constant updates for them like people expect but they will eventually drop and they will be serious game changers, I'm talking stamina system, player animation system, visual overhauls, choppers and planes, base building, soft skills, temperature system and of course beards.
There are definitely moments of despair with bugs and stuff but c'mon; for the amount of time consumed and fun had it is crazy how worth the money DayZ is.

Hell, its often used to the game's advantage in some places- such as the lighting in the waterfall area or the gloomy-ness of the dump. in fact, the  simplicity can be rather nice, as it often leaves room for interpretation of how things look.
- the best part of the entire game. very often the game is hilarious, quirky and outright silly. sometimes, it does get serious. occasionally, its pretty sad. and just rarely, its unnerving. the game does a fantastic job entertaining alll the way throughout, and no matter what choices you make the game has a plan for you to keep you interested. a lovely mix for anyone who wants to play a game to get immersed in another world, rather than just super exciting action. theres LOTS of attention to detail everywhere you look for lore.
- Ahhh, the most important part. aaannd, sadly, the games only "flaw" . most of the time you will either be walking, talking, or in "combat". and while the story is

Driving a truck through Europe delivering various loads, earning enough money to buy more trucks and upgrades sound boring? Think again. This game is strangely compelling. The sense of achievement earned through driving a long journey and safely reaching your destination with an undamaged trailer is just as rewarding as any kind of videogame I've played.
Obviously you're not expected to say, drive from Grimsby to Berlin in real time, but the developers have balanced these kinds of journeys with the right amount of play time to make you feel as though you have completeled a mammoth journey through various Countries across Europe.
Not only can it be immensely satisfying, it is also strangely relaxing. You could find yourself navigating mile after mile of motorway to then lead off onto a winding B-road, where you might be desperately trying to overtake the slow lorry in front so that you can make your delivery in time. Why not tune the cabs radio into any number of real life stations to keep you company on your journey?
The game engine is superb. The day and night cycles show off the various scenery to good effect, and the AI of the traffic is sufficient to make you think real people are going about their daily lives, rather than faceless automatons. Waiting at a junction to turn through oncoming traffic? You may get a car stop and flash their lights at you, helping you out onto the road. Pulling into a patrol station? You can't get any petrol until you turn off your engine! It's these kinds of details that add up to provide a simulation that has obviously been created with a lot of hard work and love.
If you have the slightest incling that this title might appeal to you, BUY IT. You will not regret it. If you have a wheel or a yoke to control rather than a gamepad, even better. You'll have many thousands of miles of relaxing, enjoyable driving ahead of you. Just remember to turn those lights on when it rains ok?

When I first heard about it, I had a hard time believing the hype that surrounded it. "It's just an 8-bit indie game!" I thought. "Game of the year 2015? Second coming of Christ? Whatever, I'll just keep playing the games I have already."
Then a friend of mine got it for me while it was on sale, and I never felt I was able to return the favor.
Undertale may not be the best game I've ever played, but it's high on the list.
The gameplay is simple, but effective and it does what its meant to do well. The puzzles provided a nice challenge, but were never pointlessly difficult.
The soundtrack is fantastic. Months after I've fully completed the game, I still love listening to a few of the songs made for this game.
The characters are lovable, with distinct personalities that you could almost believe are real.
And the story. Holy crap, the story. Imagine your standard RPG turned on its head. I can't put words together to describe the impact this game and its story had on me. It made me laugh, it made me cry. It made me feel so emotionally attached to fictional characters in ways I've never felt before. It filled me with the determination I needed to move on at some points. It made me think about my own existence and the choices I've made up to that point. It made me feel sorry for the antagonist who tried to murder me only minutes after I began playing.
If you're one of the many who hasn't played this game, you're missing out.
Everyone should own this game.

Undertale is an RPG made primarily by the beautiful writing of Toby Fox. Undertale was born as a side project of Fox's Halloween Hack for Earthbound (an SNES game from the only RPG series that I can recommend higher than Undertale itself) that snowballed into the game that you're reading this review for.
I have recommended this game to a few friends, and they have all quite enjoyed it, although some not until they have completed the game for the first time. This being said, if you can make it through the various endings of the game, you will not be disappointed. If you have just $10 to spare, it will well be worth it. Although I was skeptical of the game's art style at first, the game proved itself with its fabulous story and combat.
Do yourself a favor.
Play this game.

A surprisingly fun game. It's a fun and realistic game all around, with only a few problems. The main one is the stupidity of the AI, but this will be fixed in the coming update. Another thing which annoys me personally is the inaccuracy of junctions, which are nothing like they are in real life, but otherwise the roads are very realistic. At the moment, the game is also incompatible with Intel cards on Linux, which is kind of annoying.
Throughout the UK and other countries you can see landmarks which are the same as in real life and for example, the ratio of motorways to smaller roads in Poland feels accurate. Cities also feel realistic, with some real life features being added to give a specific feel to every city. For example, you can see the local city hall in the background as you drive through Olsztyn.
With the Going East! DLC installed, there's a wide variety of places you can go. There's also a variety of mods which add more features to the game if you get bored.
It's clear that there are more features the developer can add to the game in the future (it is frequently updated), but it doesn't feel repetetive.

It's been a little over a year since Undertale came out.  Chances are at this point that, if you're reading this review, you've heard about this game somewhere on the internet and are curious to see if it really is worth checking out.
Short answer:
Yes.  It's fun and funny and doesn't cost much.
Long answer:
Despite what you might have heard from the especially rabid fans out there, this isn't the best game ever.  No game is, really.  What it is, however, is a very well done RPG with quirky humor and lovable characters that those who have played the Mother series or some of the earlier Mario RPGs would be right at home with.  To get a little idea of what I'm talking about when it comes to this game's sense of humor, check out the "about this game" and trailer above.
Anyway, utilizing an interesting "bullet hell" method of dodging enemy attacks as well as methods to "spare" enemies, this game brings quite a few new ideas to the table while playing with some of the genre's typical conventions.  All of that is helped along with one of the best soundtracks I've heard from an indie title.
I admit, I was put off by a lot of the hype wrapped around this game when its fandom took off but my friends kept telling me to give it a chance.  In the end, I'm glad I did and I hope you'll give it a chance too.  You just might find it as charming as I did.

Originally written by myself on Metacritic: (contains spoilers)
This has to be the single greatest simulator game every made. It's hard to believe a trucking simulator is as fun as this. I can't believe I'm giving this a 10 out of 10! Anyways; let's start with the pros shall we? So, you start off at the very bottom of the totem pole. You have 0 trucks, you don't have anyone working for you, and you don't have a home garage. (Although you do have a home city that you can pick) You have to do odd little jobs to save up enough money and reputation so that the bank notices you. Once they notice you, you can pull out a loan. With the loan you can buy your own truck and start doing better and more lucrative trucking jobs. Throughout the whole game you are upgrading your stats which allow you to drive farther, haul hazardous material, drive longer distances, haul urgent deliveries, and so on and so forth. Once you gain enough money, you can buy your own garage, and upgrade it. When you have a garage, you can hire others to drive for you. Now, this doesn't mean you can stop driving, but they will start to earn a nice chunk of change. (And you can control what type of cargo they haul)
Now, on top of all of this; this game accepts mods. There are a TON of mods for this game; both user created and professionally created. Some of the mods are horrendous and will crash the game; however some of the mods are extremely useful and make the game a million times more fun. Right now, with my game, I have over 200 different loads I can carry at any given time and I can travel thousands of kilometers. (Then again, everything on mine is maxed out) This is not a game you will beat in one setting, in one day, or even in one week. This is a nice relaxing game to play.
Since I did the pros, I'll do the cons. (Which don't affect my rating because they don't matter much to me) You don't have any damage simulation. Well, you do and you don't. It's a partial simulation. If you damage your truck high enough you will have a tough time driving it as the engine will stall out on you. However, you won't notice any physical damage to your truck. It's all internal and nothing cosmetic will actually show. (Even the AI cars won't show damage when you hit them) Other than that big one, there aren't too many cons. Each person is different though.
I personally recommend this game to anyone into simulation games and anyone who is interested in trucks. You will not be let down.

It's been a little over a year since Undertale came out.  Chances are at this point that, if you're reading this review, you've heard about this game somewhere on the internet and are curious to see if it really is worth checking out.
Short answer:
Yes.  It's fun and funny and doesn't cost much.
Long answer:
Despite what you might have heard from the especially rabid fans out there, this isn't the best game ever.  No game is, really.  What it is, however, is a very well done RPG with quirky humor and lovable characters that those who have played the Mother series or some of the earlier Mario RPGs would be right at home with.  To get a little idea of what I'm talking about when it comes to this game's sense of humor, check out the "about this game" and trailer above.
Anyway, utilizing an interesting "bullet hell" method of dodging enemy attacks as well as methods to "spare" enemies, this game brings quite a few new ideas to the table while playing with some of the genre's typical conventions.  All of that is helped along with one of the best soundtracks I've heard from an indie title.
I admit, I was put off by a lot of the hype wrapped around this game when its fandom took off but my friends kept telling me to give it a chance.  In the end, I'm glad I did and I hope you'll give it a chance too.  You just might find it as charming as I did.

Straight up, Boarderlands 2 failed to exceed my already low expectations.
When I was introduced to the game, I was greeted with an unskippable cutscene. After that, I reconfigured the settings due to the resolution being a bit off. Crashed to desktop, had to go through the unskippable cutscene (Which ill give the benefit of the doubt to and assume its a problem on my end).
You're instantly thrown into a snowy world, where the snow just instantly dies off in a few seconds and doesnt really return to the extent it did, which is nice actually seeing. You're introducted to CL4P-TP, your egotistical, depressing voice that follows you around for a few hours. The self proclaimed lootfest then boils down into either looting $2 each or ammo, and the odd weapon that would be good to sell.
The game is heavily influenced on humor. The humor is god-awful, in all fairness. It consists of memes, saying things will happen but dont/saying things wont happen but do, and random humor. I was aware of this prior but played it on a free day on steam.
On the good side, the gun-play is great for some guns. However, enemies seem a bit too bullet spongy (as do you), which had me choosing the gun with more DPS over the gun that I actually liked to use. The gun variation in this game is odd; different brands of guns have different properties and looks which more often than not, I didn't like. The designs were disinteresting in majority, but there were some good ones, especially from the revolvers and some pistols, early game rifles and the grenades were fun to play with.
TL;DR
Pros: Good port with loads of options, some guns feel really good using, cell shading (in my opinion)
Cons: Awful writing, repetitive combat, the gunplay seems to be a bit stale altogether, looting seems unnecessary
2/10 wont launch again unless utterly bored

Originally written by myself on Metacritic: (contains spoilers)
This has to be the single greatest simulator game every made. It's hard to believe a trucking simulator is as fun as this. I can't believe I'm giving this a 10 out of 10! Anyways; let's start with the pros shall we? So, you start off at the very bottom of the totem pole. You have 0 trucks, you don't have anyone working for you, and you don't have a home garage. (Although you do have a home city that you can pick) You have to do odd little jobs to save up enough money and reputation so that the bank notices you. Once they notice you, you can pull out a loan. With the loan you can buy your own truck and start doing better and more lucrative trucking jobs. Throughout the whole game you are upgrading your stats which allow you to drive farther, haul hazardous material, drive longer distances, haul urgent deliveries, and so on and so forth. Once you gain enough money, you can buy your own garage, and upgrade it. When you have a garage, you can hire others to drive for you. Now, this doesn't mean you can stop driving, but they will start to earn a nice chunk of change. (And you can control what type of cargo they haul)
Now, on top of all of this; this game accepts mods. There are a TON of mods for this game; both user created and professionally created. Some of the mods are horrendous and will crash the game; however some of the mods are extremely useful and make the game a million times more fun. Right now, with my game, I have over 200 different loads I can carry at any given time and I can travel thousands of kilometers. (Then again, everything on mine is maxed out) This is not a game you will beat in one setting, in one day, or even in one week. This is a nice relaxing game to play.
Since I did the pros, I'll do the cons. (Which don't affect my rating because they don't matter much to me) You don't have any damage simulation. Well, you do and you don't. It's a partial simulation. If you damage your truck high enough you will have a tough time driving it as the engine will stall out on you. However, you won't notice any physical damage to your truck. It's all internal and nothing cosmetic will actually show. (Even the AI cars won't show damage when you hit them) Other than that big one, there aren't too many cons. Each person is different though.
I personally recommend this game to anyone into simulation games and anyone who is interested in trucks. You will not be let down.

This game is splendid, the genre of simulation games gets a lot of bad reputation and is generally the laughing stock. Euro Truck Simulator 2 just doesn't care and just became a really good game. If you like driving around, micromanaging your employees, or just like to mess around in simulators it is possible to do so in this.
At first I was skeptic and I bought it on impulse but at the point of writing this I have played more than 50 hours driving around Europe, every country really is a unique experience with a lot of details added to the side of the roads making you feel like you're really there. I thought it wasn't true untill I hit some areas I've been too in my past although sometimes the road was a lot shorter than in real life, it still really felt like I was there, looking around from my truck, in the mountains, over the bridges and through the forests, the view takes your breath away. If you just like traveling, this game really gives a good experience of traveling with a truck.
I really have to mention the roads, they are different everywhere, whereas in the UK you'll find a lot of roundabouts and you drive left, when you cross the pond by ship or train, you get on roads that are really specific to the countries, in the Netherlands for example you have these roads with orange browny sides that are meant for bicycle riders, in Poland you get roads that are a bit broken left and right, they are a straight contrast. Not to forget the different gasstations on the sides of the road, the tollhouses for tollroads, the bordercrossings, they all have a lot of variaty, the cities difer a lot.
The truck handling really feels, when you drive without a trailer it feels like you're weightless, you pull up so fast and you corner so nicely, put a trailer behind it and it is the opposite. Depending on the weight of the trailer, it can be really heavy, trying to get up to speed can be a drag with those weights and trying to race the corners can be a large accident, you really feel like you're heavy when you have a trailer behind you. The things you can transport also make a difference a whole lot of difference, sometimes you transport bottom heavy diggers of 25 tons and you just feel you got a lot of grip in the corners, but then the next time it is sand which is heavier in the center of height, and you go through a corner at a medium pace and you start tipping, you just know right there that the next corner you can't go as fast anymore. The difference between two trucks is also noticable, every truck is different some have a lot of horse power and torque, whereas others have barely any and need to really pull their strength to get up a hill. If you go to a garage to repair your truck you can also upgrade it and customize it, making it even better than before.
The games controls are also good, though lacking controller support, it has support for steeringwheels and joysticks. It for example does support the sticks on my controller but it does not support any of the buttons, though this can be solved with things like xpadder, it would still add a lot to the game if it had native support.
I would definitely recommend it if you enjoy trucking it really has the full experience.

This is easily one of the best games I've got in 2013, and will probably remain in my Steam Favorites list for a long time. I never played a game like this before and now it has me hooked. It keeps getting better!
At first I was just enjoying the scenery, the gameplay of driving the trucks, taking different jobs, and leveling up my XP so I could make more money and buy my own truck (Volvo FH16 Globetrotter). Now I'm working to upgrade my truck and my business. The business part is pretty addictive too. You can take a loan, expand your first garage, start buying more trucks, and hire drivers to work for you. I'm anxious to get enough money to buy another garage somewhere else and start another fleet.
You can not only use your skill points from XP to strategically improve your abilities and rewards one step at a time to make more money, you can do the same with your drivers (or choose to have their skills auto-balanced).
The scenery is gorgeous and there are some nice little touches of different things to see on the road and in different cities.
The changing weather and day/night transformations are great. Rain storms are awesome.
Driving in Europe is really not that different than driving in North America. Although, for some reason driving in the UK made me a little nervous--maybe it's the little extra traffic; maybe it's just driving on the other side of the road; or maybe I was expecting The Stig to cross my path.
I play with a  Driving Force GT wheel, and even though as a fan of racing games I at first had doubts about this game, I gotta say if you have a wheel you really should try this game. Everything about the game is pure pleasure, but the driving is not just enjoyable but challenging as well. Things like parking your trailer; traveling swiftly but balancing your trailer's loads around all kinds of bends, inclines and declines; driving at night; dealing with other drivers (watch out for the evil empire of busses!) and trying to overtake slow pokes who follow the speed limit; traveling as fast as you can and watching for speeding cameras and changing speed limits make this one of the best driving games I've ever played. Oh yeah, don't blow those red lights--all the tickets you could get for various things can really ad up on one trip.
It actually is becoming a racing game as I'm travelling longer distances. Right now in order to not interrupt my delivery with rest stops and not be late (which costs money) or get fined for driving while tired (happened to me four times at the end of one trip), I'm trying to make my trips even faster. So I'm balancing my loads at top speeds, taking the ever changing curves of the road as gracefully as possible, putting the pedal to the metal but watching for speed cameras and changing speed limits (watch out for those road hazard areas and be careful in town), and trying to overtake just like in a racing game--but it's more challenging with opposing traffic on busy highways!
It's also a great music game. Hit the road and use your in-game radio to tune into different internet stations or play your favorite music on a media player in the background (I recommend AIMP3, which has a great interface and features but is very low resource).
I highly recommend ETS2! I hope they make more expansions, and I am looking forward to American Truck Simulator.
