Wake up, Devs, you're game's on fire!
It's not hot, it's burning down into generic insignificance.
You've almost killed it. Not even with the SLOW progress but with the WRONG one!
I can't possibly downvote it, given the time i played this game. But i'm very tempted to, believe me! Because the game i played almost doesn't exist anymore.
Many reviews cover the lack of progress.
As a former big fan of the multiplayer part I wanna talk about GAMEPLAY..
Back when Dayz Standalone was popular, it was so because of OTHER PLAYERS! Full stop.
The main focus of the game was the frequent meeting of other players.
Be it for cooperation, be it for Roleplay, friendly or hostile or be it for plain PVP. It suited different Multiplayer AND singleplayer playstyles
AND it offered also(!!) to go alone into the woods and live of the land, rather then of tinned food. That should have been ONE focus in the development of the game NOT the only one, forced on everybody.
_______________________________________________
But due to the devs obsession with lonely hardcore survival, any kind of civil, friendly or hostile mass  multiPLAYER play OR roleplay is almost completely dead. The very core of the original game, the very reason why i and many others have so many hours in it, is DEAD.
It's killed by plain Dev stubborness and arrogance.
_________________________________________________
Now they pushed and push with every of the rare patches towards hardcore survival. „everybody or small groups for himself in the woods“ or (eventually)„pvp at the military camps“. They are so desperate to get people off the coast where most actual multiplayer happened. That seems to be their main focus nowadays.
Criticism is exclusively met with censorship.
And no serveroptions to cancel that. You're stuck with the balance and focus idea of the devs which is BAD!
There is no option to have more (civil) loot at the coast again,so that people can stay there, adjust the number of zombies or turn that absolutely silly fog off.
With simple preselections for civil loot, coast and inland and military loot you could already adjust focus and gameplay on a server.
You don't have to give full access to serverfiles, which would make bugtracking impossible. That's their excuse.
All would help having more actual multiplayer, with whatever focus, in some sort of (very large) hotspot again.
And all the way the player numbers IMPLODED over these hardcre survival focus. Yes, some love it. but apparently the game has/had the wrong players for turning it into „7 Days 2 die“. Which of course DOES have gameplay and server options to adjust gameplay.
Again: This variety of playstyles the game offered made it actually UNIQUE amongst all the multiplayer survival crafty games. Dayz has so much more options in dealing with other players apart from shoot or not. Many focussed on banditry roleplay and interactions, but also for cooperation.
But not anymore. These options and game mechanics are still there of course. But you don't meet enough players anymore apart from the military camps where there is plain counterstrike PvP. Even that spoiled by hackers and the still unsolved Duping pest (dupering cheaters  are only marginally smaller ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s then actual hackers!!), that makes it hopeless for honest players.
THAT versatility and flexibility differentiated it from Rust, from H1Z1, Miscreated and others where you either shoot or not. Made it more interesting for me, even (actually because) it has no options in terms of base building and stuff as those games have.
In short: in gameplay old DayZ was a VASTLY BETTER GAME then the current one.
In technology it has improved. But  enough for 4 years? No!
That brings  us to:
The attempted objective, neutral part of the review:
___________________________________________
Its pointed out a lot down here, that progress is painfully slow. Hard to argue with that. With the best will in the world it is unaccectable now.
Performance improved massively (from very low levels), Persistence works, Zombies don't run through walls anymore 0.61 also finally kinda fixes lighting and shadows. 
The map has been improved. Although its now almost too filled with cities and stuff now for my liking. It feels rather spammy in places. 
What are the fails? 
They built a new car system from scratch, which is still a disaster. They should have adjusted and improved the Arma 2 Car system and used free time and ressources for more important things.
I'm not expecting "Project Cars" or even "Need for Speed" but at least something working.
In the one patch per year, they now mainly fiddle with gameplay, balance and focus of the game, adding new trees and wolves, without adressing ANY of the technical issues. 
Introducing much more zombies and wolves - together with probably the worst melee system, the game ever had. And it was always bad.
It's still possible to melee zombies, but the feedback, the feel, the hitboxes, the sound, the lag - it's STILL rather terrible. Increasing the number without solving the technical issues underneath, including the lag, is just stupid.
Zombie AI is actually much better now, but somewhat eaten up by their laggy and glitchy movement.
Devs want you to go military and shoot things though, so the crappy melee system shouldn't matter to those players. I however don't like DayZ being played as a shooter. 
And a melee system is in the game so it has to work! I'm not expecting "Dying light" but at least something working....
______________
Conclusion independent from personal concerns:
Is it a Early Access(ea) ripoff, as many claim?
No! Sorry here come the facts:
1. Slow progress is not against the rules of ea! Fact.
While perversions of the ea concept like pay dlc and real money ingame shops in various other games, should force a release out of early access imho! 
2. The game costs currently 28€. Thats all you spend and possible lose. Fact.
No microtransactions, no pay2win pay dlc.... Just 28$. Even in it's current state it's well worth that! Or maybe was... see review beginning..
3. There is enough to see and to do in it, as it is. The map is the most complex, interesting and probably biggest (non-procedural) map of all those survival games. There are plenty of game mechanics, that work well, despte the issues. And if you LIKE shooting stuff you won't have some of the issues, i have with DayZs game mechanics. You might have others, i'm not aware of..
4.Given all this, if you're aware that this game is and will be for a long time, very unfinished, and live with its glitches, it's worth it's money. If you don't want to risk 28€ or expect a somehow finished, polished or unglitchy™ game, DON'T buy it (yet).

Straight up, Boarderlands 2 failed to exceed my already low expectations.
When I was introduced to the game, I was greeted with an unskippable cutscene. After that, I reconfigured the settings due to the resolution being a bit off. Crashed to desktop, had to go through the unskippable cutscene (Which ill give the benefit of the doubt to and assume its a problem on my end).
You're instantly thrown into a snowy world, where the snow just instantly dies off in a few seconds and doesnt really return to the extent it did, which is nice actually seeing. You're introducted to CL4P-TP, your egotistical, depressing voice that follows you around for a few hours. The self proclaimed lootfest then boils down into either looting $2 each or ammo, and the odd weapon that would be good to sell.
The game is heavily influenced on humor. The humor is god-awful, in all fairness. It consists of memes, saying things will happen but dont/saying things wont happen but do, and random humor. I was aware of this prior but played it on a free day on steam.
On the good side, the gun-play is great for some guns. However, enemies seem a bit too bullet spongy (as do you), which had me choosing the gun with more DPS over the gun that I actually liked to use. The gun variation in this game is odd; different brands of guns have different properties and looks which more often than not, I didn't like. The designs were disinteresting in majority, but there were some good ones, especially from the revolvers and some pistols, early game rifles and the grenades were fun to play with.
TL;DR
Pros: Good port with loads of options, some guns feel really good using, cell shading (in my opinion)
Cons: Awful writing, repetitive combat, the gunplay seems to be a bit stale altogether, looting seems unnecessary
2/10 wont launch again unless utterly bored

Let's get one thing out of the way before this review starts... if you haven't played undertale yet, don't watch a let's play, don't go to the wiki, don't even go type undertale into google. This game has so many spoilers that literally the first minute of game play has♥♥♥♥♥♥you don't expect, it defies expectations on so many levels.
Now with that out of the way, let's talk how I found this game. One night, I was browsing reddit and I got linked to a little subreddit, no css style, just basic subreddit look, called R/undertale, I looked at the sidebar and saw that it was about a little RPG that nobody had to die in, I groaned, this is going to be some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ little rpg where the game forces you down a path with no agency of your own, that's what I thought, it's such a cliche to use the "oh where different because we defy the genre standards" which in most cases I've seen means the game doesn't focus on any real gameplay, and for all intents and purposes could be a goddamned book. Look, I love video games as a art, but part of them being a art is the unique idea to the media, viewer agency. But I digress, I reluctantly subscribed to the subreddit as a part of me wanted it to be the game that I wanted it to be deep down.
Fast forward a couple months, and my youtube feed was blowing up with undertale LP's from everyone, it was getting reviews from people like totalbiscuit, the Jimquisition, and wait, no yahtzee put it at the number 1 spot on his games of 2015? WAIT HE PUT A GAME HE DIDN'T REVIEW ON HIS TOP 5? WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ HE SAID IT WAS GOOD? (for those who don't know, yahtzee is possibly, the most cynical game reviewer, ever, he has only truly sung the praise of games that he considers near-perfect, portal and the like.) OK, OK, I'll try it, and let me tell you, this game is possibly one of the most impactive games you will ever play.
Undertale deconstructs so much of the rpg genre, nay, the gaming medium, that I know for a fact it will, and already has, left huge waves in the game's as art or as a story area. It gives the player complete control of their actions, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, you decide how the plot will progress. Every actions you take, will leave a mark in this playthrough, or the next, and yes, I realize that is said by so many games, but Undertale is the only game i've seen where it rings true.
I wish I could explain to you the perfection that is its soundtrack, or the absolutely amazing writing and storytelling a game  with mostly one dev just so casually has, or even just the little details that litter the game like little nuggets of genius and artist polish you think could only be achieved by a whole team of devs that stayed up night and day to make such a masterpiece.
However, instead, I think I'll put my effort into failing to explain the one thing I love most about the game the amazing use of comedy, sadness, motivation, and the whole human array of emotions to create a world that the player feels truly immersed in. This game truly draws in the player and absorbs them, every little minor NPC has their own personality, and major NPC's have so many layers of character that it seems like they're real people. Seriously never before has a game been so amazing at pulling in a player into the story then Undertale. Not only does the story pull you in, it never leaves you, when you are finished, the game stays with you, honestly this game left such a impact on me that I still chant stay determined in my head when I face a hard conflict in my life. This game leaves you with one thing, the Determination to face your own problems, knowing that no matter how hard something gets, if you stay determined and keep on going, you can, and will, achieve your goal. No matter how many times you fall down, you must get back up and face the fight head on, and learn from your failed attempts. THAT, that is what true art is, leaving the viewer with something, that never leaves them.
If for some reason, you haven't played undertale, and haven't had it spoiled for yourself, please, spend $10 and buy this game, sit aside a afternoon for it. It's shining polish, that can only come from true love in a project, it's beautiful story, that only exists once in a generation, it's amazing soundtrack, that still to this very day give me the same emotions I first felt listening to them, and much much more will pull you in and show you what true art really is.
To say I adore this game is a understatement, I believe this game should be the very foundation for story based games in the future, this game is the start of a new generation of story based games, and I for one, can't wait to play every single one of them.
This game in my humble opinion is the clear choice for a steam reward, anyone of them. It does so much right it deserves all the praise it gets.

Lag is constant, frame-rate dips to the teens and lower (heck I think it hit -5 at one point, something I didn't know was possible) and it even got to the point where I had to look away from the computer cause my head started to hurt. Finally, for me at least, it is nigh impossible to control the camera with the mouse as it also lags and has a major 5 second delay to it. I want to know what the developers of this game have been doing these past year cause it sure as heck doesn't look like they were working on improving this game. Looking at the updates to it, it seems they are more focused on adding content and fixing small, minor issues then working on actually IMPROVING the game and fixing the major issues plaguing this once promising game. In short, avoid this game for now, until the developers stop dicking around with pointless weapon updates and actually work on IMPROVING this game.

Wake up, Devs, you're game's on fire!
It's not hot, it's burning down into generic insignificance.
You've almost killed it. Not even with the SLOW progress but with the WRONG one!
I can't possibly downvote it, given the time i played this game. But i'm very tempted to, believe me! Because the game i played almost doesn't exist anymore.
Many reviews cover the lack of progress.
As a former big fan of the multiplayer part I wanna talk about GAMEPLAY..
Back when Dayz Standalone was popular, it was so because of OTHER PLAYERS! Full stop.
The main focus of the game was the frequent meeting of other players.
Be it for cooperation, be it for Roleplay, friendly or hostile or be it for plain PVP. It suited different Multiplayer AND singleplayer playstyles
AND it offered also(!!) to go alone into the woods and live of the land, rather then of tinned food. That should have been ONE focus in the development of the game NOT the only one, forced on everybody.
_______________________________________________
But due to the devs obsession with lonely hardcore survival, any kind of civil, friendly or hostile mass  multiPLAYER play OR roleplay is almost completely dead. The very core of the original game, the very reason why i and many others have so many hours in it, is DEAD.
It's killed by plain Dev stubborness and arrogance.
_________________________________________________
Now they pushed and push with every of the rare patches towards hardcore survival. „everybody or small groups for himself in the woods“ or (eventually)„pvp at the military camps“. They are so desperate to get people off the coast where most actual multiplayer happened. That seems to be their main focus nowadays.
Criticism is exclusively met with censorship.
And no serveroptions to cancel that. You're stuck with the balance and focus idea of the devs which is BAD!
There is no option to have more (civil) loot at the coast again,so that people can stay there, adjust the number of zombies or turn that absolutely silly fog off.
With simple preselections for civil loot, coast and inland and military loot you could already adjust focus and gameplay on a server.
You don't have to give full access to serverfiles, which would make bugtracking impossible. That's their excuse.
All would help having more actual multiplayer, with whatever focus, in some sort of (very large) hotspot again.
And all the way the player numbers IMPLODED over these hardcre survival focus. Yes, some love it. but apparently the game has/had the wrong players for turning it into „7 Days 2 die“. Which of course DOES have gameplay and server options to adjust gameplay.
Again: This variety of playstyles the game offered made it actually UNIQUE amongst all the multiplayer survival crafty games. Dayz has so much more options in dealing with other players apart from shoot or not. Many focussed on banditry roleplay and interactions, but also for cooperation.
But not anymore. These options and game mechanics are still there of course. But you don't meet enough players anymore apart from the military camps where there is plain counterstrike PvP. Even that spoiled by hackers and the still unsolved Duping pest (dupering cheaters  are only marginally smaller ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s then actual hackers!!), that makes it hopeless for honest players.
THAT versatility and flexibility differentiated it from Rust, from H1Z1, Miscreated and others where you either shoot or not. Made it more interesting for me, even (actually because) it has no options in terms of base building and stuff as those games have.
In short: in gameplay old DayZ was a VASTLY BETTER GAME then the current one.
In technology it has improved. But  enough for 4 years? No!
That brings  us to:
The attempted objective, neutral part of the review:
___________________________________________
Its pointed out a lot down here, that progress is painfully slow. Hard to argue with that. With the best will in the world it is unaccectable now.
Performance improved massively (from very low levels), Persistence works, Zombies don't run through walls anymore 0.61 also finally kinda fixes lighting and shadows. 
The map has been improved. Although its now almost too filled with cities and stuff now for my liking. It feels rather spammy in places. 
What are the fails? 
They built a new car system from scratch, which is still a disaster. They should have adjusted and improved the Arma 2 Car system and used free time and ressources for more important things.
I'm not expecting "Project Cars" or even "Need for Speed" but at least something working.
In the one patch per year, they now mainly fiddle with gameplay, balance and focus of the game, adding new trees and wolves, without adressing ANY of the technical issues. 
Introducing much more zombies and wolves - together with probably the worst melee system, the game ever had. And it was always bad.
It's still possible to melee zombies, but the feedback, the feel, the hitboxes, the sound, the lag - it's STILL rather terrible. Increasing the number without solving the technical issues underneath, including the lag, is just stupid.
Zombie AI is actually much better now, but somewhat eaten up by their laggy and glitchy movement.
Devs want you to go military and shoot things though, so the crappy melee system shouldn't matter to those players. I however don't like DayZ being played as a shooter. 
And a melee system is in the game so it has to work! I'm not expecting "Dying light" but at least something working....
______________
Conclusion independent from personal concerns:
Is it a Early Access(ea) ripoff, as many claim?
No! Sorry here come the facts:
1. Slow progress is not against the rules of ea! Fact.
While perversions of the ea concept like pay dlc and real money ingame shops in various other games, should force a release out of early access imho! 
2. The game costs currently 28€. Thats all you spend and possible lose. Fact.
No microtransactions, no pay2win pay dlc.... Just 28$. Even in it's current state it's well worth that! Or maybe was... see review beginning..
3. There is enough to see and to do in it, as it is. The map is the most complex, interesting and probably biggest (non-procedural) map of all those survival games. There are plenty of game mechanics, that work well, despte the issues. And if you LIKE shooting stuff you won't have some of the issues, i have with DayZs game mechanics. You might have others, i'm not aware of..
4.Given all this, if you're aware that this game is and will be for a long time, very unfinished, and live with its glitches, it's worth it's money. If you don't want to risk 28€ or expect a somehow finished, polished or unglitchy™ game, DON'T buy it (yet).

If you play lone wolf you're most likely gonna avoid all contact with players and try to loot places quickly and take longer ways into towns and scope them out, where as if you were in a group of 4 one person would quickly scope out a town and then the other 3 would quickly scan the town or base for loot and if there is none there you move on.
This game I only have about 50 hours clocked in stand alone, but if I were to clock in my Arma II Dayz mod time it would in total be around 375-400 hrs. And to be quite frank, I don't exactly know my way around the map like I use to but it takes planning and overall playing the game constantly to get use to it. You also can't play this game for 30 minutes and log out, you have to fully experience a large amount of hours spent in the day on DayZ. Many players also miss out many unique situations by logging out before combat starts or when they see players they log out instantly or server swap.
Overall this game is truly a game I will continue to keep playing and I ♥♥♥♥ing enjoy ever moment of it.

Rust is a game that I will not be recommending because of how hostile the game is toward players who aren't in groups. Rust is a game where you will spend hours gathering resources to slowly build a wooden house only for a six man squad to tear everything down in a heart beat. Now I understand that the nature of these games is cruel but Rust seems to have certain crafting aspects that makes the game easy for groups and almost impossible for lone players.
I could go into excruciating detail but all I'm going to say is. Grouped up players can pop up large bases with ease because there's multiple of them gathering and defending, lone players will spend hours building a basic wooden shed which is ridiculously easy to smash down.  Building wooden things in this game is pointless because of how easy it is to break, for a group building a stone house with a metal door is easy but for a lone player building a stone house with a metal door takes an extremely long time and there's a very good chance that a kill-on-sight 12 year old will blast you away before you complete anything.
If you plan to play this game alone stay far far away from it.

In 2009, I was given Borderlands to me as a gift, I hadn't heard much of it, so i wasn't expecting anything great out of it, but nevertheless I gave it a go.
I was completely blown away, the experience of that game was unlike anything i'd ever played before, the millions of guns, the bosses, the loot, the humour, the characters, and DLC that made me keep coming back, it was fantastic, and I loved it.
Then, in 2011, Borderlands 2 was announced. I was excited, but at the same time, anxious. "Surely it can't top the first game?" I thought.
I was wrong.
Borderlands 2 has everythng the first Borderlands had, and so much more. It added elements to the game i never would have dreamed of, introduced 4 new inventive, unique vault hunters (with 2 more as DLC!), new characters, a fantastic story, over a hundred side quests, more loot, more humour, more everything I loved about the first Borderlands.
Even as a standalone game, rather than a sequel, Borderlands 2 is still an amazing experience for anyone to play.
So, if you're looking for a game with a beautiful world design, great story, humour, action, and endless amounts of replayability then look no further, because this is one of the best games I've ever played.

This game should be taken as an example of a good simulator. It is not anything like the classical "Some Thing Simulator 2010" which are infamous for being terribly bad, no, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a genuinely good simulator.
The cities are small (only the freight parts have been modeled) and close together for entertainment reasons. Depending on how you like to play, this may be inconvenient or convenient:
I personally made a mistake during the game, and chosen to increase my perks at long-distance driving, when I realized after playing that I don't like long-distance driving, the short-distance driving assignments become very rare, and there's no way to decrease your perks without the help of suspicious cheating programs (or starting over, which I may do).
Handling of the truck is pretty nice but I didn't have a steering wheel for the full experience. There are a lot of options to adapt to controllers such as joysticks, mouse or keyboard. The control feel of different trucks may vary.
Some assignments are strange as your truck with lower tier gear will not be able to drive up certain rough ramps in quarries.
The entire interior of the truck is modeled, and you can use the mouse (or other controller way) to look around peek your head out of the window.
The perks system is based on your experience and performance, it will let you drive different types of freight at different distance with different time restrictions (which isn't time restrictions, but pressure as you might take a wrong turn or fail to manage your sleeping before taking the assignment).
There are some faults that are quite problematic, like taking left turns in right-hand side roads (or right turns in left-hand side roads) due to the continuous flow of vehicles that are barring your way. It looks like they have tried to fix it by letting some vehicles stop and give you a headlights signal, but it doesn't seem to apply if you aren't the vehicle waiting (= there is a bottleneck of vehicles in front of you).
Buying a truck of your preference is very satisfying. There are a handful of customization of your truck as you progress through the game. I like pink trucks.

Rust is a survival game with an apocalyptic atmosphere. It shares some similarities with other titles in the survival genre, but also has some unique features. Currently, the feedback for Rust has been up and down, here are some pros and cons... Keep in mind this review is from August 2017.
How about the cons first for a change?
Cons:
- Early access for 2+ years (EA is not a bad thing, but when a game is in this stage for too long the party may feel over before it begins, if you get me. But things may improve, providing for a fresh experience when the game is fully released.
- Toxic community
- Controversial Updates (The game has been getting a few yes/no updates currently. These are game changers and could be called a pro or a con depending on how you enjoy playing.)
- Unoptimized (Rust is not preforming as well as it could be, but is by no means running terribly, and there are updates further optimising the game.)
Pros:
- Nice graphics (Rust has some great graphics, just make sure you meet the reccomended specs)
- Good feeling controls
- Fun and easy building system
- Player Suggestions (players can suggest features to be added to the game)
- Constant updates (new material is constantly added to the game)
Overall, Rust is a great survival title in anyones library. Worth the 20 dollars, just make sure you play with a team, or some friends, as solo is currently difficult. Remember it is still being worked on.

You'd think Euro Truck Simulator would be some kind of gargantuan♥♥♥♥♥♥take. A game where you simply drive at sensible speeds in an unwieldy vehicle from one town to another freighting apples and pencils and other sundry? Who would want to play this?
And yet... It is fun. It's fun. Somehow. It's fun trying to stay under the limit, it's fun simply driving for an hour or two, trying to make your delivery on time. It's fun driving at night with the driving rain with the in-game radio cranked. It just *is*.
Beyond the driving bits there's a strategic business simulator buried in here as well. Once you have enough money to purchase your own truck, you can take more profitable jobs. And once you can afford a few extra trucks you can hire drivers to run freight for you and run your own trucking business. You can visit dealerships across Europe to get the best deals.
So yes. Despite every gamer instinct screaming "run away," Euro Truck Simulator 2 is fun. It's a good time.

Driving a semi around Europe doesn't sound all that fun, but unlike most simulators where the fun is further depressed by terrible gameplay, SCS Software has created a masterpiece. There is a lot of long drives for sure, but as the modding community comes alive there are new and larger challenges around every corner. The graphics are excellent, the trucks feel right, and when you mess up and hit the wall you pay for it. These aren't race cars and driving them as such will only come out of your pocket.
The added ability to hire drivers and build a trucking empire, while it still sounds tedious, is not nearly as boring as it sounds. The more you grow your company the more you can goof off and risk that speeding fine, car crash, or other poor decision.
All in all Euro Truck Simulator 2 is worth a look by all gamers. Sit back, turn on the radio (which links to streaming radio stations from Europe), and drive!

ETS2 is probably one of the most studio-supported games out there. There's nothing that the developers haven't reworked, overhauled, teared out and replaced with better, right down to the frigging graphics engine since I own this game.
And they're still not done. SCS is working on solidifying the community, SCS is working on making the game better accessible to modders, SCS runs events.
And they're still not done. New trucks to drive get added in FREE updates.
And they're still not done. A new map that adds Scandinavia is close to release as DLC.
And they're still not done. Everything they improve upon in their upcoming title American truck Simulator gets added to ETS2. Better skyboxes for ATS? Well, have them for ETS2 too. Free of charge.
SCS puts skinpacks up for DLC and the proceedings of those skinpacks flow directly back in the game, with SCS reporting on their website where the money went to, how it was used and what that will mean for your game. Realistic crashing sound-effects? Done.
ETS2 is not only a great game, it's also the result of a success story of developers that actually love what they're doing, love what their game is about and love how their community reaches out to them.
Yes. The community reaches out to SCS, with praise, personal stories and honest appreciation.
SCS is so good that people come to them.
And that reflects in the game.
To think that truck simulator was actually a enthusiast project for SCS only meant for themselves to flex their coding muscles...
SCS deserves special mention as the one studio in a wasteland of corporate greed that does it right.

Ok, so I can't explain why I like this game.
The only thing that I can come up with is that it is a zen experience. Perhaps, the monks carefully constructing their rock gardens were on to something. All of that doesn't matter. This game requires you to pay attention to it. It requires you to be involved and at the controls. In a time when many games can be played while watching TV or a movie, or distracting yourself in other ways, this game forces you to be engaged because if you look away, you may cost yourself thousands.
If you get this game, you will either love it or hate it, and I'm not sure what drives that passion, but for me I can see no way that someone would have mild feelings about it, yet I'm still astonished that I have as strong of feelings as I do.
Anyway, pick this game up if you see it on sale (I got it for six bucks) and give it a shot, you may find that you too like it for unexplicable reasons.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of the most enjoyable sims I have ever played with a superb balance of fun and realism combined with a well-deigned career mode. The game isn't complicated in the slightest which enables you to pick up and play straight away without worrying about minor attention to detail that in other simulators you may have to adhere to.  This game provides a realistic experience but retains the fun which is a major factor for its success.
The presentation is simple but slick with a well organised menu and beauitiful visuals.  The trucks look fantastic as do the other vehicles and weather effects.  The world map covers Great Britain and a large part of Europe on a watered-down scale which is a truly excellent accomplishment considering how big this game is regardless of being scaled down. You can go from Edinburgh to Warsaw in under an hour but this helps keep the gamer interested and allows you to complete several jobs in a single session.
The career mode sees you starting off a truck business from scratch where you are presented with a rundown shack as a base. You need to raise money to buy your own truck to further your bank balance or you can just grab a loan to kickstart your venture off with that extra bit of captial.  You can improve your base, customise and improve your truck, buy new vehicles from numerous real-life manufacturers and hire staff to enhance your growing company. You can rank XP to unlock extra items from new engines to even extra mirrors and minor truck accessories.  You also have a skill tree to unlock more lucrative jobs and longer distance trips.
The driving side is absolutely fantastic from manual to auto controls, filling up petrol, taking a rest, speeding fines and crashes. Everything is there that you'd expect. You can even be penalised for a late delivery. All these factors add to the challenge and ensures that you don't take crafty shortcuts in trying to complete your job.  The sleeping and fuelling element also adds some tactical spice to the game so you have to plan some jouneys beforehand else you may have an accident or breakdown which can lead to penalties such as fines or unnecessary expenditure.
Overall this game is a perfectly balanced sim that isn't overly serious but is executed superbly so it appeals to all gamers who enjoy driving experiences. The excellent presentation and learning curve makes this instantly playable with a well-designed career mode and brilliant driving physics.  Definitely the best simlator out there and highly recommended.

A unique, immersive, relaxed driving experience with business management simulation backing it up and a wide range very highly detailed trucks.
Just so you know - this game does not contain huge simulated cities for you to navigate through, or real-time, actual-duration trips between cities - That's just something you should know up front.
But really, who would want that?   Here's what Euro Truck Simulator does really well:  it takes a long-haul job and comfortably squeezes it into a shorter, simplified (and satisfying) game experience.
The driving is great, after you get your controller settings right (which can take a little trial and error.)  I used a joystick and once I had everything set up, I was very impressed with the way my truck handled and the physics in general.
You have to keep your eyes on the road, or you'll find yourself in trouble pretty quickly, but it is worth using the mouse to look around - the scenery is diverse enough, a few more landmarks and surprises would have been good - some of the locations (especially places like sawmills and refinieries) feel very re-used, but it's hard to imagine how the developers could have improved on this without a truckload of cash.
All the detail is in the vehicles themselves.
If you're into trucks (which I'm not) you'll probably need to change your pants after you take a look at what's on offer; major European truck brands and LOADS of accessories and parts are availble to add to your favourite rig as your progress.  That doesn't float my boat, but I really appreciate the attention to realistic detail.  The cabs are simply stunning and make me wish I owned an Oculus Rift or similar VR headset.
Overall - if you're big into trucks OR you enjoy realistic, immersive vehicle simulators - get into this one, it's well worth the asking price.

How I laughed when I first heard about Euro Truck Simulator 2.
"What a silly idea for a game!" I thought, whilst mocking my friend Jack for appreciating the game.
Well, now I'm here eating my own words because this is one of my favourite games of all time. The concept is so small and drab but the execution is excellent and the appeal is abundant. I've always been a fan of Tycoon games and ones that involve money/time management and the general growing of a business. In ETS2, you have to work your way up from a rookie driver doing local deliveries to a pro driver who is trekking across europe in the truck of his choice.
The game is realistic, with great sounds and amazing physics. There are so many customisable options that add great depth. Driving is a joy and it really feels like you have your own job in trucking. But best of all, you're free! This is the PERFECT game to settle down, relax, put some music on and just drive and think. It's truly amazing and that's the appeal I referenced earlier.
So, to conclude, don't judge the book by its cover! Give this gem a go if you see it on sale because I promise you, it will not disappoint! Easily one of my top 5 games ever.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 isn't a game for everyone.  However, if you've ever driven a truck of any kind, and towed some sort of cargo (i.e. - a trailer, boat, camper), then this game may appeal to you.  The basic premise is to drive your truck through the cities and rural areas of Europe while "loosely" following traffic laws and safely arriving at your destination with cargo intact, on-time.  It doesn't sound like much, but it is quite time consuming, and can wear on you if you try to log too many hours on this game.
The graphics and sound are not great, but adequate for this type of game, but the control is superb when compared to driving a real big rig.  Especially if you manually park the trailer at the end of a run.
I bought the main game and DLC during one of the major Steam sales, so it makes playing this game even sweeter.  I enjoy picking this game up from time to time, logging maybe 3 hours, and then leaving it to come back weeks later, although some people I know like to play for weeks at a time.
If you're looking to break the monotony of the usual gaming experience, maybe give this one a try.   To me, playing this game is kind of like reading a book series that you like to keep coming back to.

Yes, I've put more than 250+ hours into this game. The vast majority of those were within the first year of this game going Early Access. I must admit in that first year I had a good deal of fun playing with a couple of buddies with an understanding that this game was but an alpha. I didn't expect it to perfect or ready to ship by any means.
However the fun soon wore off. The gameplay got stale and the bugs and general lack of features made the game grow uninteresting. Over time I played the game less and less frequently, then stopped playing it all together. I would check the release notes every now. After each update I'd log in and find a few new features or additions to the game. Oh great! You added campfires, cool! Effect on my gameplay? Negligable. You added some new weapons? Also cool, except for the fact that the loot system is so ♥♥♥♥ed I'd be lucky to find a magazine let alone ammo to put in it.
Before long I stopped playing more than an a couple of hours after each update. Now 3 years in I've seen practically zero progress on the game. The same bugs I encountered at the start are still present. What prompted me to write this review was firing up this game after not having played for several months. I rejoined the server where I last left off (surprising in itself as I expected a character wipe giving the time that passed).
To my delight I picked up a rifle that I hadn't encountered since when the game first launched. I even found some mags, awesome! (though the ammo was still scarce, nbd). Then I encounter some zombies, a even bigger surprise considering the last time I played they weren't even in the game anymore. I killed them, awesome again! I actually had a motivation to use the  gear I picked up. And then I went to patch my wounds. I use my bandages and lo and behold, the rifle I was so happy to have just picked up disppears, the same problem I had when I first started playing the game. Stupidly I forgot that I ran the chance of losing whatever I already had in my hands if I used something else without first dropping what I was holding. What was  an annoyance 3 years ago is still par for the course, how stupid of me to expect that they'd fix it by now.
The developers made their money, and as far as I can tell they have no interest in actually producing a playable and working game. This game is the sole reason I will never again back an early access game. The game had such great potential and none of it came to fruition. I've played Arma DayZ mods that are further along than this stand-alone title. This is pathetic given the  amount of money this game has raked in.
My verdict, unless this game makes serious progress and soon there is absolutely no reason to purchase this  game. DatZ is basically the same early access title I first picked up years ago. If you're remotely interested, just buy Arma 3 and play the mods instead, there's more to do and just as functional. If this game was a mod, it'd get a pass. Instead its a stand-alone title that can't stand on its  own legs and has been a massive disappointment.
Bang up job, Bohemia. 3 years in and you still haven't released a proper build? You managed to get my money on this POS, and again on Arma 3 to install someone elses mods to get the sort of experience as what you promised with DayZ. It certainly won't happen again.

Overall, Undertale is a great game and deserves any praise it gets. I'm not an emotional guy nor do I really care about the fate of fictional characters in any game/movie/book/show, but Undertale gave its characters such a personality and such a backstory that I legitamately felt bad for killing them, making me hesitant to do a genocide run. The only real flaws with the game are the fanbase and the game's replay value. I'm not the first one to mention the fanbase warning, but I'm sure the majority of these other reviews don't mention the fact that the game is sadly only truly fully playable about 3 times before you get bored, and that's including the multiple endings. One thing I recommend with this game is to go in blind to have the best experience and do it your own way for at least the first few playthroughs. If you want to get a specific ending but you couldn't really figure out how, just check online. The game is definitely a work of art and one of the best indie games I've ever played next to Shovel Knight.

How I laughed when I first heard about Euro Truck Simulator 2.
"What a silly idea for a game!" I thought, whilst mocking my friend Jack for appreciating the game.
Well, now I'm here eating my own words because this is one of my favourite games of all time. The concept is so small and drab but the execution is excellent and the appeal is abundant. I've always been a fan of Tycoon games and ones that involve money/time management and the general growing of a business. In ETS2, you have to work your way up from a rookie driver doing local deliveries to a pro driver who is trekking across europe in the truck of his choice.
The game is realistic, with great sounds and amazing physics. There are so many customisable options that add great depth. Driving is a joy and it really feels like you have your own job in trucking. But best of all, you're free! This is the PERFECT game to settle down, relax, put some music on and just drive and think. It's truly amazing and that's the appeal I referenced earlier.
So, to conclude, don't judge the book by its cover! Give this gem a go if you see it on sale because I promise you, it will not disappoint! Easily one of my top 5 games ever.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 isn't a game for everyone.  However, if you've ever driven a truck of any kind, and towed some sort of cargo (i.e. - a trailer, boat, camper), then this game may appeal to you.  The basic premise is to drive your truck through the cities and rural areas of Europe while "loosely" following traffic laws and safely arriving at your destination with cargo intact, on-time.  It doesn't sound like much, but it is quite time consuming, and can wear on you if you try to log too many hours on this game.
The graphics and sound are not great, but adequate for this type of game, but the control is superb when compared to driving a real big rig.  Especially if you manually park the trailer at the end of a run.
I bought the main game and DLC during one of the major Steam sales, so it makes playing this game even sweeter.  I enjoy picking this game up from time to time, logging maybe 3 hours, and then leaving it to come back weeks later, although some people I know like to play for weeks at a time.
If you're looking to break the monotony of the usual gaming experience, maybe give this one a try.   To me, playing this game is kind of like reading a book series that you like to keep coming back to.

So this review is just a drop in the bucket of glimmering reviews, but I have to say that this game was amazingly crafted. The gameplay, though simple, requires some skill and attention to detail, as well as problem solving. The soundtrack is fantastic (as well as the officially sanctioned Undertale "Determination" album bu Richaad EB and Ace Waters). And the layers to this game, as well as what it suggests about the human person, are wonderfully thought-provoking. For me to highly reccommend a game without Steam achievements is nigh unheard of, but that's how wonderful this game was.
Mild spoilers ahead:
I highly recommend playing all the endings for this game. Not only is the depth of character creation and the unique status of being a "player" related, but it makes you think about just what an experience playing video games can be. The endings will make you think deeply about what our choices mean, how our actions affect others, and maybe - just maybe - reinforce the idea that one bad choice doesn't make a bad person. Rather, a person who continues to make bad choices for the sake of others' sufferring... well, I'll let you make your mind up about that one. ;)

This Game is good. It isn't the best rpg, or the greatest game of all time. Many fans hype it up to be THE GREATEST THING EVER, but I can't really agree with it. I love games like Earthbound. I love Mother 3 as well. I find those two games to be better than this one. This game has a strong beginning, but it gets worse as it goes on. After Waterfall (which is the best area in the game IMO) the games slowly gets worse. Once the character Alphys gets introduced the game feels like it has to talk to you nonstop to remind you "IM FUNNY RIGHT?” It gets a little irritating.  The game also gets more linear and boring. The combat in Undertale is... all right. The bullet hell inspired selections are really fun, but have huge difficulty spikes. But combat is repetitive and boring, and when you’re doing a genocide run it’s SO bad. The pixel art in Undertale is a little ugly at times too. The over world sprites are bad, showing little to no detail. The battle sprites all much better, but in a weird design choice aren't in color. It does give the game some style however. I know some people might not enjoy the lack of color, but I don’t mind it too much. It may seem like I hate this game, but I don’t. I might not feel like it's the greatest game of all time, but it’s still good, and DEFINIETLY WORTH PLAYING! It’s an experience. By the way I don’t find Ocarina of Time the best game either so I’m not just saying it isn’t the best game because of that. I can’t get into why I don’t like Ocarina of Time in this review however.

This is literally the greatest bloody game I've ever played.. And it's not even a game!
Euro Truck Simulator 2 really knows how to involve the 'player', and make him or her feel like they're actually driving a truck across Europe. The driving mechanics are mostly simple and easy to use, as is the management of the business, and buying/upgrading trucks and garages, hiring and firing drivers, and even receiving emails about income/outcome, making the game easy to use, whilst providing features that make it so much more realistic.
Though it focuses on the roads, the atmosphere and surroundings in Euro Truck Simulator 2 are ASTONISHING! With everything from aeroplanes to hot air balloons decorating the skies, and hills, farms and wind turbines seasoning the land, it's impossible not to appreciate the beauty of the world as you go through yet another long day of work. As if this wasn't enough, the "game" world is HUGE, and takes literally hours to cross, as well as perpetuating the realism (after all, it is supposed to be a large chunk of Europe) this makes it much more interesting, as there are so many diverse places to see you'll just have to spend the hours it takes to see them all!
The presence of things such as tiredness and reducing fuel levels make the game even more real, and can add a nice amount of tension at the right (or wrong) times. When I found myself driving in the dark in Belgium one night, and all of a sudden the word "Drifting" polluted my screen I was hectic! I was desperately checking my map for the nearest place I could stop to rest, while simultaneously ensuring that I'd finish the job on time if I did so. These moments really do make what may be considered a dull and boring job as exciting as it is, and can take at least a few hours for the 'player' to begin to adjust and remember to keep an eye on when they sleep and how much fuel they have.
As a whole, many will see this as a 'game' in which you merely "drive a truck", but it's so much more than that. In a similar way to improving a character on an RPG, the expansion of your company in Euro Truck Simulator 2 is incredibly rewarding, allowing you to deliver more dangerous things or do longer jobs. These produce intense motivation in the 'player', and you'll find yourself striving to expand even when away from the "game".
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is truly amazing, it provides endless unforgettable experiences, not all good, but none at all that you won't think back on and smile about your first day, when you held up traffic for almost 30 minutes because you got stuck on that sharp turn, seems almost like yesterday. And that's exactly what this "game" aims to do, to give you something you'll both enjoy and feel good about, and it not only acheives that, but goes a step further and pulls at your heartstrings.
If you haven't bought this game already, why not? You will not be disappointed.

Rust, a true survival game by Facepunch Studios. Inspired by DayZ, Minecraft and Stalker. It aims to create a hostile environment in which emergent gameplay can flourish. Your ultimate goal is to survive. To do this you should gather resources. Hitting a tree with a rock will give you wood, hitting a rock with a rock will give you rock and ore. You can then craft a hatchet from the wood and rock, allowing you to gather faster. You can go out and hunt a variety of wildlife such as boars, chickens, rabbits, bears, wolves and deer. Or be hunted by them...
Once you have killed an animal you can butcher it to gather its meat and skin. You can craft a fire using wood and cook the meat inside the fire. Then you can eat. You face two major dangers in game. Rust is a multiplayer game, so there will be other players trying to survive in the same way that you are. Unfortunately for you they can find you, kill you and take your stuff.
But in opposite to them, you can kill them and take their stuff as well. Or maybe you can make friends and help each other survive? Better is to take your true friends you trust and rule the world.
World is harsh. Falling from a height will kill you. Being exposed to radiation for an extended period will kill you. Starving will kill you. Being cold will kill you. Animals will kill you. Player will kill you. Helicopters will kill you. Bleeding will kill you. And automatic guards can kill you.
So yes, hardness? Australia, everything want to kill you.

Very good timewaster. Usually play it whilst I'm downloading a video game/movie. The game itself can be addictive, with it's good use of 3D graphics tech, it provides some pretty and light-hearted visuals, particularly in bad weather. The gameplay can be entertaining, but after a while it gets a bit repetetive, since all you are doing is delivering supplies across Europe. Although once you deliver the supplies you've been carrying for around 30 minutes, depending on the distance of the delivery, you feel a sense of satisfaction that you've delivered them in one piece, which can be rare if you get impatient with the speed cameras and A.I. Euro Truck Simulator 2 provides realistic physics for the official drivable trucks in the game, but it gets a bit silly - but fun - once your speed is over 100 mph. The modding community is quite large for ETS 2; there are mods that swap the companies in the game - ranging from the truck companies to the supply companies - for the real life companies that they represent, respectively. The customisation system for your own personal trucks is a bit scarce, but seperates your truck from the other NPC trucks roaming around Europe. When you first start the game, you'll need to create your character, name him/her, pick his/her portrait and name and pick a logo for the company they will work for. You'll start at level 0, and there will be an optional tutorial to teach you the basics of the game. Part of the tutorial is your first truck delivery. You will start the game without your own truck, and you will have to deliver supplies for companies in their own trucks. The more deliveries you complete, and the better condition the supplies arrive in, gives your character more XP to level up with. Once you level up, you'll be able to contribute 1 point towards 5 hierarchy-style skill routes, as well as being able to buy upgrades for your truck once you get your hands on one.
I've just noticed this review has got a bit long, so I'll end it here. If you like good time-wasting, driving games, that gives you a vibrant look at modern day Europe, with a company simulation counterpart, this game might be for you.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a truck simulation game created by SCS Software, using OpenGL. It is the sequel to Euro Truck Simulator, with a redone physics and game engine. The player can drive across a significant part of Europe.
Player should pick up a variety of cargoes, and delivering them to the desired destination.
The game features 8 different trucks, includes: DAF, Volvo, Man, Scania, Renault, M. Benz and Iveco. 4 of them are licensed already.
Gameplay
You can start your game in one of the following countries: Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Slovakia, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. You will be asked to select your desired city in one of them. Your garage will be located there. So the journey will be begin. In the beginning, you wont have enough money and experience to buy a truck, so you will start with quick deliveries. You also can get loans. You can open your own company, hiring drivers from all over the map. What you need is to have enough money to afford their trucks purchase and a free slot in a garage. You can buy a garage in every city you tend, Then you should upgrade it.
The gameplay is so sweet and handy. Its obvious how the developers have worked on it. and they have done it nicely. Riding trucks seems so realistic with a great system of handling. So after delivering any cargo, you will be given an amount of money and EXP will be gained. EXP is needed to unlock trucks and items. As you gain an amount of EXP, you earn a level as well. You also will be estimated as your level in the game. The system of opening of company makes a motivation for the player. Its almost the goal of the game. AI of the vehicles in ETS 2 is actually OK. its average, but they are making it better with every patch to make the game an awesome experience for the player. Accidents are not so realistic. Plus you wont get any physical damage. After any accident your truck will be damaged, but not physically. actually nothing happens to your truck. Its a defect. The game physic is good and its being improved by every patch.
You wont see any police in the game. But there are traffic lights, speed limit, toll stops and accident penalty. if you violate any mentioned things [except toll], you should pay an specific amount of fine. This systems made without any defect. The driver will become tired, so you should pull over in an specific place to get rest. Gas stations, repair stations, drivers agencies, Truck showplaces and resting stations are available in the game. For buying a truck, you need to visit its shop [which are in its own particular city] or you can use online purchasing. Any truck needs a slot in your garage. The limitation of slots is 5 in per garage. Also drivers you can hire are limited at 116 at the moment. Overall, this part of the game is decent. except some defects like lack of physical damages. Also the map is so much big. thats a fantastic point. so much to explore with a great system of running company that let you enjoy the title for many days.
Graphic
The graphics are stunning. Lighting system and shadows are awesome. Vegetables, trees and environments made perfectly. Designing of trucks is amazing. Into the cabin has very good details with a perfect designing. But designing cities are kinda average. You also can see humans in the cities. There are also some famous places made in the game. Cargoes have a good variety. Weather system is great. Raining seems so realistic. You can enjoy the darkness of the night, the sunset, the sunrise and the sunlight in the middle of the noon. Also Other vehicles seem average.
This part is one of the most important factors that makes this simulator so special, and puts it as the best truck simulator ever made.
Sound
Well, the sound effects part is nothing special. I cant really talk about this. The sound seems so low when you are into the cabin camera. You should switch to another camera mode to hear it better. Its overall made well. There is also online radio streaming. Its decent. Also you can make your customized track list from your own music library.

Do you like big trucks? Do you like Europe? Are you willing to eat sleep and♥♥♥♥♥♥behind a wheel of 10 tonne road monster? Are you willing to deliver a giant tank of gasoline from Paris to Glasgow? If the answer is yes, this game is just for you. A beatiful environment, active community and an actual developers who listen to the fans, this game have all the things a car simulation game has to offer. Be sure to turn off that damn parking brake.

DayZ is a bit hard to talk about in terms of an overall positive or negative because there are so many aspects of the game that go either way.
There are numerous bugs with the title, and sometimes it feels as though they will never be resolved. I've been playing for a few years now, and I can safely say that these glitches have turned me away more than a few times. This is indeed the biggest problem with the title.
On the other hand, the gameplay itself can be a lot of fun, with a few qualifiers. I enjoy the slow pace, which is present in travel time, briefly interrupted by moments of panic. I can be constantly engaged, and thus not bored. It's soothing , and the gun fights feel more special because they're not common. Here's where we get to the qualifiers, however...
First, you have to be willing to put up with bugs that will result in an unfair death. Although the last two patches (.59 and .60) have dramatically improved performance, there is still the occasional issue of server side lag.
Second, this game is hard on new players and people with low-end PCs. Again, this was more true before the current patch, but is certainly still an issue.
Finally, be ready for the game to change. Right now, DayZ is focused around the pvp element, as surviving is relatively easy. The Devs have said, however, that in .61 and upcoming patches they are attempting to move to a more survival oriented game. That's fine, there will still be pvp, but it may not be what you are looking for.
Overall, I would say you should consider what you enjoy when purchasing DayZ. Although "walking simulator" is a bit of an over simplification, there are indeed large segments of the game that involves travel. Will that kill the game for you, or are you the type of person who can forgive a game for problems that you feel aren't important? Either way fine, don't feel judged if you don't like the concept when I did. It’s your money.

Euro Truck Simulator 2.
Exec Summary: Great graphics, good immersion, plenty of functionality to live up to 'Sim' status.  It's almost addictive and it keeps getting better. Chances are high you'll love it too!
Unless specifically noted, this review refers to the official game content only.
The Trucks
All the main Euro marks are covered albeit Mercedes are listed as Majestic due to a licence issue. Within each mark, there are various models available within the game with more being added regularly, officially into the game. Customisation of your truck offers a vast set of paint jobs, lights, furniture and other options.
The Map
Recently expanded to include the "Going East DLC", the map is both graphically pleasing and pretty extensive affording long multi country trips which can include ferry trips and  Channel Tunnel train trips into and out of the United Kingdom. There is lots of scope to develop this map but as a default within the game, it offers plenty of diversity in routes and scenery
The Game-play
Build your trucking empire is the principle point here. This means starting off driving jobs as a employee driver until you gain enough in-game money to buy a garage and truck. As you develop, you can hire drivers, expand the garage, buy additional trucks, open new garages and take over the ETS2 trucking world. Starting as a driver for hire is good as you can access all the various models of truck before you'd be able to as an owner operator.
The in-game clock is accelerated, the distances are shortened and in so doing, it is possible to cover the large distances necessary in an augmented real-world time period. This is balanced well and makes the game very playable and still maintains it's Sim status.
Penalties
Fines are payable for, amongst other things, speeding, crashing into other road users, failing to rest on time and cancelling the job your previously accepted.
This is a single player game.
There is a World Of Truck website linked to the game [not steam exclusive!] which as of this review is early in it's development. This resource however bodes well for the future, whatever this will mean!
The Developer
SCS Software is the developer and deserves a special mention. They've been in Truck Sims for a while and they fully understand their ETS2 community. They are regularly updating meaningful patches, DLCs and minor updates to the game and have communicated a future roadmap which they are actively executing on.
As a small developer in terms of headcount, this Prague based team remain transparent with the community and deserve the strong community respect that they have earned. They are a shining example of the new breed of game developers that have emerged in the recent years who clearly put community right up there on their priorities list by 'action' and not merely by 'words'.
Other coming and already in work projects from SCS include 'Bus Simulator' and 'American Truck Simulator'
Gaming Peripherals
With support for various steering wheels, pedals, TrackIR and already announced support for Oculus Rift, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a game that will allow all players to use their preferred peripherals in their game playing style.
Areas for development
Too many 2 lane Motorway with no exist lane ramps!
Map does not cover Ireland or Western Europe, Scandanivia
Cities are pretty small
A lot of repetition in buildings and assets on the official map
Traffic is not heavy ever and there are no traffic jams
The is no physical damage model
AI is a little too predicable and occasionally display a strange behaviour [SCS official AI update is due within weeks of this review]
No accident, random delays or random diversions programmed into the AI game play. [There are some roadworks and speed limitations however]
Driver management is limited
The Mods and amazing Modding community:
SCS Software have been supportive of the vast and capable modding community which springs up quickly around all successful gaming titles. Unlike some developers, SCS has been open to supporting mods within their game. Notable mods include Map additions, trailer and loads, traffic and weather/season mods. Moreover, if there is a truck [tractor unit] of interest that is not in game officially, chances are someone has made a mod which can be used within  the game. Much of this addresses the above 'Areas for Development' points in advance of SCS themselves bringing in official updates to address them.
This all makes for a game that will likely command your gaming time for quite a deal longer than you might think upon initial purchase.

- AI traffic have their annoying quirks  (but the developer says they are working on improving this).

Let me start by saying it is an amazing experience! Fun to drive and totally enjoyable. Its still needs some polish (AI, I'm looking at you), but overall it's a great game. Let me illustrate.
Major buying points:
- Great Simulation: The truck drives and feels like a truck in the road, plus it has a lot of "simulation" customization. For instance, you can simulate a 12 gearbox with a 6 gear stick wheel + shift button. Fully compatible with the XB360 controller makes it a relly nice simulation experience for a couch driver like myself.
- Great Scenery/Lanscapes: It's not Crysis 3 nor BF4, but you will love the scenery and special Europe landscapes it shows to you while driving. It is static scenery, but not less beautiful.
- Great Weather Simulation: It has its own "rain probability" slide to adjust how often you would like to see rain (too bad no snow though) and when it does rain, everything changes like it should and you would expect (maybe driving simulation could change a little more).
- Night/Day Cycle: Night is gorgeus, specially when there's rain. Small roads make this challening as hell when you're on a quick/urgent delivery. And while in the topic of night, headlights. You can not have a big truck and not have big lights, right? High beams are a great thing to watch as they make dark into glorious day! Well, not like that, but yeah. Oh, opposing lane drivers won't like it though, heh. And Day, well, you get to see the scenery and all that. Foggy mornings are great (I just made this up, haha).
- Other stuff models: Ok, the trucks are the great main dish of visual pleasure, but when you're driving, you get to say stuff like this: "hey, I know that car!" and "well, I think that's my car!". I got a close look at the other stuff and they might not be the greatest visual fest, but they are and try to be realistically accurate (not graphically, again).
- Economy: This is a great thing from the game and that is you can become a Truck overlord and go from driving to managing a spread sheet with numbers! Ok, that doesn't sound so fun at first, but you get to manage your own company or be a lonely wolf forever; the choice is there while you level and earn money at least. And yes, you can drive AND manage, haha.
Things that need to be worked on:
- Traffic AI: This is a really troublesome point, since the BIG part of the simulation is to have a decent environment you're doing the simulation on. The traffic takes a major part in that regard and it is still "not there" in terms of "yeah, a regular driver would do that" impressions. Good thing is that it is being worked on and it should improve sooner than later, but it is acceptable in its current state.
- Amount of other stuff: Ok, scenery and landscapes are there, they're great looking and all that, but cities do not reflect the HUGE size they should.
- Winter! Yes, this one is self-explainatory. There is no "snow season" in the game. I'd love one. We get rain though, but not "seasons". Maybe the way time goes by made this one a tough call.
- GPS: There is no exploration mode GPS. This one is puzzling for me, since they had one in the other 18 Wheels of Steel series. You do get the transport GPS though (helps a LOT), but when you're just driving around and want to get to "B", where "B" is on the other side of Europe, you have to stop from time to time and check that you're not lost. Maybe it's part of the simulation, but this is not 1990 when I had to look at a map for directions.
Well, there you have them.
My veredict is that you should really give this game a try if you like to drive stuff (sims or not) and enjoy a little extra on your "simulation dish" (economy point; read back a lil').
Cheers!

Earthbound + Homestuck + Touhou + Feels: The game
Okay, That's not the most accurate description in the world, but if you want to know what I actually feel about the game, keep reading.
I first heard of this game after scrolling through Ifunny and finding a picture of a pixellated skeleton talking about spaghetti. I was confused, and assumed this was from OFF, another video game that I was uninformed about (and still am) at the time. As time went on, I realized that "OFF" had a different art style than I remembered it having, and went into more investigation. Eventually, I found out the name: UNDERTALE, and noticed several of my close friends at school had taken an interest in the game, mainly my crush. From what I saw of the game at that point, there were two skeletons named after typefaces, and a flower. And, that was about it. So, one day, I downloaded the demo, and found out about the flower's nefarious intentions, and met a motherly goat woman, who literally held my hand throughout the first section of the game, before going off to run some errands, leaving me unattended.
From there, I explored the ruins and fought monsters nonchalantly, with little consideration of the MERCY or ACT buttons, with a belief they were simply options that allowed for a slightly different ending with largely unaffected gameplay. I continued to believe this, picking up the full version after getting stuck in a room with a breakaway floor that I couldn't solve. When I found out the same problem was present in the full game, I sat for 5 minutes, wondering where I was supposed to go, before I found the solution, and continued in my progress. Soon, I met a comically depressed ghost and discovered the importance of the ACT and SPARE buttons, as they allowed me to conclude the fight peacefully. The ghost bid me farewell, and I progressed onward to The goat woman's house, where she caringly checked to see if I was okay, and invited me inside. After a short while in this humble abode, I took a short nap in my new room, awaking to find a slice of cinnamon-butterscotch pie. I took it, knowing I'd likely have to use it soon, and inquired about how to leave the Ruins. My Adoptive Goat mother left quietly into the basement, and I soon followed. What ensued was a heartstring-tugging battle, which I won by showing nothing but MERCY. The goat woman hugged me tightly, wishing me well on my journey, and I left silently.
What proceeded afterwards would most likely be too much of a spoiler to speak of in this review, but I can outline it.
You will have several romantic outings with two skeleton brothers
You will Duel a Fish Woman Determined to take your soul
You will Fight a spider woman who wants your money
You will have a dance-off with an effeminate robot
You will hear the heartbreaking tale of the monsters' hopes of seeing freedom crushed
You will Discover you aren't the first human to fall into the underground
You will find out the evil flower has a closer relationship to the royalty than anyone may think
You will be forced to take the soul of a broken man who only wishes to see his children and wife
You will remind another child what love feels like
You will hug the main antagonist
You will have a good time
You will stay determined
You will have fun
You will cry
But...
No crying until the ending!
